description: Prosthetic Technology 3 builds on prior learning, focusing on removable partial prosthodontics. In this course, students further develop their understanding of the design principles, biomechanics, and functional requirements of removable partial dentures. The theoretical concepts introduced in Prosthetic Technology 3 are directly applied in Laboratory Practicum 3, enabling students to translate knowledge into practical laboratory skills. The course also introduces fixed prosthodontics, laying a foundation for Prosthetic Technology 4 in Year 3. As part of the course, students participate in Communication Skills for Oral Health 1, a structured module that progressively develops interpersonal and professional communication skills relevant to the oral health environment. Students also complete the online-based Public Oral Health module, which explores key public health principles as they relate to oral health. Much of the course content is delivered online, with compulsory assessment tasks that support independent and flexible learning.
title: Prosthetic Technology 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course examines accounting from a holistic perspective by examining not only financial and management accounting topics, but also the social, environmental, and governance impacts of business activities. The course prepares students to understand, analyse, and report upon an organisation's financial, social, governance and environmental information and to use this information for accountable decision-making. Students are presented with methods and tools required to analyse and understand the meaning of financial data that will facilitate their role as managers running a sustainable business. The course also introduces a focus on social, environmental and governance using external reporting that addresses the accountability of organisations. Lastly, it focuses on gaining an understanding of accounting in light of natural resources, namely water accounting. The course offers insights into the use of Water Accounting Reports to report on water as well as key aspects of corporate water accounting. All students are expected to begin studies before the first designated face to face lecture presentation or online session for this course.
title: Accounting for Accountability
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course examines financial accounting and information disclosure requirements for reporting entities at various junctures in their life cycle. The first weeks of the course introduce the company form of business organisation and applies accounting standards to more complex business transactions than those introduced in 7111AFE. The remainder of the course introduces and applies accounting standards to corporate groups. Students analyse and interpret complex transactions in the consolidated financial statements of an Australian listed company.
title: Corporate Accounting
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Effective management decision-making requires reliable, valid and up-to-date market research. This course introduces the basic concepts of the research process including problem definition, research design, measurement, data collection, data analysis and presentation of research findings. This is an important skill set to add to your career credentials.
title: Marketing Research and Intelligence
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Marketing success is highly dependent on the effectiveness of marketing communication between your organisation and the target customer, and these communications are achieved through various product, advertising and promotional strategies. This course will introduce you to the fascinating world of advertising and the strategic use of advertising to raise customer awareness and appreciation of your organisation's products and services.
title: Advertising and Integrated Marketing Communications
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: In a fast-paced, constantly changing sector, it takes a new kind of mindset to stay ahead of the game. Developing this digital marketing mindset is a core part of this course. You'll be capable of explaining and applying digital marketing concepts, conducting a digital audit, and understanding the benefits of an integrated marketing plan that utilises new and traditional tools. Your strategies will be supported by digital marketing concepts that will work as online platforms evolve, because they are based on timeless attributes such as exceptional communication, creativity, problem solving, and critical thinking skills. Guided by a digital media mindset, you'll be proficient at integrating media channels within a robust, evidence-based plan. It's these skills that will ensure you stay relevant in marketing, because even as the platforms, channels and algorithms change you'll be able to respond with initiative and innovation, backed by a deep understanding of how to influence consumer behaviour in the digital space.
title: Digital Marketing and AI
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course helps students become competent and ethical strategic communicators. Student are immersed in the craft of persuasive writing within contemporary communications industries, while considering relevant conceptual and ethical issues that are typically encountered in a professional communications environment. Prior Assumed: At least one first year unit in Business Communication, Creative Writing, Journalism or Public Relations.
title: Public Writing and Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: In just two decades, digital media and the world wide web have fundamentally altered the operations of businesses around the globe. This course gives you a strategic-level working knowledge of digital and social media marketing. The course further introduces best practices in acquiring, communicating with consumers, and retaining customers on the internet. The course examines digital technologies and their impact on, and implications for, marketing strategy, consumer behaviour, market segmentation, advertising and media planning.
title: Digital and Social Media Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces the importance of microorganisms to natural and designed ecosystems, biogeochemical cycles, trophic pathways and their beneficial applications. The course provides an understanding of the relationships between living organisms and their abiotic environment, and the living nature of soil, water and air. The course covers fundamentals including cellular transport, microbial growth, environmentally significant biochemical pathways and the taxonomic classification of autotrophic and heterotrophic organisms together with their resource requirements - light, oxygen and nutrients. Ecosystem concepts of food webs, energy flow and mineral cycles are introduced with particular emphasis on applications: decomposition, biogeochemical cycles, wastewater treatment, composting, bio- and phytoremediation, catchment management, and human and ecosystem health. The laboratories cover microbial biodiversity, techniques for the culture, staining and enumeration of microorganisms, animal and plant diversity with an emphasis on water quality and macroinvertebrate sampling, and environmental field monitoring.
title: Environmental Microbiology and Ecology
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course serves as a general introduction to the field of Marine Science, and the scope of materials to be covered by the Bachelor of Marine Science degree and the Marine Biology major of the BSc. Elements of biological, physical and chemical oceanography and their applications to marine and coastal management will be discussed, with the help of local and global examples.
title: Introduction to Marine Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: An understanding of the chemical structure of drugs, as well as the relationships between drug structure and pharmacological activity is fundamental to Pharmacy. Continuing with the themes developed through Chemical Pharmacology I (3023PHM), this course aims to provide students with a detailed understanding of the mechanism of action of drugs, the medicinal chemistry that underpins drug structures, the relationships between chemical structure and pharmacological activity, and the metabolism of drugs. In conjunction with information gained during the first two years of the program, this course provides essential skills and knowledge required in the MPharm program. It is a companion course to Human Pharmacology II (3028PHM). The two courses cover the same general topics and drug classes, but the emphasis here is on structure-activity relationships, mechanism of action and broader pharmacodynamics (PD), pharmacokinetics (PK) and physiochemical properties of drugs.
title: Chemical Pharmacology II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course deals systematically with important aspects of the main drug groups. This includes their chemical origin and synthesis (where relevant), as well as their chemical properties that are relevant to their mode of action, side effects, toxicity, and metabolism.
title: Chemical Pharmacology I
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Focusing on the teaching of Measurement and Geometry, and Statistics and Probability, this course aims to develop personal understanding of mathematical concepts and processes, and develop an understanding of teaching strategies which promote problem-solving, mathematical reasoning and use of ICTs at the primary level.
title: Mathematics Education 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course considers the molecular organisation of cells and the biochemical properties of the major classes of biological compounds which exist in and contribute to the cellular environment. Biochemistry laboratory studies are included.
title: Structural Biochemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course examines the molecular and cellular basis of the immune system, with a particular focus on human immunology, the immune system's role in response to infection and contributions to some common immune pathologies including auto-immunity and allergic diseases.
title: Immunology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces students to science education in the primary school. It examines the nature of science, inquiry learning and scientific literacy as important areas of development in science education. This course emphasises teaching science as a way of thinking about and explaining events and phenomena. Relevant concepts and manipulative skills are developed to teach topics in the physical and chemical sciences and the space content from Earth and Space sciences in an integrated and ecologically sustainable manner. The Lectures are interactive and delivered Live as Hybrid to allow students unable to attend the location to fully participate in the live experience. The lectures will also be recorded.
title: Primary Science Education 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course gives students a thorough grounding in the physical and biological processes occurring on the coastline and in near shore marine habitats, especially sandy beaches, wetlands, rocky headlands and coral reefs, the habitats that dominate the eastern Australian coastline. Anthropogenic threats to these habitats will also be discussed. Assessment involves a literature review assignment, laboratory written reports, and an end-of-trimester written examination. The course is aimed primarily at Bachelor of Marine Science and Bachelor of Science (Marine Biology major) students, but is also suitable for students from other biological or environmental science disciplines. Assumed background: 1041SCG, 1007ENV or equivalent
title: Coastal Environments
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: From the mid-18th century to the present time we have witnessed a series of major technological innovations that have transformed business, work and jobs. Examples include the steam engine, electricity and steel, Henry Ford's production line system of manufacturing and, nearer our own time I.T. biotechnology and nanotechnology. The Austrian economist, Joseph Schumpeter famously referred to such innovations as "gales of creative destruction" old industries being swept away, to be replaced by new ones. Schumpeter's gales of creative destruction continue to impact business, work and jobs. Organizations now have to compete globally; organizational structures have to be flatter, work contracts more flexible, business functions more interlinked, and strategies more innovation-based. Business has become a learning race, with human talent and intangible intellectual capabilities at its core. This course is about how contemporary organizations are dealing with these issues and what we can learn from their attempts to anticipate, adjust to and take advantage of change. The course is both theoretical and practical with insights being provided from the academic literature and businesses. We will look at change from an organizational perspective and seek the answers to a number of questions that are important to those of us that live our lives in organizations. What is happening in the world that may deliver changes in the future? What is the best way to manage change? What do I do if I am asked to lead a change? How do we effectively implement a change? What do we do about resistance? How can we better adapt to the changes we encounter as employees?
title: Leading Policy and Organisational Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: GBS Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: GBS Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course will provide students with a detailed understanding of the nature, process, coordination and management of business logistics in achieving sustainable business outcomes. Current issues considered include: warehousing and packaging, transport and its management, supply network designing for material/service/information flows; performance measurement and the engagement with external logistics service providers, logistics in a carbon constrained environment; scheduling in transport and service industries, and redesigning material and service flows in supply chains/networks.
title: International Business Logistics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course is intended for engineering and project managers. The main features of this course stress the importance of proactive performance measurements. Topics related to quality and safety management systems will be covered in detail. Students will be provided with the skills needed to asses existing performance management systems, introduce improvements, and communicate effectively with top management and with colleagues in multi-disciplinary teams.
title: Quality and Performance Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course serves as an introductory platform to business processes. It offers both conceptual and practical guidance for achieving competitive advantage by managing business processes. Business process management involves the deliberate and collaborative design, management and goal definition of end-to-end sets of activities that create value for customers. Extensive use of supplementary material from Management, Marketing, Logistics and Human Resources literature is made. Key aspects of business processes at the management, operational and support level are investigated and supporting theories explored looking at the work of Taylor, Harmon, Davenport, Hammer and Porter to name some. By taking a holistic view of the organisation, that transcends vertical, horizontal, external and geographical boundaries, this course provides a road map for guiding organisations to analyse, re-design and improve business processes. Finally, the effects of the application of Information Systems on business processes are investigated in terms of how the processes themselves are captured and become an integral part of the technology.
title: The Management of Business Processes
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This unit develops theoretical understandings and practical skills in training and development processes. It covers group facilitation and training, adult learning theories and principles, and individual and organisational development. The unit focus is on the critical issues of training and skills development faced by today's organisations as they strive to meet the changing needs of their competitive environments. In this regard, national frameworks and organisational strategies are also examined.
title: Developing Talent
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The primary emphasis of this course is about Human Resource Management (HRM) in organisations. A central theme throughout this course is the contribution of HRM to the efficiency and productivity of organisations. The course delivery will balance theoretical developments in HRM with practical and strategic considerations of the management of diverse people in the work place and its surrounding environment.
title: Strategic Human Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course provides a basic knowledge of changes which occur in the body as a result of exercise and conditioning. Some aspects of fitness testing and programming are included with particular attention to young children and adolescents. Essentially, it is an introduction to the study of human anatomy and of exercise physiology.
title: Scientific Basis of Physical Activity I
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Laboratory Practicum 3 is a practice-based course focused on the construction of removable partial dentures and complete cast restorations. Students build on knowledge and practical skills developed in previous courses to strengthen their technical competence, accuracy and confidence in dental laboratory practice. Learning is centred on intensive laboratory sessions supported by lectures and tutorials that reinforce theoretical understanding, clinical relevance, problem-solving and compliance with professional standards. To successfully complete the course, students must submit all required assessment items and achieve an overall passing grade across the graded assessments by the end of the trimester. Further information about learning activities, assessment requirements and course progression is provided in the relevant sections of the course record.
title: Laboratory Practicum 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course introduces students to municipal solid waste management. The contents include municipal solid waste characteristics, storage and collection, transfer and transport, separation and processing, recycling, composting, incineration and sanitary landfilling.
title: Solid Waste Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course aims to provide theory and knowledge about comorbid substance use disorders, intellectual disability, and physical illness, occurring in the context of mental illness. The course approaches these topics from the perspective of understanding the additional complexity comorbidity adds to assessment and treatment. It explores the challenges for practitioners in managing complex issues within interprofessional settings and the importance of effective communication in achieving positive outcomes for consumers.
title: Mental Health and Co-occurring Conditions
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Equip yourself with the strategies and practices required to critically assess issues of diversity in human services settings. You will develop your cultural competence so you can help people achieve positive health outcomes by ensuring cultural safety within health care institutions and community settings. You will think about difference as a complex concept, providing you with the frameworks to explain critical contemporary issues in human services, social work, public health and law enforcement. These skills can also be applied to ensuring your research collaborations and community partnerships are conducted within best-practice ethical frameworks. Upon completion of this course, you will be able to make sound recommendations to improve health care, public health and social policy and practice outcomes for diverse populations.
title: Working with Diverse Populations
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is designed to equip students with the skills needed to analyse quantitative social science data.
title: Quantitative Social Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course offers a focused exploration into the realm of environmental criminology, a branch of criminology that examines the role of the immediate physical environment in influencing the potential for criminal activity. Environmental criminology operates on the principle that the environment can shape, facilitate, or hinder criminal behaviour, thus playing a crucial role in understanding and preventing crime. Unlike traditional schools of criminology that may concentrate on the sociological or psychological aspects of criminal behaviour, environmental criminology places a significant emphasis on the spatial and temporal distribution of criminal events in relation to the environment. The course will be particularly beneficial for students aspiring to operational or policy positions in crime prevention and control. It provides a practical approach to these ends, equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills to effectively address and mitigate crime through environmental strategies. By understanding the intricate relationship between the environment and criminal behaviour, students will gain valuable insights applicable to real-world scenarios in crime prevention and policy formulation.
title: Environmental Criminology
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Employers within the field of Human Services require students to be 'work ready'. This means that you need to graduate with a set of transferable generic skills, understand the nexus of theory and practice; recognise knowledge presented in unfamiliar contexts; and reflect by critiquing your own professional practice. Students must complete 52 days of supervised field placement (4 days per week). A strict requirement for this course is that students must undertake and complete Fit For Professional Practice requirements. These should have been completed by the end of your 1st year of study. Students must register for pre-placement by the end of Week 2, Trimester 1 to enrol in a Trimester 2 placement. Students must register for pre-placement by the end of Week 2, Trimester 2 to enrol in a Trimester 1 placement.
title: Field Placement
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course explores secondary schooling and the school to post-school transition process for students with diverse learning needs. Preservice teachers will explore evidence-based principles and practices that support effective transitioning for diverse students throughout the senior secondary years of schooling. The various pathways of learning in Year 11 and 12 that best suit diverse students will be explored. Further course content will explore a range of high quality, evidence-based teaching and instructional practices essential in multi-ability classrooms to enable students at different Response to Intervention (RtI) levels of support to be engaged in learning, develop competencies, and achieve academically to their full potential. The course follows on from 4104EDN which is offered in Trimester 1. This course is restricted to students enrolled in the Learning Support strand of the Bachelor of Education (Secondary) degree or the Masters of Secondary Teaching and it is highly recommended that 4104EDN is studied prior to students enrolling in 4812EDN.
title: Learning Enhancement 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The central purpose of this course is to provide pre-service teachers with fundamental understandings of the nature of the process underpinning literacies. It considers the role of the communicative partner and environmental contexts in learning as well as methods of assessment and intervention.
title: Literacy Intervention
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The course is broken into two parts. The first half of the trimester examines the Australian system of Government, and the policy making process. It is intended to equip new front line human service workers and social workers with the knowledge and skills needed to be effective practitioners, policy professionals and advocates for social change. The second half of the course examines aspects of the Australian legal system that impact on both practitioners and their future clients. The course has a strong focus on the interface between social work, human services and the law.
title: Influencing Policy and Legislation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: In Dangerous Pleasures: An Introduction to Literary Studies, you will be introduced to the discipline of literary studies through a wide and diverse selection of shorter fiction. This course combines detailed attention to the formal design of fiction with a consideration of geographical and social location, and historical context. The course examines literary form and language, develops methods of close reading, and is designed to increase your confidence when responding to literature. Further, it looks at the study of literature as a discipline with its own history, topics, methods, and debates. Dangerous Pleasures: An Introduction to Literary Studies aims to demonstrate how the study of literature can be an important practical, vocational, cultural, and social component of a university education.
title: Dangerous Pleasures: An Introduction to Literary Studies
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Information systems (IS) play a vital role in today's organisations and information is considered a valuable asset. Rapidly changing information technology (IT) is increasing the complexity of information management, while concerns about the confidentiality, privacy, validity, and accuracy of the data stored have been heightened. As a result there is a growing need for both IS users and IS professionals to be aware of issues concerning information management and control and to develop appropriate practical skills in this area.
title: Information Management and Control
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Information Technology or Bachelor of Computer Science with Honours undertake a detailed study, literature survey, analysis, solution, and evaluation of a selected research problem relevant to their degree. Students present the details of their work in a dissertation, seminar and if applicable, an academically assessable implemented system. Students choose a research problem in consultation with academic staff members. Prior to being admitted to an Honours program, students negotiate the supervisory arrangement with the Program Director. Students should complete 6190ICT_P1, 6190ICT_P2, 6190ICT_P3 and 6190ICT_P4 in sequential order. A grade will be assigned upon successful completion of 6190ICT_P4. This course is part three of a set of four courses.
title: Honours Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The supply of good quality water, together with the removal of subsequent wastewater, is essential for modern communities. This course deals with the theory, methods, processes and design principles involved in treating and managing water and wastewater, including reticulation systems. The main focus is on municipal use of water and municipal wastewater production. This course concentrates on providing a solid understanding of conventional practice.
title: Water and Wastewater Treatment Fundamentals
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course deals with continuous-time signals and systems and is designed to build on the basic circuit analysis concepts covered in the course Electric Circuits. It provides a detailed study of continuous-time signals and systems in time domain as well as in transformed domain. Signal transforms (Fourier series, Fourier transform and Laplace transforms) are covered in detail. Further concepts such as signal sampling and aliasing are introduced. The theory is exemplified with processing of signals in Python and MATLAB. Incompatible: 2075ENG Signals and Systems
title: Signals and Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces structural design including dead, live and wind load estimation to AS1170, structural analysis of statically indeterminate skeletal structures using approximate manual methods and a frame analysis package. It introduces basic steel design to AS4100 (hot-rolled steel) and AS4600 (cold-formed steel). Steel members are designed in tension, compression, shear and bending. Local examples are used to bring the course to life. Assessment is by tutorial exercises, an in-class exam, a design assignment and a final examination.
title: Advanced Steel Structures
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Geotechnical Engineering forms a major part of the work of a professional civil engineer. This course is designed to enable students to do the analysis prior to design of foundations. It also forms an integral part of the civil analysis and design training provided in the four-year Bachelor of Engineering program in Civil Engineering. The course covers: design and construction aspects of shallow foundations, piled foundations, earth pressure calculations, and slope stability analysis. The main purpose of this course is to develop the ability of the students to design the basic geotechnical foundations (i.e., shallow foundation and piled foundation) and analyse the common geotechnical engineering problems (e.g., slope stability).
title: Geotechnical Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Structural engineering is the science and art of planning, analysing, designing, and constructing safe, effective and economical structures that will serve their intended purposes. Structural design forms a major part of the work of a professional civil engineer. Structural analysis is an integral part of any structural engineering project, its function being the prediction of the performance of the proposed structure. This course is designed to enable students to do the prerequisite analysis prior to design. It also forms an integral part of the structural analysis and design training provided in the four-year Bachelor of Engineering program in Civil Engineering. This course is to help students develop a fundamental understanding of the basic principles of structural analysis and the physical behaviour of structural systems under load. The course provides a thorough coverage of the theoretical basis for linear analysis of various types of skeletal (planar) structures encountered in Civil Engineering design work. The main purpose of this course is to develop the ability of the students to analyse planar structures using manual and computer-based methods. Prerequisites for undergraduate programs only: 1501ENG Engineering Mechanics, 2101ENG Mechanics of Materials 1
title: Structural Analysis
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Business intelligence (BI) is a broad term which refers to the combination of software tools, architectures, databases, models and methodologies for assisting decision makers to achieve business objectives. The course provides students with an understanding of the principles of decision making in organisations, an appreciation of the concepts of business intelligence systems (BI) across various disciplinary areas, and the acquisition of basic skills in the construction of BI systems. This course is suitable for students with minimal information systems background since students are introduced to the fundamentals of decision making and BI.
title: Business Intelligence Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Information derived from data is important to the management, productivity and competitive advantage of an organisation. Data must be efficiently collected, organised, retrieved and managed to make it meaningful to the organisation. It is the role of the IT professional to develop, deploy, manage and integrate data and information systems to support the organisation. This course includes the organisation, modeling, transformation and presentation of data.
title: Database Design
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This postgraduate course in Application Systems delves into the analysis, integration, and design of socio-technical systems with a focus on user experience and contextual considerations in ICT domains. It covers advanced topics such as human activity systems analysis, ontological modelling, and specifying the organisational and external context of computing systems. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of application systems, their analysis, integration, and design, as well as the importance of user experience and contextual considerations in various ICT domains. The course also emphasises the evaluation and enhancement of user experience in application systems, ensuring that interfaces are intuitive, efficient, and user-friendly. Additionally, students will explore application contexts specifically linked to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) domains, considering factors like e-health, e-business, transport and logistics, agriculture, and e-government, and will be able to analyse and adapt application systems to meet the specific requirements and challenges of different ICT domains. This course was previously known as 7610ICT Introduction to Information Systems and is incompatible with 7610ICT Introduction to Information Systems.
title: Application Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course explores contemporary communicable diseases and infection prevention and control, with a particular emphasis on aetiology, natural history, diagnosis, transmission, monitoring and treatment. It examines public health strategies for the control of communicable and infectious diseases, including outbreak investigation and management. The epidemiology of classic and contemporary infectious diseases in national and international populations, including surveillance and systems for their prevention and control, are also considered.
title: Clinical Infectious Diseases
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Environmental engineers and managers will often find themselves in charge of complex projects and operations which require systematic evaluation and development of management plans to meet regulatory and business goals. This course introduces the principles and elements of environmental management systems that can help business, government and other organisations move operations towards sustainable practice. The course examines multiple approaches to environmental management and reporting, with a focus on understanding and applying the ISO14000 series (an international framework for environmental management) to move an organisation's performance beyond compliance.
title: Environmental Management Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: 7009PHM Pharmacotherapeutics III provides an in-depth look at the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of neurological disorders, psychiatric disorders, men's health, organ transplantation, and neoplastic disorders. Students are provided an overview of the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of disease.
title: Pharmacotherapeutics III
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Devising and communicating policy advice for decision-makers is an art and a science. Advisers must be capable of effectively supporting leaders in a range of different situations and contexts with judgement and foresight. This course will teach you to identify and describe various decision-making contexts, so you can deliver prudent advice in a range of scenarios. To ensure you can remain consistent and evidence-based, you'll also learn how to identify and evaluate appropriate analytical techniques that inform policy outcomes. You will be able to present persuasive arguments outlining the rationale underpinning your recommendations, which take into account the interests of groups, citizens and the needs of decision-makers. Recent trends in governance have created dilemmas for policy advisers, and this course will give you the ability to skillfully navigate them and deliver elegant, evidence-backed policy advice to leaders.
title: Policy Advice: Evidence, Argument and Persuasion in Policy-Making
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course explores the place of human rights in contemporary international politics. It examines the roles played by human rights principles and practices relating to global governance and treaty regimes, human security, global poverty, Indigenous peoples, gender and other areas. It also explores critical views on human rights doctrine.
title: Human Rights in World Politics
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: The course explores sociological thinking on the origins, construction and political implications of identity. It will review classical conceptualizations and then examine the shift toward contemporary understandings that view identity as dynamic, fluid and fragmentary. The main focus will be on the questions how people learn to produce and reproduce themselves through engagement in social interaction and how interactional dynamics shape their sense of who they are.
title: Sociology of Identity
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course will provide students with an introduction to child welfare and well-being. Students will examine current socio-cultural, ecological, psychological, sociological and biological theories of child development and consider how different contexts shape a child's development and life trajectories. Students will also develop skills in critical analysis and interprofessional dialogue relating to current issues, professional responses, welfare practice and services for children birth to five and their families.
title: Childhood: Early Years
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Like most contemporary societies, Australia is characterised by an omnipresence of diversity. However, some people's experiences, perspectives, traditions, and practices dominate over others, who may experience economic, cultural, and political forms of marginalisation as a result. In this context, human, social service, and health professionals can easily become implicated in unjust and oppressive practices. These contradictions can cause demoralisation in staff and even lead to burnout. This is the background against which the course, Equity and Diversity, seeks to equip students in human, social service, and health professions with a selection of conceptual tools and practice skills that will enable self-compassion and self-care to converge fruitfully with a growing ability to contribute towards building a diverse yet equitable society.
title: Equity and Diversity
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This Honours course builds on undergraduate psychology courses to develop an advanced-level understanding of cutting edge theory, research, and practice. The course covers specific topics in the major areas of applied and experimental psychology. The course will not only extend students' knowledge, but may assist in preparing students for postgraduate programs within applied or research fields. The topics covered in the course will differ depending on the year of enrolment to accommodate current psychological research directions, student interest, as well as using lecturers' expertise. Each topic will include a review and critical assessment of some key psychological theories, methodologies, and research findings in that area. Topics may also explore some practical applications of accumulated knowledge within an area.
title: Advanced Topics in Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course introduces students to law, politics, and criminal justice in Australia. It explores how laws are made, the influence of politics on law reform, the role of the media, human rights protections, and criminal responsibility. It considers the historical treatment of First Nations peoples in Australia's legal system and the role that law plays in promoting justice and accountability. This knowledge provides a foundation for further study on criminal law and justice systems.
title: Law, Crime and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Social Construction of Welfare explores discourses around provision of welfare. The course aims to critically examine different types of welfare, who benefits from welfare, the systems responsible for welfare provision, and the role of human services practitioners within those systems. The course explores discourses around poverty and wealth; employment and unemployment; the relationship between the state and citizens; and equity and injustice.
title: Social Construction of Welfare
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Do you want to make a difference in the world? Understanding how international law operates is the first step towards making such difference. In today's increasingly globalised world, legal problems now span countries and often involve regional and international treaties and laws, so it's essential that law undergraduates as future practitioners comprehend how the global legal system works. The emergence of Islamic State and the ever-present threat of terrorism has highlighted the role of international law. Law is no longer something that operates only within State boundaries in isolation, and there is significant demand for young lawyers to understand this. Everyone is affected by war in the Middle East, terrorism, cyber-attacks, and piracy in the South China Sea. Whether you want to prevent environmental degradation, mass atrocities, or advance human rights for vulnerable populations this course will give you introductory knowledge as to how you may go about it. Whether you hope to pursue a career in Australia or internationally, knowledge of international law will be useful because of the globalisation of legal practice, and will place you in a good position to apply for non-legal internships or work placements at the United Nations or the European Union, including at the European Commission, the Council of the EU and the European Parliament. 5045LAW will introduce you to the fundamentals of law beyond the nation-state and as it applies to global and public issues and concerns. Students who complete this course will develop an understanding of the fundamentals of the legal system itself such as who can participate in law-making and where rules and principles come from when there is no world government or enforceable judgments of courts. Having studied the fundamental structures of public international law, students will also have the chance to engage at an introductory level with four more specific and fairly detailed bodies of law including: the use of force and enforcement; human rights; international criminal law and territorial issues including the law of the sea pertaining to maritime boundaries. These bodies of law are significant for public international law and an introduction to them will develop the students' capacity to engage more widely with international law issues and concerns. This course will also make you eligible to enroll into the Jessup International Moot course that will further polish your knowledge in some of the most pertinent legal challenges that our world faces.
title: Public International Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course is an introduction to the different aspects of the broad study of ecology. It provides knowledge of ecological principles and theory, experience with practical techniques, and an understanding of the application of these methods. Topics include processes at the individual, population and community levels, characteristics of ecosystems (terrestrial, freshwater, marine, and global), introduction to the methods used in ecological sampling, research design and analysis, and the application of concepts and techniques to current ecological management issues.
title: Ecology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course explores the theory and practice of sonic art and its presentation in live contexts including performance, installation, and interactive media. The course draws on students previous experiences and investigates issues related to experimental music with electronic and digital technologies in particular. Student investigate these ideas in the context of their own creative practice and through the development of new sonic art works for public presentation. This course is delivered through tutorials and seminars.
title: Music Technology Live Capstone
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will challenge both the students' musical and technical skills and help prepare them for the rigorous demands of the profession. This course provides an opportunity for students to extend themselves in the ensembles space by selecting extended ensemble/collaborative activities to participate in beyond 4551QCM (Ensembles and Collaborative Activity 4C), depending on their specialisation and interests.
title: Ensemble and Collaborative Activity 4D
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will examine and discuss a wide range of popular music from blues and roots to early rap and house. As well, it will critically examine current developments such as cultural appropriation, the impact of the Black Lives Matter movement, the #metoo movement, and other important sociocultural developments.
title: Vinyl to Viral - the Evolution of Popular Music
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Pedagogy Practicum I is a program of activities offered at post graduate level that addresses the practical skills of studio teaching. Its core activity is reflection on pedagogical practice through lesson observation. The concepts of a team approach to rehabilitation and habilitation is also explored. It exposes students to the principles of successful methodologies and the psychology of teaching and learning.
title: Pedagogy Practicum 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Delivered in intensive mode, this course will teach students the fundamentals of the comic book medium for solo creations/collaborations/freelance and other commercial-based concerns. Utilising professional works and examples, and guests/industry contacts in the field, students will cover a broad range of disciplines related to the production of comic books, strips and graphic novels, with the objective of becoming more fluent in the various languages and considerations pertaining to this unique medium.
title: Comics
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Honours Research Project constitutes a 40CP honours research commitment within the Bachelor of Design with Honours program. Each of the four components of the course combine to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The expectation is that the research project undertaken will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item. Co-requisite/Pre-requisite: 6511QCA Design Research Methods.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course contains a series of seminars, training and workshops will take place throughout the trimester. Please refer to the QCA-HDR research training program that is offered by the QCAD. This will provide you with an opportunity to engage with research methods and relevant HDR training, including talks and workshops by invited guests that will enable you to better understand and explore your chosen area of research.
title: Visual Arts Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The Honours Research Project courses constitute a 40CP honours research commitment within the Honours program. Each of its four courses combine to introduce students to the rigours of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual/screen production practice. The expectation is that the artefacts and production practices arising from this research project will operate synergistically with the theoretical work to result in a project that is cohesive in all respects and which demonstrates high levels of visual and textual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item at the end of the program, which is to be presented with the Exegesis (completed in 6012GFS) for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Undertaking a Planning Practicum Course is compulsory for all students studying within the Urban and Environmental Planning Programs at Griffith University. In this course we collegially explore issues underpinning contemporary planning practice such as: planning ethics; professionalism; education and the practice-theory relationship; and the boundaries, scope and role of the profession. Students also contribute their ideas for the continuing development and advancement of the profession. To participate, students must either (a) undertake a specified period of approved work placement in a planning related role within a specified time frame or (b) be employed in a professional planning role. Pre-enrolment assistance and guidance is provided for students seeking work placement.
title: Planning Practicum 20
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: First of two professional practice courses, this course examines and explores the nature of being professional in architecture practice. It introduces the cultural context for contemporary architecture practice, and the values, attitudes, legal and regulatory frameworks which govern professional practice. Social responsibility, ethics and community engagement are addressed. The course considers the roles of professional bodies, and the organizational structure and processes of contemporary architecture practice.
title: Architecture Professional Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course commences with an overview of the forces transforming the business landscape in which we operate into a global economy. As marketing managers of the future, you need to learn how to cope with the complexities and challenges of this global marketplace. The course focuses on three fundamental questions: (1) Which international markets to enter; (2) How to decide on the mode of international market entry, and (3) Whether to standardise or adapt the international marketing mix - product, price, promotion and distribution.
title: International Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Branding is at the cutting edge of marketing theory and practice and participants will be able to apply the knowledge and skills that they develop during this course, in many spheres. One strongly interwoven thread of the course is sustainable branding, which is fundamental to sustainable businesses and other organizations, such as government and the not-for-profit sector. Sustainable branding has significant socio-economic benefits. This course takes students through the evolution of branding theory with an emphasis on integrating theory and relevant practical applications. The course takes a strategic approach to branding, and the processes, challenges and issues related to planning, implementing and evaluating sustainable branding strategies. The structure and processes of the course create a forum for open discussion and debate.
title: Brand Strategy and Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Economic events, regulatory reforms and the pace of change are influencing and changing the role of both the Financial Advisor and the profession. The course will keep you up-to-date with the very latest issues and rules that affect the life-cycle processes of preparing for life after work and the efficient distribution of assets after death. Specifically, this course commences with the facts and strategies relevant to individuals seeking retirement and estate planning advice. The course addresses the importance of wills, living wills, estate plans and strategies relevant to the distribution of wealth and inheritances.
title: Retirement and Estate Planning
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course studies core aspects of equity security analysis and valuation, debt security valuation, security market indices, market efficiency, and portfolio management risk and return. The rapidly changing financial environment and the number of new instruments available have made investment analysis a task which can only be carried out by persons who have been equipped with updated skills. The course covers current advances in the analysis of international capital markets, and presents a range of analytical techniques.
title: Investments
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is for students enrolled part-time in the Doctor of Visual Arts (6009). Course content is to be determined in consultation with the nominated supervisors.
title: Studio Practice and Research
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The research project is designed to provide training in the developmental and practical elements of research, including epidemiology, public health and health services research, clinical research and biomedical research. Students will be required to design and conduct a research project of special interest to them, and within the competence of the School to direct, and to prepare this work for publication. All students, irrespective of their own research topic, will be required to evaluate published, current and future research across a broad range of topics relevant to their chosen discipline, as the basis of their clinical practice, and with the expectation of research forming the platform for lifelong learning.
title: Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The research project is designed to provide training in the developmental and practical elements of research, including epidemiology, public health and health services research, clinical research and biomedical research. Students will be required to design and conduct a research project of special interest to them, and within the competence of the School to direct, and to prepare this work for publication. All students, irrespective of their own research topic, will be required to evaluate published, current and future research across a broad range of topics relevant to their chosen discipline, as the basis of their clinical practice, and with the expectation of research forming the platform for lifelong learning.
title: Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course requires execution, analysis and presentation of a research thesis. This involves development of a project, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms. Restriction: FOURTH YEAR BY APPLICATION ONLY
title: Dissertation Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course requires execution, analysis and presentation of a research thesis. This involves development of a project, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms.
title: Dissertation Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course considers the role of media relations in strategic communication and equips students with relevant skills, knowledge and theory. Students will develop an understanding of the critical relationship between the strategic communicator and the media.
title: Media Relations
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Green Marketing is particularly relevant in today's context of a growing demand for products, services and systems that are environmentally sustainable. In this course you will learn how organisations develop environmentally friendly strategies for product innovation, brand reputation and brand equity. Marketing communication and supply chain issues are also explored, with an emphasis on the concept of more sustainable product life cycles.
title: Green Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces students to the newly emerging fields of marine chemical ecology and biotechnology. The course is all about tastes and smells and has a specific focus on the interface between biology and chemistry to study marine invertebrates such as sponges, corals, ascidians and nudibranchs and marine plants. Marine chemical ecologists investigate the role of chemicals produced by marine organisms to help them survive and includes studies of defensive, offensive and communication strategies. Marine biotechnology involves the use of cutting edge molecular and chemical techniques to develop commercial products and monitoring tools used in medicine, aquaculture, food production, conservation and environmental monitoring. Lectures and field/laboratory activities will cover topics such as defence, venoms, biofouling, communication, food safety, bioluminescence, molecular biology, drug discovery. Students must have completed 80 credit points. Prerequisites 1041SCG Biological Systems and 1014SCG Statistics and also Chemistry (1021SCG Chemistry 1A or 1022SCG Chemistry 1B or 1023SCG Chemistry I or 1024SCG Chemistry II or 1411ESC Chemistry I or 1422ESC Chemistry II or equivalent)
title: Marine Biodiscovery
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines basic principles of human genetic disease processes from molecular and diagnostic perspectives. The course is strongly orientated toward developing and learning useful laboratory skills for diagnosis of genetic disease including DNA analysis, clinical genetics, cytogenetics and forensics.
title: Molecular Diagnostics
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course considers how teacher beliefs, attitudes and values impact on both making adjustment to content, instructional strategies and assessment to accommodate learner diversity in inclusive educational settings, and extending collaborative relationships to strengthen learning communities. You will consider the MTSS framework, principles of inclusive education, and the criteria for pedagogical choices to diverse learning needs, including students with disability, with cultural responsiveness, including EAL/D students, and the engagement of families.
title: Inclusive Classrooms
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will explore the biological processes on which the continuity of life is based including cell reproduction, basic genetics and evolution. Case studies and laboratory activities will provide a challenging opportunity to develop the practical and intellectual skills of a scientist or health care worker.
title: Genes and Disease
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course will combine an examination of the theoretical underpinnings of leadership with practical personal development tools in the context of the social context of government and the key drivers of public sector change. The course will examine: Leadership - public/private/community comparisons; development of leadership capabilities; drivers of public sector change; aligning organisational culture; change management; communication; entrepreneurship in the public sector; and values, morality and professionalism. Overall, this course investigates the challenges and practices of exercising leadership in helping systems and organisations to adapt to as well as drive societal change.
title: Leading Public Sector Change
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: GBS Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course provides a study of business logistics in a global context. Business logistics is presented as enabling ethical and socially responsible business. Logistics is an integral part of the business supply chain, and essential to the effective management of goods, services and information. The course includes a focus on logistics in a global environment, logistics innovations, and logistics and the environment. Commencing with an overview of logistics as an essential element of sustainable business, the course then considers logistics systems and finally contemporary issues in logistics management.
title: Global Business Logistics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Effective management processes are critical to identify and respond to the challenges that can emerge at any time within complex organisation systems. Designed for current and aspiring managers, this course will help you develop your critical thinking, decision-making and communication skills to improve your confidence and capability to maintain a high-performing network. You'll be introduced to the theories behind effective problem solving and learn how to research and identify problems, drive innovation and implement new strategies. You'll gain experience in tackling problems both big and small, structured and nebulous alike, applying the theoretical knowledge to solve practical challenges through troubleshooting, investigation, presentation and root cause analysis. Working independently and in collaboration with your peers, you'll be prepared to navigate the social, political and managerial reality of management, equipped with the core skills necessary to take ownership of these challenges and implement iterative processes for continuous improvement in your organisation.
title: Managerial Problem Solving
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will provide undergraduate students with consolidation of their learning throughout the major and provides skills for high level analysis of HR organisational challenges and opportunities with a specific focus on organisational change and strategy. This course will provide students with opportunities to apply their previous HR learning and knowledge to a range of current organisational problems/scenarios giving consideration to HR's relationship to the broader business strategy and external influences through the change management process.
title: Applied Human Resource Management and Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The dissertation is undertaken in the final trimester for full time students and in the final year for part time students. It is between 15,000 and 25,000 words in length depending on the research topic and methodology. Students work with an academic supervisor who maintains regular contact and provides support and direction in the design and execution of the dissertation.
title: Dissertation 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Business operations in Australia and around the world have become increasingly globalised over the past several decades. To create a worldwide marketplace, multinational corporations (MNCs), governments and non-government organisations have all played a major part in breaking down the barriers of international trade. Simultaneously, the transformation of the global economy has impacted people at every level, affecting the notions of community, citizenship and governance. To sustain social license across regions, new norms have emerged for business in areas such as ethical decision making, diversity, workplace culture, social responsibility, stakeholder management and sustainability. As a global businessperson, it's essential you have a grounding in the key social, political and economic impacts of globalisation and its implications for management practice here and abroad. As part of this course, you'll explore the key drivers and contradictions of global competitiveness and examine the ways in which social pressures and calls for accountability have influenced how MNCs and other organisations do business. Exploring historic and current business practices and concepts in collaboration with student peers, you'll resolve a range of authentic business problems using tools such as case studies, video analysis and group discussions. The newfound understanding of the complex system of interactions that make globalisation possible will ensure you'll be poised to take on international business opportunities and challenges of the 21st century.
title: Globalisation and Corporate Social Responsibility
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Exploring the interplay between education and socio-cultural digital activities, the course examines three aspects of this interplay: the historical interaction between education and digital culture; the influence on education from contemporary changes in digital culture; and the application in education of computer games and esports, in response to and as expressions of, digital culture.
title: Education and Digital Culture
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines the origins and development of corrective services in Australia. The correctional system is studied in terms of custodial and non-custodial sanctions, and considers special client populations including men, women, juveniles, and Indigenous offenders. The issues of privatisation and deaths in custody are examined.
title: Introduction to Corrections
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course examines the relationship between mental disorder and criminal offending. The course aims to increase students' knowledge and understanding of models of criminal behaviour and mental disorders, and the potential interaction between the two. The course aims to develop in students a critical appreciation of the issues involved in defining both mental disorder and criminality, and an evidence-based understanding of the extent to which criminal behaviour is caused by mental disorder. The course also addresses specific mental disorders, in the context of their potential relationship with criminal offending. The course aims to develop students' knowledge and critical thinking skills applicable in a forensic mental health setting.
title: Mental Disorder and Crime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Globalisation has had a meaningful impact on education policy, ensuring leaders in this sector face additional complexity when engaged in decision-making processes. This course provides space for leaders, and aspiring leaders, to investigate the impact of education policies from the local to the global level. It also explores the role of the educational leader when developing ethical and legal cultures in educational environments. As a student, you will use social, cultural and educational theories to interrogate ethical and legal issues, concepts and terminology and develop the skills and resources to more confidently navigate the terrain of educational leadership and school leadership. This course engenders professionalism for key decision-makers in education, such as principals and district leadership, ensuring they have the means to implement global education best practice policy, whether they are at the school, district or government level.
title: Navigating Educational Leadership
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course focuses on developmental prevention to construct a framework for thinking about the prevention of crime and associated problems at the individual, family and local level. Students will examine the challenges associated with developing and implementing evidence-based programs for disadvantaged communities. This will involve consideration of the influences of multiple risk and protective factors as well as strategies to empower local residents and change developmentally relevant institutions and social policies.
title: Developmental Crime Prevention
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will provide students with the skills required to manage their honours research and future research projects. An integral part of good research is the establishment of parameters within which their research should proceed. Knowledge of the literature in and around the chosen topic is vital to establishing the basis of a good research project. Firstly, students will learn how to plan out the various phases of their research project. Second, students will be guided in the development of research questions and hypotheses for their research. Thirdly, students will be guided in positioning their research in relevant theoretical, empirical and methodological knowledge. Finally students will learn about presenting their research ideas and findings. Students must be enrolled in the Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice Honours program.
title: Managing Research Projects
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course provides students with information about mental health policy and legislation, mental health systems and mental health practice in Australia.
title: Contemporary Mental Health Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Students enrolled in the Bachelor of Information Technology or Bachelor of Computer Science with Honours undertake a detailed study, literature survey, analysis, solution, and evaluation of a selected research problem relevant to their degree. Students present the details of their work in a dissertation, seminar and if applicable, an academically assessable implemented system. Students choose a research problem in consultation with academic staff members. Prior to being admitted to an Honours program, students negotiate the supervisory arrangement with the Program Director. Students should complete 6190ICT_P1, 6190ICT_P2, 6190ICT_P3 and 6190ICT_P4 in sequential order. A grade will be assigned upon successful completion of 6190ICT_P4. This course is part two of a set of four courses.
title: Honours Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course provides an introduction to complementary metal oxide semiconductor (CMOS) Integrated Circuit (IC) design. Students will be exposed to topics including transistor level logic gate design, and digital and analog IC design. It is intended that this course will provide a useful insight both for students contemplating postgraduate study/careers in the field of VLSI chip design; and also for those who wish to increase their understanding of the internals of semiconductor components used in board and system designs. Incompatible: 6310ENG Integrated Circuit Design
title: Integrated Circuit Design
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces students to the basic concepts and principles of thermodynamics, and its selected engineering applications. Topics include the first law of thermodynamics, volumetric properties of pure substances, heat effects, the second law of thermodynamics, thermodynamic properties of fluids, thermodynamic analysis of processes, power cycles, heat engines, refrigeration cycles and combustion.
title: Engineering Thermodynamics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces students to four fundamental engineering concepts related to electrical and electronic engineering: storage of electrical energy and transport of an electrical charge, interconnection of passive components to make small or large systems, operation of systems under conditions of constant electrical load or excitation, and the operation of systems under conditions of variable electrical load or excitation. The concepts are studied using the physical processes within the components and circuits of electrical systems in a practical context.
title: Electric Circuits
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Electrical and electronic engineers need to design systems that operate successfully in the environment in which the systems are to be used. This course is a vital part of developing that expertise through the guided design, fabrication and demonstration of an electronic circuit on a printed circuit board. This is a core skill required of all electrical and electronic engineers and relates directly to manufacturability, usability, and other factors. Incompatible 3312ENG Electrical Design Project. Incompatible: 3312ENG Electrical Design Project
title: Electrical and Electronic Design Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Advanced Foundation Engineering forms a major part of the work of a professional civil engineer. This course is designed to enable students to do the analysis prior to design of foundations. This course focuses on the design of foundation systems and follows the geotechnical relevant courses at undergraduate level. The course covers: effective stress analysis, consolidation theory, bearing capacity of shallow foundation and deep foundations. The main purpose of this course is to develop the ability of the students to analyse and design advanced geotechnical foundation under critical status.
title: Advanced Foundation Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Mechanics of Materials 2 builds on fundamental concepts to equip learners with practical and widely applicable tools for analysing how structures and mechanical components behave under load. The course emphasises realistic engineering scenarios, where learners learn to determine stress and strain distributions, evaluate strength and stability, and anticipate potential failure modes. By the end of the course, learners will be able to apply these methods to the analysis and preliminary design of structural members and machine components, gaining skills that are directly relevant to professional engineering practice.
title: Mechanics of Materials 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is a practical project based course in which students are challenged to apply fundamental knowledge of analogue and digital components, circuitry and systems to design, implement and demonstrate a functional electrical device meeting prescribed system requirements. Students are guided through a systematic design process involving analysis of requirements, circuit design and simulation, component selection, prototype construction, testing, evaluation and revision. An integral part of the process is the production and maintenance of engineering documentation in the form of technical specifications, schematic diagrams, list of components, test procedures and performance results.
title: Electrical Design Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Safe, reliable, and sustainable access to energy technology is a crucial element of modern society- one we can no longer take for granted. The world must find new ways to reduce energy wastage, and energy use in general, through the development and application of sophisticated electrical engineering technology. This course will build on your existing knowledge of electromagnetic fields and propagating systems, as well as electric circuits, to explore theory underlying a variety of energy technologies and the ways in which they can be harnessed and utilised to improve efficiency and adaptability of energy systems at the domestic and industrial level.
