These lessons include laboratory experiences, giving you a hands-on introduction to various energy topics including utilisation and energy harvesting. You will also build your research and analytical thinking skills with a state-of-the-art review paper, which will help you to improve your academic writing abilities and teamwork capabilities, while examining current and future trends in energy efficiency. At the conclusion of the course, you'll be prepared to implement each of the energy efficiency solutions explored during your classes, as well as having the knowledge, confidence, and problem-solving skills to optimise a business that utilises such technologies.
title: Energy Efficiency
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides fundamental knowledge and practical skills in data communications and computer networking. Students explore network architectures, protocols, addressing, switching, routing, and wireless networks that support modern digital communication. Through laboratory-based learning, students design, implement, secure, and troubleshoot networked solutions using technologies such as EtherChannel, VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, and Layer 2 security mechanisms. The course develops competencies in network design, performance evaluation, and security for professional practice in networking and cybersecurity.
title: Data Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Students will work to develop level designs demonstrating refined gameplay. The gameplay will give the player a range of skills to learn and challenges to overcome, while the player also experiences a start-to-end progression sequence. In producing this result, students will dive deeper into the Unity game engine, learning how to manage a Unity project that incorporates game scripting and game content (e.g. artwork and audio). Students will be able to focus on their major, and draw on and advance the knowledge gained in first year, while also learning important new skills in gameplay design, and techniques for managing and professionally organising project work.
title: Games Level Design
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course examines some of the major, cutting-edge questions for criminology today. It introduces students to the contemporary key thinkers and contributors in the field in Australia and overseas. Attention is given to the relationship between research and policy in linking knowledge to social change. Importantly, the course also provides students with skills to communicate complex research questions and ideas to a variety of academic, policy and public audiences.
title: Contemporary Perspectives on Crime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The dissertation is the culmination of students' training in the fundamental sciences and professional practice of pharmacy. Qualitative and quantitative research projects serve to address topical issues relating to the practice of pharmacy (e.g. quality use of medicines; pharmacoeconomics; pharmacy management; social aspects of pharmacy; rational prescribing; drug utilisation etc.) and specific research topics within the health sciences (pharmacology; pharmaceutics; pharmacogenomics; medicinal chemistry; pharmacognosy; molecular biology etc). Students work with an experienced academic supervisor/s within and external to the School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences who maintains regular contact and provides support and direction in the design and execution of the dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course will provide students with an understanding of the drug discovery and development process including drug design, high throughput screening, lead optimisation, preclinical testing, basic pharmacokinetics and clinical trial design. It will also provide an overview of the commercial and regulatory realities that influence the drug discovery and development process. A sound knowledge and understanding of tertiary level physiology, anatomy, chemistry and mathematics is expected.
title: Drug Discovery and Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces students to the clinical use and effects of drugs encountered in dental practice. This course links the general principles of pharmacology and the oral health issues pertaining to different classes of drugs from a contemporary viewpoint. The course will cover general principles of pharmacology such as pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Topics include: the pharmacology of the autonomic and the central nervous systems, cardiovascular drugs, antimicrobial drugs, chemotherapy, anaesthetics/analgesic/anti-inflammatory drugs and endocrine drugs.
title: Pharmacology for Oral Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: 8001HLS consists of four 10 credit point courses (8001HLS_P1 to P4) and these courses make up the research component of the Graduate Diploma of Health Research program (4161). The final grade is allocated on completion of part 4. The dissertation requires students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This involves the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, and data analysis. At the completion of the four parts, students will submit a report of their research project (thesis) for examination. Students are advised to consult their School Advisor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final part (8001HLS_P4), they are expected to submit their dissertation by the due date specified in the course profile.
title: Dissertation Part 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course introduces students to perspectives on policy implementation, an incredibly important although often overlooked aspect of the policy process. Students can expect to explore challenges involved in implementing policy, as well as principles for effective implementation. The course introduces students to different instruments of implementation, to actors involved in delivering policies, and to the needs and expectations of the recipients of public services. The course explores case studies which highlight the importance of implementation, and considers some of the approaches that have been utilised to improve and transform the delivery of public services in Australia and internationally.
title: Achieving Policy Outcomes: Implementation
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: International Relations Theory focuses on the theoretical frameworks used to explain, interpret, critique and on rare occasions predict the outcomes of global political events and processes. Events may include the outbreak and cessation of armed conflict, the establishment and operation of international organisations, and responses to transnational threats and challenges such as climate change, refugee flows and pandemic diseases. Processes may include great power competition and rivalry, global economic integration and financial crises, patterns of development and poverty, migration patterns, and the transformation of the international order itself. Major theoretical approaches to be examined will include realism, which centres on power relations between states; liberal internationalism, which gives more emphasis to domestic politics and processes of mutually beneficial cooperation; and constructivism, which looks at the explanatory power of the norms and ideas at work in global politics. We will also consider a range of critical and and normative approaches, which focus more on issues of global justice.
title: International Relations Theory
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course introduces students to a range of ideas and topics fundamental to the study of political science. These include the state, democracy, political ideology and political culture. It also introduces students to the methodology of political science, in particular the ability to undertake research, think critically and develop coherent, written arguments.
title: Introduction to Political Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Delivering Public Value (DPV) focuses on how to navigate a changing world whilst creating value. Key themes include: the trends shaping government; value creation; leadership and leading in place and what this means in the 21st century; values; thinking strategically; political astuteness; collaborative governance and coproduction; and place and community. Throughout the subject we will give particular attention to two practice themes: collaborative governance and innovation. We use these as contemporary lenses through which to understand and consider how public value is shaped and delivered. In DPV we recognise the unique aspects of the public sector, but also look to important concepts and methods from other sectors. We draw inspiration from various notions of strategy and look at how value creation occurs at the level of the individual, organisations, and systems. To understand how value creation happens in practice, we need to appreciate the context in which we operate and understand that public leaders and managers must operate in multiple directions: upwards (into an authorising environment); inwards (into their own organisations),and outwards (to providers, partners, clients and communities). To be strategic and create value, public managers and leaders, therefore, need to pursue some sort of balance between politics, substance, and administration. DPV will explore these ideas across four learning modules with considerable time spent on linking theory and practice, and applying these ideas to examine practical challenges and approaches to public administration. During our intensive teaching sessions we bring together experts to focus on specific topics including leadership and values; public value creation; innovation; collaborative governance; place and community; and political astuteness in practice.
title: Delivering Public Value
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: The applied focus of the course will be upon the Australian and New Zealand economies, though opportunities for considering other nations are incorporated in the subject, as are state and regional perspectives. Applied policy problems may be presented, as far as time permits, from a wide range of areas such as defence, health, wage-fixing, law and order, education, the business cycle, tariffs, arts, environment, immigration, natural resource projects and infrastructure provision.
title: Government in a Market Economy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course is designed to teach the basic concepts of Cognitive Psychology covering topics such as attention, memory, language, and thinking. Familiarity with a diverse range of experimental methods and techniques is required to understand the research findings in these areas, and to critically evaluate theoretical explanations. Research findings and theoretical explanations will be presented in lectures. Laboratory experiments and demonstrations will complement the lectures by providing direct experience with some experimental techniques. Pre-requisite requirements: Students must have completed 1001PSY and either 1003PSY or 2000PSY.
title: Cognitive Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: You will be introduced to the theory and practice of psychological testing and assessment of individual differences with particular focus on personality and intelligence assessment. You will learn about the history of psychological testing; definition, advantages, and limitations of psychological tests; ethics in testing; and basic psychometric concepts (test scores and norms, reliability and validity, test construction). You will apply this knowledge to understanding testing and assessment of individual differences in personality and intelligence.
title: Psychological Assessment of Individual Differences
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This is an individually negotiated, contract-based project undertaken by the student under supervision. It is intended to provide the opportunity for the student to develop a particular theme or activity related to their specialised interests. Examples of possible project areas include: a course of academic reading and research; a performance project; creative project development or administration; industry placement. The project is negotiated with and approved by the Convenor and the contract will specify the required outcomes which will include a detailed written report.
title: Honours Project Study A
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

Each of the four components of the course combine to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The expectation is that the research project undertaken will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item. Honours Research Project is presented for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

The expectation is that the research project undertaken will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item. Honours Research Project is presented for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses. academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The Honours Research Project courses constitute a 40CP honours research commitment within the Honours program. Each of its four courses combine to introduce students to the rigours of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual/screen production practice. The expectation is that the artefacts and production practices arising from this research project will operate synergistically with the theoretical work to result in a project that is cohesive in all respects and which demonstrates high levels of visual and textual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item at the end of the program, which is to be presented with the Exegesis (completed in 6012GFS) for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course examines international art practices (from the 1960s until now) that address subjectivity and identity. The course begins with postminimalism in the 1960s and the renewed interest in the body as the subject matter of art. It considers the rise of body art and performance in the 1960s and 70s, and the use of the body as the medium for art. It also examines the moment when gender comes to the fore as a key way of thinking about identity, namely, women's art in the 1970s: the first art to self-consciously attempt to represent gender difference. The course tracks the shifting concerns and debates in art about subjectivity, gender and sexuality across this fifty year period. Topics to be covered include: performance and masochism; identity and essentialism; postmodern irony; female and male masquerade; queer art; and the rise of bad girl and bad boy art in the 1990s, and the current debates about global feminisms. Prerequisites: 1216QCA AND 1217QCA
title: Art, Gender, Sexuality and the Body
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Students learn about a range of core elements of planning practice, including statutory planning, development assessment, development finance and feasibility, and community-led planning. Please note: Students not enrolled in the planning programs may enrol with the permission of the course convenor. Students must be aware that in undertaking this course prior knowledge is assumed.
title: Development Processes Studio
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Understanding Australian Cities is an introductory overview of the origin, patterning and functioning of the urban system. The course specifically examines the dynamics of population, infrastructure, governance and culture in Australian cities. These understandings frame examination of the possibilities of planning intervention. This introductory course will allow students to better appreciate the range of planning challenges and the opportunities for further study. This course is delivered via weekly lectures and tutorials and is supplemented with web materials and readings.
title: Understanding Australian Cities
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course examines critical issues in services and relationship marketing. Key aspects of marketing in service organisations are addressed including the management of customer-contact employees. The nature and scope of marketing relationships between firms and with customers is also explored.
title: Services Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This core course provides you with the theoretical and conceptual foundations of consumer behaviour required to become an effective marketing practitioner. Marketing practitioners need to know and understand how organisations can apply consumer behaviour concepts when making marketing decisions. Therefore, you will review the major perspectives of how consumers make decisions and the factors that influence their decision-making processes in acquiring, using and disposing of products, services, experiences and ideas. In doing so, you will be able to apply your knowledge and skills to marketing related activities and to develop and implement more effective marketing strategies.
title: Advanced Consumer Behaviour
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Strategic marketing decision-making plays a vital role in the success or failure of both business and not-for-profit organisations. This course introduces important strategic marketing concepts and techniques for achieving success, and explains how to develop and manage them in a competitive fast-changing environment.
title: Marketing Strategy and Analytics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Student Managed Investment Fund is a course that challenges high-achieving students to apply their training and knowledge in investment simulations and work-related projects. The course is designed to equip students with the professional skills necessary to be work-ready by engaging them in real-world financial analysis and simulations. Students are supported throughout this University-based internship by Academics and Industry Practitioners, who will come to campus to share real world insights into the challenges of portfolio/investment management and advice. These individuals will provide mentoring to students throughout the course. This course is restricted to students undertaking the Finance and Financial Planning majors. Students must have completed a minimum 160 credit points.
title: Student Managed Investment Fund
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This is an ongoing subject for the PhD research. Students should be working on the literature review, data collection and analysis of the PhD thesis.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course is supervised higher degree research.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Graduate Research School

description: The course provides a comprehensive overview of medical microbiology and oral pathology. It covers a broad spectrum of topics, including disease transmission, preventive measures, diagnostic techniques, and treatment options. These areas of study are essential for clinical practice.
title: Microbiology for Oral Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: The Evidence-Based Practice (EBP) course aims to develop foundation knowledge and skills for best practice (informed by evidence) in health sciences, with a specific focus on the quality use of medicines. Students will develop critical evaluation skills for the purpose of effective implementation of evidence-based health care into practice. This will be achieved by providing fundamental knowledge and understanding of three domains: (A) applied pharmaceutical sciences (pharmacovigilance, pharmacoepidemiology and pharmacoeconomics), (B) quality use of medicine in specific patient groups, and (C) critical appraisal of research/practice studies for implications in research/clinical practice. This includes research methodologies in clinical set-up, interpretation of biomedical data and critical appraisal of published clinical evidence. This course also aims to promote the rational use of drugs and pharmaceutical services and further prepare students for future higher studies. Sound knowledge and understanding of tertiary-level pharmacology and basic statistics/medical literature search skills are expected.
title: Evidence Based Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces students to the study of human behaviour from a biological point of view. Apart from providing students with knowledge in fundamental topics of biological psychology, such as the human nervous system, psychopharmacology, and research methods in behavioural neuroscience, the course also includes more applied topics. For example, the biological basis of learning and memory, visual perception, and affective disorders are typically explored. This course has prerequisites that must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Biological Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: The course deals with the tools available to evaluate and control engineering projects. It examines the development of proposals, proposal appraisal, and post-project review. Proposal inputs such as risk assessment, cost and benefit estimation and feasibility studies are examined through a major assignment. Traditional, as well as modern appraisal techniques, are examined.
title: Project Evaluation and Control
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: A good supply chain needs good suppliers, but the actual processes that go into sourcing goods and services are as complex as they are important. In making decisions about sourcing for organisations you'll need to balance cost and environmental, societal, economic and ethical concerns to create sustainable enterprises and outcomes. This course will equip you with the knowledge to assess a variety of sourcing strategies and processes across the public and private sectors, and it will teach you market analysis as it relates to supply and demand. You'll develop strategies to identify and respond to issues you'll likely encounter in the workplace, including general issues in purchasing and supply management and their strategic planning, and specific topics on asset procurement, contract management, supplier performance management, and risk management in sourcing. Building your skills in critical analysis, you'll use a series of case studies to link and apply the theoretical underpinnings of strategic sourcing to practical experiences. By the end of your course, you'll be prepared to implement a range of plans and actions to drive innovation and achieve sustainable, successful business outcomes.
title: Strategic Sourcing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

title: Dissertation 4

description: Complex projects occur not only in manufacturing, supply chain and construction industries. Complex projects emerge across diverse sectors, including healthcare, energy and utilities, aviation, consulting, mining and public administration. This unit provides an innovative approach to analyse projects with ill-defined scope, unstable and ambiguous requirements, stretched timelines and budgets, and stakeholders with multiple views in shifting contexts. Therefore, solutions need to be novel, multidisciplinary and adaptive to changing conditions. Taking a multidisciplinary approach, this course provides a combination of theoretical insights and practical conceptual tools to diagnose project complexity and to make decisions about organizing complex projects. Unlike conventional project management courses focusing solely on the planning and control dimensions of predictable and stable projects, this course focuses on 'cross-industry' projects. Those are novel, non-routine, complex and developed in dynamic environments. This means that this course is a suitable elective for professionals from various disciplines and programs, including business administration, ICT, environmental engineering, public health, event management, public administration, aviation management and climate change adaptation.
title: Managing Complex Projects
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Develop a broad-based analytical approach to the strategic choices, challenges and opportunities faced by managers in an increasingly international business environment. Managing in the global context requires complex problem solving skills, thorough understanding of business strategy, and clear, thoughtful communication that is sensitive to a diverse range of stakeholders. In this course you will evaluate strategies of multinational enterprise (MNE) strategies and small firms internationalising, and the theories and frameworks that explain the factors shaping those strategies. Key to your learning with be developing critical thinking and evaluation skills. By gaining a thorough understanding of differences in cultures, institutions, economies and societies across borders, you will strengthen your ability to lead an organisation that is resilient to global shocks and capable of navigating complex relationships both locally and internationally.
title: Global Business Strategy
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The course closely examines issues of data management when data are considered as a strategic resource. In so doing data are looked in a different light, stressing their intertwined (symbiotic) relationship with business. Data should be protected, categorised, understood in their atomic from as well as in their relationships. But above all they should be managed within the context of the domain of the enterprise that owns them.
title: Data Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course focuses on diagnosing mathematical errors and misconceptions to inform effective intervention and differentiated teaching. It also develops problem-solving approaches that integrate mathematical concepts through real-world applications, modelling, and inquiry. As part of the STEM major, the course examines the central role of mathematics within STEM education.
title: Mathematics Education 3 - Diagnosis and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course addresses the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching to address learner diversity in classrooms. It enables students to become familiar with current research in the area and to develop an applied knowledge of educational adjustments (curriculum, instruction and assessment), and the process of educational planning and teaching that is beneficial for all students. Differentiation as an inclusive, student-centred approach to teaching for students with varying abilities will be explored in detail. Assessment for the course is designed to strengthen understanding of the kinds of adjustments to curriculum, instruction and assessment for students to enable them to reach their maximum academic potential and what is considered reasonable, and how differentiated teaching practices are beneficial for all students.
title: Adjustments and Differentiation
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines strategies for changing criminal behaviour. The interventions explored in the course are most frequently observed within the correctional system in both custodial and community settings; however, programs utilised in other sectors of the criminal justice system (i.e. police, courts) and in affiliated social service organisations are also included in the course where forensic populations are their target treatment group. The course draws on psychological principles and research evidence, linking theories of crime causation to foundations of behaviour modification and propensity-reducing interventions. A review of specific programs is presented, although the focus of the course is on the overarching design principles associated with positive client outcomes.
title: Interventions for Correctional Clients
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Hearing directly from people with disabilities about their lives is vital to good research, effective policy and compassionate, sound practice. This course exposes you to the lived experience of people with a disability from the 'insider perspective'. By examining a diversity of personal narratives such as memoirs, autobiographies and documentary films about and by people with a disability, you will come to understand how disability is just one influence sometimes significant, sometimes minor, but always fluid in shaping the direction and quality of people's lives. This course requires a commitment from you to read deeply and broadly, and to be open to fresh perspectives of understanding the experiences of people with disabilities, in Australia and globally. Such openness is essential in advancing the rights, dignity and opportunities of people with disabilities. Your newly developed disability awareness will be the foundation upon which you can build your practice and assist in providing best-practice experience and disability support.
title: The Lived Experience of Disability
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course focuses on Visual Arts curriculum and pedagogy for the junior secondary classroom. Students investigate, interpret and synthesise Visual Arts research, curriculum documents and international best practice to refine their discipline content knowledge and design innovative resources, assessment and pedagogical strategies that support creative, practical and critical learning in Years 7 to 10. Through an integrated program of studio-based Making and Responding experiences, students develop the knowledge, skills and understanding required to plan, sequence, resource and assess Visual Arts learning for diverse students in the junior secondary context.
title: Visual Arts Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Understanding the politics of the environment and sustainability has never been more important. In the context of global climate and environmental change, this course explores issues at the forefront of today's political agenda. This course examines the politics and power relations of environmental sustainability in Australia and globally. It investigates the business-government-environment relationship, asks whether we can 'green' politics, and explores the role of major actors and ideas in shaping politics including NGOs, social movements, and the international community.
title: The Politics of Environment and Sustainability
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course covers the use of multivariate and advanced univariate statistical techniques. There is an emphasis on the usefulness of statistical techniques as an aid to answering research questions and interpreting data in psychology. Emphasis is placed on the development of independence through the application of good research methodology, statistical skills and advanced use of SPSS. This course is a core requirement of the Honours in Psychology programs.
title: Issues in Quantitative Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Students are required to conduct an analysis of a complex problem and to design, implement, install and test a high-quality solution to the problem in one of the specialisation areas available. Assessment includes a dissertation and seminar on work completed. Students must complete components 7590ICT_P1, 7590ICT_P2, 7590ICT_P3 and 7590ICT_P4 in sequential order, preferably not enrolling in more than three components (30CP) in any one trimester. A grade will be awarded on successful completion of 7590ICT_P4. This course is part one of a set of four courses. Students in a Masters program must have completed 40 credit points of core/foundation courses and have a GPA of at least 6.0 prior to enrolment in the Dissertation courses. Co-requisite / Pre-requisite: 7113ICT Research for IT Professionals. For students in the Graduate Diploma program, the Co-requisite / Pre-requisite is 6112ICT Research Methods in IT. Students must submit a Department Consent Form applicable to Honours Thesis courses prior to enrolment in 7590ICT_P1.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

A grade will be awarded on successful completion of 7590ICT_P4. This course is part two of a set of four courses. Students in a Masters program must have completed 40 credit points of core/foundation courses and have a GPA of at least 6.0 prior to enrolment in the Dissertation courses. academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Web applications interact with users, connecting to back-end databases and dynamically generating results to the browser through a web server. This course presents a systematic introduction to the development of dynamic, community-based, Web applications through the integration of HTML/CSS, with server-side scripting languages, database systems, modern web frameworks and other related technologies. Previously known as 7005ICT Programming Principles 2 and therefore incompatible with 7005ICT Web Programming.
title: Web Programming
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course is a continuation of the topics introduced in the Engineering Materials (1017ENG), and Engineering Mechanics (1501ENG), with an emphasis on construction materials. It covers the behaviour and performance of widely used construction materials such as (i) concrete, (ii) steel, (iii) masonry, (iv) timber, (v) pavement materials, and (vi) polymer. Particular emphasis is placed upon concrete technology as specified by Australia Standards, and its practical applications. Attention is also given to recognising construction materials and their selection in various situations. The handling, treatment and deterioration prevention of selected construction materials is also introduced.
title: Construction Materials
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course aims to provide students with the necessary skills to make better decisions regarding the analysis and management of risks in engineering projects. The subject information acts as a guide for practitioners managing real projects. Topics include risk environment, understanding the human aspects to risk assessment, dealing with uncertainty, quantitative methods and qualitative assessment for risk management.
title: Risk Analysis and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The advanced analysis and design of reinforced and prestressed concrete members in flexure, shear, torsion and compression are taught at a professional level. Both strength and serviceability design requirements are covered. The concepts are applied to a design project involving a conventional concrete structure. The course also investigates advanced topics such as non-rectangular sections and the analysis and design of concrete flat plates. Assessment is by design assignments and a major design project.
title: Advanced Reinforced and Pre-stressed Concrete
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides students with valuable opportunities to learn how to apply relevant theories from Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering into practice so that they can effectively conduct field surveys and laboratory examination of soil samples, correctly interpret and analyse results of such geotechnical investigations, select appropriate parameters for numerical models, evaluate stability of natural slopes and embankments, and develop skills to write comprehensive and concise geotechnical reports. In addition, the fundamentals of geology and rock mechanics will be introduced and discussed through a number of case studies. Students will also have the opportunity to become familiar with leading computer programs, which are commonly used in the industry, and through performing project-based assignments students will acquire sufficient knowledge and develop critical computer skills that will enable them to solve various practical problems
title: Advanced Geotechnical Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Linear Electromagnetics is a lecture and laboratory based course in which students are introduced to tools and design techniques for engineering applications in which electromagnetic waves generated by sources of alternating current play a dominant role. These applications typically involve the transmission of waves over metallic or dielectric transmission lines or through free space, with the purpose of transporting either information or electric power.
title: Linear Electromagnetics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Organisational cultures and their sub-cultures play a significant part on the success of adopting new technology. Digital systems applications provide an effective framework for changing how workers work. This course examines the trends towards mobile, networked work practices. It aims to provide students with knowledge of the strategic uses of information technology to bridge the gap between traditional work practices and newer forms of mobile work practices to achieve the goal of mobilising and networking an organisation's workforce.
title: Digital Transformation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course introduces the underlying structures and mechanisms of modern computer systems, networks and security concepts. All students enrolled in an ICT degree need to have an understanding of the basic architecture and operation of computer systems and a general understanding of relevant security concerns. This course provides an overview of the hardware, software, network, and security concepts and technologies that define modern computer systems. The course aims to provide students with the basic knowledge of how the components that define a computer work together and by extension an appreciation of the capabilities and limitations of computer systems. This knowledge assists students in the application of computing technologies to solve real world problems. This course material builds a foundation for further study in the field of information technology, and is a suitable prerequisite for many ICT courses. This course was previously known as 1807ICT Computer and Network Architecture and is incompatible with 1807ICT Computer and Network Architecture
title: Computer Systems and Cyber Security
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course examines the principles, architectures, and applications of Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs). Students analyse DLT mechanisms and challenges, design blockchain-enabled solutions for real-world and agentic AI applications, evaluate smart contract integration strategies, and assess standards, governance, and regulatory frameworks for trusted and sustainable digital ecosystems.
title: Fundamentals of Blockchain and Distributed Ledger Technology
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Pharmacy has at its core the discipline of pharmaceutics, which is the study of drug formulations and the processes by which these are designed, manufactured and delivered to the body. Simply stated, pharmaceutics converts drug substances into medicines - delivery systems capable of administering drugs to the body in a safe, efficient, reproducible and convenient manner. Specialised Dosage Forms provides an in-depth pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical knowledge of advanced drug delivery technologies utilised in medicine and addresses formulation aspects relating to special industries including; cosmetic, dental, veterinary, and traditional, complementary and integrative medicines.
title: Specialised Dosage Forms
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: 7006PHM is the second course in the Professional Pharmacy Practice series. Professional Pharmacy Practice II will engage students in the topics of women's health and dermatology. The course utilises a range of learning activities, including face-to-face discussions, problem-based learning (PBL) and practical case studies that will support students' self-directed learning. Students will continue to build on their knowledge and skills obtained from previous pharmacy practice courses, with particular attention placed on patient-centred care and the quality use of medicines.
title: Professional Pharmacy Practice II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: The dissertation is the culmination of students' training in the fundamental sciences and professional practice of pharmacy. Qualitative and quantitative research projects serve to address topical issues relating to the practice of pharmacy (e.g. quality use of medicines; pharmacoeconomics; pharmacy management; social aspects of pharmacy; rational prescribing; drug utilisation etc.) and specific research topics within the health sciences (pharmacology; pharmaceutics; pharmacogenomics; medicinal chemistry; pharmacognosy; molecular biology etc). Students work with an experienced academic supervisor/s within and external to the School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences who maintains regular contact and provides support and direction in the design and execution of the dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: 8001HLS consists of four 10 credit point courses (8001HLS_P1 to P4) and these courses make up the research component of the Graduate Diploma of Health Research program (4161). The final grade is allocated on completion of part 4. The dissertation requires students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This involves the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, and data analysis. At the completion of the four parts, students will submit a report of their research project (thesis) for examination. Students are advised to consult their School Advisor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final part (8001HLS_P4), they are expected to submit their dissertation by the due date specified in the course profile.
title: Dissertation Part 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides an introduction to the contemporary debates in the social sciences and their relevance to social interventions in the health and human services arena. The social sciences provide human services practitioners and health professionals with theoretical and methodological frameworks for professional practice. Frameworks, informed by the discipline of sociology, connect important concepts such as class, race, sex and age to social inequalities. This course is intended to expose students to the wider social and cultural context in which health and human services operate, including an understanding of culture, globalisation, environmental sustainability and issues surrounding disadvantage. Incompatible: 1008CCJ Social Problems - Inequality and (In)Justice, 1007LHS Understanding the Social World, 1723LHS Towards A Just World.
title: Introduction to Social Theory
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Terrorism is a major global security challenge for states and citizens. This course explores various dimensions of modern terrorism by examining a series of individuals, groups, and movements that have adopted the strategy as a means of achieving political or social change. It looks at the motivations of terrorists and how they justify their violence, at the changing ways terrorist groups and movements have organised themselves, at exploitation of new technologies, from international air travel and television to drones and social media, and at how terrorists learn and adapt their tactics. The course also looks at why terrorist groups succeed or more often fail. Finally, it examines how states might counter terrorism individually or in cooperation with others. This course is offered at Nathan in odd years, and Gold Coast in even years.
title: Terrorism and Counter-terrorism
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Effective communication is the key to success in modern politics and the media and is, in all its forms, a vital and integral part of a functioning democracy. We will examine to what extent political actors try to influence each other and the public in setting the political agenda. This course focuses on how political actors communicate with voters through the traditional mass media and social media, media effects, how media facilitate political communication, and the strategies used by political actors to compete for media attention in elections, through the government, and in the public sphere.
title: Politics, Spin and the Media
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course introduces students to the major themes and issues studied in the discipline of International Relations. Topics to be engaged include the development of the current international system, war, terrorism and non-traditional security threats, international law and organisations, diplomacy and foreign policy, international political economy, development, and global environmental issues. Students will be introduced to the primary theoretical approaches used by International Relations scholars to explain or interpret global events and processes. The course also introduces students to key concepts and practices related to employability and career readiness in International Relations and related fields.
title: International Relations
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course develops the capacity of public managers to operate effectively and appropriately within a democracy governed by the rule of law. Public servants work within a web of 'rules', ranging from Codes of Conduct and professional ethics through legislative instruments and the constitution to international legal obligations and human rights. This subject explores how that web of regulatory 'rules' shapes policy design and implementation. Although understanding the core concepts of regulation and administrative law are crucial, the subject is grounded and practical, making use of case studies, expert guest speakers and contemporary examples from practice.
title: Governing by the Rules
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

title: Exchange Studies-Undergraduate
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

description: This course is an advanced level course in counselling theory and practice. The course aims to introduce students to a diverse range of counselling theories and practices. The course enables students to begin the development of a conceptual framework for an area of professional practice. Theoretically, the aims of this course are for students to develop a good understanding of some of the major schools of thought in psychotherapy and counselling. Practically, the course aims to build students' competence in more advanced counselling and interviewing techniques.
title: Counselling Theory and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course sets out the foundations for human services processes and practices, establishing students as 'emerging practitioners' and providing the knowledge, skills and values framework for development of professional identity. In particular, it tracks the identification of need, service delivery models and systems, and the organisational context in which assessment and intervention processes take place across the domains of practice. The course also explores the influences of knowledge and theory, and uses case analysis to identify the perspectives of service users, as well as the challenges for practice.
title: Human Services Processes
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course critically examines case management and steps students through the knowledge and skills necessary to practise case management, a service delivery approach used in a range of fields and disciplines. Professional practice draws on a theoretical and evidence base for determining individual need and for planning, procuring and coordinating a range of services and supports.
title: Case Management for Human Service and Health Professionals
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Students complete an independent investigation of a research question of some significance in Psychology. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. This is the second of two components. PREREQUISITES: 6000PSY_Y1. Students must only enrol in this component after enrolling in 6000PSY_Y1 in the previous Trimester.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course explores the relationship between cameraless and analogue darkroom techniques and their mediation of the natural environment. These ideas will be studied through several core conceptual and material examinations. By exploring historical processes and their impact on our understanding of the natural world, students will reconsider traditional photographic processes in a contemporary context and reconceptualise how photography has, and can, interpret and reconfigure.
title: Photography Studio 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: How do we come to know music, and know through music? How can knowledge be embedded in creative processes and products? How do we make meaning of (and through) sound and music? This course explores music not just as sound (an artefact) or as practice (a behaviour), but as a way of knowing and understanding the world. Through close listening, critical enquiry, and case studies, students will examine how musical knowledge is formed, shared, and contested. Students will build foundations for lifelong enquiry into music by drawing on a range of perspectives and genres, including creative, embodied, and Indigenous ones, students will build foundations for lifelong enquiry into music.
title: Thinking Through Music
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The Music Industry Internship is a Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course that provides students with an opportunity to apply their skills in an industry work placement in host organisations where they will work at least 100 hours during the course. Placements may be intensive or take a longer form such as one day per week over a period of weeks. Students are placed in organisations after an assessment of their interests, skills and post-graduation employment aims. Host organisation staff are responsible for the day-to-day supervision of students with the University providing training and support. In addition to the placements students are required to attend a series of meetings and to complete a final report. Students will be attached to a host organisation through which they will negotiate and develop their project proposal. Internships may be in the areas of broadcast, arts administration, education, production or similar. During placements students will reflect on career planning strategies and further develop their career portfolio. Students will complete their internships under the direction of both a Workplace Supervisor and a University Academic Supervisor. Note: This is a Consent course. Students will not be able to enrol online until the Course Convenor has approved and allocated internship places.
title: Music Industry Internship (WIL) A
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The acquisition and development of Acting, Speech, Singing and Dance techniques are interdependent elements in a process that culminates in a Performance Project, a learning opportunity consisting of a short 'song & dance' performance presented simply, to an audience of tutors, fellow-students and members of the public. This course aims to develop the student's potential as a musical theatre performer as fully as possible, through individual and group tuition in singing and class tuition in acting, dance, voice and speech. Master classes, workshops, seminars and public performances are also utilised from time to time. It is the principal study for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Musical Theatre program.
title: Musical Theatre 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The course is an intensive activity in the area of Opera Studies. The options available are for singers (operatic roles) and pianists (Repetiteur activities.)
title: Opera Project A
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to design and implement a self-directed project either individually, or as small groups, under the mentorship of a nominated staff member. These projects should be directly related to their creative and/or professional specialisation, and able to be completed within a one-trimester duration. NOTE: Enrolment is subject to approval of the Course Convenor - upon enrolment students should submit a proposal (according to the template provided in assessment item 1 on the Canvas course site) and submit before the end of Week 1. If no proposal is submitted, or the proposal is not approved, enrolment will be cancelled.
title: Project Study A
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course examines how sound production interacts with our perceptions of space, time and place. It explores sound spatialisation, the layering of complex sonic elements to create sonic and spatial musics, and the relationship between the listener and the overall sonic context. These issues are explored as they apply to real or imaginary, commercially oriented, creative, new and/or experimental contexts, with an emphasis on how musicians can employ music technologies to augment and enhance the spatial presentation of music and sonic art. Activities include critical listening, the study and use of sound spatialisation techniques, project-based work and investigations into the relationships between listening and context. This course is delivered through tutorials and seminars.
title: Multichannel Sonic Environments
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Honours Research Project constitutes a 40CP honours research commitment within the Bachelor of Design with Honours program. Each of the four components of the course combine to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The expectation is that the research project undertaken will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item. Co-requisite/Pre-requisite: 6511QCA Design Research Methods.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This studio will address the strategic and multi-disciplinary nature of broad scale regional planning. It could take the form of a conservation, community development or a resource management study and involve the preparation of a spatially based, geographic specific plan or policies. Emphasis will be given to scientific input and research techniques, handling of multiple objectives, integration of ecological, social, economic, cultural aspects, forecasting techniques, and to strategic thinking. Pre-requisite: Students must have passed 1027ENV Introductory Planning Studio or 1901ENG Design Studio 1, 1511ENV Environmental Planning Studio, and 2067ENV Development Processes Studio and completed 150 credit points or have the permission of the course convenor before enrolling in this course.
title: Strategic Planning Studio
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This studio will address the strategic and multi-disciplinary nature of broad scale regional planning. It could take the form of a conservation, community development or a resource management study and involve the preparation of a spatially based, geographic specific plan or policies. Emphasis will be given to scientific input and research techniques, handling of multiple objectives, integration of ecological, social, economic, cultural aspects, forecasting techniques, and to strategic thinking. Prerequisites: Students must have passed 7128ENV Advanced Development Processes Studio and completed 70 credit points or have the permission of the course convener before enrolling in this course
title: Advanced Strategic Planning Studio
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces students to the theories surrounding malocclusions, orthodontics and thermoformed appliances. This course is integral to the function of a dental technologist as the physics of design and function introduced in this course will provide the foundation for Professional Practice course in final year. The design principles learnt in this course will be applied in Laboratory Practicum 2; providing a solid grounding for future commercial practice. Pre-requisite: All year 1 courses must have been successfully completed prior to proceeding to year 2 courses. Co-requisite: 2202DOH and 2220DOH must be studied simultaneously.
title: Prosthetic Technology 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Marketing is a philosophy that permeates the entire organisation and not just the marketing department. The course presents a number of strategic concepts and then shows how they can be integrated to either evaluate or develop a marketing strategy. Some of the key concepts include distinctive strategies, generic strategies, sustainable competitive advantage and market positioning. However, the most important lesson is to adopt a holistic approach to a firm's marketing strategy.
title: Strategic Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: In the past several decades, the field of investment analysis has evolved from a descriptive process to a highly formalised and quantitative area of study. The rapidly changing financial environment and the number of new instruments available have made analysis a task which can only be carried out by persons who have been equipped with updated skills. This course studies the controversial issues and the current advances in the analysis of international capital markets, and presents a range of analytical techniques. Investment analysis and management is important to both individuals who manage their own personal investments and investment managers who invest on behalf of their clients or companies. The course aims to consolidate the investment theories to make informed decisions.
title: Investment Analysis and Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is supervised higher degree research.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Graduate Research School

description: This course introduces the practical application of dental technology and its relationship to dentistry and oral health. This course allows students time to develop and craft their skills in the precise technical application of design and construction of removable oral prostheses and appliances. It provides students with the opportunity to develop dexterity, hand-eye coordination, and pay attention to detail using the skills gained in 1110DOH Introduction to Dental Technology and Dental Morphology. Students will have the opportunity to improve their skills within a commercial laboratory setting in the Prosthetic Laboratory that services the Griffith University Dental Clinic and externally on work experience (in own time). Prerequisite: 1110DOH. All year 1 courses must be successfully completed prior to proceeding to year 2 courses.
title: Laboratory Practicum 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course introduces students to the professional practice of dental technology. Students will study the clinical and technical principles behind the design and fabrication of removable prosthodontics and associated components. It will include theory on occlusion, workplace health and safety, ethics, infection control, care of equipment and efficient use of materials will be included as underlying principles of laboratory practice. Prerequisite: 1011DOH. All year 1 courses must be successfully completed prior to proceeding to year 2 courses.
title: Prosthetic Technology 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course requires execution, analysis and presentation of a research thesis. This involves development of a project, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms.
title: Dissertation Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Businesses operate within a dynamic landscape shaped by internal, external, and global influences. Navigating this landscape effectively is crucial for optimizing a business's economic, financial, and social performance. In this course, students are introduced to the fundamental concepts, techniques, and principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics, particularly within the Australian context. This knowledge equips students with practical decision-making tools, empowering them to become future business leaders capable of making informed and effective decisions amidst complexities.
title: Economics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Green Marketing is particularly relevant in today's context of a growing demand for products, services and systems that are environmentally sustainable. In this course you will learn how organisations develop environmentally friendly strategies for product innovation, brand reputation and brand equity. Marketing communication and supply chain issues are also explored, with an emphasis on the concept of more sustainable product life cycles.
title: Green Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Marketing for behaviour change offers a framework for designing effective behavioural change programs which can be used to change social, environmental and financial behaviours. This course brings together a range of skills required by government, not-for-profits and behaviour change consultants to effect positive behaviour change programs to stem a wide range of societal issues.
title: Marketing for Behaviour Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course will provide students with the knowledge and quantitative skills needed for the management and conservation of marine living resources. Students will learn about the modelling methods that inform ecosystem management. Students will utilise the R programming environment to simulate the processes that determine marine ecosystem population dynamics.
title: Marine Ecosystem Modelling
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will provide students with theoretical and practical knowledge of the role of haematology and blood grouping in the patient care by investigation and diagnosis of blood disorders. Students will develop skills in blood test result interpretation and reporting to doctor for patients' final diagnosis.
title: Haematology I
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces students to specialist topics in biology that are relevant to conservation of biodiversity. It includes study of extinction and its causes including habitat loss, disease and alien species, addresses the nature and cause of natural rarity, examines processes of restoration ecology and reintroductions. The course also includes an appraisal of international initiatives in conservation and international agreements with implications for conservation. Assessment is by written and oral reports, and examinations.
title: Conservation Biology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines the diversity of plants in the landscape and gives students further experience in plant identification. It considers the major structural components of the flora of regional ecosystems and the factors which determine the distribution of plants. There are sections dealing with plant diversity, ecology, plant-animal interactions and biomes as biological indicators. Practical work includes fieldwork and assessment is by reports, written and practical examination.
title: Botany
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: NOTE: THIS IS AN INTENSIVE COURSE. The Field Trip component will consist of 2 full days in the field prior to the start of the trimester, as well as a full Laboratory Day on the Gold Coast campus. The other classes will be Lectures or Workshops held on campus but available online after each day as recordings - see timetable for more details. This is a 3RD-YEAR COURSE, restricted to students for which it is a core or major requirement. This course covers the ecology of estuaries, where freshwater mixes with seawater. The biology of estuarine habitats is covered in detail, emphasising their role in coastal productivity and their sensitivities to pollution and habitat modification. The course will cover conservation and restoration practices. Assessment is by written assignment and final examination.
title: Estuarine Ecology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The course is designed to provide students with the basic principles and concepts required to become better managers of themselves, their role and performance within workplace teams, and to begin to consider their own input upon the management of workplaces they may find themselves in. Basic concepts and principles used to manage the resources of personnel, finances, inventory, time, space and 'self' will be addressed.
title: Pharmacy Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course provides you with an understanding of the concepts, principles and factors of corporate communication. This course examines the various factors of planning, developing and implementing corporate communications. It also supports the development of your skills in critical evaluation, problem-solving and decision-making.
title: Corporate Communications
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Honours Dissertation Part 4
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: Behind every great business lies effective, efficient and sustainable supply chain management. Informed by the 'Five Rights', Right Goods, Right Time, Right Place, Right Quantity and Quality, and Right Cost, being able to deliver products and services to clients and consumers in a timely, reliable and responsible way is a crucial element of organisational success. This course will teach you strategic aspects of the major elements of supply chains and the extent to which they are inter-related in delivering organisational value, adaptability and resilience. You'll learn how to identify the challenges and opportunities facing managers of supply networks as they work to balance competing priorities, interests, and interpersonal and interorganisational relationships. As corporate sustainability and global supply chains enter a new era in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, you'll be equipped to take a proactive approach to planning and organising. Teamwork is key, and you'll be capable of working in collaboration with peers to critically analyse and improve inventory, distribution, procurement and risk management strategies and processes across a range of industries and sectors.
title: Strategic Supply Chain Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Managing conflict and cooperation through negotiation is a fundamental part of life. In a professional context we often negotiate within and between organizations. Negotiation planning and analysis, strategy and tactics, communication and decision making, interdependence and alternatives, and power, ethics and social responsibility comprise the fundamentals of negotiation, which establishes the foundation for negotiating professionally. Often we negotiate in teams bilaterally and in groups multilaterally. Culture adds an element of complexity in international negotiations, as does the environment through the pursuit of sustainable goals. Students will use skills gained through a mastery of negotiation fundamentals to develop and understand how to manage different types of negotiations. This course focuses on interpersonal negotiations in management context.
title: Negotiation Strategy and Skill
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Rapid changes in society, international relations, technology and communication have led to flexible ways of, and increasing numbers of people, working across global borders. This course provides an opportunity for students to critically analyse global dimensions of the core aspects of human resource management, such as linkages with business strategy, structure, policies and practices; staffing, recruitment, and selection; training and development; rewards management; and performance management. The course examines how human resources are managed and problems solved within and across differing global cultural, political, economic, legislative and technological contexts. The course aims to develop globally engaged and responsible future leaders of GHRM and cross-culturally competent globally mobile employees.
title: Global Human Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course explores the basic principles and the practical application of pedagogy as related to the student's major area of study. Effective teaching practices for the instruction of the beginner level in the studio environment will be central to the program. Recent trends in studio teaching will influence the perspective of the discussion and research. Areas of focus include Keyboard, Strings, Vocal, Wind and Brass, Drums & Percussion, and Guitar & Bass.
title: Instrumental and Vocal Pedagogy
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course is designed to teach students the logic of research methodology and evaluation in the social sciences. Students will learn how to articulate a program evaluation research proposal, formulate research designs, and logically determine what research methodology provides the best avenue to carry out different forms of research.
title: Research and Evaluation Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The course will provide students with a basic understanding of the main pieces of legislation dealing with competition and consumer law with an emphasis on the Competition and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth). Although the emphasis in the course will be on the practical application of the law, an understanding of theories relevant to particularly competition law will be referred to throughout the course.
title: Competition and Consumer Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course offers students the opportunity to develop an understanding of how policymaking and planning can be used in responding to the problem of climate change. The processes and instruments of both policymaking and planning are covered. A cross-section of adaptation and mitigation policies/plans are analysed, from the international to the national, state, and local levels of government. No prior knowledge of policymaking, planning, or climate change is assumed.
title: Policymaking and Planning for Climate Change
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course focuses upon preparing teachers to teach mathematics from Years 7 to 10. The course is designed both to improve Pre-service capacity to assess and report on student learning and to deepen their content and pedagogical knowledge. Restriction: Students must be enrolled in program 1567 or 5700
title: Mathematics Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Build skills in communication, research and leadership in this course as you explore the increasingly important interrelationship between advocacy and leadership. You'll undertake a substantial research project to prepare yourself to better promote the rights, interests and needs of individuals and their families, communities and organisations. Developing your capacity for critical thinking and creativity, you'll examine theoretical and practical strategies to establish, administer and improve social and professional programs and reflect on the key health, education, legal and social issues and government policies that shape and influence the Australian human services sector, including the continuing push for equity and greater inclusion. This includes practical efforts such as community engagement, diplomacy and coaching, which are essential for effective leaders. Throughout, you'll gain an understanding of the socioeconomic and environmental forces that impact on the condition of people's lives in Australia and the interaction of roles and contexts that underpin your professionalism, leadership and advocacy.
title: Advocacy and Leadership
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This second field placement course provides students undertaking the Bachelor of Social Work with the opportunity to again apply their university based learning to practice situations. Students are required to complete 500 hours (approximately 4 days per week for 18 weeks) of practice based learning and engage in professional supervision with a social work qualified field supervisor. The program builds on the skills and understanding achieved during Social Work Field Placement 1. It is the final requirement of the degree program and focuses on facilitating the student's development of the skills, knowledge, attitudes and analyses to enter the field as a social work practitioner. Learning tasks assessed on a pass/fail basis.
title: Social Work Field Placement 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides a content foundation for mathematics education in middle years. It includes numeration and computation and problem solving with whole numbers and fractions, early algebra, and the application of measurement, space, based reasoning and chance understanding in problem settings.
title: Mathematical Concepts
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course will encourage students to compare and evaluate some of the current clinical approaches to managing and intervening in suicidal behaviour. Students will focus on the theoretical basis of each approach and critique its value from community and scientific perspectives. This course will encourage students to compare and evaluate some of the current clinical approaches to managing and intervening in suicidal behaviour. Students will focus on the theoretical basis of each approach and critique its value from community and scientific perspectives.
title: Approaches to People Experiencing Suicidal Distress
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Preventing and managing the spread of disease is a key task for public health agencies. The COVID-19 pandemic has highlighted the importance of this function in Australia and internationally. In this course you will examine the impact of public health measures on the prevalence and management of outbreaks of infectious illness in the community. You will examine surveillance, outbreak management, communication and contact tracing practices with a focus on community care, using real-life case studies and critical thinking in an effort to better inform future use of relevant tools in healthcare. You will evaluate the role key performance indicators play in the management of community outbreaks of infectious illness and critically analyse context-specific and practice-specific issues related to infection control in public and community health. With this new knowledge, you can build, plan and manage effective infectious disease prevention and responses in your community with a focus on health safety.
title: Infection Control for Community and Public Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery
