description: This is one of two Advanced Topics courses. Each of these courses embraces subject matter close to the current state-of-the-art. Students are strongly advised to consult the academic offering their selected topic well before the course starts. Any topic studied in one Advanced Topics course cannot be studied in the other Advanced Topics course. Students must submit a Registration Form prior to enrolment in this Advanced Topic course.
title: Advanced Topics in Information Technology A
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Students are required to conduct an analysis of a complex problem and to design, implement, install and test a high-quality solution to the problem in one of the specialisation areas available. Assessment includes a dissertation and seminar on work completed. Students must complete components 7590ICT_P1, 7590ICT_P2, 7590ICT_P3 and 7590ICT_P4 in sequential order, preferably not enrolling in more than three components (30CP) in any one trimester. A grade will be awarded on successful completion of 7590ICT_P4. This course is part three of a set of four courses. Students in a Masters program must have completed 40 credit points of core/foundation courses and have a GPA of at least 6.0 prior to enrolment in the Dissertation courses. Co-requisite / Pre-requisite: 7113ICT Research for IT Professionals. For students in the Graduate Diploma program, the Co-requisite / Pre-requisite is 6112ICT Research Methods in IT.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Students are required to conduct an analysis of a complex problem and to design, implement, install and test a high-quality solution to the problem in one of the specialisation areas available. Assessment includes a dissertation and seminar on work completed. Students must complete components 7590ICT_P1, 7590ICT_P2, 7590ICT_P3 and 7590ICT_P4 in sequential order, preferably not enrolling in more than three components (30CP) in any one trimester. A grade will be awarded on successful completion of 7590ICT_P4.This is the final part of a set of four courses. Students must submit a Department Consent Form applicable to Advanced Topics and Honours Thesis courses prior to enrolment in 7590ICT_P4. Access form here: https://forms.office.com/r/hDnDttRWzz Students in a Masters program must have completed 40 credit points of core/foundation courses and have completed/be completing 7590ICT_P1, 7590ICT_P2, and 7590ICT_P3,and have a GPA of at least 6.0 prior to enrolment in the Dissertation courses. Co-requisite / Pre-requisite: 7113ICT Research for IT Professionals. For students in the Graduate Diploma program, the Co-requisite / Pre-requisite is 6112ICT Research Methods in IT. The submission deadline is Friday of Week 13.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The course introduces paradigms and methodologies used in Information Technology research that can be applied to a range of typical research problems arising in computer science, software engineering, multimedia and information systems. The course allows students to develop the skills necessary to engage in higher degree research and to demonstrate an understanding of the scientific research practices and conventions appropriate for their selected research domains.
title: Research Methods in IT
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The course requires candidates to study in detail the way in which the principles of the whole engineering project or product life cycle including design, production and operation can be integrated. It embraces study of the general principles of systems integration and their application in an engineering management context. It also entails study of the fundamental principles of simultaneous engineering and addresses the issue of integration through a technology driven approach.
title: Advanced Topics in Engineering Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course covers the different elements of the planning process of engineering projects. It introduces the student to the processes of cost planning and control during the different phases of production. Particular emphasis is placed upon planning techniques, cost control tools and the effect the client, design team and type of contract has on the planning process.
title: Resource Planning and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Soil Mechanics is an important part of geotechnical engineering that deals with the engineering properties of various soils. This course provides students with valuable opportunities to develop their understanding of the fundamentals of soil behavior, and skills that will allow them to apply their knowledge to solve real-life problems. Students will also have the opportunity to become familiar with various testing procedures and learn how to perform laboratory tests to determine the geotechnical properties of soil such as grain-size distribution, plasticity, compaction characteristics, and permeability. After completing this course, students will acquire sufficient knowledge and develop critical skills that will enable them to solve practical problems related to soil mechanics
title: Soil Mechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces the underlying structures and mechanisms of modern computer systems, networks and security concepts. All students enrolled in an ICT degree need to have an understanding of the basic architecture and operation of computer systems and a general understanding of relevant security concerns. This course provides an overview of the hardware, software, network, and security concepts and technologies that define modern computer systems. The course aims to provide students with the basic knowledge of how the components that define a computer work together and by extension an appreciation of the capabilities and limitations of computer systems. This knowledge assists students in the application of computing technologies to solve real world problems. This course material builds a foundation for further study in the field of information technology, and is a suitable prerequisite for many ICT courses. This course was previously known as 7611ICT Computer Systems and Networks and is incompatible with 7611ICT Computer Systems and Networks.
title: Computer Systems and Cyber Security
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The focus of this subject is the governance and management of Information. Particular attention is paid to how policy is framed and implemented in modern organisations. Students will also be exposed to theories of IT governance, deep insights into modern policy problems surrounding information and be assessed on their ability to be able to effective critique and develop policy.
title: Information Policy and Governance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course introduces students to governance frameworks at the global, transboundary, national, basin and local levels and provides a practical knowledge and experience of governance system assessment using the OECD principles of effectiveness, efficiency, and trust and engagement. Across different components of the course, students will consider current themes influencing water governance and policy, including sustainable development, collaborative management, water rights and access, and equity for marginal groups. Water planning as a key governance mechanism at regional and basin levels will form one of the components. Students will select a water governance system from anywhere in the world to use a case study and undertake a critical assessment of that governance system. Overall, students are encouraged to develop awareness of the need to integrate economic, social, legal and environmental perspectives in governance and planning against a background of uncertainty and change. To achieve the learning objectives, this course is taught with a mix of lectures, workshops and student presentations.
title: Water Governance and Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This 10CP elective course is available to all undergraduate Griffith Business School students. The course is designed to facilitate a successful transition from university life to employment. A second but equally important feature of this course is the focus on raising awareness of your own personal attributes. You will participate in a task, activity or project-based internship in a face-to-face, virtual/online or blended mode which can open up possibilities to work with small and medium enterprises, business, government and community organisations in locations outside of South-East Queensland (e.g. regional and remote areas of Australia and other capital cities). Each placement offered by a 'Host Organisation' is carefully considered and matched to a student who demonstrates the required business knowledge, skills, personal attributes and motivation required to complete the activity, task or project to the level expected of an intern. This course is not available for credit based on prior studies or work experience, however flexible arrangements can be organised to allow students to commence their internship component prior to the start of the trimester (e.g., in the case of Summer or Winter Vacation Programs). Please email gbsinternships@griffith.edu.au for more information on flexible arrangements. Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
title: UG Business Internship I
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: 7005PHM Pharmacotherapeutics II provides an in-depth examination of the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of infectious disease, pain management, and endocrine disorders. Students are provided with an overview of the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of disease. Special emphasis is placed on the importance of therapeutic drug monitoring in the therapeutic plan. Lectures and problem-based clinical workshops serve to equip students with theoretical knowledge, an evidence-based approach, and practical clinical skills for the promotion and contribution to optimal use of medicines, delivery of health information and provision of health education in relation to the therapeutic areas covered in the course.
title: Pharmacotherapeutics II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: 8001HLS consists of four 10 credit point courses (8001HLS_P1 to P4) and these courses make up the research component of the Graduate Diploma of Health Research program (4161). The final grade is allocated on completion of part 4. The dissertation requires students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This involves the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, and data analysis. At the completion of the four parts, students will submit a report of their research project (thesis) for examination. Students are advised to consult their School Advisor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final part (8001HLS_P4), they are expected to submit their dissertation by the due date specified in the course profile.
title: Dissertation Part 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides students with a practical and theoretical understanding of health and safety in the workplace. It also aims to provide students with the skills and qualifications needed to work as Health and Safety Professionals.
title: Health and Safety in the Workplace
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Given the predominant role the United States has played in world affairs since World War II, American politics and foreign policy affects, not just Americans, but peoples and nations around the globe. The central aim of this course is to provide students with a strong understanding of the dimensions and dilemmas of American politics and foreign policy. This aim will be pursued through class teachings and discussions that will provide students with a solid overview of the key areas of American politics and foreign policy traditions, institutions, history and relations with particular countries and regions. Furthermore, the course will help students gain an informed understanding of some of the principal actors who have shaped American politics and foreign policy over historical time. This course is offered at Nathan in odd years, and Gold Coast in even years.
title: American Politics and Foreign Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This sequence of courses involves the identification of a research topic, the development of a research proposal to address that topic, the undertaking of the proposed research project, and its reporting in a dissertation. Where relevant, candidates will also obtain ethical clearance for the proposed project.
title: Dissertation 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Elections, politicians, the media, parliament: these are familiar and powerful features of everyday life in modern democracies. But how do they work? By comparing the experience of different countries, this course explores the ways in which institutions shape the choice and strategies of the various political actors.
title: Comparative Political Institutions
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course provides an introduction to the politics of international organisations and international law from the perspective of the International Relations (IR) discipline, with a specific focus on peace and conflict. More specifically, it aims to introduce students to i) the main IR approaches to studying international organisations and law and the key debates surrounding them ii) some of the most influential international organisations and legal frameworks and how they operate and iii) central issues pertaining to international law, norms and organisations in the areas of peacekeeping, conflict prevention and human rights.
title: International Organisations, Peace and Conflict
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course examines the use of evidence to support decision-making in the public sector. The emphasis is on the use of evidence to reduce the uncertainty confronting public sector managers, rather than as a means for providing certainty. Students are not expected to become experts in the production of evidence but rather learn to dissect evidence to assess its quality and usefulness. We begin by discussing the role of evidence in decision-making under uncertainty before exploring a framework for assessing data through acquiring, analysing and aggregating various data sources. The emphasis is not on the technical aspects of these sources of evidence but rather equipping students to critically appraise data and evaluate evidence in a bid to work systematically with evidence in effective decision-making.
title: Decision Making Under Uncertainty
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course provides an introductory-level overview of several fields within psychology. It focuses on developmental and social processes and their relationships to individual differences in behaviour, and provides a broad introduction to the areas of developmental, personality, abnormal and social psychology. INCOMPATIBLE: PB11004 AND JAD1004 OR HJ11004 AND 1006APY AND 1015HSV
title: Introduction to Psychology 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course introduces students to the theories and practices of community development within human service contexts. The evolution and current practice of community development are examined as well as the theories and key concepts underpinning practice models, strategies and roles. Issues featuring in community work, such as urban planning, accommodation and health are discussed with reference to particular community groups, for example women and families, indigenous and rural communities and young people.
title: Community Practice Approaches
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course presents knowledge and skills for working with family members who have lived, or are living in abusive relationships. The course covers family/domestic/intimate partner violence, child maltreatment, elder abuse, and young people who perpetrate violence in the home. Discussion of prevention and intervention strategies encourages students to critically reflect on social and personal values. Please Note: This is a restricted course - This course is open to students who have this course listed in their program and they must have completed 160CP of Human Services Courses (or equivalent) to be eligible to enrol in 3023HSV Working with Family Violence.
title: Working with Family Violence
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to undertake a negotiated and contract-based program of largely self-directed activity directly related to the student's professional specialisation within a one-trimester duration. NOTE: Enrolment is subject to approval of the Course Convenor - upon enrolment students should submit a proposal (according to the template provided in assessment item 1 on the Canvas course site) and submit before the end of Week 1. If no proposal is submitted, or the proposal is not approved, enrolment will be cancelled.
title: Minor Project Study
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Dissertation Project constitutes a 40CP research commitment. The course is divided into four 10CP components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The Dissertation will consist of a major research project accompanied by an exegesis of 5000 words (min). The expectation is that the research project will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in a single submission for examination.
title: Dissertation Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Building Construction and Services introduces students to the design of the technical apparatus of medium-scale and high-rise buildings. It focuses on elements and systems of construction and introduces students to the typical building services required. Core elements to the course are the research and evaluation of construction and services components; evaluation and integration of relevant regulatory requirements; the proposition of elegant solutions able to bridge construction systems and technological aspects with the physical and mechanical properties of materials; and, finally, addressing methods of achieving sustainable environmental systems.
title: Building Construction and Services
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In Systems of Adaptation, students develop an architectural proposition of medium scale and a high degree of complexity where pressing design questions regarding adaptation and the needs of human inhabitation are to be addressed. Students are guided through the process of critically exploring functional, ethical, cultural and environmental requirements acquiring specialised knowledge and skills. A holistic view of the built design process is put forth. Students will research architectural exemplars to inform design decisions, encompassing their proposals' conceptual and compositional aspects. Prerequisite 7009ENG - Research by Practice Works 2.
title: Advanced Architecture Studio 2 Systems of Adaptation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Financial statements offer a snapshot of a company's performance at a moment in time. Understanding how financial statements are compiled, structured and presented means you will have the tools to assess a company and make an informed analysis of its quality. In this introductory course you will learn to explain the role and usefulness of financial statement information in corporate governance practice. By the end of the course, you will be able to record and process business transactions through the accounting cycle and prepare a set of general-purpose financial statements. The strategic view you will foster will ensure you can explain the implications of economic events and transactions on a financial statement. You will also be equipped to help build accountability into financial reporting instruments, and you will understand the impact a weak internal control system may have on the financial health of an organisation. With new analysis tools at your disposal and a holistic view of the utility of financial statements and their importance for various stakeholders, you will be equipped to help build accountable, well-governed organisations.
title: Accounting and Governance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course adopts an integrated approach to auditing which will enable students to integrate the most important concepts of auditing with certain practical aspects in a logical manner to assist students in understanding auditing decision making and evidence accumulation. Information technology, including the application of relevant auditing software, and fraud auditing issues are also integrated into the course.
title: Corporate Auditing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Marketing is uniquely positioned to help make our world a better place. Marketing is everywhere and has shaped beliefs and influenced human behaviour for centuries. Just as marketing has served organisations to increase shareholder value and their bottom line, marketing can serve governments, charities and non-profit organisations seeking social, health or environmental change. Marketing requires a broad understanding of consumers and stakeholders ensuring solution co-creation and ultimately the building of volitional choice solutions that engage the people the organisation is seeking to serve. This course will provide you with a step-by-step process, featuring key marketing principles and activities that will teach you how marketing works. This will help you to understand and make marketing decisions in a fast-changing environment where organisations face competitive, social and environmental challenges. Enrolment in this course is restricted to MBA students. However, students enrolled in other graduate degrees who meet the entry requirements of the MBA program may be admitted to the course with the approval of the MBA Director.
title: Marketing for a Better World
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: During this course, students will be provided footage (rushes/dailies) from existing long form drama films, a theatrical feature film and a short film from a film school in Switzerland. Each student will edit the rushes in a coherent and concise manner to maximize the drama and emotion, remaining faithful to the editing style of the film from which the footage is derived. This task will be preceded by discussion concerning the aesthetics of editing for long form drama, and followed by a comparative analysis of the edited footage as it appeared within the finished films.
title: Aesthetics of Editing
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course focuses on the application of prior knowledge to the development of the necessary capacity to assess clients' needs; prepare, present, evaluate and implement tailored, comprehensive financial plans. Students will also be able to recognise the implications of legal and ethical codes that relate to financial planners and to apply them to their own work activities.
title: Financial Planning, Construction and Review
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is supervised higher degree research.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Graduate Research School

description: This course requires execution, analysis and presentation of a research thesis. This involves development of a project, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms.
title: Dissertation Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course offers an applied and policy oriented approach to the study of trade, multinational companies' strategies and global business risks. The focus is on North-East Asia and ASEAN countries.
title: Trade, Strategy and Risk in Asia
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will extend upon second-year physiology by exploring the aetiology of disease and the effects of chronic homeostasis disruption in organ systems. It will describe the fundamental causes of disease (general pathology) and apply that knowledge to understanding common diseases affecting body systems (systemic pathology), including cancers, cardiovascular, skin and gastrointestinal/hepatic disorders.
title: Pathophysiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course focuses on teaching students in the middle and upper primary years of schooling to comprehend and construct a range of spoken, print and digital/online texts with accuracy, fluency and purpose.
title: English Education 2 - Language and literature in the primary school
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: You will consider infectious diseases caused by examples of bacteria, viruses and parasites, understanding how common themes aid understanding of complex host-microbe interactions, prevention and treatment strategies. Topics covered provide a national and international perspective on infectious disease.
title: Infectious Disease
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course continues to develop the issues examined in Business Logistics and provides conceptual models for students to define, measure, manage, control and develop effectively the material and information flows throughout a supply chain. Topics may include: business strategy, policy and processes; information flows; managing information; accounting for flows of goods and services; purchase planning; existing channels; risk and cost positioning; pricing, and costing and strategic involvement.
title: Operations Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The primary emphasis of this course is about Human Resource Management (HRM) in organisations. A central theme throughout this course is the contribution of HRM to the efficiency and productivity of organisations. The course delivery will balance theoretical developments in HRM with practical and strategic considerations of the management of diverse people in the work place and its surrounding environment.
title: Strategic Human Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Globalisation presents unparalleled opportunities for international business, however, the threat of disruption looms large. Nationalism and protectionism are on the rise, and the essential rules of globalisation are re-written. It is, therefore, imperative that all managers are well informed about the dynamics of international business even if their business does not engage in international trade and investment, as global market trends directly impact on almost every business everywhere in the world. This course offers a non-technical, but comprehensive and rigorous, introduction to the diverse field of international business. It also enhances student awareness of corporate social responsibility (CSR) in an international business context and provides students with strategies that assist in the analysis and resolution of ethical problems.
title: International Business Dynamics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: With the increasing recognition of intellectual capital as a key sustainable competitive advantage, the HR discipline has rapidly evolved from being transactional to transformational. In their role as change agents and strategic business partners, HR professionals need to overhaul the tools of their trade by adopting a system, contingency and global perspective. This course develops an understanding of the relationships between business strategy, organisational change strategy and HRM strategy. The course adopts a holistic understanding of HR roles and functions by looking at key concepts, such as resource-based view of the firm, individual and firm performance, sectoral differentiation and corporate ethics as well as strategic influencing factors such as knowledge management, HR metrics and technology. It uses innovative assessment tasks, such as research project, to internalise the implementation aspects of Strategic HRM.
title: HRM and Employment Relations Strategy
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course examines the fundamental principles and processes involved in the management of important land degradation problems in Australia. These problems include wind and water erosion, soil compaction, soil salinity, sodicity and acidity. Catchment hydrology and the principles of integrated catchment management are also examined in this course using 'real world' examples. Development of predictive soil erosion models for their applications for identifying hot-spots in catchments and for the selection of best management practices.
title: Land Degradation and Catchment Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will give the student a detailed understanding of the independent approach to the Music Business. Content includes effective techniques of self-management, live performance, touring, releasing recordings and detailed study of the publicity, promotion, marketing of music products and services.
title: Music Business and Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course examines primary science curriculum materials; the role of environmental education in primary schools; and further develops computer skills in the primary science classroom. The interrelationships between science, technology and society will be explored as will the importance of science in dealing with global impacts. Relevant concepts and manipulative skills are developed to promote the effective teaching of the biological, space and earth sciences in an integrated manner. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of professional experience placements. Incompatibles: 3029EBL , 3029EPS
title: Primary Science Education 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course covers the organic chemistry and selected reactions of the principal organic functional groups - including stereochemistry, reaction mechanisms, and consideration of molecules of biological interest.
title: Organic Chemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Applied Counselling provides an introduction to counselling theories and approaches commonly used in the fields of social work, human services, mental health, nursing and rehabilitation counselling. Students will be provided with an opportunity to acquire counselling knowledge and skills that can assist individuals to find new ways to lead more productive and satisfying lives. This learning opportunity includes a focus on micro skills, Motivational Interviewing, Solution-Focused Brief Therapy and Cognitive Behavioural Therapy. The course will provide students with an understanding of the importance of ethics in in their practice and considers the multicultural context in which practitioners work. The Trimester 1 & 3 Gold Coast offering is restricted to MSW students in the following programs (5621, 5730, 5758 and 5775).
title: Applied Counselling
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This subject continues the exploration and development of suicide intervention knowledge and theory underpinning the skills required to intervene and manage suicidal behaviour. In addition, students will develop an understanding of suicide postvention, including themes and processes of suicide bereavement and support. Students are expected to have pre-existing theoretical and conceptual knowledge about engaging processes for those in suicidal distress, client-centred, psychosocial needs-based suicide risk assessment processes, and an understanding of the influence of worker attitudes to suicide and its prevention. The course 7001CSR immediately precedes 7003CSR and is also a pre-requisite course.
title: Contemporary Suicide Prevention Practice II
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course requires an onsite placement (practicum) in a professional environment. Students are required to attend their placement for at least 90 hours (7.5 hours/1 day per week for 12 weeks) during the trimester. additionally, workshops are held fortnightly to compliment the work integrated learning component of the class and provide an opportunity for continued discussion regarding professional development. Interested students should contact the course convenor with any questions regarding their eligibility.
title: Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Examine the changing conditions of children's lives within the family in Australia and how we can best protect their wellbeing. You'll discover contemporary notions of children, childhood, adolescence, family and parenting and how they can be applied in the education, legal and community services sectors. By developing critical thinking, research, analysis, communication and relationship building skills in this course, you will be able to assess various practices and frameworks typically used in child and family services and understand how they constrain and enable participation in child, youth and family practice. You'll gain an underlying theoretical approach from the literature of children's rights, the sociology of childhood and the ecology of human development. The ways in which institutions, families and community settings respect children's provision, protection and participation rights will also be examined. This knowledge is useful in a range of settings, in education, community services, law, social work, child protection, and law enforcement. You will be capable of challenging existing views of practice and building partnerships to find new, evidence-backed ways to tackle key issues such as mental wellbeing, trauma and family violence.
title: Contemporary Issues for Children and Families
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course has been designed to develop fundamental understanding of underpinning concepts, models, and theory in suicide prevention practice. This will include different approaches to prevention and intervention (including the client-helper relationship, uncovering suicidality and safety approaches for individuals with thoughts of suicide and suicidal behaviour). Different theoretical frameworks will be identified and critically appraised, and students will be encouraged to understand and apply related principles of suicide prevention. Students will be introduced to the concepts of suicide prevention and intervention and will be assisted to develop theoretical and research knowledge associated with suicide prevention policy/planning, and that associated with the practical skills for assessing and responding to suicidal behaviour. Skill and knowledge areas will include a focus on prevention of suicide at the whole-of-population and targeted levels/contexts inclusive of engagement, psychosocial needs-based assessment and support responses. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Contemporary Suicide Prevention Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course will focus on most of the scales and tools currently used to assess and predict suicidal behaviour. Students will have the opportunity to understand the theoretical basis of these instruments and will be encouraged to evaluate their effectiveness and the limits of the utilisation. This course will focus on suicide assessment tools, tests or scales used either alone or in combination with other assessment procedures for the purpose of screening or assessing suicidality. Students will have the opportunity to understand, describe and appraise the theoretical basis, utility and limitations of a sample of assessment/screening tools and scales and will be encouraged to evaluate their effectiveness (including strengths and weaknesses within the context of their application).
title: Suicide Assessment Tools
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Consistent with the scientist-practitioner model of training, this course will help to prepare students in postgraduate professional psychology programs for roles that require them to conduct professionally relevant research; access, interpret, and apply research as "consumers" of professionally relevant research; and conduct best practice evaluation of the effectiveness of their professional practice. The course will combine increasing research methods and statistics literacy, as well as including hands-on experience working with data to extract meaningful messages about human behaviour beyond the skills learned at undergraduate level.
title: Advanced Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Good ethical judgment is a core skill for all public sector leaders, policymakers, and business and civil society actors engaged with public decision-making. But good judgement is more than just a theoretical or philosophical idea, or simply a matter of following established rules and procedures. This course focuses on practical wisdom and prudential decision-making as windows into the meaning of 'good' judgement in public administration, policy-making, leadership and politics. Individual character, experience, ethical risk, value judgments, reputation, organisational culture and political context all bear on what constitutes practical wisdom, or prudence, in any given situation. This course analyses the centrality and difficulty of judgment calls in public service leadership and public life, including tough, 'right' calls that may often seem to go unrewarded. It equips participants with tools for critical, self-aware thinking about the nature and importance of integrity, accountability and professionalism in the art/science of public decision-making.
title: Ethics, Leadership and Judgement
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This is one of two Advanced Topics courses. Each of these courses embraces subject matter close to the current state-of-the-art. Students are strongly advised to consult the academic offering their selected topic well before the course starts. Any topic studied in one Advanced Topics course cannot be studied in the other Advanced Topics course. Students must submit a Registration Form prior to enrolment in this Advanced Topic course.
title: Advanced Topics in Information Technology B
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course provides a practical and theoretical introduction to manufacturing technology with a primary focus on metal processing technologies and their applications in modern manufacturing industry. The course is designed for the 2nd year engineering students that already possess university-level fundamental knowledge about the properties of common engineering materials, the application of forces in engineering systems and have a basic understanding about the tools, machines and processes employed in fabrication of engineered products.
title: Manufacturing Technology
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Rebuilding ecosystems represents one of the major responsibilities of the next generation of environmental engineers, scientists and managers. This semi-intensive course exposes students to professional green infrastructure and water sensitive urban design scenarios that enable them to develop hands-on land rehabilitation monitoring techniques, professional reporting, and engagement with a range of industry perspectives.
title: Green Infrastructure and Landscape Rehabilitation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Pharmacy Practice is the discipline of pharmacy that focuses on the application of scientific and clinical knowledge for patient improved outcomes and the quality use of medicines. The Professional Pharmacy Practice I course involves the development of student's understanding of the professional role of the pharmacist in Australian society as a primary health care provider and medication manager within the multidisciplinary health care team. Students begin to develop skills related to the professional services offered by pharmacists. The course utilises didactic, practical, tutorial, self-directed learning and on-line learning resources for content delivery, with a significant emphasis on the development of life-long learning skills through an evidence-based approach.
title: Professional Pharmacy Practice I
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This sequence of courses involves the identification of a research topic, the development of a research proposal to address that topic, the undertaking of the proposed research project, and its reporting in a dissertation. Where relevant, candidates will also obtain ethical clearance for the proposed project.
title: Dissertation 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course introduces students to the major psychological disorders covered in the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (5th ed.). By completing this course successfully, students will have acquired the following types of information about a range of psychological disorders: - Epidemiology (Incidence, prevalence, lifetime prevalence) - Aetiology (Factors predisposing and precipitating the onset of disorders) - Specific diagnostic criteria employed by the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual (5th Ed.) for major psychological disorders - Assessment and treatment approaches for these disorders - Current debates that exist about specific psychological diagnoses and the general field of psychopathology. Prerequisites must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Abnormal Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: The course aims to develop the conceptual, analytical, and problem-solving skills required to design, conduct, and evaluate survey research in the social sciences, as well as competencies in critical analysis, communication, and data interpretation. The course complements other research methods and statistics courses. Material covered includes practical considerations in conducting survey research, such as selecting a sample, constructing instruments, ensuring validity and reliability, and applying principles of open and transparent research. Students are introduced to a range of quantitative, qualitative, and mixed-methods approaches to survey research, including cross-sectional and longitudinal designs, and develop skills in selecting, analysing, and interpreting appropriate forms of data. Topics include: survey and correlational research designs; sampling and measurement; parametric and non-parametric analysis; regression and categorical data analysis; longitudinal research; qualitative and mixed-methods approaches; and Open Science. Prerequisites must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Survey Design and Analysis
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course equips students with a good knowledge of planning law with particular reference to the law in Queensland. The course involves statutory interpretation, case law analysis and a contextual critique of the principal statutes, including the Planning Act, Qld, 2016, principles and doctrines. It includes a case study of planning and climate change. It is recommended that students have successfully completed at least 80 credit points of courses towards their degree program before enrolling in this course.
title: Urban Planning Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course provides students with an overview of the Australian legal system as it pertains to commerce and management. It also provides detailed knowledge in the area of contract law and a knowledge of the law as it applies to torts, particularly professional negligence and to partnership. Prerequisites: Successful completion of a minimum of 40 credit points of first year courses in the Program. Students undertaking a Law Degree should make note that 2105AFE is incompatible with the LAW courses and they should seek further advice from the Law School if choosing an elective. NOTE: Students who are undertaking a Double Law degree are restricted from enrolling in either 2007GIR/2087GIR Legal Issues for Managers, 2010EHR Legal Issues for Managers or 2105AFE / 2185AFE Intro to Business Law as a GBS elective course.
title: Introduction to Business Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course examines the main taxation revenue raising techniques used by the Australian Commonwealth Government, including income tax, capital gains tax, goods and services tax and fringe benefits tax. The course also concentrates on particular taxation aspects governing different entity types, such as individuals, minors, partnerships, companies and trusts.
title: Income Tax Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: The Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot is an annual competition involving teams representing law schools throughout the world. The Moot is designed as a clinical tool to train law students in the writing of memoranda of argument and the oral presentation of those arguments. The second component of the moot - which is the subject matter of this course - is the oral presentation of argument in an international commercial arbitration moot competition. Students will be selected through a competitive process after completion of 5056LAW (Vis moot written course).
title: Vis International Commercial Arbitration Moot (Oral Competition)
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: The course explores Australian art history from its First Nations foundations and early Colonial art, through to the present day. It includes the study of art of the First Fleet, Colonial art, Aboriginal art of the 19th century, Australian Impressionism, landscape and figure painting, Modernism, art and war, myth, figuration, abstraction, and international developments such as conceptual and performance art. Revolutionary art of the late 20th century is also investigated, including Indigenous art, women's art, environmental art, and art engagements with the Asia Pacific, which continue to grow in fascinating ways into the new millennium. Prerequisites: 1216QCA Introduction to Theory 1 AND 1217QCA Introduction to Theory 2.
title: Australian Art
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course continues comprehensive training in music theory, aural studies and keyboard musicianship for music theatre students.
title: Materials of Music (Musical Theatre) 4
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This internship provides professional training and supervision in teaching for graduates in their major area of study. Core content will include in-depth study of pedagogical concepts and effective practices in studio teaching at a variety of levels. Activities will include lesson observation, scheduled conferencing and teaching under the guidance of the course supervisor. The internship will allow the flexibility to respond to the specific needs of the individual student, whilst exposing the student to specific areas of research interest and practical experience.
title: Pedagogy Internship
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Following Music Industry Internship 1, Music Industry Internship 2 is another Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course that provides students with an opportunity to apply their skills in an industry work placement in host organisations where they will work at least 100 hours during the course. Placements may be intensive or take a longer form such as one day per week over a period of weeks. Students are placed in organisations after an assessment of their interests, skills and post-graduation employment aims. Host organisation staff are responsible for the day-to-day supervision of students with the University providing training and support. In addition to the placements students are required to attend a series of meetings and to complete a final report. Students will be attached to a host organisation through which they will negotiate and develop their project proposal. Internships may be in the areas of broadcast, arts administration, education, production or similar. During placements students will reflect on career planning strategies and further develop their career portfolio. Students will complete their internships under the direction of both a Workplace Supervisor and a University Academic Supervisor. Note: This is a Consent course. Students will not be able to enrol online until the Course Convenor has approved and allocated internship places. Applicants must have completed Music Industry Internship 1.
title: Music Industry Internship (WIL) B
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will challenge both the students' musical and technical skills and help prepare them for the rigorous demands of the profession. This course provides an opportunity for students to select an ensemble or collaborative activity to participate in for credit, depending on their specialisation and interests.
title: Ensemble and Collaborative Activity 4C
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course advances the critical study of basic principles and the practical application of pedagogy as related to the student's major area of study. Core content will include an in-depth study of effective practices in studio teaching, for instruction at fundamental and intermediate levels, but will establish a bridge to the understanding of the teaching skills required for more advanced levels. Recent trends in studio teaching will guide the perspective of the discussion and research.
title: Pedagogy 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The course is an intensive activity in the area of Opera Studies. The options available are for singers (operatic roles) and pianists (Repetiteur activities).
title: Opera Project A
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Honours Research Project constitutes a 40CP honours research commitment within the Honours Programs. Each of the four components of the course combine to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The expectation is that the research project undertaken will be based within the visual and incorporates high levels of visual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item. Honours Research Project is presented for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This Masters course has two key elements. First, students prepare a development proposal and feasibility study (e.g. subdivision; mixed use; tourism), working completely through the process from the perspective of the proponent including site evaluation, design, negotiations and financial appraisal. A strong competency in the incorporation of environmental management principles in the completed proposal and supporting material is expected. Second, students examine and reflect critically upon the implications and lessons for planning theory and practice and for urban development. Restriction: Students must be enrolled in program 5576 M Urban and Environmental Planning OR 3216 Graduate Certificate Urban and Environmental Planning.
title: Advanced Development Processes Studio
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Second of two professional practice courses, this course provides a more detailed understanding of the business and management of an architecture practice, and provides a detailed understanding of the range of activities and professional services undertaken within the office from contractual engagement to the completion of an architecture project. Prerequisite: 7605ENV - Architecture Professional Practice 1.
title: Architecture Professional Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Financial crime encompasses those activities that dishonestly generate wealth, or those activities that attempt to conceal the source of illicit funds. Forensic accountants and anti-financial crime professionals play an important role in preventing and detecting financial crime. This course examines an array of financial crimes including, but not limited to money laundering, corporate fraud, and financial statement fraud and is designed to equip students with skills to detect and report financial crime. Using an investigative mindset, theoretical knowledge is integrated with practical application for compliance and investigation purposes.
title: Forensic Accounting, Fraud and Investigation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: To effectively plan, implement and evaluate advertising and promotional programs requires an understanding of the overall marketing process, consumer behaviour, communications theory and the media of advertising and promotion. This course examines the various factors that must be considered in planning, developing and implementing advertising and promotional campaigns and programs. Attention will also be given to the environment in which advertising and promotion operates and promotional decisions are made.
title: Integrated Marketing Communication
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Communication for ICT Professionals provides students with the real opportunity to work in cross-cultural collaborations to develop the communication skills that will be essential to increasingly globalised and diversified IT-related work environments. The course will further provide academic, linguistic and cultural support for students' understanding of the pedagogy, assessment and expectations in an Australian academic context through a focus on the development of intercultural, academic, and professional literacies.
title: Communication for IT Professionals
academicOrgDescription: Griffith English Language Institute

description: This course, through an analysis of the application of modern banking and finance theory to the process of the management of financial institutions, adopts a risk-management approach to the issues of structure, regulation, policy formulation and implementation in today's financial institutions, with the particular emphasis on banking sector. Coverage is given to the areas of analysis of financial management and performance under current regulatory environment, interest-rate and liquidity risk management, asset-liability management, and strategic planning.
title: Financial Institutions Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is supervised higher degree research.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Graduate Research School

description: This is an ongoing subject for the PhD research. Students should be working on the literature review, data collection and analysis of the PhD thesis.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: The research project is designed to provide training in the developmental and practical elements of research, including epidemiology, public health and health services research, clinical research and biomedical research. Students will be required to design and conduct a research project of special interest to them, and within the competence of the School to direct, and to prepare this work for publication. All students, irrespective of their own research topic, will be required to evaluate published, current and future research across a broad range of topics relevant to their chosen discipline, as the basis of their clinical practice, and with the expectation of research forming the platform for lifelong learning.
title: Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explains how economic tools and techniques are used to assist in managing environmental resouces and water resources. Holistic approaches to environmental economics regard the economy, society and environment as an interlinked system. Sustainable management solutions recognise limits to resource availability, acknowledge the importance of an equitable (fair) distribution of the costs and benefits of resource utilisation, and aim to achieve efficient allocation of scarce resources among competing uses. The course will address all of these dimensions from an economics perspective.
title: Environmental And Water Economics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Cells, Tissues and Regulation examines how a single cell exists, and how when they come together in their trillions, we end up with human beings who can adapt to changing environments. Fundamental knowledge for any future health professionals.
title: Cells, Tissues, and Regulation
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course covers the anatomy and physiology of the cardiovascular, lymph and blood, respiratory, renal, digestive and immune systems. Both the study of the anatomy and the physiology of these systems draw on the experience gained in the lectures, laboratories, and practicums.
title: Anatomy and Physiology Systems II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course examines the interrelationships between physiology and anatomy in select systems: cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, and reproductive. It studies development, structure, and integrated responses to (patho) physiological perturbation. The theory is underpinned by extensive cadaveric material investigation.
title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces students to important concepts in Pharmacology. The major topic areas will provide an in depth understanding of drug targets, pharmacodynamics, pharmacokinetics and pharmacogenomics. Basic concepts in adverse drug reactions, drug interactions, toxicology and complementary medications will be introduced. Pharmacology is a fundamental course that brings together chemistry and biology to understand the basis of drug effect.
title: Pharmacology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course will prepare students to teach the Australian Curriculum: Design and Technologies with a focus on creativity, problem solving and project based learning in a student centred and ICT enhanced learning environment.
title: Technologies Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Molecular Basis of Disease explores the genetic and molecular drivers of human diseases, revealing how mutations and cellular processes lead to conditions such as cancer. Students will engage with cutting-edge molecular biology techniques and bioinformatics tools to explore how genomic data is transforming diagnosis, treatment, and patient care in the era of personalised medicine.
title: Molecular Basis of Disease
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course examines the physical and biochemical characteristics of cellular macromolecules and their roles in mediating essential cellular processes. Prerequisite: 2011MSC Metabolism
title: Macromolecular and Cellular Biochemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: GBS Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Honours Dissertation Part 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

title: Honours Dissertation Part 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Honours Dissertation Part 3
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: High-level communication and leadership skills are essential for professional engineers. This course therefore explores communication theories and investigates the role of information as an engineering resource. It addresses the leadership process, the different approaches to leadership and flexibility of leadership styles. It emphasises both theory and practice, and elaborates on leadership from a communication standpoint.
title: Engineering Communication and Leadership
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course develops your understanding of project management principles and the professional capabilities required to plan and deliver projects in practice. It is informed by contemporary international project management standards and guidance, including PMI's PMBOK Guide, and supports the development of professional competencies identified by Engineers Australia. The course is relevant across engineering, the built environment, science and design disciplines. Working through the project lifecycle, you will apply project management tools to select, initiate, define, plan, execute, monitor and close projects. Topics include project organisation and leadership; project selection; scope definition and work breakdown structures; stakeholder engagement; scheduling and network analysis; cost estimation and budgeting; risk and resource management; procurement and delivery models; performance measurement; and project closeout. Learning is applied through individual and multidisciplinary project work, real-world project examples, industry case studies and hands-on workshop activities that reflect professional project management practice.
title: Project Management Principles
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Sustainable development challenges conventional business concepts: it requires a new way of thinking about management, strategy and economics. In this course, you will learn about sustainability, and you will also learn about key components of a sustainability mindset, including systems thinking. You'll learn about the paradigms through which we see the world, and how language impacts our views. When you complete this course, you will be able to recommend and justify some of the basic tools and strategies that can be applied to organizational sustainability governance, innovative thinking, adaptiveness, resilience and ethics. You will be able to apply your problem solving and critical thinking skills to finding new ways to make efficient use of natural resources in a drive for sustainability. This course will make you think differently about business and marketing and how your organisation can make sustainable practices a core value, which is vital for the future prosperity of our world. When taking this course, all students are expected to begin studies at the first designated session (face to face or online). Enrolment in this course is restricted to MBA, Graduate Certificate in Business Administration, Master of Supply Chain Management, Graduate Diploma of Supply Chain Management, Master of Environment, Master of Climate Change Adaptation and the Graduate Certificate in Aviation Management. However, students enrolled in other graduate degrees may be admitted to the course with the approval of the MBA Director.
title: Sustainability and Systems Thinking
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Purpose is the reason an organisation exists. This course centres on the role of strategy for building a purpose-driven organisation. Strategy has historically been applied as a tool for shareholder returns and has been taught as 'strategy for profit'. Whilst learning important milestones in the historical path of strategic thinking and acting, the course focuses on changing this traditional mindset. It challenges students to think about the purpose and the guiding philosophy when it comes to all levels of strategy across private, public, and not-for-profit industry sectors. The course centres on the responsibility of organisational strategy in all dimensions of value creation and the mutual relationship between organisations with stakeholders, communities, and the environment. The course also focuses on the opportunities - and challenges - of shared value creation and social innovation for strategy across many different industry sectors. Lastly, the course introduces key elements of building and flourishing as a sustainable organisation whose purpose is to create shared value for its community, society, and the planet. Enrolment in this course is restricted to MBA students. However, students enrolled in other graduate degrees who meet the entry requirements of the MBA programme may be admitted to the course with the approval of the MBA Director. Note: Students are encouraged to complete this course in their final trimester of study.
title: Strategy for Purpose
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The course serves as an introductory platform to business processes. It offers both conceptual and practical guidance for achieving competitive advantage by managing business processes. Business process management involves the deliberate and collaborative design, management and goal definition of end-to-end sets of activities that create value for customers. Extensive use of supplementary material from Management, Marketing, Logistics and Human Resources literature is made. Key aspects of business processes at the management, operational and support level are investigated and supporting theories explored looking at the work of Taylor, Harmon, Davenport, Hammer and Porter to name some. By taking a holistic view of the organisation, that transcends vertical, horizontal, external and geographical boundaries, this course provides a road map for guiding organisations to analyse, re-design and improve business processes. Finally, the effects of the application of Information Systems on business processes are investigated in terms of how the processes themselves are captured and become an integral part of the technology.
title: The Management of Business Processes
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This is the capstone course for the employment relations major. This course provides students with an opportunity to build on the theory and practice of industrial relations that has been studied thus far. This course provides continuing students with an excellent springboard into Honours study and graduating students with excellent industry understanding and networks.
title: Employment Strategies in Action
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course focuses on the techniques of managing in different cultures, in particular on the 'people problems' that invariably arise in international business relationships. It examines sources of management conflict due to cultural differences in attitudes, values and behaviours. The course aims to develop intercultural awareness and effectiveness in global business context, and the successful implementation of strategy, structure and systems in cross-cultural and multicultural management. It also examines corporate and personal ethical behaviour in a global economy. There is a strong emphasis on teamwork in factual case study analysis. Please be advised that this course involves high-level critical thinking and theory application. A basic knowledge of management concepts and academic writing is helpful. Students can catch up on both aspects but it requires additional work.
title: The Culturally Competent Workforce
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course introduces students to the value systems underpinning human/community services (eg social justice, rights, consumerism, social change) and the key ethics principles, practices and dilemmas which face workers employed in human service delivery systems. It also allows students to examine professional issues pertinent to work in their chosen field. Pre-requisite: 160CP of HSV Courses or equivalent (requirement waived for students enrolled in the 1548 program)
title: Ethics and Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines theories of literacy instruction and their practical application with a particular focus on the teaching of reading and writing in diverse classrooms using print and multimodal texts. Students will reflect critically on a range of approaches that facilitate evidence-based instruction in contemporary times.
title: English Education 3 - Teaching reading and writing for the twenty-first century
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Chemistry is essential for understanding the natural world, offering insights into biological processes, metabolic pathways, the mechanisms of medicines, disease diagnosis, cooking, exercise, energy, environmental issues, and the development of new materials. This course introduces the chemistry of organic and biological molecules, exploring the properties and reactions of functional groups. You will study the chemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, enzymes, and nucleic acids, laying the groundwork for comprehending the biological oxidation of fats and carbohydrates, which is crucial for cellular energy production. While no formal prerequisite exists for Chemistry of Biological Systems II, students are expected to have foundational chemistry knowledge (e.g., atomic structure, bonding, acids and bases). For those without prior experience, resources such as online modules and practice questions will be provided. Students are encouraged to engage with these to build their knowledge base and succeed in the course.
title: Chemistry of Biological Systems II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Gain an introduction to historical and contemporary global issues in disability, including theoretical, philosophical and ethical perspectives on policy development, service provision, and diversity and inclusion. Working alongside peers from a diversity of fields, including social work, human services, law, psychology, nursing, special education and more, you'll learn about interrelated sectors such as education, employment, health and rehabilitation, housing, ageing and beyond. Through your lessons, you'll be equipped with the knowledge to conduct critical analysis across a range of challenges facing the national disability sector, namely the design and implementation of the NDIS and the impact of inclusive education and fair employment on the lives of people with disabilities. With these skills, you will empower people to innovate in the disability services space, with advocacy guided by ethics and a thorough understanding of theory and practice. By the time you complete your study, you'll be well prepared to work effectively alongside people with disabilities and their families, and advocate for their accessibility and inclusion in the social, political and cultural context.
title: Disability Theories and Approaches
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: 3036HSV (Social Work 1) provides knowledge acquisition related to social work theories and their application across fields of practice. The course addresses key theories and practice methods in contemporary social work and how essential theory is to social work practice, students' developing practice framework and to achieving practice standards. The development of theories in relationship to historical and socio-political contexts are explored as well as their relevance to interpersonal and community work. Students will develop the capacity to critically appraise various approaches used in practice and to understand theory in the context of their first field placement.
title: Social Work 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides an introduction to common qualitative methods used in criminological research, theoretical underpinnings of qualitative research, strengths and weaknesses of different methods, and approaches to qualitative data analysis and reporting.
title: Qualitative Social Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will provide a practical understanding of how risk assessment and management is utilised within forensic mental health. This will include a foundation of the key principles for evaluating risk assessment tools, management processes and professional writing in forensic mental health. This course will provide students with an understanding of how these principles apply in the assessment and management of different offender populations (violent offending, sexual offending, stalking and juvenile). Students will apply their learning to a number of client case studies across these population groups and develop practical skills in professional risk assessment report writing.
title: Advanced Risk Assessment and Management in Forensic Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Take a close look at the microbial basis for infection, focusing on the core scientific concepts of microbiology, pathophysiology, immunology and pharmacology as they relate to infectious disease. You will learn how these factors affect disease transmission, diagnosis and management, essential knowledge for planning for disease control by health leaders. Looking at the structure and characteristics of the main groups of microorganisms, you will also explore the natural history of infection, the body's immune defences and their roles in infection prevention, important knowledge for patient safety. You'll see how systematic hygiene practices are essential for patient care and health safety. Finally, you will apply principles of epidemiology in contemporary infection prevention and control and the management of infectious diseases for individual and public health practice.
title: Sciences of Infection and Disease
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course introduces students to both distal and proximal factors which may contribute to suicidal risk. The social, demographic, cultural correlates and biological mediators that impact upon suicidal risk are also examined. Students will develop insight into current suicide research and the methodological problems associated with it.
title: Advances in Suicide Research 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course provides the 'capstone' for the combined degree, explicitly drawing together the psychology and criminology and criminal justice strands. The course examines the criminal justice system and related elements in terms of psychological theories and perspectives, and examines the role which individuals with training in psychological science can play within the system. Topics covered include police occupational stress, the accuracy of eyewitness testimony, psychologists as expert witnesses, jury dynamics and decision-making, sentencing adjudication, and the prediction of dangerousness.
title: Psychology and the Justice System
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: A systemic approach to infection prevention and control is crucial for preventing the spread of infectious disease. This course examines how to design, develop and implement clinical governance frameworks for infection prevention and control programs. The course explores the role of the infection control professional, systems of clinical governance, infection prevention and control framework and management plans, and performance indicators for infection prevention and control. You will be ready for contemporary, specialty practice as an infection prevention and control professional.
title: Contemporary Infection Prevention Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course focuses on the relationship between crime, business, and politics in East and Southeast Asia. Specifically, it examines organised crime, corruption of governmental institutions, the globalisation of criminal networks, the economic, political, and social impact of crime, and the response of states and international organisations to crime.
