Though paying the most attention to the present-day situation, the course also looks at the history of such activities as drug trafficking and piracy. A central theme is the issue of how, when, and with what consequences various activities have been regarded as criminal.
title: Crime, Business and Politics in Asia
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course focuses on the disciplines of the learning of physical skills, exercise physiology, processes and effects of training and exercise and the sociology of sport, physical activity and exercise. It seeks to relate relevant theory and practices to the teaching and learning of specific sports and/or physical activities within school-based settings. The broad aim of the course is to provide an in-depth 'foundational' base in the sports sciences for students who will be teaching HPE in Queensland high schools from Year 7 to 10 as well as Senior Physical Education Board Courses.
title: Foundations of Physical Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Professional Practice in Special Education (PPSE) is the specialised professional experience course within the Special "Needs" Award Major of the Bachelor of Education program. Values, knowledge, and skills acquired during the course will provide a foundation for the professional experiences in special education settings. This course draws on material covered in previous professional experiences courses, curriculum and assessment courses, and other education courses in the program.
title: Professional Practice in Special Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This is the first of two complementary courses in the Bachelor of Education - Secondary and Master of Secondary Teaching concerned with the curriculum foundations and implementation of Geography in secondary schooling. This course focuses on preparing beginning teachers to be effective in planning, implementing, and assessing geography in the junior secondary years of schooling.
title: Geography Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course focuses on interpersonal skills and strategies at the individual, group and systems levels for special needs/learning support teachers to develop collaborative working partnerships to maximise educational opportunities, to meet the learning needs of all students in special and multi-ability classrooms. Teachers require a range of communication and interpersonal skills, including consultation, collaboration and negotiation skills to be effective in these areas. The course also introduces co-teaching which is increasingly being considered as an optional teaching arrangement as schools shift to the whole-school approach and collaboration increases between regular and special needs/learning support teachers. This course has two elements: Knowing you and then using your 'you' knowledge to effectively work with others (colleagues, parents and carers, school leaders, support staff and others) to benefit all students. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of professional experience placements.
title: Collaboration and Co-teaching
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course addresses the theoretical and practical aspects of individualised, intensive interventions for students with special needs and problem behaviour. It enables preservice teachers to become not only familiar with current research in positive behavioural support but also to develop a working knowledge of behavioural assessment and intervention. Assessment is case-study based and involves (a) the collaborative conduct of a functional behavioural assessment for a student, and (b) the subsequent collaborative design of a behavioural intervention.
title: Positive Behavioural Support
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Environmental law has become increasingly embedded across many areas of legal and professional practice that prioritise sustainability and social responsibility. This course aims to apply your critical analysis, reflection and problem-solving skills to real world environmental challenges, preparing you to navigate and influence Australia's complex landscape of environmental law and policy.
title: Environmental Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course considers the law of succession which concerns the devolution of rights and obligations upon death. In particular it deals with the transmission of property interests through testamentary processes (wills) and when there is intestacy.
title: Succession
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course provides a solid introduction to applied statistics for students in criminal justice and related fields. The course covers both descriptive and inferential statistics, and students learn to use Microsoft Excel for statistical analysis.
title: Quantitative Methods for Social Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This capstone course acts as the arch at the apex of the Politics and Public Policy major within the Bachelor of Government and International Relations, and associated degrees in which this major is offered. It draws together the knowledge students have gained from previous courses and also looks forward to the workplace. It will focus on both by considering theoretical approaches to problems and their practical solutions. Students will be expected to relate various issues to one another and to understand the implications of different policy approaches. The course will build on and further develop skills which will be useful in the workplace.
title: Solving Policy Problems
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: In this course, students will engage with the principles of water resources engineering design while developing a broad skill set that applies to various engineering disciplines. Through hands-on problem-solving, they will address real-world issues such as flood management and the design of hydraulic structures. The course provides a solid foundation in modern engineering techniques, tools, and methodologies, enabling students to analyze and design systems in line with relevant industry standards. While the focus is on water resources engineering, the design skills and problem-solving approaches developed in this course are transferable to other areas of civil and environmental engineering. By the end of the course, students will be equipped to apply their knowledge in professional environments, making informed, sustainable engineering design decisions.
title: Civil Engineering Design Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course emphasises the academic and professional aspects of modern engineering, science, and technology practice within an industrial environment. It incorporates a major capstone project designed to demonstrate the application of engineering, science, and technology principles, from research and problem definition through to the specification and/or development of a solution that delivers value to the industry partner. Students are required to plan, execute, and report on a research project with a degree of independence, while working closely with an academic supervisor who provides guidance, support, and direction throughout the design and execution of the research. Students intending to undertake this course must register for the Industry Affiliates Program (IAP) at least 12 weeks prior to the commencement of the trimester via the Griffith Sciences WIL SharePoint site (https://griffitheduau.sharepoint.com/sites/wilgs). Students who do not register by this deadline may not be permitted to enrol in the course. A minimum of 80 CP within the degree program must be completed prior to enrolment. This course is offered throughout the year. However, in Trimester 3, it is available only to students who have secured an approved industry placement.
title: Industry Affiliates Program - Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Programming is a foundational skill for all computing disciplines. This course develops skills and concepts that are essential to good programming practice and problem solving. It covers fundamental programming concepts, object-oriented programming, basic data structures, and algorithmic processes.
title: Programming Principles
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course examines the scientific evidence and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on the natural environment and society. The course will adopt an Earth System Science perspective to elucidate the role of environmental systems in determining global climate and consider how their simulation can contribute to developing policy within the climate change debate. The course will also explore the challenge of incorporating complex climate knowledge into decision making, both with respect to mitigation and adaptation.
title: Environmental Systems and Climate Change
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to hazardous waste treatment and disposal. The contents of the course include introduction to hazardous waste, hazardous waste generation and characteristics, transportation and storage of hazardous waste, physical, chemical and biological treatment, thermal treatment and energy recovery, stabilisation and solidification and land disposal of hazardous waste.
title: Hazardous Waste Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides the fundamental knowledge of fluid mechanics and hydraulics including fluid properties, fluid statics, conservation of mass, energy equation, flow in conduits, pumps and turbines, flow around objects, open channel flow and compressible flow. Assumed knowledge: 1501ENG Engineering Mechanics. Prerequisites: 1010ENG Engineering Mathematics 1 Incompatible: 7413ENG Fluid Mechanics. Students in the Electrical and Renewable Engineering major only are not required to have completed 1501ENG Engineering Mechanics prior to enrolling in 2002ENG Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics.
title: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: 8001HLS consists of four 10 credit point courses (8001HLS_P1 to P4) and these courses make up the research component of the Graduate Diploma of Health Research program (4161). The final grade is allocated on completion of part 4. The dissertation requires students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This involves the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, and data analysis. At the completion of the four parts, students will submit a report of their research project (thesis) for examination. Students are advised to consult their School Advisor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final part (8001HLS_P4), they are expected to submit their dissertation by the due date specified in the course profile.
title: Dissertation Part 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In this course you will examine the principle of responsible government and its implications for policy analysis, and the values and ethics of the policy sciences in a democracy. Using case studies, you will examine the actors and interests at play in policy decisions, and how they are managed with contemporary governance practices. You will learn about models of how public policy is made, and describe the role of the professional policy analyst in Australian government, drawing on insights from the policy studies literature, as well as from practitioner perspectives. The political ideas, principles and institutions that underpin Australian governance frameworks are also explored in this course. You will be able to identify the forces that have challenged these institutions and traditions and evaluate their contemporary role in shaping policy-making. You will demonstrate the capacity to think critically about issues and dilemmas in policy and analysis and effectively research, evaluate and communicate their arguments. The foundation in political governance this course provides will ensure you have a solid understanding of the policy making process and how it is influenced and governed.
title: Machinery and Principles of Policymaking
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course examines fundamental questions about the public policy process through a range of key concepts and theories. It explores how policy is shaped by institutions, political actors, organised interests, advocacy and competing sources of influence, and evaluates these dynamics through the analysis of selected policy areas. The course is offered at Nathan in odd years and at Gold Coast in even years.
title: Power and Policy Making
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course provides a graduate introduction to issues and problems in Australia's foreign policy and foreign relations. The course covers: the history of Australian foreign policy; the shift to Asia; the foreign policies of recent Australian governments; Australia's relationships with the United States and the great powers of Asia; Australia's defence policy and new security issues; Australia's foreign economic relations; foreign aid and the environment; and the concept of national interest.
title: Foreign Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course provides a broad introduction to Australian politics and government. While Australia shares much in common with other democracies around the world, it has its own unique context and set of political institutions. This course will explore how Australian politics is distinctive and situate Australia in comparison to other democratic countries. A wide range of themes are investigated, including political leadership, women's representation, voter behaviour, and citizen disaffection with politicians. This course aims to equip students to understand Australian politics as a foundation for engaged citizenship and to support careers in a wide range of sectors, including the public service and the non-profit sector.
title: Australian Politics and Government
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This is a third year general elective course open to students across the University. The Parliamentary Internship provides exposure to decision-making in the Queensland Parliament where students will be engaged on specific research topics under the guidance of a University supervisor and a Member of Parliament or other suitable official. This course has a limited number of places and students are required to contact the Course Convenor or the School of Government and International Relations, at Griffith University, as enrolment is by permission only. This is not a timetabled course.
title: Parliamentary Internship
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course provides the opportunity to develop and enhance your knowledge of group dynamics and facilitation and to work toward mastery of the skills required to apply that knowledge in practical situations. To assist with your skills development, this course adopts an active learning approach. Learning actively will provide you with the opportunity to develop both a theoretical understanding of group dynamics and a practical ability to work with groups. Note: Trimester 3 offering is restricted to students in external/distance Human Services and Social Work programs only.
title: Group Facilitation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This second field placement course provides the students undertaking the Master of Social Work with the opportunity to again apply their university based learning to practice situations. Students are required to complete 500 hours (approximately 4 days per week for 17 weeks) of practice based learning and engage in professional supervision with a social work qualified field supervisor. The program builds on the skills and understanding achieved during Field Placement 1. It is the final requirement of the degree program and focuses on facilitating students' development of the skills, knowledge, attitudes and analyses required to enter the field as a social work practitioner. Learning tasks assessed on a pass/fail basis. NOTE : This course is a designated course for the purposes of exclusion - a student who fails 7044HSV may be excluded from the Master of Social Work program.
title: Social Work Field Placement 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This initial field placement course provides the students undertaking the Master of Social Work degree with the opportunity to apply their university based learning to practice situations. Students are required to complete 500 hours (approximately 4 days per week for 17 weeks) on-site practice with a social work qualified field supervisor in a suitable human service organisation. The course will focus on facilitating students' development of the skills, knowledge, attitudes and analyses necessary to enter the field as a social work practitioner. NOTE : This course is a designated course for the purposes of exclusion - a student who fails 7034HSV may be excluded from the Master of Social Work program.
title: Social Work Field Placement 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Engaging social justice and human rights perspectives, you will take a critical look at historical, political, institutional and social forces that have shaped welfare and health policies and practices for Australia's First Peoples. You'll analyse the implications of colonisation since British invasion and develop a clearer understanding of the identities, histories, experiences and needs of First peoples, whether they reside in urban, rural or remote areas. By becoming more aware of the attitudes, values, opinions and beliefs that underpin mainstream representation of contemporary First Peoples in Australia, you'll be better placed to identify the extensive and complex manifestation of systemic racisms, white supremacy, and privilege and deconstruct them. These things manifest in the treatment of First Peoples in the Australian criminal justice system, its health policies and in juvenile justice, among other areas. You'll have the ability to critically analyse and articulate the societal constructs, policies and practices that impact First peoples' social justice and human rights outcomes in Australia and apply an anti-colonial practice framework for working alongside the diverse peoples of First Nations of Australia.
title: First Peoples and Social Justice (Advanced)
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the two most common methods of inquiry in research - qualitative and quantitative. Topics include theoretical paradigms (emic and etic), research questions, literature reviews, research design, sampling, data collection and analysis, reliability and validity, and ethics in research. At the completion of this course, students will be able to understand the research process, critically analyse the methodology of published research, and design their own research proposal with a methodology that is appropriate for their hypothesis/research question. Incompatible: 3012CCJ Criminology and Criminal Justice Research Methods.
title: Human Services Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Only students who have been accepted into the Psychology Honours year of their degree are permitted to enrol in 6000PSY_Y1. Students complete an independent investigation of a research question of some significance in psychology. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course introduces students to the law relating to financial products, financial markets, lending and other finance related activities of Australian banks and other financial institutions in the private sector. Topics covered include the Australian financial system; the relationship between lender and borrower; the statutory regulation of credit; loans to differing forms of business organisations; consumer credit - including Consumer Credit Code, EFT Code of Conduct, payment system and mechanisms, Managed Investment Schemes: real and personal property and the law and enforcement of securities and consequent remedies through the courts/tribunals as well as alternative dispute resolution methods.
title: Law of Finance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course explores the relationship between actor, director, text and the camera, through a series of workshop exercises in which students develop visual storytelling, pre-visualisation and performance adjustment skills.
title: Directing for the Screen
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Family law will deal with the following topics: the nature of the modern family; perspectives on family law; the constitutional and jurisdictional context of family law in Australia; marriage and divorce; mediation; domestic and family violence; child protection; impact of separation on family members; living arrangements for children after family breakdown; property adjustment; spousal maintenance and child support and some of the processes and procedures of the family law system. It situates family law in the context of social issues and the complexities of families who turn to the formal family law system. Note: This course will be withdrawn from offer if there are fewer than 15 students enrolled by the end of week one.
title: Family Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course examines the development of Australia's migration law and policy, from pre-Federation with infamous race-based legislation to the present day system of apparently objective visa criteria. Students will leave the course with a solid foundation in current migration law and practice, with tangible legal research skills in using LEGENDcom, the Department of Home Affairs electronic database for accessing current law and policy. Topics covered in the course include the current visa framework, advising on protection and other visa options, advocating in visa cancellation, merits and judicial review cases. These broad areas of practice set students up to use their migration law knowledge and skills in future migration law practice and also in specialist areas such as refugee and humanitarian law, crimmigration, administrative law and family law.
title: Immigration and Refugee Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course will focus on the awareness of the physical needs of the performer/teacher and reveal how physical coordination impacts on the musical performance. Specific experiential activities will be employed to engage embodied learning and increase the range of effective movement options for each performer. This will be done in weekly 2 hr Feldenkrais Method classes. The application of the methodology will focus on the individual's performance skills and attentional focus, aiming for efficiency, ease and independence through the exercise of self-evaluation. The course also aims to develop the student's ability to observe another person's self-use then learn how to assist their improved function in relation to performance.
title: Awareness through Movement
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course presents an opportunity for students to undertake a self-directed research project on a topic of their choosing. Students will develop a research proposal and conduct this inquiry under the general supervision of the lecturer, as supported through collaboration and peer feedback. Research projects can be artistic, theoretical, empirical or methodological and can address various historical, aesthetic, educational, critical, social or cultural issues related to the history, literature, and practice of music. Collaborative discussions and workshops will further develop skills in research practice and communication that are applicable to academia and beyond. Attendance at all seminars will enable participation in practical and/or collaborative activities during classes and greatly enhance the learning experience.
title: Music Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides comprehensive training in music theory, aural studies and keyboard musicianship assisting music theatre students to develop accurate listening and inner hearing skills within a practical setting. Lectures explore repertoire from music theatre and the basic principles of pitch organisation, rhythmic structure and musical form with the aim of improving the student's comprehension of melodic and harmonic structure in music through the study of pitch relationships. The course also provides the opportunity to develop appropriate aural and keyboard musicianship skills through engaging in activities such as sight-singing, rhythm performance, and aural analysis of melody, rhythm, harmony and form. This course sequence is exclusively for students enrolled in the Music Theatre program.
title: Materials of Music (Musical Theatre) 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will challenge both the students' musical and technical skills and help prepare them for the rigorous demands of the profession. This course provides an opportunity for students to extend themselves in the ensembles space by selecting extended ensemble/collaborative activities to participate in beyond 4531QCM (Ensembles and Collaborative Activity 4A) depending on their specialisation and interests.
title: Ensemble and Collaborative Activity 4B
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to design and implement a largely self-directed project directly related to their creative and/or professional specialisation, within a one-trimester duration. NOTE: Approval of your proposal is essential for your continued enrolment in this course. Please submit your proposal before the end of week 2, through the assignment section. A template and exemplar are available in the Phase 1 module. Failure to submit a proposal and have it approved will result in the cancellation of your enrolment.
title: Postgraduate Project Studies
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The Honours Research Project courses constitute a 40CP honours research commitment within the Honours program. Each of its four courses combine to introduce students to the rigours of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual/screen production practice. The expectation is that the artefacts and production practices arising from this research project will operate synergistically with the theoretical work to result in a project that is cohesive in all respects and which demonstrates high levels of visual and textual literacy. Assessment of the four courses will culminate in one assessment item at the end of the program, which is to be presented with the Exegesis (completed in 6012GFS) for assessment in a professional context at the completion of all four courses.
title: Honours Research Project
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Marketing for behaviour change offers a framework for designing effective behavioural change programs which can be used to change social, environmental and financial behaviours. This course brings together a range of skills required by government, not-for-profits and behaviour change consultants to effect positive behaviour change programs to stem a wide range of societal issues.
title: Marketing for Behaviour Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course demonstrates the importance of the service sector, how marketing theory differs for this sector, the unique challenges faced by service businesses and the application of service theory in practice. You will develop and expand your management skills in the application of marketing strategies to improve service quality, increase and maintain customer satisfaction, generate customer loyalty and create and manage a healthy service-oriented environment.
title: Service Experience
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: As the variety and complexity of problems facing marketers has increased in recent years, so has the need for information. This course enables participants to identify the marketing information needs of an organisation and to develop appropriate research to provide that information. It introduces concepts in sampling, measurement, data collection, and data analysis.
title: Market Research
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The internship will be undertaken with School approved commercial or government entities whose primary business is the production or dissemination of film, television, interactive media and related programming. Host companies maybe located in Australia or abroad in target markets facilitated by exchange agreements with off-shore partner Universities. The minimum period of an internship shall be 2 weeks with a maximum period of 8 weeks per 10CP.
title: Professional Internship Project
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course is a great entry point to learn theoretical and practical aspect of Financial Systems. The course covers (a) types and classes of financial markets include evaluation of the financial markets and instruments, (b) operations of the major financial institutions, and (c) evolution in the financial systems in reference to Australia.
title: Financial Markets
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Finance has a central role in any organisation, as it helps managers make decisions on how to fund the business, where to responsibly invest and how to allocate financial resources for responsible value creation. This course provides students with a broad understanding of important finance concepts and introduces new frameworks that allow business leaders to make informed and responsible decisions for a sustainable future of their organisations. The course covers a variety of modules that focus on how to make informed and responsible decisions in relation to corporate governance, valuation, risk, capital budgeting, and dividends amongst others. The course will empower students with a novel toolkit that allows sound financial decision making and an understanding of how 'good' finance goes beyond shareholders' value creation. Students will be able to use finance to make beneficial decisions that go well beyond profit. All students are expected to begin studies at the first designated lecture for each course of their program. Students who cannot attend must gain written approval from the MBA Director to continue in that trimester. Enrolment in this course is restricted to MBA students only. Students enrolled in other graduate degrees who meet the entry requirements of the MBA program may be admitted with the approval by the MBA Director.
title: Finance for Responsible Value Creation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Research. This is an ongoing subject for the PhD research. Students should be working on the literature review, data collection and analysis of the PhD thesis.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This is an ongoing subject for the PhD research. Students should be working on the literature review, data collection and analysis of the PhD thesis.
title: Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: In an increasingly interconnected world, an understanding of Australian politics, economics and the business environment requires an appreciation of what is happening in the world outside Australia. The dual effects of globalisation and regionalisation profoundly affect Australia. This course offers an introduction to the discipline and subject matter of global political economy, including theoretical political economy frameworks; the historical and contemporary global political economy; the rise of Asia and the regional order; global trade, finance and investment; the role of the state; and the impact of the global and regional political economies on Australia.
title: Global Political Economy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course examines foundation marketing concepts and processes applied in business and market development activities. Section and use of secondary data analysis to gain insights for your marketing initiatives and justify the categorisation of products and services within identified target markets. We'll guide you as you expand your creative and investigative skills to marketing strategy, including the marketing mix, for application in real-world business practices. Upon completion, you will be able to demonstrate high awareness of the nature of the discipline with a clear professional self-concept of marketing.
title: Marketing Foundations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Histology is the study of tissue biology: the study of the structure and function of each tissue type and how those tissues form the organs and systems of the body. This course will cover the defining features of epithelial, connective, muscle and nerve tissues. Students will understand the processes of preparing paraffin embedded tissues for viewing by light microscopy and understand the physical basis for the appearance of these tissues.
title: Histology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Microbiology focuses on theoretical and applied knowledge of HEALTH and MEDICAL MICROBIOLOGY including types of microorganisms, growth and culture, control of microbial growth and antibiotics, microbial taxonomy, microorganisms involved in disease, aspects of clinical microbiology and techniques for isolating and identifying microorganisms.
title: Microbiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course provides a foundation for understanding the cognitive and biological bases of human behaviour, including the role of the brain and neural processes in behaviour, perception (how the senses allow you to see, hear, taste, touch and smell the world around you), conditioning and learning (how humans and other animals learn about their environment), cognition and memory (how people think, solve problems and remember). Drawing on various research traditions in experimental psychology, this course demonstrates how cognitive and biological psychology contributes to our knowledge of human well-being and performance. Students apply this knowledge through a series of practical in-class exercises. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: 1004HLS_Y2 and 1015HSV Human Behaviour
title: Introduction to Psychology 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: The course provides the opportunity to develop professional HR skills through the examination and application of learning theories and HRD frameworks to individual, group and organisational development needs and challenges. Content includes the development of skills in needs assessment, design, delivery and evaluation of training and development, reflection and analysis, the HRD professional role, application to organisational cases and current issues. This course emphasises both theoretical and practical aspects in the understanding and integration of learning theories, models and processes of HRD, sustainable organisational development, and professional L&D/HRD practices. The course is designed to encourage students to examine 'real world' issues through critical thinking and the application of their learning to organisational challenges. This course encourages the learner to evaluate their own L&D/ HRD competencies and apply them to their future career development plans.
title: Human Resource Development
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Management Employee Relations aims to provide you with an understanding of industrial relations. It includes the roles of trade unions, the industrial tribunal system and employer associations. It places these in an historical and theoretical context that explains their present structures, activities and limitations. It will also address the contemporary approaches to workplace relations between managers, employees and unions. You will become acquainted with critical approaches to the practice of industrial relations.
title: Management Employee Relations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course prepares students to conceptualize qualitative research in terms of research questions and design, methodology, data collection and qualitative analysis. In doing so, this course focuses on the issues, problems, and strategies related to 'small-N' qualitative research, for the most part setting aside the techniques of large-N statistical analysis, which are covered in 7011GBS. This course is divided into five main parts focusing on the following topics: (1) the goals, origins and contributions of qualitative research in the social sciences; (2) elements of research design; (3) sources of data and their collection; (4) analysis and interpretation of qualitative data, including theory generation; (5) representation and dissemination of qualitative research. Students will read and discuss scholarly texts that either demonstrate or critique core aspects of qualitative research and actively engage in practice based and peer learning through activities and group discussion. Prior to enrolling in this course it is expected that you have nominated a supervisor for your dissertation and have discussed a topic of research with that Supervisor.
title: Qualitative Methods
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: Prosthetic Technology 4 focuses on fixed prosthodontics and builds on the theoretical knowledge developed in Prosthetic Technology 1, 2 and 3. Students advance their understanding of the biomaterials, design principles and manufacturing concepts that underpin the construction of fixed dental prostheses. The theoretical concepts explored in this course are directly applied in Laboratory Practicum 4, enabling students to integrate conceptual knowledge with practical laboratory procedures. Students also participate in Communication Skills for Oral Health 2, a structured module that further develops the interpersonal and professional communication skills required in contemporary oral health practice.
title: Prosthetic Technology 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores the basic principles and the practical application of pedagogy as related to the student's major area of study. Effective teaching practices for the instruction of the beginner to intermediate level in the studio environment will be central to the program. Recent trends in studio teaching will influence the perspective of the discussion and research.
title: Pedagogy 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The impetus for 4001HSV Developing Practice and Leadership is the need for human services practitioners to have the knowledge and skills, consistent with social justice values, to lead individuals, teams, and organisations. This course explores leadership in the human services, discusses the relationship between leaders and followers, looks in detail at leadership in organisations and the types of activities in which leaders engage, and examines the role of leadership in facilitating change. Along the way, students are encouraged to embark upon their own leadership journey by exploring their leadership framework, increasing self-awareness of leadership capacities, and implementing plans for development. The aim of the course is to develop leadership capacities for working at individual, relational, and organisational levels of leadership in social work.
title: Developing Practice and Leadership
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Human services and welfare workers are engaged in a complex array of changing practice contexts, characterised by institutional arrangements, histories, politics, accountabilities, and technologies. Delivering effective and thoughtful service delivery requires practitioners to understand these internal and external factors. With this knowledge, human service workers can gain the confidence and skills to engage in constructive debate around the direction of service delivery and their role within it while balancing the impact of change and continuity for self, client and organisation. These are essential leadership skills for contemporary human services workers, and they're supported by values of integrity, ethics, respect and empathy. By taking this course, you will be exposed to a range of strategies and analyses to assist you to consider your own approach to practice, so you can contribute to human service policy and practice in organisations. Complemented by advanced relationship building and engagement skills, your client advocacy will become more powerful. You will be capable of evaluating the current practice approaches within the human services sector and how they affect your own professionalism, guided by key principles, values and ethics that apply across the human services industry.
title: Human Service : Knowledge and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will provide you with an overview of the professional, legislative and regulatory frameworks that apply, and provide knowledge and skills to order and interpret clinical investigations, create medication plans, and write prescriptions relevant to midwifery practice. You will gain a sound understanding of pharmacology and the rational use of medicines and investigations, as they apply to pregnancy, birth, postpartum and neonatal care. NB: Students must hold a current and unrestricted license as a registered midwife with the Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia. You can apply for this course as a single course of study by applying here https://www.griffith.edu.au/apply/admission-pathways/single-course-of-study.
title: Prescribing for Midwives
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course examines the areas in which the criminal justice system and psychological theories of behaviour interact. Topics include the reliability of eyewitness testimony, truthfulness and credibility of witnesses, questioning victims of sexual assault, the social dynamics of juries and the role of expert testimony.
title: Law and Behaviour
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is designed to consolidate the knowledge gained in the previous courses by analysing a live crime problem. Students working as a group will generate hypotheses, apply various analytic techniques to test these, prepare a report to be presented to the relevant command team.
title: Intelligence Led Policing
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is designed to support student learning, personal development and professional practice for students completing a Post Graduate Human Services or Mental Health program as they apply their university-based learning to practice situations. Students are required to complete 200 hours (minimum) on-site supervised practice in a suitable human service/mental health agency. The course will focus on facilitating student's development of the skills, knowledge, attitudes and critical analysis necessary to enter the field as Human Service/ Mental Health practitioners. 7048HSV is a capstone course with preparatory pre placement requirements that must be completed in Year 1, with the course itself undertaken in the final trimester of the Master's program.
title: Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Sport performance depends not just on athletes' physical and technical skills, but also on their mental or psychological skills. This course will help students as teachers, coaches, psychologists, or sport technologists to develop suitable psychological skills training programs, consider the psychological factors affecting children's performance and participation in sport, and work with athletes who have special needs.
title: Sport Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The aim of the dissertation courses (7009CSR_P1 to P4) is for the student to carry out a research project under supervision of a member of staff with research experience. The student will need to prepare a dissertation which is a coherent exposition of a research study that follows an ordered sequence in which the research objectives, relationship to other scholarly work, methodology and strategies employed, and the results obtained are identified, analysed and evaluated. Through the dissertation a student establishes her/his capacity for independent research and knowledge of the topic and the discipline. Specifically, the student needs to develop an argument which demonstrates an ability to initialise and frame a question, respond to and represent a variety of viewpoints, provide balanced evidence for positions adopted, develop appropriate methodologies and methods, collect data in an ethical manner, and interpret and generalise data in a defensible way. Students will develop dissertations in suicide research through a guided approach encompassing academic liaison. Students will be given individual feedback and supervision on the development of a hypothesis, techniques for research design and appropriate statistical methods. Assessment will require a written report of the research.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course introduces students to major theories of adult development and ageing including the theories of Baltes, Erikson, Levinson, and Schaie. Areas covered include cognitive development, personality and moral development, relationships and sexuality, family life and parenting, career development, biological processes and ageing, leisure and retirement, and death and dying. Prerequisites must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Adult Development and Ageing
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course takes concepts covered in previous classes across creative music technology and popular music and connects them through targeted multi-media briefs. Students work in cross-disciplinary teams to design, research, resource and deliver a major project incorporating original music, custom sound design and support, and original vision capture. Projects are formatively completed via regular deadlines with students utilising current technologies to communicate and collaborate with each other throughout the entire process.
title: Music, Sound and Vision
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course introduces students to the practice of second language teaching. It does this through a combination of lectures/workshops together with classroom observation of practising second language teachers. To facilitate their observation, students will be introduced to techniques of classroom-based research. They will use these techniques to focus on major issues which arise in the second language classroom. Students will use their developing understanding of second language teaching to plan and teach classes for second language learners.
title: Second Language Teaching in Practice (Internship)
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This clinically-based, research informed course expands on the basic principles and concepts relating to the specialty discipline and introduces clinical procedures and management of patients, research-informed case presentations and journal reviews. Part 1 of year long course. 8010DOH_Y1 must be completed before proceeding to 8010DOH_Y2
title: Knowledge and clinical practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course introduces the research environment and a candidate will utilise discipline specific literature to identify a research question and develop a research protocol.
title: Research Proposal
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides the critical care nurse with the foundational knowledge and skills required to manage common critical care presentations using the best research evidence.
title: Foundations of Critical Care Nursing Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: In this course students will develop the knowledge and skills necessary to provide comprehensive cardiac care within the critical care environment. Students will use an evidence-based approach to apply advanced cardiac assessment and cardiac care skills to manage complex cardiac disorders and conditions, including the assessment and management of patients who have had cardiac surgery.
title: Managing Clients with Complex Cardiac Presentations
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Health professionals supporting women experiencing perinatal mental health challenges will complete this course to better understand how evidence-based psychosocial interventions are applied to improve the emotional health of childbearing women, and how personal beliefs and attitudes impact upon their own ability to work with women. Furthermore, students will develop a greater knowledge of how to engage with First Nations women and those from culturally and linguistically diverse backgrounds experiencing perinatal mental health challenges.
title: Perinatal Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course presents a comprehensive introduction to human nutrition; describing the requirements for macronutrients (carbohydrate, fat, protein, alcohol) and micronutrients (iron, calcium, zinc, thiamine, Vitamin C, folate), their food sources, digestion, absorption, storage, and metabolism. Students will explore energy balance and fad diets, and implications for human health. Students will be introduced to the Australian Guide to Healthy Eating, Nutrient Reference Values and dietary collection methods. Students will gain skills in analysis and interpretation of dietary records, and be able to develop recommendations to meet nutrient requirements. At the completion of this course, students will have knowledge of basic human nutrition, nutrient requirements, nutrient content of foods and the broad role of nutrition in maintaining optimal health.
title: Nutrition
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides an introduction to contemporary social issues and phenomena that affect language learners. Topics include language contact and change, language variation, gender, identity and culture, migration and citizenship, and the role of language in contributing to inequality. Students also learn about applications of sociolinguistics in the fields of education, language policy and planning and become familiar with current debates in the fields of language testing, language endangerment and linguistic human rights.
title: Sociolinguistics for Second Language Teachers
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of major contemporary issues in the field of second language curriculum development. Students will be required to demonstrate their developing understanding of second language teaching by designing and implementing a unit of work which meets the language learning needs of a particular group of learners. This course does not require students to have any prior knowledge or experience in the content area. However, students with prior teaching experience or education will find many opportunities to draw on and extend their existing knowledge.
title: Second Language Curriculum Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course is designed to develop skills necessary for understanding Japanese business culture, manners, customs and protocol with increased communicative command in Japanese. The ultimate goal of the course is to prepare students to work with confidence internationally and/or cross-culturally in a career related to Japan. The course focuses on speaking and listening skills and develops the usage of the honorific language (keigo) appropriate to workplaces in a Japanese environment. As a 10CP course, 3533LHS comprises approximately 150 hours of work in total. Students should follow the enrolment pattern for their major.
title: Japanese for Professional Purposes
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Environment and Population Health examines how the state of health of the population is interrelated with and dependent upon the integrity and health of the global physical, social, cultural and economic environments.
title: Environment and Population Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course will provide undergraduate students with consolidation of their learning throughout the major and provides skills for high level analysis of HR organisational challenges and opportunities with a specific focus on organisational change and strategy. This course will provide students with opportunities to apply their previous HR learning and knowledge to a range of current organisational problems/scenarios giving consideration to HR's relationship to the broader business strategy and external influences through the change management process.
title: Applied Human Resource Management and Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This English course introduces students to the three interrelated areas of learning of the Australian Curriculum English. Language, Literature and Literacy. The course will develop students' understanding of language, texts and their use as a tool to promote effective literacy instruction in the early years of learning. It considers a range of approaches for the effective teaching of literacy, including the discerning use of the explicit teaching of phonics in early reading and the explicit teaching of reading and writing in subjects other than English.
title: English Education 1 - Reading and writing in the early years
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course builds further knowledge, skills, and personal qualities required for supporting communication and/or swallowing in individuals and communities across the lifespan. To develop skills in evidence-based speech pathology practice, you will attend a 2-day per week external clinical placement, working within different service delivery models. You will work with increasing levels of independence, under the supervision of a speech pathology practice educator. Learning is further supported by simulated learning experiences. Competencies required for speech pathology practice are informed by the Professional Standards (Speech Pathology Australia, 2020) and assessed by COMPASS® (Speech Pathology Australia, 2011).
title: Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course develops students' abilities to work with individuals, groups and populations to implement care based on primary health care principles and practices. Students undertake 80 hours of clinical practice to develop nursing competence in community-based settings.
title: Community Nursing Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: A key definition distinguishing human beings from other animals is that humans live in the knowledge of their mortality. This unit explores the human condition of death and dying as it draws from interdisciplinary research literatures and cultural objects, including film and memoir. It examines major psychological and psychoanalytic concepts of grief, mourning and melancholia as well as key themes and topics such as: death and memorialisation online; cross-cultural death rites and beliefs; the politics of mourning; legal issues and the politics of euthanasia; dark tourism; death and memoir, death and celebrity culture; death denial and taboo; death and representation; love and death. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Death, Grief and Culture
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course covers advanced statistical mechanics and topics in condensed matter physics of relevance to current research. It will cover both fundamental and applied skills, including development of advanced theoretical techniques, and introduction to physical problem solving techniques. Contact time of approximately two hours per week will be organised around other commitments from students and staff. Assumed knowledge: Students enrolled in this course are expected to have completed an undergraduate science degree with a physics major (including content covered in 2304NSC Statistical and Solid State II, 2307ESC Analytical and Statistical Mechanics, 3309ESC Condensed Matter Physics and 3301NSC Quantum Physics III). Knowledge of quantum mechanics, elementary statistical physics and elementary condensed-matter physics is assumed.
title: Honours Statistical and Condensed Matter Physics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The project will allow the student to combine all of the knowledge and practical skills which have been developed during the degree. Students will be required to conduct a short research project. Although not essential, students may be sponsored by an organisation or individual within the aviation industry. The research project will address an issue of relevance to the industry. Incompatible: 3001AVN/AVN3001 Aviation Project
title: Aviation Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course covers fundamental aspects of linear algebra with applications to data science and physical problems. Topics may include: matrices and determinants; vector spaces; linear independence; basis sets; orthogonality; inner product spaces; eigenvalues and eigenvectors; general spectral analysis; and modern applications of linear algebra.
title: Linear Algebra and Applications
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course is the fourth of eight courses that comprise the Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma in Australian Migration Law and Practice is a prescribed academic qualification for registration as a migration agent in Australia. 7232LAW (Practitioner Focus) is the companion course to 7132LAW as it builds on skills and knowledge taught in 7132LAW to immerse students in a virtual office environment. Like the other companion courses in the Graduate Diploma Program, in 7232LAW, students learn and apply the practitioner skills they need to effectively integrate the legislative content they acquire in 7132LAW. In addition to providing a practical background and focus for the knowledge learnt in 7132LAW this course continues the client file life cycle commenced in 7231. Students learn and practice how to prepare for an initial client interview, provide written advice to the client, establish a client agreement and account and prepare and lodge a successful visa application. Students will practice these skills within a broad ethical and Code of Conduct compliant framework. As such, in addition to the horizontal alignment between 7132LAW & 7232LAW, both courses are also aligned with the previous courses in the Program (7131LAW & 7231LAW) and the subsequent courses 7133LAW & 7233LAW and 7134LAW & 7234LAW. The deliberate alignment allows students to progress logically through the growing complexity of both legal and practitioner skills as they follow the life of a client file from initial client contact to file closure.
title: Client Skills in the Visa Application process
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course, which includes an embedded 15-day school experience, will help preservice teachers to develop an understanding of young people aged 5-12 years with a special focus on their diverse and complex interests and abilities. Preservice teachers will also consider research about how learning occurs (such as how the brain learns and retains information, the perpetuation of neuromyths) and the influence of the social context on young people's lives and learning. Various teaching approaches, responsive to students needs will be examined (including explicit teaching, modelling, and scaffolding) and ways to develop culturally safe and predictable classrooms will be investigated. The course consists of two non-graded assessment items one of which includes the school-based professional experience component.
title: Understanding Diverse Learners
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is divided into two components, each in turn is subdivided into two modules. The first component is basic electromagnetism: the laws of electrostatics, magnetostatics and electromagnetism are generated from experimental observations leading to the derivation of Maxwell's equations in both vacuum and media. The propagation of electromagnetic waves in various media is studied. This component consists of two modules: Electrostatics and Magnetostatics & Time-varying fields. The second component of the course gives a general coverage of physical optics, introduction to light as an electromagnetic wave, the properties of such waves and their interaction with material media. This treatment is developed to cover the behaviour of light at interfaces (reflection and refraction, Fresnel equations), interference, coherence properties of light, diffraction, Fourier optics and image formation. The optics component consists of two modules: Optical propagation and Interference and Diffraction. Prerequisites: 1031SCG Physics 1A; 1032SCG Physics 1B; 1201SCG Linear Algebra AND 1202SCG Calculus (or 1010ENG Engineering Mathematics 1 AND 1020ENG Engineering Mathematics 2). Prior Assumed knowledge: 2205NSC Calculus II.
title: Electromagnetism and Optics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Students are introduced to Geographic Information Systems (GIS), which enable the capture, storage, manipulation and analysis of different types of spatial or geographical data. These systems are important tools for environmental scientists in understanding and managing changes in environmental systems. Earth resource satellites provide vast geospatial datasets for GIS and underpin our capacity for environmental monitoring and management. The course also introduces how to access and retrieve satellite data for GIS applications. Incompatible: 2205ENV Geographic Information Systems, 3047ENV Geographic Information Systems.
title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to the criminal justice process using the crime of homicide. Starting with a focus on the key elements of the crime event, including the current state of homicide in Australia and abroad, students will develop an understanding of serious violent offences through the lens of offenders and victims of violence. Students then learn how the criminal justice system responds to serious violence offences through an examination of the interconnectedness of the police, courts, and correctional agencies. Students will learn how serious violent offences are detected and investigated by the police and move on to an understanding of how these offences are processed in the courts, which includes the criminal trial and sentencing. Students review the various forms of custodial sentencing and will be introduced to concepts of rehabilitation and desistance. Throughout the course students review the ways that criminological theory has informed the crime of homicide, as well as the criminal justice system and social responses to homicide.
title: Homicide
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is the foundational compulsory course in the Master of Social Work/ Master of Mental Health Practice programs. All students must complete and pass this course in their first trimester of study to progress to placement and continue in the program. Foundations of Social Work Practice introduces the fundamentals of working in the human services including institutional structures and welfare discourses, theories, models, research and processes of human service delivery and methods of social work intervention: interpersonal helping, group work and community work. Restrictions: This course is restricted to students in the Master of Social Work/ Master of Mental Health Practice programs only. This course contains a compulsory intensive.
title: Foundations of Social Work Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course builds on content from previous trimesters, and provides students with an in-depth understanding of the physiological responses that occur during exercise. Particular attention will be given to the responses of the cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine and metabolic systems during exercise, their integration and regulation. The adaptations to acute and chronic exercise will be examined in healthy and diseased populations.
title: Physiology of Exercise
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: 6001DOH_P2 is the second part of Dissertation (with CTG grade). The dissertation courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. The dissertation involves the identification of a research question, selection of any appropriate research design and data analysis. At the completion of the five dissertation courses students will submit a research report for examination. Students may have to defend their work at a research seminar. Students are advised to consult the relevant course convenor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final dissertation component (6001DOH_P5) they are required to submit their dissertation by Friday of the first week of June for students submitting in Trimester 1 or Friday of the last week of October for students submitting in Trimester 2.
title: Dissertation 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In this course students will complete a scholarly exegesis of no less than 5000 words (or equivalent - 12000 to 15000 words). The exegesis must address and unravel the new knowledge or conceptual advancement inherent in the Honours Research Project. This course requires students to apply the knowledge associated with their research project and identified in the other Honours courses they have undertaken, to fully develop the exegetical paper. That knowledge will include a topic or research question, literature review, research method/methodology and theoretical base to the student's research. The Honours Research Project and the exegetical paper will be examined together.
title: Exegesis
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course provides students with a systematic overview of the research skills necessary to undertake research projects in music. Training in the use of relevant bibliographic and electronic resources, in critical writing, and in requirements of a thesis will be included.
title: Music Research Design 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course begins with an overview of conventional energy supply systems and their environmental impacts. Following a brief review of some basic concepts in energy and power, energy systems analysis is introduced. The course then focuses on three major renewable energy resources: solar, wind and biomass. Other renewable energy resources such as hydro, hydrogen, geothermal and ocean energy are then studied but in less detail. The course will also consider some issues in energy policy, impacts of renewable energy systems and the commercialisation of renewable energy systems in Australia and around the world. Substantial use is made of spreadsheets and other computer programs for computations on renewable energy systems and the evaluation of energy resources. In addition to the material in the textbook and that presented in the formal lectures, students will have access to online reading lists and other resources such as mini-lectures, lecture notes, module notes, and tutorial captures and workshops videos. These online resources will enable some independent learning activities. Students are encouraged to participate in the collaborative session with the lecturer.
title: Renewable Energy Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides students with valuable opportunities to learn how to apply relevant theories from Soil Mechanics and Geotechnical Engineering into practice so that they can effectively conduct field surveys and laboratory examination of soil samples, correctly interpret and analyse results of such geotechnical investigations, select appropriate parameters for numerical models, evaluate stability of natural slopes and embankments, and develop skills to write comprehensive and concise geotechnical reports. In addition, the fundamentals of geology and rock mechanics will be introduced and discussed through a number of case studies. Students will also have the opportunity to become familiar with leading computer programs, which are commonly used in the industry, and through performing project-based assignments students will acquire sufficient knowledge and develop critical computer skills that will enable them to solve various practical problems.
title: Geotechnical Engineering Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The risks that outbreaks of infectious disease pose to society are significant, but they can be managed. In this course you'll gain the tools needed to help build prevention structures that safeguard communities from danger from uncontrolled infection. It's centred on the One Health perspective, which fosters collaboration on health programs across sectors and industries, fostering a multi-faceted, proactive public health framework. Critical analysis of key issues, including the role of governments and non-government organisations in facilitating disease prevention and response, will ensure you have a broad understanding of how to structure prevention methods in civil society with a focus on resilience and with understanding of the needs of the varying demographics within society. With this knowledge, you will be capable of evaluating the risks posed by key contemporary global health issues such as biosecurity, biowarfare, emerging infectious diseases, antimicrobial resistance, and health behaviour.
title: Global Issues in Infection Prevention and Control
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The course aims to provide with knowledge and analytical tools for the analysis of derivative markets and derivative securities. It discusses pricing and risk management aspects of derivative securities. Topics include: forwards and futures markets, options markets, swap markets, credit derivatives, basic pricing concepts, the cost-of-carry model, the Black-Scholes model, hedging and risk management techniques.
title: Derivatives and Risk Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course teaches linguistic concepts and skills for understanding how speech sounds are produced (phonetics) and combined to form words (phonology), both in English and in other languages around the world. Writing systems and sign languages are also covered.
title: Sounds and Sound Systems in the World's Languages
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course leads students to a level of proficiency necessary to engage in basic everyday situations. It satisfies prerequisites for 2040LHS Japanese 2A and 2043LHS Japanese 2A (Enhanced). Prerequisites: 1032LHS Japanese 1A OR equivalent. Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Japanese 1B
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course course surveys how the Colonial Nation-State of Australia has identified and interacted with Indigenous peoples'' identities to form changing socio-political contexts throughout the colonial ear. Students will gain an understanding of government policies introduced to define and manage relationships with Australia's first peoples, and the responses by Indigenous Australians to these policy frameworks. The course will explore and challenge theoretical and cultural perspectives that underpin and describe both the policies being pursued and Indigenous engagement within them. Lectures and tutorials will examine the values and political philosophies that directed and gave shape to these social and political movements and, in particular, Indigenous peoples continuing progress towards self determination.
title: Indigenous Australians and the Colonial Nation-State
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: 2204LHS looks into aspects of English words and grammar through the lens of modern linguistics. Though the focus is on mainstream English, some case studies are drawn specifically from colloquial Australian English. The course aims to be useful for linguistics students, for intending teachers of English and other languages, and for anyone interested in language and culture. 2204LHS assumes a minimum of background knowledge about grammar and dictionaries, such as used in secondary school English or in learning English as a second language. More advanced linguistic concepts from morphology, syntax and semantics are explained as they are introduced.
title: English Words and Grammar
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course develops the essential skills learners need to understand basic Japanese sentences, communicate in routine tasks, and describe personal and familiar topics. It helps learners gradually progress towards basic social proficiency, equivalent to B1 Threshold level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). In addition to the 4 contact hours of 2040LHS, this course includes a dedicated 2-hour class that utilises authentic and semi-authentic oral and written materials further to enhance listening and reading comprehension and written expression. As a 20C course, 2043LHS comprises approximately 300 hours of work in total. Students should follow the enrolment pattern for their major.
title: Japanese 2A Enhanced
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course examines ecological attitudes from the sixteenth to the nineteenth centuries, chiefly in Europe. Students will learn about changing ideas of nature during the transition to modernity, identifying their colonial and global dimensions as well as their legacies.
title: A History of Nature
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. Pre requisites: 6001HLS Dissertation Preparation
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces concepts and methods of general chemistry appropriate for Environmental Engineering. Laboratory chemical analysis skills are developed. This course introduces students to working with a chemical laboratory and students will be encouraged to develop problem-solving skills and apply these to the solution of real-world chemical problems. Assessment is by self-assessment quizzes, laboratory reports and examinations.
title: Chemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to the foundations of drama through practical exploration of a genre. Students engage in ensemble-focussed workshops. Through the study of a published modern Australian text, students rehearse towards performance.
title: Performance Project: Storytelling and Ensemble
