academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Psychology Curriculum - Senior Secondary is concerned with curriculum foundations and implementation of Psychology in the senior secondary years (Years 11 and 12).
title: Psychology Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course will continue to develop students' knowledge, skills and attitudes in occupational therapy, with a focus on working with collectives. Students will consider what constitutes 'community', explore ways of understanding the occupational issues facing collectives, and understand barriers to health and participation. Students will further develop their ability to devise and implement occupational therapy interventions.
title: Occupation, Health and Participation - Communities and Populations
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course delves into futures thinking and climate change adaptation, with a focus on transitioning to societies that can sustain high levels of well-being while addressing justice and equity. The course operates on the premise that environmental and social dimensions of future human systems are deeply interconnected, and it emphasizes the critical role of foresight in shaping adaptive strategies. Indigenous perspectives are integral to the course, highlighting their contributions to preferred futures, especially in diverse economic and developmental contexts. Students will explore the tools and methodologies of futures thinking, and their application to climate change adaptation, with a focus on three core areas: 1) Future Scenarios: Examining potential climate futures, their key dimensions, and the role of ethics and values in evaluating these scenarios; 2) Social Sustainability and Equity: Investigating indigenous perspectives, postcolonial realities, environmental ethics and the relationships between humans and the natural environment, and 3) Transformative Adaptation Pathways: Identifying and designing transformative strategies for achieving resilient and equitable environmental and social futures. The course aims to equip students with the skills to contribute to the growing demand for professionals who can guide communities toward sustainable futures. Assessment focuses on a major project in which students outline pathways for climate-resilient, adaptive communities. Additional assessments, including online posters, will ensure progressive understanding of key content. All readings and materials will be provided through the online learning platform.
title: Environmental and Social Futures
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines the planning and management of the wide range of possible sport facilities. The ways in which these facilities and the programs and events hosted in them are linked to the economic, social, and environmental planning of the regions that they serve are described. Requisite needs analysis techniques, and feasibility assessments are illustrated, including financial considerations. Strategic considerations in the operation and marketing of facilities are described, including competitive tendering, franchising, and merchandising. Risk management techniques are examined.
title: Managing Sport Venues and Facilities
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive coverage of events and sponsorship strategies. This course will first expose students to basic principles of motivation for participants and spectators to develop the ability to apply broad principles underlying why consumers attend events across a variety of contexts and situations. Students will then utilise this knowledge on motivation to develop a marketing plan, as well as a customised sponsorship proposal, on behalf of a designated event organisation.
title: Event Marketing and Sponsorship
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course provides students with an opportunity to understand how the various dynamics of the property industry, which have been studied in previous courses, are synthesised and take form through the Property Development Process. This process largely determines the property lifecycle which takes into consideration the various sectoral disciplines, together with the social, political, economic and environmental factors of property development.
title: Property Development Process
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Around the globe, events including festivals, carnivals, exhibitions and conferences continue to play a significant role in society as they help define and shape our personal lives, culture, communities and nations. This course will provide students with an understanding of Event Management Principles that underpin the development and management of events in the dynamic, burgeoning event industry.
title: Event Management Principles
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces the main environmental spheres and important natural processes of the Earth, considered as a series of systems interacting at various scales. Features of the lithosphere, atmosphere, hydrosphere and biosphere are explained, with emphasis given to the interrelationships between these spheres. In doing so, basic concepts of the more specialized fields of meteorology, climatology, hydrology, oceanography, soil science, geology, geomorphology and biogeochemistry will be studied.
title: Earth Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Paramedics are required to develop knowledge about major incidents or disasters involving a mass casualty situation in line with current national and international frameworks. In this course students develop knowledge, critical thinking, decision making and technical skills required to provide the initial management in a major incident/disaster in an out-of- hospital setting. Prerequisites: 2801MED Work Integrated Learning 2.
title: Major Incident Management in Paramedic Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This 50 Credit Point course provides the individually supervised context in which a student may complete written and (where appropriate) practical work for a dissertation/project at one-year Honours level in the humanities, languages and social sciences. Assessment is by Dissertation (100% weighting, between 15,000- 18,000 words) or by Creative or Professional product (60% weighting) with a minor dissertation/exegesis (40% weighting, between 5,500 and 7,500 words).
title: Dissertation/Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course is a basic introduction to digital media production, providing students with exposure to the theory and practice behind communicating with and through a variety of digital media formats including photography and web design.
title: Digital Media: Portfolio Production
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Through the study of a published modern Australian text, students rehearse towards performance.
title: Performance Project: Australian Theatre
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course continues the work begun in Acting I, II, III, IV and V. The acquisition and development of Acting, Voice and Speech, Movement and Dance. Students will deepen and broaden their audition practice and portfolio. This course continues the development of the student's potential as a performer as fully as possible, through class tuition in Acting, Voice and Speech, Movement and Dance through master classes, workshops, seminars and public performances.
title: Acting VI
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The program culminates in a public/industry showcase of works where students use the skills and knowledge they have accumulated through and across the program's courses.
title: Performance and Engagement 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Excellence in practice is predicated on a reflective and rigorous approach to design practice as a method of inquiry and comment. This course introduces students to a number of exemplarily research practices through which they may contextualise their work. It looks at different modes of inquiry and encourages students to develop research practices that are appropriate to their particular area of study. This course provides an opportunity for students to explore the basic principles of research methods and consider how these may be applied to their research project. Students will identify their topic/research question and appropriate methods of inquiry through peer review, students will present their research topic, investigations and work-in-progress for scholarly interrogation. INCOMPATIBLE: must not have completed 7539QCA Design Research Methods
title: Research Methods for Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Business Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course provides opportunities for pre-service teachers to develop their pedagogical content knowledge in the key learning area of English and to further develop their knowledge and understanding of the Australian Curriculum: English. The course provides pre-service teachers with an opportunity to develop a repertoire of inclusive teaching practices that engage primary students and promote English literacies in the primary classroom. Pre-service teachers will understand the importance of early intervention to support language and literacy development especially for children who speak languages other than and in addition to English. This course will focus on reading and reading strategies in the middle to upper primary years, with a focus on literary texts in this age bracket, as well as 'reading and writing to learn' with informative and persuasive texts as well. It is recommended that students have completed 7113EDN Language, literacy and literature for Prep to Grade 3.
title: Language, literacy and literature in the primary years.
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will examine a range of policies, practices and legislative requirements that impact on teaching in secondary school contexts. It will particularly highlight the constantly evolving nature of these and the impact they have on educational practices. Key policies addressed will be those relating to: student pathways into, within and out of secondary schooling; teacher professionalism; and ethical behaviour and responsibilities. A further component of this course will be consideration of how policies, practices and requirements are communicated to parents and the broader community.
title: Contemporary Influences on Secondary Schooling
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides a range of activities that will further develop inquiry and problem-solving skills and put the professional responsibilities of environmental science students into practice. A range of authentic learning experiences will see students conduct research investigations (field experiments, ecological surveys, etc.) as individuals, working in small teams to collect data that is then interpreted using appropriate discipline specific approaches. Conclusions will be drawn and questions for future investigation highlighted. Assessment will be by the combination of research conceptualisation, a high-quality written report and an oral defence of this report. This course is designed as a final year course and students should have completed at least 140CP.
title: Environmental Capstone
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides an opportunity for students to integrate theoretical knowledge and empirical analytic skills acquired in their program through a practical research problem. Students will be expected to complete a small research project (based on topics provided by the course convenor).
title: Individual Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course introduces fundamental concepts of data and computer communications, providing a foundation for further study in engineering systems. Topics include (i) communication systems and network architectures, (ii) data transmission, signalling, and communication media, (iii) data link communication, error detection, and error correction, (iv) communication protocols and technologies such as UART, RS-485, CAN, and Ethernet, and (v) network and transport protocols, including TCP/IP and UDP.
title: Data and Computer Communications
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course aims to foster the development of ethical, reflective, collaborative, and creative practitioners. Students work as part of a collaborative studio team under the guidance of expert teaching staff, connecting with external industry partners on numerous public-facing design projects. Students will develop a working knowledge of professional design practices while creating a range of industry-connected design outcomes. IMPORTANT: refer to www.liveworm.com.au for more information and how to gain permission to enrol.
title: Liveworm 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: LiveSpace projects provide opportunities for students to work on real spatial design projects within the broader community, where they are challenged beyond the limitations of a typical studio environment. These projects are best suited to third-year design students, who are expected to have a good working knowledge of spatial design documentation and the design process. Working on projects outside the 'safety' of a classroom environment, students gain insight into the complexity of the whole design process and the crucial interaction between designers, clients, consultants, trades, community members, and stakeholders through a continuous feedback loop. Students are encouraged to develop appropriate research methods, community consultation processes, and professional practices to support successful outcomes for all involved.
title: Livespace
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Communication Research Skills equips students with foundational knowledge and skills needed to research a range of communication forms, practices, audiences, and institutions. It should be either completed prior to COM110 Introducing Communication Studies or undertaken simultaneously with it. COM190 has two 5-lecture Groups. Foundations (Weeks 1-5) deals with the following topics: using the university library and other information resources; academic writing formats, skills and strategies; effective study practices and habits; and the work contexts and ethics of communication research. Methods (Weeks 6-10) builds on the first Group's foundations. It covers key methodologies used in researching communication texts, practices, and users/audiences: semiotic analysis, content analysis, quantitative techniques, and qualitative techniques.
title: Communication Research Skills
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces students to the scope of evidence-based speech pathology practice for individuals and communities across the lifespan. Through inquiry-based learning, students will engage in group work to learn about communication and swallowing across the lifespan, including typical development, an introduction to disorders, and the impact of the social context on health. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) will provide a framework for analysis and understanding of clinical scenarios, with an evidence-based practice (EBP) approach underpinning students' knowledge about speech pathology practice.
title: Communication and Swallowing Disorders 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course covers the fundamental principles of modern synthetic inorganic and organic chemistry. Emphasis is on problem solving, specifically the construction of quite complex organic molecules from easily available starting materials using contemporary synthetic methods. Topics also include major areas of research in modern inorganic chemistry and organometallic/materials chemistry.
title: Advanced Synthetic Chemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will introduce advanced numerical techniques that complement the analytic approach students will have encountered over their degree program. These are primarily discrete methods used to solve ordinary and partial differential equations, including finite difference and finite element schemes, and related theory such as the solution of sparse linear systems of algebraic equations. Students will consider numerical and analytic approaches to applied problems, often of a discrete nature, such as linear and nonlinear recurrence relations, counting problems, and stochastic differential equations. Students will be assessed on the basis of reports (in the form of electronic documents) outlining their work on various open-ended numerical problems. Prerequisites: 2202NSC Numerical Methods and 2205NSC Calculus II. Advised Prerequisites: 2201NSC Linear Algebra and Applications, 2204NSC Introduction to Mathematical Modelling, 3201NSC Advanced Differential Equations and Modelling.
title: Advanced Numerical Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines the structure and function of the human nervous system from neuroanatomical, neurophysiological, cellular, and molecular perspectives. Students investigate major neuroanatomical structures, neural pathways, cranial nerves, and associated nuclei through lectures and laboratory-based learning activities, including human cadaveric and brain dissection laboratories. Topics include neural communication, sensory and motor systems, cognition and emotion, the influence of emotion on learning, and the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying memory formation. A systems-based approach is used to examine neurological disorders and demonstrate the functional significance of cranial nerves, neural pathways, and motor control systems. Students also develop skills in scientific inquiry through the design, analysis, interpretation, and communication of neuroscience research, including the application of statistical methods and peer review.
title: Neuroscience
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course covers transition to parenting and outlines the role of the midwife in promoting optimal maternal and infant care in the postnatal period. This will include gaining an in-depth knowledge of strategies known to promote protect and support sustained breastfeeding. Additionally, students will develop their knowledge in the areas of sexual health, family planning and transition to parenting. This course provides the theoretical knowledge required to underpin postnatal care delivered through the clinical courses in the Bachelor of Midwifery program.
title: Maternal and Infant Wellbeing
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course describes the origin of the signals which are generated within the body and which can be measured by the physiologist. The principles of the biomedical instrumentation used to record and analyse these signals is presented.
title: Principles of Biomedical Instrumentation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will cover the discovery and optimisation of new drugs, their metabolism and delivery. Topics will include chemical libraries, screening and computer modelling; natural products; structure elucidation and NMR in drug discovery. It will examine the importance of drug delivery technology; the rationale behind the development of drug delivery systems and the manufacture of such systems. Topics include: chemistry of biologically important molecules (such as proteins, carbohydrates, penicillins, opiates and nucleic acids) and introduces some aspects of drug design and drug target interactions.
title: Drug Design and Delivery
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course explores the highly specific economics associated with the aviation industry. It will introduce students to basic economic theories and concepts and applies these concepts to the aviation industry.
title: Economics in Aviation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course will be undertaken in the final trimester for full time students and in the final year for part time students, who will produce a dissertation to apply an advanced body of knowledge. It is between 15,000 and 25,000 words in length depending on the research topic and methodology. Students work with an academic supervisor who maintains regular contact and provides support and direction in the design and execution of the dissertation.
title: Aviation Management Research Paper
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course focuses on a key skill of social work practice, critical reflection, and its relevance to practice and professional growth. Students will be required to bring together their learnings thus far to be able to articulate, critically reflect upon and defend their beginning framework for practice. Brings together knowledge (of self, of human behaviour and society, theory and research), ethics, values and skills.
title: Critical Reflective Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will provide foundational knowledge of medicines and pharmacology for allied health professions. The course will cover principles such as pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, pharmacogenomics; drug interactions and side effects; and orientation to the use of medicines for common disorders of the musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, respiratory, endocrine, and gastrointestinal, and immune systems. It is expected that students wishing to study 2011PHM will have completed tertiary level courses in anatomy and physiology.
title: Clinical Pharmacology for Allied Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course provides construction business management skills which help produce a generation of business leaders in construction. The perspective of all parties, including national and international construction companies, major contractors, house builders, construction clients and government agencies, manufacturers, consultants and others, is considered. Topics include fundamentals of construction industry operations, leadership, persons in organizations, financial analysis and control systems, and innovation in construction. Prerequisite for this course is 1606ENG Construction Economics
title: Construction Business Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course begins with a broad examination of cybercrime and moves to a specific focus on cyber fraud. The course explores contemporary criminological theoretical approaches to explaining cyber fraud, analyses offender methodologies and examines cyber fraud victimology. The course addresses contemporary approaches to prevention and enforcement in Australia and across the world. The role of relevant government, law enforcement, regulatory agencies and the corporate and private sector in the prevention and detection of cyber fraud is addressed.
title: Understanding and Preventing Cyber Fraud
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course requires the execution, analysis and presentation of a scientific research thesis. This course involves the development of a research project, an analysis of appropriate literature background and the execution of research methodology, data collection and data analysis. Results from these experiments are also evaluated and conclusions drawn with findings presented in a formal context in written form. Restriction: FOURTH YEAR BY APPLICATION ONLY
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course equips students with the theoretical knowledge and practical skills necessary for effective health program planning, implementation, and evaluation, with a strong focus on community needs assessment, empowerment, and sustainability. Aligned with the core competencies of Masters of Public Health and Masters of Global Public Health, these outcomes prepare graduates to design evidence-based health initiatives, apply key frameworks and critically assess strategies for long-term public health impact.
title: Health Program Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: "Despite the public's obsession with crime, victimisation and criminal justice, despite the morbid fear that crime and victimisation arouse, despite the endless volumes written to account for offending, victimisation and criminal justice processing, gender, the most powerful social factor of all has been virtually ignored by criminologists." (Leonard, 1982). This course explores the persistent and profound differences in women's and men's experiences of crime. The course considers how gender intersects with other social categories such as race, class, socioeconomic status, and ethnicity to shape crime and responses to it.
title: Gender, Crime and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: You will learn what core skills are gained through the study of psychology or counselling and how these are used in the various professional contexts that psychology or counselling graduates are qualified to work in. You will learn psychology and counselling theories that inform how people come to understand themselves as they relate to the world of work and their place in it and how this understanding of themselves can change across the lifespan. Relevant careers in counselling, community and welfare, human resources, justice, marketing, policy, professional psychology, and social research are described. You will gain skills in selecting a suitable study pathway, selecting appropriate elective courses, and identifying paid and volunteer work opportunities that will enhance your employability in these areas. You will be able to describe the role of ethics, interprofessional learning, work integrated learning, and ongoing professional development in a successful career. Additional skills are gained in building a professional profile, including through LinkedIn and other public portfolios, and in managing your public identity on social media.
title: Psychology and Counselling in Professional Contexts
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Students will be introduced to the major theories of psychological development during childhood, adolescence, and adulthood. The course will cover physical, cognitive, and psychosocial development, drawing on the work of Bowlby, Freud, Erikson, Piaget, Vygotsky, and Baltes among others. Reviewing both classic and current research, the course will consider conceptual and methodological issues in developmental psychology. Important aspects of development from conception to late adulthood will be covered. This course aims to provide a conceptual foundation for practice in clinical, counselling, educational, community, and organisational settings with children, adolescents, and adults. Prerequisites must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Developmental Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course is designed to equip you with project management skills and particularly emphasised on construction site management and the management of design and development of infrastructure/building projects. Management aspects on project planning, risk and environmental impact assessment, cost and cash flow management, and progress progress management throughout the life cycle of projects, from project development state through delivery, commissioning and operation, are taught in this course. Attention is also given to modern management topics such as benchmarking, life-cycle costing, value analysis and concurrent engineering. Your ability and proficiency will be assessed through assignments and written examinations.
title: Construction Project Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course introduces basic vector algebra in two and three dimensions, matrices, complex numbers, probability and revises basic functions. It provides a foundation in the mathematical sciences for later studies in science and engineering. Prior Assumed: Successful completion at senior level Mathematical Methods or equivalent study over four semesters of a high school subject that includes the study of linear algebra. For students who do not have this level of mathematics background, it is strongly recommended you first complete 1017SCG Foundation Mathematics. Incompatible: 1201SCG Linear Algebra. NOTE: this course is only offered on-campus, and students are expected to attend exams and weekly classes on campus, in person.
title: Engineering Mathematics 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course prepares students for clinical practice. Foundational knowledge and skills in health assessment, nutrition and healthy lifestyle practices, infection prevention and control and workplace health and safety are covered, along with the concept of wellness and illness within society.
title: Preparation for Midwifery Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course will introduce students to the important concepts of human movement and function. Students will develop knowledge and understanding of human anatomy, posture, mechanics of movement and function, and an appreciation of the different mechanical properties of different body tissues. Students will develop skills in the observation, description and measurement of joint movement, muscle function and human function including gait.
title: Introduction to Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will provide students with knowledge, understanding, and skills in the physiotherapy assessment and treatment of people with neurological conditions. Students will study the pathology, disability, recovery and prognosis of common neurological conditions and be introduced to evidence-based, holistic, and multidisciplinary management approaches. The pre-requisites for 3405AHS Neurological Physiotherapy are: Must have completed 1 of 2404AHS Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy 1 OR 2406AHS Upper Limb Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy AND must have completed 1 of 2407AHS Introduction to Neurological Physiotherapy OR 1403AHS Physiotherapy 3.
title: Neurological Physiotherapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the application of human factors topics in various departments of the aviation industry. Theoretical and practical examples will even compare and contrast how human factors topics are applied in aviation industry and other high-risk industries; with the aim of learning from each other to enhance safety. Prerequisites: 1504NSC Aviation Biology and Medicine and 2515NSC Human Factors for Pilots.
title: Applied Human Factors
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this course you will discover the power of poetry. You will develop a familiarity with many different forms of poetry, and practice ways of talking about and reading these forms. We'll look at a wide range of modern and contemporary work, sourced from across the 20th and 21st centuries and from around the world. Rather than attempting a historical survey of any particular tradition, our reading will be much more wide-ranging. By looking across cultures, languages and epochs, we will develop a series of criteria that can be used to appreciate and enjoy poems from almost anywhere. We will look at different aesthetic trends, from the conservative to the avant-garde, as well as some of the key themes in contemporary poetry, including colonialism, environmentalism and feminism. We will also read poems in translation, and you will have the opportunity to makes translations of your own. In your final assessment, an independent research project, you will have the freedom to explore those aspects of the course that were most interesting to you. Poetry and Poetic Imagination will show you how, in reading poetry, you learn more not only about literature and language, but also about the power of the poetic imagination and how it can infuse the world around us with fresh energy and meaning.
title: Poetry and Poetic Imagination
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course is designed to provide students with advanced theoretical knowledge and practical skills for the prescription of resistance, endurance, and speed exercise programming. The information presented in 3013AHS will be applicable for those wanting to improve health and fitness, sports performance and rehabilitating and preventing common musculoskeletal injuries. Effective exercise prescription requires identifying individuals' goals, competency in determining specific demands of different sports, understanding exercise responses and adaptations and the ability to design and individualised and evidence based training program. Finally, the course will also further develop a student's appreciation on how evidence-based research supports exercise prescription.
title: Exercise Programming and Prescription II
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines issues involved in the management of energy resources and the strategies required to develop sustainable energy systems. The course will be taught principally by specialist professional engineers from industry. The exact topics covered may vary from year to year and may include: estimation and evaluation of energy resources, energy reserves, forecasting, modelling and simulation of renewable energy systems, energy management in relation to sustainable development, energy demand management, resource management in relation to power infrastructure, power infrastructure planning and energy distribution, organisational challenges in sustainable energy management.
title: Energy Resources Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The supply of good quality water, together with the removal of subsequent wastewater, is essential for modern communities and for maintaining water quality in the environment. This course deals with specialised and advanced aspects, theory, methods, processes, design principles and associated trends in treating raw water and the subsequent wastewater to the required quality. The main focus is on municipal use of water and municipal wastewater production. This course concentrates on providing a solid understanding of the more advanced aspects of the treatment processes.
title: Advanced Water and Wastewater Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Community Internship provides students with the opportunity to integrate academic learning with real-world experience through a minimum of 80 hours of volunteering in a non-profit organisation. The course focuses on community engagement, social justice, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as a framework for understanding and responding to local and global challenges. Students can select from university-supported placements or propose their own (BYO), and are required to complete pre-placement processes, including interviews and relevant compliance requirements such as a Blue Card where applicable. Alongside the placement, students participate in structured academic learning through workshops and guided activities that support reflection, critical thinking, and understanding of their role as emerging professionals and active citizens. The course emphasises the development of key employability skills, including communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability. Available as a 10 credit point elective for students who have completed at least the first Trimester of study within a Griffith University degree program, this course supports career readiness while encouraging students to build a deeper awareness of community issues and their capacity to contribute to meaningful social impact.
title: Community Internship and Partnerships for SDGs
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Information derived from data is important to the management, productivity and competitive advantage of an organisation. Data must be efficiently collected, organised, retrieved and managed to make it meaningful to the organisation. It is the role of the IT professional to develop, deploy, manage and integrate data and information systems to support the organisation. This course includes the organisation, modeling, transformation and presentation of data. Incompatible with 1804ICT Data Management AND 1011ICT Applied Computing AND 1814ICT Data Management
title: Data Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Master of Medical Research thesis, including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussions and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words. Enrolment depends on availability of research topic and supervisors.6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor. Prerequisite: 6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The course is designed to provide students with advanced understanding of promotion and communication strategies utilised in the sport business industry. This course will examine marketing activities employed by a) sport organisations to promote and communicate sport products and services and b) the use of sport as a communication platform to promote products and services by profit and not for profit organisations. The function of the course is intended to provide Sport Management graduate students with an in-depth understanding of sport promotion and communication through consumer behaviour, market research, branding, advertising, sponsorship, media relations, community relations and sales. It builds on this understanding by providing the hands-on practice necessary to becoming an effective sport marketer.
title: Sport and Social Media
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Manage Tourism and Hospitality Information will introduce students to ways of understanding the role of research in the tourism, hospitality, sport and event sectors in a global society. The focus would be threefold: understanding the service industry in a global society (a focus on tourism, hospitality, sport and event sectors); understanding how we know about tourism, hospitality, sport and event issues (a focus on how research informs our knowledge of these sectors and, therefore, on how to read, and act on, research in order to strengthen the nexus between research and practice); and understanding how we show what we know about tourism, hospitality, sport and event management (a focus on academic literacy and issues such as plagiarism and ethical research). In addition, it gives students entering the Master of Business an overview of possible issues/directions for further investigation.
title: Manage Tourism and Hospitality Information
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course is part of a series of courses in which students plan and execute a substantial piece of research, which is reported in the form of a thesis or creative/professional product with dissertation. The thesis or dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 30,000 words. This research is designed to build on previously studied research courses that have developed student's understandings of current social, cultural and educational theories, research methodologies and design. The main objective of the thesis or dissertation is to provide students with the opportunity to engage in a major piece of research in the Humanities within a relevant discipline. By doing this they will come to understand better the nature and dynamics of the discipline and to demonstrate the capability to work at a high level in the application of theory and research skills to a substantial piece of research and to further doctoral study.
title: Dissertation 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course will explore the theory and applications of big data and demonstrate the process from data to decisions. Students will learn big data in various formats, data processing platforms and data analytics tools to transform, visualise, model, and communicate the insights hidden in the data.
title: Introduction to Big Data Analytics
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course introduces the essential cyber security concepts, the procedures for risk mitigation, data privacy protection and governance. It covers a broad range of technical countermeasures from cryptographic algorithms to Internet protocols. It also thoroughly introduces how to enhance the cyber security from three dimensions: people, technology and policy. Previously known as 7905ICT Fundamentals of Cyber Security.
title: Cyber Security Essentials
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Clinical Dental Sciences 1 develops critical understanding of the foundations of dental care and provides students with fundamental knowledge of cariology, prevention of dental disease, restorative dentistry and materials sciences. Students will be introduced to the legal and professional requirements for safe health care delivery.
title: Clinical Dental Sciences 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course requires writing and presenting a new venture proposal. Students learn to develop marketing, operations, human resource, risk- and financial management knowledge and skills required to start and operate a new business or social venture. This course runs in a semi-intensive mode.
title: Building the New Venture
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This advanced final year course provides you with the opportunity to apply your university learning drawing on your disciplinary knowledge, skills and theory acquired through your studies to work as a multi-disciplinary student consulting team to create better business outcomes for a live industry client project. Industry projects will see student teams working with a diverse profile of clients across industries, ranging from large Australian and multinational companies to niche agencies, Start-ups and not-for-profit organisations. The list of client projects will be updated each trimester based on available projects and industry partners. Supported by interactive online material, workshops with experienced academic coaches and industry mentors and a final interactive oral assessment with the industry client, this course and its assessment platform have been specifically designed to facilitate a critical reflection on your employability skills and provide you with evidence to demonstrate that you possess the attributes of a Griffith Graduate.
title: Creating Better Business
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: In an increasingly complex financial system, independence and effective decision-making are important life skills. In business, financial skills drive profitability within the rules and regulations of government, institutions and organizations. In this course you will understand basic monetary flows in the economy, and the interrelationships and dependencies between money, society, groups and organizations, locally and globally. You will develop core skills in financial literacy for business and an understanding of the key principles of accounting, finance and economics. Sound accounting, finance and economics skills are sought by employers in any business graduate, as they enable a solid understanding of the principles that drive enterprise toward success.
title: Why Money Matters
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course is the second in the research dissertation. This course requires you to complete a dissertation under the supervision of an academic staff member. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, analysis of data and completion of a research project and thesis for examination. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. Students are encouraged to publish their findings with their supervisor/s.
title: Dissertation Part 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This law elective course examines and critically evaluates contemporary law and legal responses pertaining to domestic and family violence. All elements are examined and evaluated through feminist, critical and criminal legal theoretical lenses.
title: Domestic and Family Violence
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course will focus on developing essential physiotherapy knowledge and skills required to assess and treat clients with cardiorespiratory disorders in acute care and rehabilitation settings. Students will apply understanding of anatomy, pathophysiology, and exercise physiology to clients with cardiorespiratory disorders, to interpret assessment findings and implement evidence-based treatment plans. Students will also be taught a range of evidence-based treatment interventions, and need to demonstrate competency in the selection and application of techniques, and evaluation of treatment outcomes.
title: Acute Care Physiotherapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: To be an effective leader, self-management is critical. This course will help you develop the consistent mindset and behaviours which are the foundation of good leadership. Leaders can be made, and natural leaders can learn to apply their abilities in more effective ways. Upon completion, you'll be able to recognise key challenges and understand how to use strategy and tactics to overcome them and achieve your goals. You'll apply problem solving and problem management theories and frameworks, so you can lead effectively in alignment with your organisation's values and get the best out of your teams.
title: Developing Values-based Leadership
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The content of this course will provide students with an advanced, integrated understanding of the knowledge and skills required for safe and effective vascular access device insertion, care and management. The course is designed to translate scientific knowledge into practice improvement for healthcare practitioners caring for patients requiring vascular access devices and intravenous therapy, with a strong emphasis on professional standards.
title: Vascular Access Devices and Intravenous Therapy: Transforming Evidence
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course focuses on consolidating the knowledge, skills, and personal attributes required for supporting communication and/or swallowing in individual and communities across the lifespan. To develop skills in evidence-based speech pathology practice, you will attend a 32-day block placement in an external workplace, working within different service delivery models. You will work towards being ready to enter the profession, with increasing levels of independence, under the supervision of a speech pathology practice educator. Learning in this course is further supported by simulated learning experiences and clinically focused workshops. Competencies required for speech pathology practice are informed by the Professional Standards (Speech Pathology Australia, 2020) and assessed by COMPASS® (Speech Pathology Australia, 2011).
title: Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces general coordinate transformations using tensors, and the theory of physical symmetries using groups and their representations. Some of these key concepts are then applied in studying the physics of spacetime -- the general theory of relativity and Einstein's field equations. Advanced topics in the course may vary year to year. Assumed Knowledge: Undergrad Science degree with Physics Major.
title: Tensors, Groups and General Relativity
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to a perspective on the purpose of business that incorporates values such as responsible leadership, integrity, ethical behaviour, respect for others, trust, and sustainable enterprise. The relevance of these values and their impact on behaviour and outcomes in a business context are illustrated through case studies and real-world examples. Building on this discussion, the course examines how businesses develop solutions to meet growing demands for sustainability, transparency, and good governance. The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework is introduced and used to explore the alignment between business practices and sustainable solutions to real-life challenges. The course also considers the role and responsibilities of professionals and the importance of professional standards in today's society.
title: The Purpose of Business
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course develops skills and competencies around digital innovation. New technologies have contributed to enormous changes in the dynamics of business and society. Students will be exposed to the tools to deal with rapid change and fast growth of managing digital innovations.
title: Managing Digital Innovation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course offers a conceptual framework covering public policy perspective on international trade, the impact of multilateral institutions and trade blocs on global business, foreign direct investment and management of multinational corporations. The course provides a basic foundation for understanding specialised courses in technology and the global economy, global marketing and entrepreneurship in a dynamic business environment.
title: Global Business
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course advances student knowledge and skills in estate planning, from the regulatory environment, including the legal and tax implications of ownership structures in the management and transfer of assets, through to strategies to manage the client-professional relationship in the face of difficult circumstances including family breakdown, bankruptcy and the loss of a loved one.
title: Estate Planning
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This is the first course of the Master of Pharmacy program that contains a placement component. These placements will help you to understand, and further envision, current and future roles for pharmacists within the continuum of care. Prerequisites: 7024PHM Introduction to Pharmacy Topics; 7002PHM Professional Pharmacy Practice I & 7006PHM Professional Pharmacy Practice II. Co-requisite: 7025PHM Placement Preparation.
title: Experiential Rotations I
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: In General Dental Practice 1 students develop knowledge and skills of principles, techniques and materials applied to the practice of endodontics, periodontics and removable and fixed prosthodontics. Students will attend professional practice sessions to enable them to reach a level of clinical competence to operate safely in a clinical environment. Pre-requisite: Students must have successfully completed all preceding years courses to progress to year 3. Must be enrolled in Bachelor of dental health sciences (1577)
title: General Dental Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In Clinical Dental Sciences 4 students will develop a critical understanding of the concepts, principles and theories applied to the practice of orthodontics and paediatric dentistry. Students will gain critical knowledge that supports professional practice. Pre-requisite: Students must have successfully completed all preceding years courses to progress to year 3.
title: Clinical Dental Sciences 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Students will take this course in their final year of study towards completion of an undergraduate degree in Environment or Science. Students in the Bachelor of Medical Science (1280) can undertake this course in Trimester 3. This course takes the form of a research project consisting of a supervised investigation or study, and may include laboratory or field work, analysis of experimental data and the writing of a scientific report. Prerequisite: Completion of 130CP and a cumulative GPA of at least 4.5. Enquiries are to be directed to the Course Convenor. Incompatible: 3181ENV Special Topic, 3191ENV Special Topic, 3005NSC NSC Project
title: Research Special Topic
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines the modern reality of work and its future in light of developments in technology, the economy, globalisation, demography, income distribution and climate change. It will look at differing visions of the future and analyse such issues as digital platforms and work, management, voice, collective behaviour, gender and regulation.
title: The Realities and Potentials of Workplaces
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Pharmacy has at its core the discipline of pharmaceutics, which is the study of drug formulations and the processes by which these are designed, manufactured and delivered to the body. Simply stated, pharmaceutics converts drug substances into medicines - delivery systems capable of administering drugs to the body in a safe, efficient, reproducible and convenient manner. Specialised Delivery Systems II provides an in-depth pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical knowledge of advanced drug delivery technologies utilised in medicine and addresses formulation aspects relating to special industries including; cosmetic, dental, veterinary, and traditional, complementary and alternative medicines. The course builds on knowledge gained in 2023PHM Specialised Delivery Systems I.
title: Specialised Delivery Systems II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This subject covers a range of technology-enabled crimes, including attacks on computer hardware (i.e., viruses, ransomware attacks, etc.) and those crimes in which computers are used as the primary facilitator of the crime (i.e., online fraud, cyber terrorism, cyberstalking, cyberbullying, online child exploitation, etc.).
title: Fraud and Cybercrime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is only available to students enrolled in an Honours program offered through the School of Environment and Science. Students will undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of one or more supervisors appointed by the Honours Program Director. The topic and nature of the Research Project will be determined through consultation and mutual agreement of the student and supervisor and approved by the Honours Program Director. The project will involve original research and will be under the direct supervision of an academic staff member.
title: Honours Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course mainly covers the analysis and design of reinforced and prestressed concrete structural elements. Both strength and serviceability design requirements are covered. Problem solving exercises based on actual design situations are utilised extensively in this course. After completing this course students will be able to analyse and design structural concrete elements and structures. Assessment is by, tutorial and design assignments, and examinations.
title: Concrete Structures
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The key to understanding catchments is understanding the processes that form, maintain and transform them. Understanding these processes requires understanding elements of geology, geomorphology, hydrology, biogeochemistry, soil science, ecology and microbiology. The interplay of these processes and their management are at the heart of what makes catchment restoration and catchment management so challenging. World class catchment scientists are able to integrate and apply their understanding of these complex earth, water, land and ecological systems to manage them sustainability and, where necessary, to improve catchment stewardship. This course will provide an understanding of key catchment processes from a multi-disciplinary perspective to provide an integrated scientific framework for management intervention design, planning and implementation.
title: Introduction to Catchment Processes
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This dissertation course gives research students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest and is a good preparation for the student to undertake higher research studies and other research endeavours. This course involves the execution of a research proposal, including experimentation and analysis of research results. It involves the preparation and presentation of a completed master degree thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Students may have developed research skills in the completion of pre-requisite research methodology courses with the view of undertaking a research topic in this course. Alternatively, a research project may be fully developed within the size and scope of the topic as part of this course. This course is a 40cp dissertation study.
title: MHSM Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This theory based course expands on undergraduate dentistry-related topics. It has a multidisciplinary focus, and all activities will be shared amongst students doing different majors. These will include guest lectures, and journal clubs in areas that interconnect with Dentistry.
title: Interdisciplinary Advanced Dentistry 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This clinically-based course introduces advanced clinical dentistry in the major selected by the candidate. It is based on research informed seminar/tutorials, case presentations and advanced clinical practice. Learning activities are presented by staff with expertise in the specific major.
title: Advanced Clinical Dentistry 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course represents the main research component of the program. Students will gather and analyse data, document and present findings in the form of a dissertation which is potentially publishable in a peer-reviewed journal.
title: Master of Clinical Dentistry Research Project 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In this course, students conduct an industry-based placement within a commercial or industrial environment under professional supervision while managing their learning and course assessment. The placement provides students with the opportunity to undertake a substantial body of work that has an industry application and brings together the wide range of knowledge and skills already developed in earlier courses within their degree program. The aim is for students to develop the necessary attributes, skills and competencies expected in a graduate/postgraduate professional while working within a relevant workplace while under the guidance and direction of an Industry Partner. To be eligible for this course, students must have registered online with the Griffith Sciences Partnership Office in the trimester prior to enrolment. Please contact wil-gs@griffith.edu.au to register. If your registration is successful, you will be given permission to enrol prior to the start of the trimester. Prerequisites: Must have achieved at least 50CP which define the program AND 20CP from the major AND the student must have achieved a GPA of 5 or greater AND must have completed 7808ICT Project and Cyber Security Management OR must have completed 7002ICT Systems Development
title: Work Integrated Learning - Placement
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The research project is designed to provide training in the developmental and practical elements of research, including epidemiology, public health and health services research, clinical research and biomedical research. Students will be required to design and conduct a research project of special interest to them, and within the competence of the School to direct, and to prepare this work for publication. All students, irrespective of their own research topic, will be required to evaluate published, current and future research across a broad range of topics relevant to their chosen discipline, as the basis of their clinical practice, and with the expectation of research forming the platform for lifelong learning.
title: Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course is to equip students with the skills and knowledge to procure, establish and manage all resources and services required for efficiently and safely operating a construction site. The students will gain a practical understanding of the site establishment and organise personnel, site accommodation and amenities, material coordination and managing plant and equipment. The course content ensures students learning capacity to evaluate work health and safety principles, procedures and legislative and regulatory requirements applicable to construction sites. Prerequisite for this course is 1604ENG Construction Communication. Note: 1492 Bachelor of Architectural Design students are exempt from this prerequisite.
title: Construction Site Operations and Safety
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course recalls and extends key traditions and debates in jurisprudence and the philosophy of law, including Western analytical and critical traditions, Indigenous legal thought, and other theoretical perspectives on law. It integrates signature themes and methods from the law degree, engaging students in critical reflection on the foundations and authority of law, on legal interpretation and judgment, and on the relations between law, justice, and the subjects and worlds it shapes. Through close engagement with primary theoretical texts, it develops students' capacity to theorise the legal questions, doctrines, and problems they encounter in practice. This course must be completed in students' final year of study. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Theories of Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course examines the processes involved in the resolution of civil disputes in the context of our court systems. Following a consideration of the differences between, and the interrelationship of, substantive and procedural law and the theoretical foundations of our procedural system, students will closely examine the various steps involved in a civil matter. The emphasis of the course will be on the operation of the Uniform Civil Procedure Rules 1999 (Qld). Consideration will also be given to Federal procedure.
title: Civil Procedure
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Property 2 complements the content of Property 1, and continues to explore the concepts introduced there through a detailed consideration of key land law doctrines. The Course focuses on land law and features the regulation of land through the introduction and operation of the Torrens System, and covers doctrinal areas including boundaries to land, co-ownership, covenants, easements, equitable interests, mortgages and general law leasing. Students in Property 2 will develop and refine their skills in hypothetical problem-solving in the context of property disputes involving land. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Property 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Pre-service teachers will explore key curriculum, pedagogy and assessment principles in order to effectively teach the QCAA Physics syllabus at a senior secondary level. Pertinent content from the syllabus will be covered in order to design and create differentiated and inclusive learning experiences that caters to all students. A range of pedagogical and assessment (including QCAA processes) strategies will also be modelled and explored in order the create engaging and academically rigorous sequences of learning.
title: Physics Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines the process of research and key design decisions in planning a coherent and valuable project. Students define a research topic, formulate questions, review literature, develop a conceptual framework and outline a plan for a research project.
title: Designing Educational Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Diverse disciplinary traditions inform contemporary research in education and professional practice. This course explores and evaluates some of these different influences to provide students with a foundation for critically understanding research and developing their own projects.
title: Foundations of Education Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The focus of this course is on strengthening development of midwifery practice knowledge and skills required to support the well woman and baby across the normal-complex childbirth continuum. This course builds on foundational midwifery knowledge and skills.
title: Midwifery Practice 3: Integrating Care with Complexity
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course addresses Indigenous Knowledges in broad terms, including the epistemologies and worldviews of Indigenous peoples all over the world. It also covers the contributions of non-Western thought and discovery to our society. These ideas will lay an important groundwork for students that culminates with 4299EDN Indigenous Issues for Teaching later in the program.
title: Indigenous Perspectives in Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The course is designed to prepare students for the Independent Research Project in the Master of International Law and teaches research methodologies. Students are assumed to have completed the courses of the Masters in International Law.
title: Advanced Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This introductory course explores the application of psychological knowledge to real-world human behaviour and problems in non-psychology fields including business, health, education, and science. It takes a 21st century and global perspective on how psychology can address issues of public concern such as changes in the world of work, multiculturalism, adaptation to global crises, and personal optimisation. This online free choice elective will complement your discipline-specific knowledge by developing your 'psychological literacy' and teaching you how to apply that in your future career and personal life.
title: Applied Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course focuses on curriculum and pedagogy for effective learning and teaching of Food and Nutritionin senior secondary school (Years 11-12). Students will gain an understanding of the QCAA Senior Food and Nutrition Syllabus by examining key requirements for senior secondary students and will develop planning skills emphasising selection and sequencing of effective pedagogies. Students will be supported to confidently develop assessment strategies and design unit plans and lessons for Senior Food and Nutrition students.
title: Food and Nutrition Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is one of a series of courses in which students plan and execute a substantial piece of research, which is reported in the form of a dissertation. The dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 60,000 - 80,000 words. The dissertation builds on previously studied research courses that have developed the student's understandings of research planning, research methodologies and research design.
title: Research Project - Part 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is one of a series of courses in which students plan and execute a substantial piece of research, which is reported in the form of a dissertation. The dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 60,000 - 80,000 words. The dissertation builds on previously studied research courses that have developed the student's understandings of research planning, research methodologies and research design.
title: Research Project - Part 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Using the life cycle of a company the operation of the Australian corporate regulatory framework is illustrated. Thus, the course examines: company registration; corporate governance issues arising from the company's daily operations, and the external administration of a company on its insolvency. Students undertaking a Law Degree should make note that 2106AFE is incompatible with the LAW courses and they should seek further advice from the Law School if choosing an elective.
title: Company Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course enables students to extend critical thinking and problem-solving skills to manage people with chronic health conditions at an advanced level. Students apply knowledge and skills in person-centred management of the physical, social and psychological problems experienced by individuals, families and communities related to a range of chronic health conditions.
title: Advanced Healthcare Practice in Chronic Health Conditions
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Industrial Design Studio 4 runs under the theme of Medical Design. As part of this course students will learn Materialise Mimics/3Matic software. This software is the global industry standard for hospitals and medical practitioners for dealing with medical imaging (CT/MRI) scans and for the planning of complex medical procedures of all types. Materialise is a partner of Griffith University and students will be taught and certified by Materialise professionals. Projects will concentrate on the learning of the various medical imaging workflows used when undertaking projects in the medical/health field. Students will learn first-hand the practice of 3D digital scanning and its role in the fields of patient specific medicine and its critical importance to the field of Mass-Customisation of all types. Prerequisites 2108ENG Industrial Design Studio 2. 1102ENG 3D Modelling for 3D Printing
title: Industrial Design Studio 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Industrial Design Studio 2 is the second of four core studio courses in the Industrial Design program. ID Studio 2 will focus on User Centred Design, Inclusive Design and Co-Design with Disability. Extending on user centred design processes introduced in first year, to collaborate with industry partners and user groups with complex requirements to design solutions for real-world participants. Students will be introduced to co-design methods and DfAM approaches when designing customised inclusive solutions.
title: Industrial Design Studio 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The sharing economy has completely transformed the tourism and hospitality industry by offering alternative options to traditional forms of service and accommodation. As part of the course, students will be trained (hands-on) in the use of short-term rental data analytic, Channel Managers, and Property Management Systems which will enhance the knowledge of the P2P and the overall functioning of the field.
title: Tourism and the Sharing Economy
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces undergraduate students to academic learning skills for successful progression to further University studies and beyond. Through this course, you will develop transferable life skills, including time and self-management, learning skills and digital literacy, as well as become oriented to university and consider your career goals. With an emphasis on academic integrity, research, and academic communication, this course provides an opportunity for you to build confidence as an independent learner.
title: Foundation Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This subject introduces students to the sociology in a fresh local context, exploring key theories social scientists use to explain Australian and global societies, and considering the ways that our understanding of the social world has an impact on social life.
title: Understanding the Social World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces preservice teachers to the role of the learning enhancement teacher in secondary schools. Pre-service teachers will examine the characteristics, difficulties and differences of students who are most likely to engage with learning enhancement teachers. They will also explore diagnostic processes, tools and instruments for collecting on student progress. Specific resources such as the Nationally Consistent Collection of Data on Students with Disability (NCCD), a nation-wide process in which data are collected annually for school-age students with disability who are receiving adjustments, will be analysed. Secondly, other documents to specify these adjustments are examined, for example, an individual education plan (IEP), individual curriculum plan, personalised learning plan or Individual curriculum plan. Further to this, is the ability to interpret data and the collaboration required with all those involved (student, teachers, parents and carers, learning support team) to enhance student learning and who may require support academically, socially/emotionally and behaviourally to meet the needs of the curriculum.
title: Learning Enhancement
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course invites students to work with industry and community groups to create real world public art outcomes. With a focus on large-scale wall paintings, students will develop public artworks that engage with histories of place. Public Art 1, 2 and 3 cover range of theoretical and practical skills integral to collaborative public art projects including concept, artwork and communications development. By encouraging students to link their individual studio practices with these industry-based projects, students will develop important skills for extending their practices beyond the studio setting.
title: Public Art 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course is conducted primarily as individual student placements. The course introduces the concept of industry-based training and experience, while assisting in the transition from university to the workplace. Students will consolidate their scientific training and knowledge by undertaking a practical placement in a professional workplace whilst simultaneously managing their learning and course assessment. The course emphasizes that competence in legal (OHS/WHS), ethical, scientific, academic and social responsibilities are essential and key components of the scientific profession.
