academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: Global forces are rapidly changing the way we work. Globalisation, automation and digital communication have altered the way that employees engage with the workplace and provide value to employers. Career pathways have changed too. It is likely that you will have many jobs across a variety of careers and industries in your lifetime. Rapid advances in technology are enabling firms to automate processes, which is displacing or changing routine work. Simultaneously, the power of knowledge workers is rising. In parallel, new industries and new forms of collaborative and distance-based work are emerging. All of this is offering new challenges and opportunities. In this course you will explore how rapid technological advances are creating digital disruption that will impact your work in the future. It will enable you to identify opportunities to craft your own career pathway in a rapidly globalising, knowledge and service-intense economy.
title: The Future of Work
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: The world has become increasingly interconnected as a result of increased trade, communication and cultural exchange. This interconnection, or globalisation, creates a need for you to develop intercultural, knowledge, understanding and competence. In this course you will explore Australia's place in the Asia-Pacific region with its accompanying strong cultural ties to the history of Australia's First Peoples and the Western world. You will examine the influences of the past, contemporary issues and possibilities for the future. This course is designed to commence your professional learning about the cultural protocols and knowledge required when engaging in cross-cultural relationships within Australia and across the Asia-Pacific region.
title: Engaging Australia and the Asia-Pacific
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course supports students undertaking an independent research project culminating in a thesis. Students are introduced to different methodologies of legal research and learn to articulate research questions, identify appropriate methodologies for answering those questions, and refine their research based on iterative feedback. Students also examine the practical, institutional and ethical dimensions of undertaking legal research both within and beyond the academy. Co-requisite: 6002LAW_Y1 Thesis Work in Progress.
title: Legal Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course requires candidates to prepare the initial plan of their proposed major research project, pertaining to (1) the explanation of the problem, (2) the literature which informs the topic, and (3) relevant prior studies and/or theoretical or conceptual considerations which assist with investigating the problem. It extends the work undertaken in the course 8240EDN Initial Research Planning and together with 8266EDN Research Design and Proposal II, will conclude the coursework leading into confirmation of candidature. A significant part of this course will involve updating your initial literature review in relation to both contemporary theory and recent research findings and refining the research questions. The initial research plan should include three sections: (1) a current statement of the research problem/ research question and sub-questions as they stand, (2) a rationale for the project including significance, and (3) relevant literature which informs your research problem. Methodology and the final research design will be more fully developed in 8266EDN.
title: Research Design and Proposal I
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines how governments make and conduct foreign policy with a focus on Australia. It first investigates approaches to foreign policy making and diplomacy, including the determinants and politics of foreign policy, and defence strategy and doctrine. The course then examines the theory and practices of diplomacy before moving into the specialist areas of economic, public and sports diplomacy. In each trimester of offering the course features guest subject experts and a special topic or case study in contemporary diplomacy. Overall, the course covers the functions and roles of the main areas of government engaged in international affairs to inform students' career choices and pathways. The workshop program immerses students in the problems and practices of foreign policy making and diplomacy through scenario-based, experiential learning.
title: Diplomacy and Foreign Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course helps prepare students to pursue a range of careers in Political Science, Public Policy and International Relations. It provides insights from video interviews with established staff members in local, state and federal government, diplomacy and foreign policy, the United Nations, non-governmental organizations, academia and international business. It introduces students to career readiness resources and training available at the university. It also helps students gain the skills and knowledge they need to develop and pursue their own possible career pathways. Lectures are pre-recorded, and most feature interviews with Griffith alumni and others who have developed careers in areas salient to the study of Political Science and International Relations. Workshops will focus on career networking tools and skills, identifying and preparing effective applications for internships, graduate programs and job sites, and the development of teamwork, communications and critical thinking skills that are vital in the workplace.
title: Career Pathways in Political Science and International Relations
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course is aimed at final year undergraduate business students wishing to develop greater understanding of some of the complex strategic issues facing organisations today and in the future. In a marketplace where organisations are continually being disrupted through industry landscape change and technological innovation, strategic management can be the key to delivering a solid bottom line. As traditional sources of competitive advantage are being eroded, managing strategic change is becoming a crucial factor in the survival and performance of business organisations. As parts of this course, students will explore the following broad areas: the concepts and techniques of strategic position, strategic analysis and implementation at the business and corporate levels. These will include the external environment, competitive industry dynamics, resources and capabilities, stakeholders and governance, business and corporate strategic choices, international strategy, mergers and acquisitions, strategy evaluation, the strategy development process and the practice of strategy.
title: Managing Strategic Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: In The Storytellers: Reading Fiction, you will read, discuss and write about some major Anglo-American literary works written over the past 200 years. This course provides a comprehensive introduction to concepts, tools and techniques required for the analysis of fiction and verse. Further, the course will explore the historical development of various genres and chart the movement from realism to Modernism. The Storytellers: Reading Fiction aims to develop the disciplinary grounding necessary for advanced literary studies, but also to introduce you to practices of individual reading and writing that lay the foundations for lifelong learning.
title: The Storytellers, Reading Fiction
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: The course is an intensive activity in the area of Opera Studies. The options available are for classical singers (operatic roles) and pianists (Repetiteur activities.) Vocal technique, musicality, language and ensemble work are combined, consolidated and refined through intensive rehearsals. New skills are integrated into the discipline of the theatre.
title: Opera Project C
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course explores the historical, sociological and criminological context of youth offending and youth justice. Students will become familiar with age-related crime and anti-social behavioural patterns, as well as current theoretical and empirical debates about how these patterns can be explained. In light of our understanding about youth and crime, students will be encouraged to critically examine how we respond to young people's antisocial behaviour and offending, with particular attention to youth justice. Through this, young peoples' experiences with the branches of the youth criminal justice system are explored. Consideration is given to the legislation governing approaches to young people and crime.
title: Youth, Crime and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course engages jazz history from its roots through a broad range of contemporary practices, focusing on stylistic innovations, improvisational and experimental concepts, key figures, lines of influence and dispersion, socio-political contexts, and intersections with other Black American musical traditions.
title: Jazz Music and Black American Culture
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Advancements in mechanics largely come from innovations in manufacturing and new materials like metamaterials and liquid crystals. Structural and Mechanical Engineering research focuses on accurately modelling material behaviour, which requires developing constitutive material models. Continuum Mechanics (CM) is a key tool for this, providing a framework to describe solids and fluids under external forces (e.g., mechanical loads, thermal variations, electromagnetic fields, etc). This course covers the fundamentals of material models, using elementary tensor calculus and continuum mechanics. This course aims to address the following critical aspects for mechanical engineers: 1. Unifying the basic mechanics stream courses (Engineering Mechanics, Mechanics of Materials 1, and 2) to ensure you have a comprehensive understanding of solid mechanics. 2. Providing the fundamental theory behind modelling solids and fluids, which is crucial for understanding Computational Statics/Dynamics (CSD) and Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD). You will have a better understanding of commercial analysis packages and understand the notation in their user documentations. 3. Summarising applied/simplified material models for elasticity, plasticity, and viscosity, which are widely used in solid and fluid modelling.
title: Constitutive Material Modelling
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Explore American literature and its connections with the formation of cultural and political identities, institutions and histories through three case studies: expatriatism, regionalism and the representation of the city. This unit surveys some key writers and movements in American literature since the late nineteenth century, and draws links to important trends in American culture and history. It also develops your awareness of comparative perspectives, drawing out similarities and contrasts in the concern and themes of this literature with European modernism and Australian literary nationalism.
title: American Literature
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course embraces subject matter close to the current state-of-the-art in Information Technology. Students select a topic from the list. Students are strongly advised to consult the academic offering their selected topic well before the course starts. Students must submit a Departmental Consent Form prior to enrolment in this Advanced Topic course.
title: Advanced Topics in IT
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course enhances independent learning strategies and study management, with a focus on research, and critical thinking. It fosters the development of academic skills, boosting student confidence for future academic pursuits and employability across disciplines. Pre-requisite: Students undertaking a part-time study load must have completed 9100EPP University Preparation. Co-Requisite: Students undertaking a full-time study load must be enrolled in 9100EPP University Preparation.
title: Learning Strategies for University Success
academicOrgDescription: EmpowerED

description: In this course, students will examine a particular issue in the criminal justice system: the role of the victim. To do this, students will gain an understanding of the role and characteristics of crime victims, how victims interact (or not) with the criminal justice system, and the differential impacts of victimisation experiences. Students will then apply this knowledge to assessing initiatives to recognise victim suffering and enhance victim support. Issues of inequality and rights will be central themes to understanding victims and their experiences.
title: Victims and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Industrial Design Fundamentals has a focus on foundation Industrial Design processes, to include, design process, creative problem solving, sketching and modelmaking to analyse and design products. User Centred Design principles are introduced with methods for understanding users, evaluating, and designing for usability. This course enables students to develop their core industrial design skills.
title: Industrial Design Fundamentals
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Critical infrastructure in a security context, security requirements of Operational Technology (OT systems), and distributed ledger technology.
title: Critical Infrastructure and Distributed Technologies
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course is a great entry point to learn theoretical and practical aspect of Financial Systems. The course covers (a) types and classes of financial markets include evaluation of the financial markets and instruments, (b) operations of the major financial institutions, and (c) evolution in the financial systems in reference to Australia.
title: Financial Markets
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: An intensive course, exploring human movement as an expressive and dramatic medium.
title: Movement and Stagecraft
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The course "Data Processing and Visualisation" provides a comprehensive understanding of techniques, tools, and best practices for processing and visualising data. Students learn data collection, cleaning, integration, transformation, and reduction techniques. They explore principles of effective data visualisation, including choosing appropriate visualisation types, encoding data attributes, and design principles. Students gain hands-on experience in creating visualisations for different data types, such as numerical, categorical, time series, spatial, and textual data. They also learn advanced techniques for large-scale data processing, statistical analysis, and machine learning.
title: Data Processing and Visualisation
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Outbound Griffith Exchange students who are studying at a partner university must enroll in exchange courses for the trimester(s) they will be studying overseas. The tuition fees for each trimester will be determined by the course code(s), which considers the credit points and field of study. These factors are set by the Australian Government. This course is specifically tailored for both undergraduate and postgraduate students who are pursuing fields of study that include Nursing, Indigenous and Foreign Languages.
title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

The tuition fees for each trimester will be determined by the course code(s), which considers the credit points and field of study. These factors are set by the Australian Government. This course is specifically tailored for both undergraduate and postgraduate students who are pursuing fields of study that include Nursing, Indigenous and Foreign Languages.
title: Exchange Studies

academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

title: Exchange Studies

This course is specifically tailored for both undergraduate and postgraduate students who are pursuing fields of study that include Engineering, Surveying, Environmental Studies, and Science.
title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

description: With tourism businesses becoming more global and with thousands of professionals hosting international guests, it is becoming increasingly important to analyse and understand the cultural differences among international visitors and employees with various backgrounds, and the impact of these differences on tourist and employee behaviour. Such analysis should allow for identification of similarities and differences among international tourists, as well as locals and decision-makers and employees in different countries. This contributes to more adequate and effective tourism marketing and management.
title: Diversity and Culture in Tourism
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces students to the fundamental questions and skills of public policy analysis. Policy analysis is a professional and academic discipline dedicated to understanding and shaping the public policy process. Public policy is about the choices we make together as a society. It is the process through which societies define public problems, navigate unequal power and influence, and manage societal tensions and trade-offs. Students learn about the different policy tools governments can use, the main reasons governments make policy decisions, and the challenges of policy implementation. The course includes a deep dive into a major policy issue that affects all Australians. The course is essential for anyone considering a career in politics, the public service, international organisations, community or advocacy work, academia, consulting, or business.
title: Fundamentals of Policy Analysis
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: The aim of this first-year course is to introduce students to the written and oral communication skills required for study and practice in health studies. Using the broad topic of intercultural communication for healthcare, students will develop foundational academic strategies for communication within a wide range of contexts that they can transfer to study within their specific disciplines..
title: Communication Skills for Health Studies
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course aims to develop linguistic proficiency in four key languages of vocal repertoire, namely: English, Italian, French and German with emphasis on the principles of lyric diction in building greater fluency and authenticity of pronunciation in singing.
title: Lyric Diction
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This is the core econometrics course of the major. The course introduces students to regression analysis, starting with OLS and then progressing to GLS and Instrumental Variables estimation. The key elements of panel and time series econometrics are also introduced. These will be the building block of the capstone course in the third year.
title: Econometric Analysis
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course introduces fundamental cloud computing concepts, explores Infrastructure as Code (IaC). This course provides a practical understanding of virtualization technologies, covers networking in the cloud, discusses storage and backup strategies, emphasizes security and compliance, and provides insights into monitoring and troubleshooting. Students require basic IT and computer networking knowledge and must have completed 1007ICT Computer Systems and Cyber Security. The foundational knowledge delivered in this course can serve as a stepping stone for further cloud-based certifications, such as the Amazon Web Services Certified Cloud Practitioner and Cloud Architect certifications.
title: Cloud Architecture and Administration
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course builds on the foundations of computer networking essentials learnt in 2809ICT Computer Networking Essentials and enables students to understand the various network protocols, architectures and considerations related to the configuration, operation and troubleshooting of enterprise networks. After completing this course, students should be prepared to undertake industry certification.
title: Enterprise Routing and Network Architectures
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: In order to be an effective leader an individual must first understand their own perspective on the world and the strengths and opportunities this perspective brings. From this point, it is possible to more effectively engage and lead others. The importance of effective leadership, self-development and communication to the success of the modern organisation cannot be overstated. While the need for technical and professional excellence in the various functional disciplines in any organisation is unquestioned, ultimately success is determined by the quality of leadership present. This course will focus on leadership from a relational perspective. Upon successful completion participants will have an increased understanding of themselves, of interactions amongst others and of the variable contextual elements that have an impact on leadership effectiveness. The learning process includes a combination of current leadership literature, dialogue and reflection. This will be undertaken within the context of: intrapersonal and interpersonal leadership; bright and dark side of leadership; persuasive communication; organisational values and culture; and personal resiliency. Assessment of course components is designed to reinforce these aims and facilitate alignment among content, process and outcomes.
title: Developing Values-based Leadership
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Production in Practice 1 immerses students in the dynamic environment of film production, emphasizing experiential learning through active participation. This course bridges theory and practice by providing hands-on opportunities to engage with industry-standard workflows, equipment, and collaborative processes. Students will learn by doing - developing skills, problem-solving abilities, and an understanding of on-set roles - while gaining on-set experience that prepares them for future production challenges.
title: Production in Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course explores the core principles of set etiquette and production protocols, with students gaining insight into the structured workflow that underpins every shoot. From understanding the machine of filmmaking to navigating the communication structure, students will develop the ability to operate confidently within complex production environments. The screen industry thrives on collaboration, precision, and professionalism. Success on set is not only about technical skill but also about understanding the protocols, etiquette, and interpersonal dynamics that keep productions running smoothly. This course equips emerging professionals with the knowledge and behaviours essential for thriving in the fast-paced world of film and television. By the end of this course, students will not only understand the technical and procedural aspects of production but also develop the professional mindset and interpersonal skills that distinguish reliable crew members in the industry.
title: Set Etiquette and Production Protocols
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Production in Practice 2 expands the experiential learning introduced in Production in Practice 1 by offering students additional opportunities to work on film sets and deepen their practical understanding of production processes. This course focuses on reinforcing and broadening hands-on experience through varied on-set roles and collaborative projects, allowing students to apply and refine their skills in new contexts. By continuing to learn through doing, students gain further insight into industry practices while building confidence and adaptability in real-world production environments.
title: Production in Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: A Life in the Arts aligns with your current and future ambitions to succeed within and beyond the arts career domains of performance, composition, teaching and production. It addresses the results from several Australian-based studies that, amongst many skills, the majority of artists require knowledge of available artistic support in addition to strategies that nurture and strengthen their employability oppportunities that sustain and further contribute to artists' lives, whether it be for full/part-time or freelance activity. As the list of capabilities required to enact these activities is vast, two core assessment pieces have been chosen to develop your self-promotional, self-funding, career planning and project management skills.
title: A Life in the Arts
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course imparts the principles and practices of setting music for orchestras, jazz groups, and other ensembles across classical, jazz, and contemporary music practices. Students learn orchestration, voicing, instrumentation, texture, organology, and score preparation. Focuses include orchestra, big band and chamber and contemporary ensembles. Lectures present broad concepts while tutorials are streamed into classical and jazz/contemporary pathways (students may attend either or both streams). Ensemble reading sessions provide opportunities to workshop student arrangements and hear them realised by performers.
title: The Art of Arranging
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course explores the changing face of innovation, that is, the ways in which businesses, governments and civil society organisations address problems, add value and generate growth, in the context of a growing array of global social, environmental and technological challenges. This is generally described as 'mission-oriented' innovation, where innovation policies, practices and investment are centered on achieving large, inter-sectoral challenges, such as those at the heart of the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The course introduces participants to the opportunities mission-oriented innovation creates for generating smart, sustainable and inclusive growth. Participants will embark on designing and evaluating an innovative project that could potentially contribute to responding to challenges as diverse as growing inequality, ageing populations, adapting to climate change and declines in biodiversity.
title: Innovation for Impact
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Business success is highly dependent on the effectiveness of the selling process, sales management and business negotiation. This course will provide the knowledge necessary for students to understand the selling process and be able to apply key principles of successful sales management. It provides an introduction to personal selling, as well as a detailed analysis of the selling process, environmental influences, business negotiation, estimating demand, account management and sales force management including the recruitment, selection, training, motivation and performance of salespeople and control of the selling effort.
title: Sales and Negotiation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The course further extends students' proficiency in all four macro-skills, enhancing students' competence in speaking, listening, reading, and writing, their vocabulary and understanding of Italian grammar. Class work draws on texts from a variety of media and Italian short stories. Through the study of these texts, the course also aims to further develop students' understanding and familiarity with Italian culture and society. The course is offered on-campus or online, with one 3-hour workshop per week. Prerequisites: 2090LHS Italian 2A OR 2190LHS Italian 2A (Enhanced) OR equivalent. Co-requisites: NIL; Incompatible: 2092LHS Italian 2B Written.
title: Italian 2B
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides students with foundational skills and methods used in contemporary design practice. Using techniques such as observation, journey mapping and problem framing, students develop skills in creativity design thinking, idea generation, iterative testing, and documentation. The course emphasises collaboration, with students working in teams to address "wicked problems" through iterative design responses. Students learn problem solving methods, refining concepts based on feedback and testing.
title: Design Studio 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course provides a solid foundation for moving your sketch ideas into 3D tangible outcomes. From here you will begin to understand the influence the design of 3D Products have on the experience of those interacting with them. It covers the fundamental principles and elements of 3D design, and the positive role product and UED designers have on society, the environment, contemporary, and future culture. Through studio-based projects, you will be introduced to core 3D design materials, methods, and processes. Gain insight into 3D digital modelling, laser-cutting, 3D printing and sketch prototyping. You will learn how to respond to a design brief, meet design criteria, and apply reflective practice to strengthen your design decision making. By the end of the course, you will have developed the skills needed to communicate core 3D concepts through tangible and experiential prototypes to a new audience.
title: Introduction to Product and User Experience Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This advanced-level capstone course is designed to prepare students for industry by providing a structured framework to demonstrate career readiness through one of four professional pathways: freelancing, employment, research, or entrepreneurship. A key feature of the course is its strong industry alignment, with students encouraged to source their own Work Integrated Learning (WIL) opportunities, collaborate with external partners, or receive feedback from professional mentors. The course culminates in a major project that demonstrates the student's creative leadership, industry readiness, and ability to define, develop and deliver a meaningful body of work that positions them for transition into their chosen industry pathway.
title: Design Studio 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Video games are often the first virtual environments people engage with, whether these are 2D platformers, 3D shooters, puzzlers or eXtended Reality (including virtual and augmented reality) environments. Building these environments requires a diverse skill set, including creativity, human-centered design, modelling knowledge, and development knowledge including object-oriented principles, mobile design, gamification best practice, technical frameworks and graphics engines. This course utilises advanced techniques and frameworks to engage students with key ideas in game/XR design, programming, architecture and the reuse of game engines, to develop a fundamental knowledge and skills required to create interactive digital environments that engage users.
title: Advances in XR Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The planning, implementing and evaluating of major sport events is characterised by dynamic management environments that bring together a wide array of stakeholders. Large multi-sport events present both logistical and organisational challenges for host cities, as well as opportunities to plan for and create a range of short- and long-term benefits and event legacies. This course will introduce students to the complexity of managing major sport events. Students will study a number of planning, operations and event legacy management issues across the life span of major sport events, from the bid phase to event evaluations. This course will offer students practical as well as theoretical insights into the dynamic and at times challenging nature of sport event management.
title: Sport Event and Facility Planning
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The mass media have a unique fascination with sport. Sport obtains its own section in newspapers, as well as in radio and television broadcasts. There are numerous magazines devoted to sport. Coordination of relations between sport organisations and media has become a specialised realm of sport management. Sport organisations coordinate their media relations through the Sports Information Director (SID) or media liaison officer. That person is responsible for developing relations with reporters and editors, formulating a media plan, and providing information to the press. Sport information is a pivotal component of the sport organisation's marketing communications campaign.
title: Sport Digitisation and Communication
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course focusses on the application of innovative new technologies across the supply chain network. Currently, for-profit and non-for-profit businesses are increasingly using new technologies to simultaneously improve efficiency and deliver flexibility across supply chains. Specifically, this unit discusses the application of artificial intelligence (AI), blockchain, automation, big data and internet of things (IoT), as well as the use and result interpretation of optimisation packages for supply chain management.
title: Supply Chain Innovation and Optimisation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course presents advanced topics in microeconomics. The aim is to ensure that students have a full understanding of the micro-foundations of economic analysis and policy-making. In this course the student will develop skills to translate real world issues into economic framework, evaluate them using economic theory to develop comprehensive outcomes/policy inferences.
title: Micro Foundations of Markets and Behaviour
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course provides students with a broad overview of personal financial advice and the role of financial advisers in a dynamic environment. Students apply the knowledge and skills covered in this course to discussions of contemporary issues, such as ethics, regulation, technology and government policy, and authentic financial planning tasks.
title: Financial Planning 1
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course continues to develop the issues examined in Business Logistics and provides conceptual models for students to define, measure, manage, control and develop effectively the material and information flows throughout a supply chain. Topics may include: business strategy, policy and processes; information flows; managing information; accounting for flows of goods and services; purchase planning; existing channels; risk and cost positioning; pricing, and costing and strategic involvement.
title: Operations Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The subject begins with a broad examination of cybercrime and moves to a specific focus on cyber fraud. The course explores contemporary criminological theoretical approaches to explaining cyber fraud, analyses offender methodologies and examines cyber fraud victimology. The course addresses contemporary approaches to prevention and enforcement in Australia and across the world. The role of relevant government, law enforcement, regulatory agencies and the corporate and private sector in the prevention and detection of cyber fraud is addressed.
title: Understanding and Preventing Cyber Fraud
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: In this course, you will learn the communication, physical examination and procedural skills related but not limited to the gastrointestinal, endocrine, and reproductive systems. You will also engage in work-integrated learning opportunities to put your Clinical Skills into practice. Clinical practice courses emphasize hands-on learning and supervised skill development, which cannot be fully achieved through independent study. Therefore, attendance is mandatory for all sessions. Students must meet both of the following attendance requirements to progress: Minimum Attendance Requirements At least 80% of total sessions (15 of 18) AND At least 70% attendance in each module: Communication skills: 4 of 5 Physical examination skills: 4 of 5 Procedural skills: 3 of 4 GP teaching: 3 of 4 WIL (e.g. placements): Successful submission of the ITA. Note: Session numbers may vary depending on delivery, and attendance thresholds will be adjusted proportionally. Monitoring and tracking attendance are the student's responsibility. No warnings will be issued when a student approaches or reaches the non-attendance threshold. Students arriving more than 10 minutes late or leaving more than 10 minutes early will be marked absent, unless exceptional circumstances are documented. Permissible vs. Unexplained Absences: Permissible absences (up to 20% for the course and 30% per module) apply only to exceptional circumstances such as illness, emergencies, or other valid reasons. Please refer to MD Guidelines for details. These must be reported promptly through the Student Absence Form (available in Course Essentials) and supported by appropriate documentation (e.g., a medical certificate). Where appropriate, the Course Convenor may assist students with approved absences by offering alternative sessions, subject to availability and class capacity. These sessions are for skill attainment only and do not count toward attendance requirements. No provisions will be made for unexplained absences, and individual remediation sessions cannot be arranged.
title: Introduction to Clinical Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course will further your knowledge of health of Australia's First Peoples. You will also learn about essential critical appraisal skills for evaluating research evidence in clinical and public health contexts.
title: Community Medicine and Professional Practice 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: 'Studio Making' is a temporary course open only to those students who have already completed a 10CP Major 4 courses (pre-2025). Following from 'Studio Thinking' this course supports students to create artwork for and to participate in the Graduate Exhibition. The course is co-taught with the 2025+ Major 4 courses in Painting, Photography and Sculpture, Performance and Installation, attending 2 hours of Major 4 courses in the morning (10am-12 noon) and 1 hour of cross-disciplinary lecture in the afternoon (4-5pm). This cohort will also be supported and assessed by the 'Studio Making' convenor/lecturer. Note: - Students must have completed Studio Thinking, preferably in T1 of the same year. - This course should be undertaken only when a student will participate in the Graduate exhibition in their third year. - Students who have not yet completed a 10CP Major 4 course from 2025 onward are not eligible for enrolment in this course and should instead enrol in the 20 CP Major. - Students who have completed a 20CP Major course are not eligible to enrol in this course.
title: Studio Making
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course will introduce students to the fundamental theoretical and practical principles of the chemical sciences. This course provides the foundation to future chemistry courses and introduces students to working with a chemical laboratory. Students will be encouraged to develop problem-solving skills and apply these to the solution of real-world chemical problems. Assessment is by self-assessment quizzes, laboratory reports and examinations. Incompatible: 1021SCG Chemistry IA, 1023SCG Chemistry 1, 1001MSC Chemistry of Biological Systems I.
title: Chemistry I
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will discuss chemical properties and the mechanisms of chemical change, with everyday examples from environmental science and medicine. It covers core chemistry concepts in a biological and physical context in the areas of organic chemistry, inorganic chemistry and the energetics of matter and living systems.
title: Chemistry II
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Hearing directly from people with disabilities about their lives is vital to good research, effective policy and compassionate, sound practice. This course exposes students to the lived experiences of people with a disability from the 'insider perspective', as well as exploration of theoretical, philosophical and historical standpoints of disability. Students will learn about the National Disability Insurance Scheme, in addition to examining disability equity and access issues in health, education and ageing. This course requires a commitment from students to be open to fresh perspectives of understanding the experiences of disabled people. Such openness is essential in advancing the rights, dignity and opportunities of people with disabilities.
title: Effective Disability Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course constitutes part 2 of a 2 part project in which students will produce a recital or folio of compositions, informed by an artistic research framework. Students engage in a combination of individual practical sessions in performance or composition alongside theoretical artistic research workshops.
title: Artistic Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Exegesis 1 is part one of the Masters research commitment. The course is the first of two 20cp components. Assessment of the two courses will culminate in a single submission for examination at the completion of part two. The combined components introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within visual practice. The Exegesis will consist of a major research project accompanied by an exegesis of 5000 words (min). The expectation is that the research project will be based within the visual and exhibits high levels of visual literacy.
title: Exegesis 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course is the first of two (practical/research) project components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigor of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within design innovation.
title: Major Project: Specialisation
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course invites students to work with industry and community groups to create real world public art outcomes. With a focus on large-scale wall paintings, students will develop public artworks that engage with histories of place. Public Art 1, 2 and 3 cover range of theoretical and practical skills integral to collaborative public art projects including concept, artwork and communications development. By encouraging students to link their individual studio practices with these industry-based projects, students will develop important skills for extending their practices beyond the studio setting.
title: Public Art 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This laboratory-based course focuses on fixed prosthodontics and advances the practical skills developed in previous laboratory courses. Students integrate existing theoretical knowledge and technical competence to analyse cases and plan, construct and evaluate fixed dental prostheses. Through work-integrated learning, students undertake increasingly complex laboratory activities and provide an expanded range of dental laboratory services for the Griffith University Dental Clinic. These authentic learning experiences support the continued development of technical accuracy, efficiency, professional judgement and accountability. Students also strengthen their capacity to communicate, collaborate and contribute effectively within a professional dental team. Students must also be enrolled in 3031DOH, 3121FPH and 3220DOH.
title: Laboratory Practicum 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Professional Practice 2 simulates private practice and continues to develop a critical understanding of the principles, techniques and materials applied to the practice of dentistry. Students will attend professional practice sessions to enable them to apply knowledge and further develop clinical competence. All year 1 courses (commonly known as year 4) must be successfully completed prior to proceeding to year 2 (commonly known as year 5) courses.
title: Professional Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Advanced Dental Hygiene Practice 2 is designed to give the student a deeper understanding and practice in a clinical environment. The course provides students with the opportunity to learn and practice along side other students preparing for dental specialties. Students will apply the principles of patient care and practice management required to achieve a high level of clinical proficiency in the provision of dental hygiene care. Students must have completed 3036DOH Advanced Dental Hygiene Practice 1 to enrol in this course.
title: Advanced Dental Hygiene Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This capstone course examines the financial crime investigation and compliance issues faced by major Australian Financial Institutions. This includes the investigative mindset required for monitoring and reporting suspicious behaviour, as well as the vital role each staff member plays in the prevention, detection, and resolution of financial crime. Incorporating insights from Criminology, Forensic Accounting and Data Analytics, this applied course is designed to equip students with the latest techniques in financial crime investigation and compliance practices.
title: Applied Financial Crime Investigation and Compliance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course critically examines core Planning theories, practices and ethics, equipping students to analyse how planning theories and practices shape cities across historical and contemporary contexts.
title: Planning Theory and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course, you'll have the opportunity to participate in hands-on interior and spatial projects alongside a variety of stakeholders, including NGOs, government departments, community groups, and councils, all aimed at creating tangible and lasting impact. Within our vibrant studio setting, you'll work closely with fellow student designers, receiving guidance from experienced industry professionals. Together, you'll work on a wide range of design challenges, drawing upon your collective skills and expertise to develop innovative design solutions.
title: Livespace
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: An introductory biomechanics course designed for Exercise Science and Clinical Exercise Physiology students. In this course, you'll learn about the fundamental physics that underpins human movement and practical ways to measure and analyse a range of clinical and athletic tasks. Whether you're interested in performance, injury prevention, rehabilitation, or simply understanding the human body better, this course will equip you with essential knowledge.
title: Introductory Biomechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This clinic placement runs in partnership with our Community Legal Centre partners for a day a week during the Trimester. Attendance at your centre on the allocated day of the week is compulsory. Students will assist clients who rely on Community Legal centres to access justice, promoting social justice and inclusion. This course invites you to move out of your comfort zone, acquire practical legal skills in a supportive environment, and to challenge yourself professionally and personally. You will be guided and supported by experienced supervisors and will finish the clinic with a real sense of accomplishment. Students report that work integrated learning {WIL) makes them more employable, and employers back this up, reporting WIL favourably influences their perception of students' abilities. Students say WIL helps them assess their career direction, complements their learning, increases their networks, increases their motivation to study and helps them prepare for future employment.
title: Social Justice Lawyering 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course examines the role of the game designer by introducing participants to the fundamental skills and knowledge associated with contemporary game design and production. In this course, students will explore and analyse established game design principles and apply them in the creation of tabletop and digital games. Participants in this course will gain practical experience and a foundational understanding of the critical concepts related to designing games.
title: Introduction to Game Design and Production
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course simulates the experience of working in a professional game development studio. In an intermediate role, students will take on complex tasks in-game production and work in small teams to create fully functioning video games from initial concept to launch while engaging with industry professionals. In this course, students will gain experience in all aspects of game development, including the social, cultural, and ethical implications of producing games. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies and receive guidance and feedback from experienced game development mentors. Guest lectures and engagement with the games industry will provide students with a deeper understanding of game development and its potential career opportunities. At the end of this course, students will have developed a polished, playable game, focusing deeper into the technical aspects of game development and beginning to specialise in areas such as programming, game art, animation or virtual production.
title: Game Studio 2: Intermediate
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The course is the first of four Masters (practical/research) project components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within design innovation. This project will consist of a major research/practice project accompanied by a designed report. The expectation is that the research/practical project will be based within and extend the student's existing creative research/practice and incorporate high levels of design/strategic literacy.
title: Masters Design Project 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course is the third of four Masters (practical/research) project components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within design innovation. This project will consist of a major research/practice project accompanied by a designed report. The expectation is that the research/practical project will be based within and extend the student's existing creative research/practice and incorporate high levels of design/strategic literacy.
title: Masters Design Project 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course develops advanced animation skills for professional studio-based production using industry-standard tools and processes. The course focuses on developing high-quality character animation incorporating character profiles, acting, performance, emotional engagement, and timing techniques for 2D, 3D and stop-motion animators.
title: Character Animation: Applied Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course is for aspiring 3D environment artists and 3D immersive environment designers. In this course, students will learn the techniques and tools necessary to design and create immersive, detailed virtual landscapes and environments for games, films, 3D animation, and VR applications. Participants in this course will acquire the essential skills and knowledge required to actively participate as a 3D environment artist in a professional production environment.
title: Immersive Worlds: 3D Environments
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course allows students to develop a strong understanding of the curriculum areas and learning trajectories of science, technology, engineering, arts, mathematics and social and environmental education with young children. Students will create and implement learning experiences and engage in intentional teaching to support high quality learning experiences with young children. Students will also complete 20 days of placement with children aged 3-5 years as a block placement (weeks 11-14). 80% of attendance is required at synchronous classes with 100% engagement with course materials.
title: Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics and young Children (STEAM and Young Children)
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course allows students in the Pedagogy Major to put knowledge and skills developed into practice. Students will learn through peer-partnership lessons and will bring together coursework studies in the form of a Lecture/Recital presentation.
title: Performance and Teaching Practice
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Studio Immersion is a visual arts practice based course. Students will be introduced to foundational contemporary visual arts practices and will create works and undertake research for presentation. Lectures and tutorials will be studio specific and students are required to engage with, and gain knowledge and foundational expertise of their chosen studio specificity.
title: Studio Immersion 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: In this course, students demonstrate the high-level performance and/or creative practice skills developed through the program. Students engage in a combination of individual practical sessions in performance or composition alongside artistic research workshops. Note: There is a sequential relationship in the Principal Study courses. Students develop their potential as artists through this progression.
title: Principal Study Capstone
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course explores the computerized modelling, analysis, and control of transmission and distribution systems. It covers steady-state analysis in power systems, including load flow and optimal load flow analysis. Additionally, the course addresses the dynamic behaviour of power systems, covering balanced fault analysis, asymmetrical fault studies, and power system transient stability.
title: Electric Power Systems and Control
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course explores how language-related digital technologies are reshaping the way we communicate, learn and conduct research. It investigates linguistic technologies across various domains, including AI, translation, language analysis and documentation, speech recognition, technology-mediated communication (e.g. social media and text messaging), and language teaching and learning. The course also examines the social and ethical considerations surrounding these technologies and provides the opportunity to reflect upon how we navigate these challenges and harness the many opportunities they present.
title: Digital Technologies and Language
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course delves into the intricate dynamics of international migration, ethnic relations, and the role of public policy in shaping migration patterns and addressing associated challenges. Through interdisciplinary perspectives, students will explore the historical roots of migration, Indigenous perspectives on mobility and displacement, and the evolving governance structures at regional and global levels. The course provides a nuanced understanding of the complex interactions between migration, ethnicity, and public policy, equipping students with analytical tools to navigate contemporary migration issues.
title: International Migration, Race Relations and Public Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This linguistics course examines the nature and function of gender differences in communication on a cross-cultural basis. The emphasis is on verbal language, but some attention is also paid to differences in nonverbal communication. The contrasts between stereotypes about how women and men communicate linguistically and the actually occurring patterns are carefully examined. The significance of different communication patterns is considered in connection with theoretical models drawn from sociolinguistics, anthropology and psychology. Topics covered include: Gender differences in linguistic forms (pronunciation, vocabulary, syntax, etc.); conversational patterns; issues of status and politeness; gender bias in language use; developmental aspects of gender-differential language use; case studies in language use (i.e., gender-related differences in legal language, in education, in the mass media) and strategies for changing sexist linguistic practices.
title: Language and Gender
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: In this first of a four-course series on Techniques and Practice, students will explore their potential as performers through sequences of practical classes exploring fundamental skills and techniques of acting focusing on Acting Technique, Actor and Text and Acting through Song.
title: Acting: Tech and Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course consolidates research into career opportunities nationally and internationally. Students will develop individual career plans, finalise graduation folios and resumes, and engage with international animators and industry experts. Through critical reviews of global industry trends, practices and protocols, students will prepare to graduate as industry ready global citizens.
title: Global Perspectives
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course advances students' knowledge, skills and experience in narrative form and structure, utilising the universal technique of visualising a story through storyboarding. Students' foundational learning in screen grammar will be extended via a deep focus on blocking, screen design and layout. Through the creation of script, storyboards and animatics, reflective analysis and peer-critique, students will gain advanced visual storytelling and pre-production abilities that will shape the development of future animation projects.
title: Visual Story
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This unit of competency specifies the outcomes required to perform detailed crime scene investigation of serious incidents in accordance with organisational policy and procedures.
title: Conduct Serious Forensic Crime and Incident Scene Examinations
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course simulates the experience of working in a professional studio environment across the cinematic arts. Taking on professional roles and responsibilities, students work collaboratively towards creative project outcomes following industry practices and processes. At the end of this course, students will have worked on high quality content towards a professional portfolio, be abreast of studio workflow and procedures, and be adept at working collaboratively with requisite professional proficiency.
title: Foundations of Studio Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: GFS Academies are intensive, immersive and industry-focused production experiences. In this course students will apply knowledge and skills in cinematic arts to a boot-camp styled production project. From idea generation to project delivery, students produce creative work by taking on specialist roles and working together within a fast-paced production environment. The focus is on application of learning where knowledge and understanding of craft skills is gained and reinforced through ready and active participation in practice within a mentored setting.
title: Cinematic Arts Academy
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: In this course, students will have the opportunity to work on industry-styled projects, either through a simulated industry setting, internship or project in collaboration with industry/community. The course allows students to apply their skills and knowledge within real-world settings and to anticipate future challenges in industry practice. Through work-integrated learning and mentorship, students will demonstrate an advanced capacity to lead with initiative and a high level of personal autonomy in their professional practice.
title: Practicum Project
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course focuses on the design, planning, and implementation of a group exhibition. Practical skills such as writing for exhibitions (gallery proposals, developing an artist CV, didactics and social media) will be developed. In conjunction, students will plan and implement an artistic project specifically for inclusion in the exhibition. The group show developed as part of Studio Methodologies will be on display at one of the QCAD Exhibition Venues (White Box). Students enrolled in this course are currently completing a Master of Visual Arts or a Graduate Certificate in Visual Arts.
title: Studio Methodologies
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Virtual production is an approach to filmmaking and content creation that uses real-time game engines to blend digital and live-action elements. This course introduces students to virtual production and associated technology such as motion capture, LED wall technology, camera tracking, and lighting in virtual spaces. Students in this course will develop a comprehensive understanding of real-time engines for virtual production and the cutting-edge techniques and technologies driving the evolution of filmmaking and content creation.
title: Introduction to Virtual Production
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This studio course comprises a thorough interrogative approach to drawing and the human body. The course combines practice and theory and considers the uses of the body in historical and contemporary drawing. Taking conventionalised forms of post-war life drawing as its problematic reference point, this course will systematically analyse the methods, biases and potentials of working 'from life' and introduce a contemporary and critical approach to the form. Students are expected to develop and extend drawing skills and concepts, and to initiate speculative drawing strategies. This course will blend retrospective and experimental methods of drawing. This course is open to anyone with an interest in learning drawing skills, developing knowledge and producing a folio of speculative and process-driven works within the specific context of the body.
title: Drawing and the Body
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course is the final design project in the civil engineering programs. It builds on earlier design courses and other engineering knowledge. The course involves a major 'real world' design project where students are encouraged to work in teams on a project. Students are also exposed to the project management aspects of engineering projects. The course brings together and further enhances a range of generic skills such as teamwork, problem solving and communication.
title: Advanced Design Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course explores how we navigate the social world. It focuses on the tension between structural inequalities and individual agency in contemporary society by examining issues of globalisation, class, gender and sexuality, ethnicity and race. Students reflect on examples of creative action and change to build a more just world. Incompatible : 1007LHS, 1014HSV, 1008CCJ.
title: Towards A Just World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is the first of a 4-course studio suite simulating the experience of working in a professional animation studio. Working in small teams, students will apply skills developed in associated majors and electives to a range of projects while engaging with industry professionals throughout the process. In these studio courses, students will gain experience in all aspects of animation production, including the social, cultural, and ethical implications of producing animation. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies and receive guidance and feedback from experienced mentors. Guest lectures and engagement with the animation industry will provide students with a deeper understanding of career opportunities across various fields. At the end of this studio suite, students will have developed high quality work towards a professional folio, be abreast of studio processes and procedures, and be adept at working collaboratively with requisite professional attitudes and practices.
title: Animation Studio 1: Associate
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course provides a foundation for students enrolled in Honours or Master-level programs with a research component. Topics covered in this course include research methods, research planning and management, ethical conduct in research, the philosophy and history of science, how to critically review research, how to write a research report, and how to present a scientific seminar. During this course, students will also develop the introduction of their research dissertation.
title: Research Proposal and Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science
