description: This subject examines the areas in which the criminal justice system and psychological theories of behaviour interact. Topics include the reliability of eyewitness testimony, truthfulness and credibility of witnesses, questioning child victims of sexual assault, the social dynamics of juries and the role of expert testimony. In this subject, we study the roles of various actors that interact in the courtroom, such as judges, juries, expert witnesses, eyewitnesses, victims and defendants. The unit introduces interdisciplinary literatures: criminology, law and society/socio-legal studies, and psychology. Topics include the social dynamics of juries, judicial discretion, the validity of forensic science and the role of expert testimony, the reliability of eyewitness testimony, an examination of mental health courts and indigenous justice, and the prevalence of wrongful convictions.
title: Law and Behaviour
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Foundations of Recorded and Live Sound is a second-year elective introducing students to core practices in studio and live sound applications that support a variety of creative contexts within modern music making. Learning is holistic and practice-based, immersing students in a range of approaches to instrument sound generation, genre conventions, and the relationship between artistic intention and production choices. Through individual and collaborative projects, students develop confidence, flexibility, and the capacity to contribute meaningfully to professional and artistic audio environments.
title: Foundations of Recorded and Live Sound
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This Industry Placement course is built upon Work-Integrated Learning (WIL) principles. Its primary objective is to enhance students' readiness for the workplace and boost their employment opportunities. The course provides students with the opportunity to participate in genuine work-based activities with industry partners. During these placements, students are mentored and supported in applying the knowledge and skills they have acquired in the classroom to the practical context of industry.
title: Industry Placement
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Organisations are under ever increasing pressure to attract, retain and develop employees that have high technical and professional skills. Managers need to be able to mentor, coach, and facilitate the leadership of individuals and teams within a context of supporting both employees and organisational outcomes. The success and effectiveness of the manager in relation to employees and organisational requirements is a foundation for the performance of the organisation, the retention of staff and the innovation and improvement of organisational practices. In order to do this the manager must have a realistic understanding of the nature of the work environment, its influence on individual and group performance, and the generation of and support for learning. These human factors have greater managerial and organisational impact when the above material is understood in terms of reviewing performance, enabling empowerment and delegation while understanding the cost and financial advantage of investing in both individual and group development.
title: Leading Teams
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will focus on the ways in which humans, occupational engagement and performance, and participation are located within a range of contexts. Students will be introduced to those contexts and the reciprocal relationship that exists between humans, occupational performance and engagement, participation, and the multitude of contexts (including social, political, economic, attitudinal, physical). This will enable students to appreciate the ways in which humans as occupational beings are contextualised, and the way in which occupational therapy practice is also contextualised.
title: Understanding the Context of Occupation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This theory based course expands on undergraduate dentistry-related topics. It has a multidisciplinary focus, and all activities will be shared amongst students doing different majors. These will include guest lectures, and journal clubs in areas that interconnect with Dentistry.
title: Interdisciplinary Advanced Dentistry 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In this course students participate in a project-based engagement with a real client. Projects are sought from a range of industry and university partners (project sponsors) that require significant development, communication and documentation effort. A project problem is addressed by a number of students working in a group to form a student project team. Significant importance is placed on effective project management and excellent communication strategies between team members, the project manager, and with the client. Students work in close liaison with their client and academic assessor throughout the project and are expected to demonstrate a good understanding of their project. To be eligible for this course, students must have registered online with the Griffith Sciences Partnership Office in the trimester prior to enrolment. Please contact wil-gs@griffith.edu.au to register. If your registration is successful, you will be given permission to enrol prior to the start of the trimester. Pre-requisite: Must have achieved at least 50CP which define the program AND 20CP from the major AND must have completed 7808ICT Project and Cyber Security Management OR must have completed 7002ICT Systems Development
title: Work Integrated Learning - Single Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course will cover important concepts in Data Mining including generating new information, discover patterns, and unlock actionable insights from data. Students will be introduced to techniques and tools in mining associative and sequential patterns, abnormality detection, correlation analysis, clustering, and forecasting.
title: Applied Data Mining
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course will focus on the pathophysiological basis, and clinical assessment, of a range of acute and chronic musculoskeletal and neurological conditions that are relevant to Exercise Physiology practice.

academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course explores the history and nature of Equity and its relationship to the common law, and covers equitable rights and assignments, estoppel, fiduciary duties and unconscionability. It also describes the law relating to trusts including informal trusts, family settlements, superannuation and managed investment funds. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.

academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This advanced-level course aims to hone your ability to define, specify, and produce design outcomes that are furniture-focused. Through studio-based projects, you will engage in collaborative design activity, critically evaluate notions of craft and mass-production. With a focus on construction methods, anthropometric data, material and environmental performance, applying hybrid forms of bespoke making and CNC machining to explore aesthetic and functional compositions. By the end of the course, you will be able to specify a product as fit-for-purpose and prepare a design specification suitable for third-party pre-production review.
title: Digital Fabrication: Objects and Furniture
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This immersive, introductory study tour takes you out of the classroom to explore real-world public health in a unique overseas destination. While specific travel dates and durations vary by destination, tours typically range from two weeks to a month. Travelling with an interdisciplinary group of students, you will participate in guided site visits, attend guest lectures at local universities, and observe community health initiatives in action. The aim of this field tour is to broaden your perspective and develop skills in field-based observation, critical thinking, and cross-cultural communication by seeing firsthand how public health operates in different cultural contexts. There are no formal prerequisites, although it is ideally not taken during your very first trimester of study. Please note: While the actual travel takes place during the trimester, mandatory preparatory activities occur before the trimester officially begins. Upcoming tours and EOI deadlines will be advertised via standard university communication channels. Due to limited places, students must follow a step-by-step approval process: first, submit an Expression of Interest (EOI) to attend an information session and learn more. If you decide to proceed, you must complete a formal 'Commitment' form to secure your place prior to officially enrolling in the course. Students keen to plan ahead for future tours are always welcome to contact the course convenors directly.
title: Applied Public Health Field Trip
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course will enable you to advance your academic writing and to understand impactful techniques for critically documenting, evaluating and reflecting upon the research process. You will learn how to generate effective and engaging content for communicating research across physical, social and online platforms, and to disseminate your research to professional, peer and academic audiences.
title: Communicating Visual Arts
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Mechanical Engineering Design is the creative development of mechanical products or systems. This course focuses on mechanical design through a project based learning approach. Students will work on a design and analyse (and/or build) project, developing a solution to a real-world engineering design problem. Assessment is done using a written design report, oral presentation/s, and peer group assessment when relevant.
title: Mechanical Engineering Design
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

The course investigates examples of this approach in education and professional practice settings and gives students practical tools to do their own qualitative research.
title: Qualitative Research in Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

title: Midwifery Practice 4: Complex Midwifery Care
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: In this course, pre-service teachers can acquire a theoretical basis for teaching science across the junior secondary years of schooling. Learning experiences in the course enable students to augment and integrate their existing knowledge with concepts about science teaching and learning and build a repertoire of appropriate skills and strategies. Current research on science learning and contemporary constructivist/conceptual change models are used to assist students to acquire pedagogical content knowledge and reasoning skills as a basis for their professional practice. Restriction: Students must be enrolled in either program 1567 (Bachelor of Education) or 5700 (Masters of Secondary Teaching).

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course introduces students to various accounts about English as a curriculum formation, currently available at international, national, and state levels. The course offers opportunities to develop knowledge about contemporary theories of text, meaning and meaning-making, concepts of print, visual, digital and multimodal curricula texts and contemporary theories of language and literacy and assessment that are applied in the design, implementation and evaluation of Junior Secondary Years English curriculum and assessment programs in schools.
title: English Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Effective public health initiatives require understanding the complex systems that determine population health and health inequities. This course uses a socioecological systems approach to examine how social, cultural, economic, commercial, and political determinants influence population health and inform public health initiatives to enhance health equity for priority populations.
title: Social Determinants of Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Communicating Design Ideas and Industry Software provides students with knowledge and skills to represent and communicate design propositions and ideas via iterative and progressive processes. The course has a specific emphasis on drawing, modelling and rendering for architectural and urban design. Students will be introduced to key software techniques used to digitally draw, model and render. The approach to software is instrumental to the development of critical skills and conceptual thinking in the presentation of architectural and urban design/planning ideas.
title: Communicating Design Ideas and Industry Software
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is aimed at undergraduate students wishing to develop greater understanding of some of the complex issues facing organisations today and in the future. As traditional sources of competitive advantage are being eroded, managing change and innovation is becoming a crucial factor in the survival and performance of business organisations. As innovation and technology are key drivers of organisational success, economic growth, and sustained business competitiveness, the effective management of innovation and technology should provide solutions and strategies to tackle major challenges such as climate change and responsible production and consumption from business organisations. As parts of this course, students will explore the following broad areas: competitive industry dynamics, sources and patterns of technological innovation, formulating and devising innovation strategy, and implementing strategy for technological innovation, and responsible innovation for sustainability.
title: Decision Making for Innovation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The course equips students with fundamental knowledge and skills on sensors and actuator circuits and systems. Sensors are a key component in modern Mechatronic products, providing vital information for control processing. Along with sensors, conditioning circuits are also important to process the signal and convert it into a form suitable for the controllers. At the other end of the system, actuators are vital to provide the mechanical output required for many applications. This course examines the peripheral hardware required to gather information for the controller, and allow the controller to generate mechanical outputs.
title: Sensors and Actuators
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The purpose of this course is to encourage language students to further enhance their international engagement by including short-term in-country study or cultural experiences relevant to their studies. Students may undertake work-experience, study tours, short-courses or other projects during a study abroad period. This is the 20-credit point version of 3191LHS Language In-Country Independent Study: the difference lies in the length of the in-country stay and the assessment. The course can be taken as part of a short-term study abroad program or in conjunction with an exchange program. Students will define the in-country experience in consultation with the course convenor and other academic staff from the students' program of study. The assessment is in the form of pre-departure tasks, an online reflective journal and an oral presentation, to be delivered on return in the language of the chosen country and/or in English, depending on the students' level of language proficiency.

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

The dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 60,000 - 80,000 words. The dissertation builds on previously studied research courses that have developed the student's understandings of research planning, research methodologies and research design.

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will be introduced to the skills required for effective learning and teaching of business in the senior secondary years of schooling. Emphasis will be placed upon understanding the relationship between the learner, school context, curriculum, pedagogy and assessment.
title: Business Education Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course offers undergraduate students an introduction to evidence-based policing, and it puts key principles into practice. It serves as an introduction to the terminology, ideas and scientific method associated with evidence-based policy and outlines the existing policing applications. Introductory weeks summarize the origin and goals of evidence-based policy. The course eases students through a range of practical weekly modules and answer questions that people have about evidence-based practice. For example, what does good science look like? How do I find reliable research on police tactics and strategies? How do I evaluate research on the police? How do you design a good experiment in policing? The course provides a practical guide for reading and using existing research in policing, but also a roadmap for developing one's own evaluation. The final weeks discuss concerns around evidence-based policing and explore what is in the future for this emerging field. The course is designed to deliver essential content for policing students and professionals alike.
title: Evidence-Based Policing, Policy and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is the first of two in Year 2 that will further students' understanding and application of the core knowledge, skills and attitudes of occupational therapy practice. Specifically, students will be introduced to the information gathering, goal setting and intervention aspects of the occupational therapy process, as well as professional reasoning. Students will consider this material as it applies to occupational therapy practice in low complexity situations and within the context of a team-based approach to service provision. Prerequisites: 1321AHS and Fit for Professional Practice Mandatory Requirements
title: Occupational Therapy Practice I
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: The Law of Armed Conflict (LOAC) is a practical scenario-based approach to the specialised knowledge and skills for research, professional practice and further learning in the law, theory and practice relating to that body of law which was conceived to alleviate human suffering in situations of armed conflict as well regulate the conduct of armed hostilities. Focusing on both means and methods of warfare provides the necessary background to understand how the law regulates the conduct of armed hostilities and the protection of the victims of war. Students will have an advanced and integrated understanding of the complex body of knowledge that is LOAC. This instruction in LOAC presents and compares the distinct legal regimes governing international and non-international armed conflicts and the trajectory of convergence between these two bodies of law. The course provides specialised knowledge and skills for research, professional practice and further learning regarding: the content and historical development of LOAC in order to outline the origins of the current state of the law and the legal and practical challenges arising from contemporary situations of armed conflict; the implications basic characteristics of LOAC and its interrelation with other legal frameworks; how the temporal, personal and geographical scope of LOAC's application is constructed; LOAC governing the conduct of hostilities, the protection of the main categories of person affected by armed conflicts, namely the wounded and sick and the medical mission, those deprived of their liberty, and civilians in territory controlled by the enemy and why that is.
title: Law of Armed Conflict
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Griffith Phys is a Griffith University Head Start At School course. Griffith Phys is an online, two-year, part-time university course for Year 11 and 12 students. Complementing and building on Senior Physics delivered at school, Griffith Phys enables students to experience an integrated university course whilst completing their senior high school studies. 1306NSC_Y1 is the Trimester 1 component of Stage 2.

description: In this course you will be introduced to the skills required for effective learning and teaching of music curriculum in the junior secondary years of schooling. title: Music Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Through the study of a range of texts - written, visual, and audiovisual materials - and the contexts in which they were produced, the course aims to develop both linguistic and sociocultural competence. In addition to prescribed class materials, students undertake the independent reading of an Italian novel. The course integrates textual analysis with the examination of key social, cultural, and political issues in contemporary Italy as reflected in these texts. Grammatical structures are explored through guided analysis of examples drawn from the texts, as well as in response to student needs. Students actively participate in oral discussions of key themes and issues, and further develop their skills and understanding by conducting independent research and sharing their findings with peers. Prerequisites: 2096LHS Italian 2B or 2196LHS Italian 2B Enhanced (or equivalent). Incompatible: 3294LHS Italian Literature and Society Enhanced.
title: Italian 3A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This subject examines the major, cutting-edge questions for criminology today. These include penal politics, policing, justice and the media, restorative justice, youth crime, and state crime. It introduces students to the contemporary key thinkers and contributors in the field in Australia and overseas. Attention is given to the relationship between research, policy, and politics in linking knowledge to social and systemic change.
title: Justice and Crime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The subject considers the most widely accepted approaches, in Forensic Mental Health (FMH), to risk assessment. Subject content primarily focuses upon the prediction of an individual's likelihood of harming other or being harmed by others. Risk and protective factors are examined beyond that of a present based individual level to include an understanding of developmental and environmental factors. The utility and applicability of different risk assessment tools is also considered as a component of an effective functional analysis and more broadly risk management in Forensic Mental Health. Incompatible: 7049CCJ Risk Assessment and Management in Forensic Mental Health
title: Risk Assessment and Management in Forensic Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: In this course, students will further develop their abilities as agile professionals through developing transferrable skills within an industry-engaged project. Working in groups, students will act as "consultants" on a task that has been generated on behalf of criminal justice industry partners. This will require them to integrate the knowledge and skills from their program to a problem or issue of importance to the criminal justice sector and to provide a critical or creative output within a constrained timeframe. This will require students to continue to develop their skills in project management, engagement with experts and industry partners, and written and oral communication within a professional setting.
title: CCJ Clinic
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course provides a critical reflection on issues currently facing First Nations peoples, in Australia and globally, in achieving justice. Students will be exposed to Indigenous perspectives on justice through Indigenous-authored research that allows the lived experiences of First Nations people to be heard. Using a strengths-based approach, the course provides students to consider the intersections of history, culture and justice in the ways we have responded and should respond to crime.
title: First Nations and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course provides students with the theoretical underpinnings to meet the needs of neonates with complex care needs. The course considers the transition of the neonate to the extra-uterine environment, neonatal assessment, neonatal resuscitation, neonates requiring admission to the special care nursery, introductory concepts of caring for the critically unwell neonate and principles of family-centred care. This is a core course within the Bachelor of Midwifery and an elective course within the Bachelor of Nursing and is restricted to students of these two programs. All students are expected to have achieved a passing grade in undergraduate anatomy courses before enrolling into this course.

academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The aim of the course is to explain the way people behave and make decisions in a business environment and the role that information has in the context of decision-making. It will also tackle some of the critical questions around the use of information for business decision making: how to assess the validity/reliability and relevance of the information we receive, how to use it effectively, how to simplify information, make it relevant, and present it to different audiences.
title: Business Decision-Making
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: We live in a VUCA (volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous) world today. The grand challenges facing humanity are urgent, systemic, complicated, and evolving faster than ever before. That is why the World Economic Forum has listed complex problem-solving as one of the top ten skills for the 21st century. Complex problem-solving requires critical and lateral thinking, reasoning, analysis, interpretation, synthesising information, research skills, reflection, creativity, curiosity, imagination, innovation, perseverance, self-direction, planning, self-discipline, adaptability, initiative, teamwork, and collaboration. In this course, you will be exposed to concepts and frameworks associated with grand challenges and problem-solving techniques. Through interactive course materials and weekly workshops, you will learn by doing, looking at problems from different perspectives, applying (where possible) solutions to problems and grand challenges in a proper context, and learn how to effectively present your solutions.
title: Grand Challenges for Business
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course focuses on the resolution of international commercial disputes through arbitration (before arbitral tribunals). It commences with an introduction to the nature of arbitration and the different types of arbitration, and then takes students through the issues associated with constituting the arbitral tribunal, the jurisdiction of the tribunal to hear disputes, challenges to arbitration, the hearing itself, the rendering of an arbitral award and challenging and enforcing awards. Incompatible: 7502LAW/7602LAW International Commercial Litigation and Arbitration; 7512LAW International Commercial Arbitration; 5177LAW International Arbitration.
title: International Commercial Arbitration
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: In City Systems, students are confronted with the city scale and its network of facilities and services that support a community's healthy functioning. Students are guided through the process of critically designing a medium-scale structure that provides a positive impact city-wide and complements existing systems. A holistic view of the built environment is put forth. Students will adopt planning guidelines, community needs, aspirations, and sustainable development goals to inform design decisions that encompass their proposals' conceptual and compositional aspects.
title: Design Studio 5 City Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this course, students will be guided through the functions of management to explore the foundations of management. After exploring areas of planning, leading, organising and controlling and the underpinning management principles, the concepts will be contextualised in foundational and contemporary aspects of business including leadership, sustainability, and globalisation using topical modes of delivery and content. This course is recommended for all management students in the early stages of their studies as a platform to develop broader management skills.
title: Leading and Managing Organisations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The global tourism and hospitality industries are large, multi-faceted and complex, and represented by an array of stakeholders with both complementary and competing interests. The 'systems' perspective in this course has a threefold purpose: (1) you will learn about the key sectors and stakeholders in the tourism and hospitality industries, and the dynamic interactions which occurs between them; (2) you will understand tourism and hospitality as an economic activity connected to the socio-cultural, political, environmental systems; (3) you will apply a systems thinking perspective to create a graphical representation of a system problem to highlight the complexity of the tourism and hospitality systems, and allow you to analyse options for improving the sustainability of a tourism business within the global industry.
title: Global Tourism Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Transitional justice is a rapidly emerging interdisciplinary field of study focussing on processes dealing with past human rights violations and the transition to more peaceful and democratic states. This course deals with questions that arise in countries emerging from armed conflict or from periods of authoritarian or repressive rule. It focuses on strategies available to new democratic governments in the aftermath of a situation of massive violations of human rights to re-establish the rule of law and build sustainable peace. This course examines the evolution of transitional justice theory and practice, including truth commissions, trials and traditional practices, in such contexts as post-apartheid South Africa and post-genocide Bosnia, Cambodia and Rwanda. Issues discussed include the various types of justice, accountability, truth, reconciliation and reparations, and the challenges of balancing justice and peace. Case studies have been selected to highlight key themes and issues of transitional justice theory and practice consistent with the overarching questions considered during the course: how does transitional justice contribute to the rule of law and building democracy in post conflict and post autocratic regimes? The issues explored in this course include the apparent contradictions between pursuing justice and reconciliation; restorative and retributive justice; the interaction between imposed or introduced transitional justice mechanism and traditional, indigenous approaches; gender perspective; civil society and diaspora participation in transitional justice; and the tensions between government, civil society, local communities and outside interventions in designing and implanting transitional justice mechanisms.
title: Transitional Justice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Failure to keep up to date with employment law can lead to fines and other penalties. This course helps prepare you for a career in Employment Relations and Human Resource Management by building the skills necessary to navigate Australia's legal system. It begins with a review of the foundations of the legal system before examining the system of laws governing employment in contemporary Australia. Through this course, you will develop necessary problem solving skills to use in workplace settings. This course is not available to LAW students unless the student is also enrolled in a Double Degree Program majoring in Employment Relations and where it is undertaken as a compulsory course.
title: Introduction to ER and HR Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will enable students from both non-scientific and scientific/technical backgrounds to understand both the theory and practice of climate adaptation. Students will learn fundamental concepts in climate adaptation and be able to analyse critically adaptation projects and programs.
title: Climate Adaptation Theory and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides an advanced treatment of two key areas covering much of mechanics, specifically the motion of macroscopic systems (rigid bodies, springs, planets etc.), and the behaviour of collections of microscopic particles. Analytical mechanics is a collection of advanced formalisms for classical mechanics, describing the kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies and systems. Teaching covers planetary motion, rotational dynamics, Lagrange's and Hamilton's equations. This provides the mathematical framework for dealing with systems with many degrees of freedom, and links to the Hamiltonian in quantum mechanics. Building on this, and on elementary knowledge of thermodynamics, the latter part of the course will introduce statistical mechanics. This can give an understanding of real substances, vital in the fields of nanoscience, nanotechnology, materials science and atomic/molecular physics. It covers topics including: the relationship between microscopic structure and thermodynamic properties: microcanonical, canonical and grand ensembles; entropy; chemical potential; equipartition; Fermi-Dirac and Bose-Einstein statistics, ideal classical and quantum gases.
title: Analytical and Statistical Mechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to municipal solid waste engineering. Its topics include municipal solid waste characteristics, storage and collection, transfer and transport, separation and processing, recycling, composting, incineration, and landfilling.
title: Solid Waste Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Cleaner production and circular economy can bring overlapping benefits to business performance by simultaneously increasing profitability, efficiency, competitiveness and environmental performance. Harnessing the economics of sustainable consumption and production that can drive these benefits requires expertise in understanding, communicating and then applying complex ideas and strategies. In this course, you will explore how to use various tools, including cleaner production planning and assessment, to achieve sustainability goals. With an advanced and integrated understanding of cleaner, sustainable practices you will be capable of promoting the uptake of resource efficient, cleaner production and circular economy practices. You'll be a responsible and adaptable professional with a global perspective, able to find solutions to complex situations using advanced problem-solving skills that will help us move towards being a sustainable society with clean air and clean water and prosperous businesses. This course is aligned strongly to Sustainable Development Goal 12 on responsible consumption and production.
title: Cleaner Production and Circular Economy
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Cyber Security Standards and Operations: Building Organizational Resilience. Organizations today face a growing number of cyber threats. This course equips you with essential knowledge of industry-recognized cyber security standards and frameworks to help protect your organization's assets, operations, and reputation. Over ten comprehensive modules, you'll gain practical insights into risk management strategies, information security systems, and effective security controls. Whether you're new to cyber security or looking to enhance your existing skills, this course provides a solid foundation for navigating the complex world of digital protection. We start by exploring the fundamental purpose of cyber security standards. You'll learn why aligning your organization's practices with industry benchmarks is crucial for maintaining a strong security posture. We'll dive into risk management frameworks like NIST RMF and ISO 31000, teaching you how to identify, assess, and mitigate risks to your critical assets. Next, we'll focus on Information Security Management Systems (ISMS), with special attention to the globally recognized ISO 27001/27002 standards. You'll discover how to establish robust ISMS processes, implement key security controls, and foster a culture of continuous improvement within your organization. The course then expands into widely adopted cyber security frameworks such as NIST CSF, NIST SP 800-53, and CIS Critical Security Controls. These powerful tools offer structured approaches to identifying and addressing cyber risks, allowing you to tailor security controls to your organization's specific needs. We'll also explore specialized security domains, including: - Identity and access management - Data protection and privacy - Network and application security - Security operations and incident response You'll gain practical knowledge in areas like authentication, authorization, encryption, data privacy compliance, network segmentation, web application security, secure coding practices, and incident response planning. Recognizing the unique challenges faced by critical infrastructure and regulated industries, we dedicate a module to sector-specific security standards. This includes guidelines from NERC CIP, SOCI, AESCSF, FISMA, HIPAA, ASD Essential 8, ASD ISM, NIST SP 800-171, PCI DSS, and the Zero Trust Security Executive Order 14028. The course concludes with an exploration of cybersecurity capability maturity models, such as C2M2 and the Essential Eight Maturity Model. We'll also discuss career paths, certifications, ethical principles, and professional development opportunities in the rapidly evolving field of cyber security. By the end of this course, you'll be equipped to: - Understand and apply key cyber security standards and frameworks - Assess and manage organizational cyber risks effectively - Implement robust information security management systems - Navigate sector-specific security requirements - Contribute to a culture of
title: Cyber Security Standards and Operations
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course prepares students for employment across criminology and criminal justice settings by developing professional awareness, practical insight, and reflective capacity. Through structured reflection and applied activities, students will critically examine their own values, strengths, and areas for growth, enabling them to articulate a clear professional identity and targeted development plan aligned with contemporary criminology and criminal justice careers.

academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

title: Introduction to Biostatistics
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Students will apply their learning from 7035LFC to their own teaching contexts. Students will work on their L&T project, culminating in producing outputs that disseminate and amplify their project findings for increased impact within Griffith university and beyond.

description: Broadcast journalism covers news writing and production for radio, television and other digital platforms. It builds on the audio and visual production skills students were introduced to in the core course and applies them to a professional newsroom context.

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores the creation and realisation of music, including traditional and emerging instruments/technologies. academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: My Life as a Musician is a core course of your first year of your Bachelor of Music degree. During this time, you will have the opportunity to develop your critical inquiry and artistic research skills by exploring your developing identity as a musician, the lives and livelihoods of others' (past and present) working in a myriad of music interests, to allow you an understanding of how to sustainably manage the ecology within which we all exist, and how to thrive throughout the developing trends that guide and shape musicians' futures.
title: My Life as a Musician
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will introduce students to substantive aspects of Canadian criminal law. It focuses on the distinctive provisions of the Criminal Code of Canada and their interpretation, as well as the role of the Canadian Charter Rights and Freedoms. The range of excuses, defences and justifications that apply to criminal offences will be canvassed, as will the important central concept of criminal responsibility. Incompatible: 5251LAW Canadian Criminal Law.
title: Canadian Criminal Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course examines key actors in international education by critically analysing their policies and practices. Students will explore how international organisations operate, are governed, shape global education agendas, and influence national reforms. The course covers multilateral aid agencies, UN bodies, philanthropists, NGOs, and bilateral aid agencies

description: Education is grounded within the complex interplay of historical, political, economic, and cultural systems and practices. Sociological approaches to thinking and researching education draw attention to how and why some are better served by education than others, while also revealing ways to minimise or address these concerns.

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to respond to industry client projects. Students will work in teams to design innovative solutions that considers client and stakeholder needs to contribute to solving the real-world crises. Student teams will be guided by industry mentors as they explore solutions-based opportunities and engage in design thinking. Through this course, students will develop their problem solving capabilities and understanding of how organisations can be responsive to the concept of sustainability. academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course builds on earlier Foundations of Medicine courses and focuses on developing an integrated understanding of the neurological, musculoskeletal, and mental health domains, while strengthening your ability to apply basic science knowledge to clinical practice. You will study the normal structure and function of these systems, as well as common and clinically significant diseases and trauma, with a strong emphasis on clinical reasoning and problem-solving. Throughout the course, you will continue to develop essential self-directed learning skills and progressively integrate anatomy, physiology, pathology, and clinical concepts through lectures, practicals, tutorials, and team-based learning activities. This course has a compulsory attendance requirement for Team-Based Learning (TBL) sessions. Students who are unable to attend a TBL session must formally inform the Course Convenor prior to the session that will be missed, or as soon as possible after the session, by submitting a Student Absence Form available in Course Essentials. Where relevant, a medical certificate or other supporting documentation should be provided. Attendance Policy for 8231MED Total number of compulsory activities per course: 8 (TBL sessions) Permissible absences with a valid reason: 1 Threshold number of compulsory session attendance for course progression is 6. You may have one valid, reported absence without being required to complete make-up work. If you miss a second TBL session (even for valid or medical reasons), you will have exceeded the permissible absences. In this case, the Course Convenor may require you to complete an alternative learning activity, such as a presentation or viva, to demonstrate your understanding of the missed content. The Course Convenor will determine the format, deadline, and whether the alternative activity meets the required learning outcomes. If the work is deemed unsatisfactory, further remedial activity may be required. If your total absences exceed the attendance threshold for course progression (more than 2 TBL sessions), you will be considered non-compliant with course attendance requirements, which will result in ineligibility to sit further examinations and failing the course, in accordance with the Course Profile.

academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Discourse analysis is a key skill for linguists, language teachers and anyone who is interested in understanding how the social world is framed by language. There are a variety of techniques and approaches to discourse analysis, which you will be introduced to in this course. The techniques will be applied to both written and spoken language, in a variety of contexts and text types. Some of the key domains we will focus on include media discourse, professional discourse, pedagogical discourse, and everyday conversation.

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: In this course students will develop an advanced qualification in creative writing by studying themes and issues in contemporary fiction through a selection of award-winning creative works. Students will explore a range of forms and styles of fiction and respond to these texts through discussion, analysis, and their own creative writing practice. The course focuses on the diverse aesthetic, stylistic and thematic approaches fiction writers adopt in their work, and students will develop their own skills as fiction writers in response to their engagement with course opportunities for feedback and critique, as well as through their own reading and interpretation of contemporary fiction. The course provides a lively and supportive framework through which students have the opportunity to gain deeper knowledge and understanding of the field, and to further advance their skills in writing across a range of fiction forms and styles. INCOMPATIBLE: 7119LHS Writing Contemporary Fiction.
title: Writing Contemporary Fiction
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Software design plays a significant role in developing software: during software design, software engineers produce various models that form a kind of blueprint of the solution to be implemented. Students will create, analyse and evaluate these models to determine whether or not they will allow fulfillment of the various requirements. Therefore, students will gain the command of the tools and techniques for software modelling, as well as describing software architectures. Such software designs specify the software architecture, that is, how software is decomposed and organised into components, and the interfaces between those components. Models should describe the components at a level of detail that enables their construction. Attention will also be given to the software architectures underlying user interfaces, techniques for designing and evaluating of the human-computer interface and techniques for creating and prototyping them.
title: Object Oriented Software Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course explores multi-camera live streaming. Building on the foundations covered in TV Studio Production, students will study the form, industry applications, technical requirements and logistical challenges of producing a live multi-camera production on location. description: This course explores the intricate elements that build a film's unique voice. Through readings, discussions, screenings and critical analysis, students explore how a film's form and style contribute to storytelling, the power of genre conventions and how revealing thematic layers enrich the film's meaning. By completing this course, students will have acquired an in-depth understanding of how stylistic choices in screen production work in tandem with narrative, thematic, and emotional goals.

academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course navigates the ever-evolving landscape of global screen culture, examining contemporary disruptions and future directions. From technological advancements to socio-political movements, students analyze how devices and disruptors reshape media consumption, production, and representation. Through case studies and discussions, students analyse and synthesise the implications of emerging trends, preparing to navigate and innovate within a dynamic industry.

academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: 1515ENG focuses on the human factors relevant to the employees of the aviation industry. It also considers the human factors issues of different departments within the aviation industry. academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Patterns of growth and development in the tourism and hospitality industry have long been influenced by innovation in technology - from modes of transport that facilitate travel, to the bespoke global distribution systems that connect the different segments of the travel, tourism and hospitality sectors. In this course, you will trace significant technological developments that have disrupted existing tourism and hospitality business models over time, and consider how technology influences the effectiveness of the overall tourism system. This course will also provide you with insights into leveraging technology to improve the economic, social and environmental sustainability of tourism and hospitality operations.
title: Tourism, Travel and Technology
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This block focuses on intelligent systems and computational approaches to large-scale data analysis. Students are introduced to machine learning frameworks and develop the skills to build, test and refine data-driven models.

academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: The Corporate Finance course involves three broad aspects: The financial management of companies; financial institutions and markets; and investments. These three aspects are interrelated and complementary. In Corporate Finance the central questions are: (a) What investments should you take on (b) Where will you get the financing to pay for your investment (c) When the business is successful, how will you share in the rewards. The role of the financial manager is to answer these questions. In order to acquire funds, a financial manager needs some knowledge of the operations of financial institutions and markets. Investments involve the allocation of funds once they have been acquired. Since the three aspects are so closely related, it is impossible to study any one of them in isolation.
title: Corporate Finance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: In this course, you will combine the theoretical frameworks of the tourism system that you have discovered from across the major, with your knowledge of historical developments and contemporary trends in tourism, to investigate issues of adaptability and resilience in the tourism industry. You will develop skills in forecasting and scenario-based planning that will enable you to provide customised advice to the tourism sector aimed at preparing for, and adapting to, future challenges and opportunities.
title: Tourism Futures
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this course students will be made aware of the contemporary practical applications of fundamental Economics analytical frameworks and tools, so as to better grasp the importance and limitations of theory as they enmesh with real world circumstances. Macroeconomics covers the second half, and studies the economy as a whole. Relevant modules include national income accounting (GDP), inflation, the role of fiscal and monetary policies in boosting economic growth and economic stabilisation, as well as looking at exchange rates and international trade.

academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Career Development is designed to promote and support students' professional and career development. This course will contribute to students' professional development through self-awareness exercises focusing on a range of employability skills. Hence, assisting graduates to effectively transition into the work environment and be future leaders. Hence, this course assists graduates to effectively transition into the work environment and be future leaders.

description: This course explores the history and cultural impact of video games, from the early days of arcade games to the latest trends in modern gaming. Students will learn about key milestones in the development of the gaming industry, as well as the cultural and societal context in which video games have evolved. Topics covered include the evolution of gaming technology, the impact of video games on popular culture, and the ways in which video games have been used to communicate ideas and express creative concepts. Through readings, discussions, game post-mortems and game play, students will gain a deep understanding of the history and cultural significance of video games.
title: Games History and Culture
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course introduces students to the principles, framework and institutions involved in international environmental law particularly as they relate to our use and consumption of water, air, soil and forest. The course focuses on the way that human beings are now responsible for transforming the Earth Systems and this course asks whether or not environmental laws are sufficient to avert potential breaches in planetary boundaries established by scientists to avoid irreversible harm. This course also studies concepts and doctrines from ecological economics such as ecosystem services as well as those in ethics such as environmental and ecological justice and enquires as to whether they do or should shape our approaches to international environmental law. This course is an elective for the Master of Environment.
title: International Environmental Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Exercise and Sports Science is a multidisciplinary field encompassing physiology, biomechanics, nutrition and the psychosocial aspects of human movement. In this course students will gain foundational knowledge that is key to understanding the health and wellness continuum between performance athletes and chronic disease patients. Theoretical and practical learning includes screening, exercise prescription and delivery and physical activity promotion and behaviour change across the lifespan. Students will also engage with employability activities to increase their understanding of, and engagement with, the fields of exercise science, exercise physiology and sports science.
title: Foundations of Exercise and Sports Science II
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This wide-ranging course is about how translation, in its diverse forms, works in global communication. This involves not only language competency and intercultural awareness but an understanding of genres, the translation industry, and the changing roles of digital translation. 2403LHS is not focussed solely on literature but considers factual texts, translation in journalism and entertainment, as well as subtitling, adaptations from one medium to another, fan translation and interpreting. No knowledge of a second language is required but students studying a language at Griffith will have the opportunity to undertake an assessment item relevant to their language of study. Incompatible: 3403LHS Translation as a Bridge Between Cultures
title: Translation in a Global World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

The online modules are designed to enhance your understanding of medically important microbes and their transmission, infection control measures, effective work practice and procedures and management of infectious diseases.

academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: The course further extends students' proficiency in all four macro-skills, enhancing students' competence in speaking, listening, reading, and writing, their vocabulary and understanding of Italian grammar. Class work draws on texts from a variety of media and Italian short stories. Through the study of these texts, the course also aims to further develop students' understanding and familiarity with Italian culture and society. In addition, students meet with Italian speakers out-of-class for language practice and to deepen their knowledge of Italian culture. academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: When mass atrocities are committed, who bears criminal responsibility? International criminal law's defining answer is: individuals (commanders, officials, militia leaders, foot soldiers) regardless of whether they acted through a state, alongside one, or in defiance of one. How international law identifies, prosecutes, and punishes those individuals (and where it fails) is what this course is about. This course introduces students to the substantive law, institutional architecture, and foundational controversies of international criminal justice. Beginning with the legitimacy debates that have shadowed the field since Nuremberg, the course moves through the core crimes and into the doctrinal complexity of individual criminal responsibility, jurisdiction, and procedure. It closes by asking whether the system, as currently designed, is capable of delivering what it promises.
title: International Criminal Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course builds on knowledge of statistical mechanics, classical and quantum mechanics to give an understanding of real solid substances, vital in the fields of nanoscience, nanotechnology, materials science and condensed matter (solid state) physics. It builds from an introduction to materials, crystal bonding, crystal lattices, reciprocal lattice, diffraction, thermal properties and electronic properties, including an introduction to metals, insulators, semi-conductors, to cover: the physics and mathematics of periodic solids; phonons; phonon specific heat; anharmonic properties of solids; point defects; diffusion; dislocations and the strength of crystals; and magnetic solids.
title: Condensed Matter Physics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This intermediate-level course will teach you to create meaningful digital products, systems, and services using User Experience (UX) and User Interface (UI) design. Through studio-based projects, you will engage with essential concepts such as Design Thinking frameworks, empathy and journey mapping, ontological and human-centred design, inclusive design approaches, storyboarding, wireframing, user testing, and digital product prototyping. By the end of the course, you will have the skills to strategically investigate problems from a user perspective and create thoughtful design solutions in response.
title: Design and UI/UX
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course offers a focused exploration into the realm of environmental criminology, a branch of criminology that examines the role of the immediate physical environment in influencing the potential for criminal activity. Environmental criminology operates on the principle that the environment can shape, facilitate, or hinder criminal behaviour, thus playing a crucial role in understanding and preventing crime. Unlike traditional schools of criminology that may concentrate on the sociological or psychological aspects of criminal behaviour, environmental criminology places a significant emphasis on the spatial and temporal distribution of criminal events in relation to the environment. The course will be particularly beneficial for students aspiring to operational or policy positions in crime prevention and control. It provides a practical approach to these ends, equipping students with the necessary knowledge and skills to effectively address and mitigate crime through environmental strategies. By understanding the intricate relationship between the environment and criminal behaviour, students will gain valuable insights applicable to real-world scenarios in crime prevention and policy formulation.
title: Environmental Criminology
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will develop students' understanding of clinical psychology in relation to health and disability. Students will develop knowledge and skills in models of practice appropriate for clinical psychology practice in health and disability.

description: This course will introduce students to the structure and function of the central and peripheral nervous system, with particular focus on the sensory and motor systems. Students will develop physiotherapy skills in neurological assessment of sensation, strength, reflexes, and balance. academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

It is assumed that the students possess the basic knowledge from the first two years in engineering mathematics, applied mechanics (statics and dynamics), strength of materials, engineering materials and manufacturing processes.
