description: This course is grounded in project-based learning i.e. problem-based learning with a project outcome. The project enables all enrolled musicians and composers to consider themselves as a "Performance Educator" and develop their skills required for this role. You will form mentored groups to design a performance education show aligned with a selected primary school grade music curriculum. The show will further espouse the West End State School core values of Creativity, Confidence, Challenge, Community and Compassion for which you will be performing. Pre-show teaching tasks and solo demonstration videos will form part of the requirements to ensure a highly engaged audience.
title: Community Outreach in Practice
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The course is the second of two (practical/research) project components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigor of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within design innovation.
title: Major Project: Application
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course builds on initial research undertaken in 7008ENG where students create an honours research project proposal. In 7901ENG Students are required to develop and progress their research project and produce an honours research project and exegesis. Prerequisites: 7008ENG Research by Practice Workshop 1 AND 7161 Research Design and Methods AND 7181ESC Exploring the Literature.
title: Research Portfolio and Exegesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Painting Studio 1 provides a conceptual, art historical and technical foundation for sustained painting-informed studio practice. Through a series of presentations, readings and studio-based workshops that draw from the history of painting from 1940 onward, students will develop confidence in working with painting as contemporary art practice.
title: Painting Studio 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Clinical Dental Sciences 8 develops a critical understanding of the concepts, principles and theories in Oral Surgery; Paediatric Dentistry; Orthodontics; and Special Needs Dentistry. Students to follow program structure this is essential to avoid any potential timetable / assessment clashes, focus on the important foundational underpinning knowledge in first year master's courses, ensuring the program structure flows to their benefit as to not create gaps in their knowledge.
title: Clinical Dental Sciences 8
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Dental Hygiene Practice 1 introduces students to the fundamentals of dental diseases for oral health and dental hygiene practice. The course enables students to developing dental hygiene practice skills. It presents essential content in oral health care team to provide preventive and therapeutic dental hygiene care. The Transition Through University (TTU) modules will be a compulsory part of the course to enable students to transform their learning into future action by reflecting on important professional attributes. Students will gain knowledge in infection control, sterilisation and examination and instrumentation techniques. Corequisites: must be enrolled in 1000DOH Dental Anatomy and Physiology
title: Dental Hygiene Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course focuses on developing student's quantitative and qualitative analysis skills which are useful in solving business problems, predicting trends, and forecasting markets. Students will learn through hands-on exercises and practical applications of statistical techniques to analyse economic and financial data and relationships.
title: Predictive Analytics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Professional Practice 2 simulates private practice and continues to develop a critical understanding of the principles, techniques and materials applied to the practice of dentistry. Students will attend professional practice sessions to enable them to apply knowledge and further develop clinical competence. All year 1 courses (commonly known as year 4) must be successfully completed prior to proceeding to year 2 (commonly known as year 5) courses.
title: Professional Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The course is intended to provide an overview of the main issues involved in performance management, including rationales for conducting it, the costs and benefits of performance management, alternatives to it and expected as well as unintended outcomes that may emerge from it. The history of performance management is examined. Different techniques for conducting performance evaluations are critically examined, as are the links between performance evaluation and systems of remuneration and opportunities for training and promotion. Finally the role of performance evaluation in different industries and occupations is examined.
title: Managing Performance and Rewards
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course provides an introduction to dental technology / dental prosthetic students on their chosen profession. An introduction to materials and construction of a variety of stages of dental prosthesis and appliances will be achieved. Students will also be introduced to basic concepts in chemistry to aid their understanding in dental materials. A hands-on approach will be taken with laboratory sessions as well as lectures to provide an understanding and evaluation of how different materials are used. This course provides the basic content of material science principles to the Bachelor of Dental Technology / Bachelor of Dental Prosthetics. The course also provides the foundation and framework to critically analyse materials and make informed choices when designing and constructing dental prostheses and appliances at University and in practice. The course also aims to provide basic knowledge of tooth structures, characteristic features and anatomical landmarks of both deciduous and permanent dentitions. It also helps them be familiar with nomenclature and structure of tissues they will be operating on later in their academic and professional careers. Students must also be enrolled in 1006MSC and 1008PSY
title: Introduction to Dental Technology and Dental Morphology
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores the dynamic relationship between scholarly inquiry and creative writing practice. As postgraduate students interested in gaining an advanced qualification in writing, the course will foster your understanding of what it means to pursue creative writing in an academic context. You'll deepen your understanding of key methods and approaches used in creative inquiry; receive guidance in developing creative writing within a research framework; be encouraged to explore the relationship between writing and wider social and cultural concerns, and explore writing industry practices. PREREQUISITE: NIL. CO-REQUISTE: NIL. INCOMPATIBLE: 7115LHS Advanced Research in Creative Writing.
title: Advanced Research in Creative Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course synthesises evidence-based responsive approaches to support diverse learning requirements across the full spectrum of abilities within special education contexts. Emphasising personalised, strengths-based interventions beyond categorical disability approaches, students will develop skills in adjustments and contemporary approaches.
title: Responsive Approaches in Special and Inclusive Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course advances students' appreciation and enthusiasm for the many and varied possibilities of the language of animation across genre, discipline, cultural and societal applications through the critical lens of animation history. Via research, analysis, readings and discussions, students will critically investigate animation within broader aesthetic, social, political, economic, and cultural contexts, ultimately developing the ability to assess and articulate how animations engage with social, cultural and environmental issues. Students will apply their knowledge and skills by pitching original concepts inspired by animation's history, contemporary issues and proximity to other disciplines.
title: Animation History and Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The course is designed both as an exercise in covering the theory and literature in the field, and as a vehicle for encouraging research in migration politics. With respect to theory, the course covers themes in comparative politics including mass political behaviour, parties and party systems, parliamentary systems, elections and electoral systems, representation, legislative behaviour, social capital, identity politics, political elites, citizenship frameworks and immigration policies. With respect to research, the course includes online tasks that are designed to help you engage in research on significant questions regarding the political participation of minority groups in Australia and in comparative perspective.
title: International Migration, Race Relations and Public Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Applied Skills and Knowledge for Social Work prepares social work students for practice by exploring health and wellbeing across the lifecycle. Students will learn applied knowledge and skills relevant to psychosocial needs, mental wellbeing, and safety and protection; related to infants and children, young people, adults, and older people. The course combines theory and practice skills from contemporary social work practice. Psychosocial needs include housing, finances, community practice, NDIS, My Aged Care, and psychosocial assessments. Mental wellbeing includes mental health assessment tools, Enduring Power of Attorney, Advanced Health Directives, and palliative care. Safety and Protection includes child protection, domestic and family violence, and Elder Abuse. Students will further develop their social work identity, ethical approach to practice, professional practice and intervention skills.
title: Applied Skills and Knowledge for Social Work
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is designed to introduce students to fundamental knowledge and the business implications of trade and strategy in an international context. A number of themes are prominent, including the globalisation of business and trade, strategy and its application to global business in its many forms, the multiple reasons why nations trade, commodity composition of trade, foreign exchange rates, trade and development strategy, investment across borders and global environmental issues. The application of trade and capital flow knowledge between countries will support student understanding of the global business environment.
title: Trade and Global Strategy
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course deals with the practical considerations of creating animated characters by focusing on aspects of acting principles and psychology that specifically inform the animator. The learning here provides advanced study in analysing and applying these theories to pantomime acting in character-centred assignments.
title: Character Animation: Acting and Performance
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The power of cinematic stories transcends language and culture. This course equips students with advanced knowledge and skills to craft compelling film, animation or games narratives that resonate with global audiences. Students will explore diverse themes that resonate across cultures and create characters and story worlds that represent the richness of the human experience. Insights into international co-productions, distribution strategies, and trends in global film, animation and games consumption will also be examined. By completing this course students will understand the opportunities and challenges of developing narratives for global screen audiences.
title: Stories for Global Screen Audiences
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course advances students' art direction abilities by specifically focusing on environment design. Through the study of layout, students composition, staging, spacial relationships, and visual storytelling, alongside figure and life drawing, digital drawing, speedpainting, perspective studies, colour and lighting principles, and screen design techniques. Students develop key skills in creating effective environments, backgrounds, and visual compositions for animation, games, and illustrative design projects.
title: Concept Design: Environments
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course focuses on advanced game programming skills and knowledge essential for leading development teams in game production environments. The course explores critical technical design and advanced programming topics such as version control, procedural generation, networked game programming, and programming for animated characters. Students in this course will select and focus on a specialised topic, conducting in-depth research to uncover and apply advanced theoretical concepts in creating gameplay prototypes.
title: Advanced Games Programming
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course provides a deep dive into the world of virtual camera systems and in-camera visual effects (ICVFX), technologies that are revolutionising film and broadcast production. Students will explore how virtual production combines real-time game engines and camera movements to create dynamic visual environments captured directly in-camera. Students in this course will learn the technical setup, operation, and creative applications of virtual camera systems and strategies for integrating 3D environments, augmented reality (AR), and virtual reality (VR) elements into live-action footage.
title: Virtual Camera Systems and ICVFX
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Industrial Design Capstone Project 1 builds on and extends the skills developed in the industrial design studios to develop an independent project that engages with emerging or future-focused themes within industrial design. Students will consolidate skills in design research, project management, and industrial design workflows to develop and lead a complex project to create innovative solutions relevant to industry standards. Prerequisite:1107ENG Industrial Design Studio 1 AND 2108ENG Industrial Design Studio 2 AND 2208ENG Industrial Design Studio 3
title: Industrial Design Capstone Project 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Through developing your skills of music research you will also be gaining a deeper understanding of the Australian industry and profession within which you now or in the near future will engage. You will gain an indepth understanding of arts policy, industry trends and potential futures.
title: Professional Music Research Strategies
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: In this course, students will begin to develop high-level performance or creative practice skills. Students engage in a combination of individual practical sessions in performance, creative practice or pedagogy.
title: Principal Study 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course introduces students to the theory, methods and practice for system modelling and advanced control. Mathematical modelling, systems analysis and advanced controller design are studied. Emphasis is placed on the design of PID controller, state feedback controller, optimal controller and state observer which are widely used in contemporary engineering systems. Practical experiments are designed to help students better understand the theory and design methods. Incompatible: must not have completed 6524ENG System Dynamics and Advanced Control.
title: System Dynamics and Advanced Control
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The increasing integration of power electronics and electrical drives into modern power systems is revolutionizing the way electricity is generated, transmitted, and utilized. These technologies are enabling substantial enhancements in energy efficiency, flexibility, and system reliability across the entire electricity value chain from generation to end-use applications. Global studies estimate that the widespread deployment of advanced and cost-effective power electronic solutions could reduce overall energy consumption by up to 35%, underscoring their pivotal role in achieving sustainable energy futures. This course provides an in-depth exploration of the theory, design principles, and advanced applications of power electronics and electrical machines, with particular emphasis on their role in emerging power and energy systems. Students will develop advanced skills in engineering analysis, system modelling, and design within the domain of power electronics and machine drives, preparing them for complex problem-solving in academic and industrial contexts.
title: Power Electronics and Machine Drives
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Studio Immersion is a visual arts practice based course. Students will be introduced to foundational contemporary visual arts practices and will create works and undertake research for presentation. Lectures and tutorials will be studio specific and students are required to engage with, and gain knowledge and foundational expertise of their chosen studio specificity.
title: Studio Immersion 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course explores the way theatre and drama can be used as a form of social justice intervention. It introduces students to essential facilitation approaches and techniques that can be applied in social justice contexts including theatre for arts and health, arts and justice, arts and eco-justice and arts and well-being. Investigating how theatre can be utilised to promote social justice and action, the course explores and practices how the dramatic form can promote meaning, efficacy, awareness and education for participants and communities.
title: Drama for Social Action
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Through close and creative engagement with the musical concepts that animate a vast range of musical contexts, this course functions as a lively way of studying music theory and developing aural skills. 'Music theory' is a catch-all term that encompasses many activities and perspectives: understanding musical structure and process; crafting a shared language to describe it; refining the skills needed to fluently hear, reproduce, invent and make critical determinations about the various music's we encounter. In this course, we will pursue all these activities in conjunction, through activities that span creative cross-collaboration and intensive investigation into style-specific materials.
title: Music Theory and Aural Studies 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides an introductory overview of screen production processes and crew roles, with an emphasis on skills development and teamwork. Through hands-on project-based learning, students will produce a short film, stepping through the fundamental stages of filmmaking becoming familiar with cameras, lighting and audio tools and learning how to translate a script into a compelling visual story.
title: Foundations of Film Production
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course advances students' expertise in post-production techniques and exercises their creative potential in developing stylised responses to briefs. Students will apply advanced compositing techniques for enhancing narrative and visual continuity, become adept in advanced compositing workflows, apply colour correction and colour grading principles, and have an advanced understanding of node-based compositing tools and workflows.
title: Advanced Post-Production
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This is one of two courses modelled as a community of practice, tailored to elevate the professional skills and career trajectory of creative practitioners in the cinematic arts. The course supports students in the advancement of skills, knowledge and approaches for the acceleration of their creative and professional ambitions. As a community of practitioners, through peer-to-peer discussion and exploration, mentorship, research, and practical exercises, learning will focus on honing key areas of expertise. Putting learning into practice through iterative processes, students will have an opportunity to refine their technical and professional skills in cinematic arts and to forge a distinct professional identity.
title: Career Accelerator 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This first placement provides 15 days of professional experience, allowing learners to begin to apply learning in authentic classroom settings. They observe students, trial short teaching activities, and explore foundational professional responsibilities. Learners continue to develop their emerging teacher identity by observing how experienced teachers manage learning environments and build student relationships. Learners also develop well-being strategies they can apply to themselves and to support their students.
title: Professional Experience 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is designed to introduce students to the role of dietitians and professional career options following the successful completion of a nutrition and dietetics degree.
title: The Nutrition and Dietetics Workforce
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: As a Bachelor of Musical Theatre graduate, you will have gone through many facets of training to become highly skilled, musically adaptable and equipped to enter professional life as a creative and flexible 21st century musical theatre performer.
title: Musical Theatre 6
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This studio course teaches approaches to drawing rooted in modes and methods of storytelling, experiences of time, and phenomena of light and dark. These investigations are both literal and symbolic. Students will learn histories and methods of narrative in drawing and also the practical and conceptual problems of darkness through methods such as magic lantern and theatre d'ombres. Students are expected to develop core skills and knowledge of conventional drawing materials and to extend skills and knowledge through speculative drawing strategies. This course is open to anyone with an interest in learning drawing skills, developing knowledge and producing a folio of speculative and process-driven works within specific contexts. Prerequisite: 1324QCA Drawing Foundations OR an equivalent introductory drawing course OR permission from the Course Convenor.
title: Dark Drawing and Narrative
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Identity continues from the first year Origins course with deeper investigations and contextualising of identity to create a body of artwork that is informed by your Indigenous perspective. This course is restricted to Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art students only. Prerequisites: 1011QCA Origins or 1111QCA Origins
title: Identity
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The Design Leaders Seminar Series explores emerging trends across various design disciplines. Industry leaders-emerging and established-share their expertise through talks and panel discussions, diving into areas like user experience, service design, sustainable design, and the integration of new technologies. Students will gain insights into design's evolving role in shaping human experiences, products, and services. This series provides a platform for designers to expand their knowledge, spark innovation, and connect with a community of forward-thinking creatives. By the end of the course students will acquire a deeper understanding of contemporary design fields and the skills needed to push boundaries and create meaningful impact, while expanding their professional design network.
title: Design Leaders: Seminar Series
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course will assist you in resolving the two major outputs of practice-led research in the visual arts: an exegesis and exhibition of creative practice. Seminars are geared towards both academic writing and practice development, with a view to equipping you with the tools required for documenting, critically evaluating and communicating your research. Topics include the writing and refinement of core exegesis writing components as well as appropriate methodologies for creative outcomes. The subject facilitates the communication and management of self- directed research projects with written and creative outputs.
title: Communicating Research in the Visual Arts
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Language, Culture and Society provides an introductory overview of the sociolinguistics of English-speaking societies, with a particular focus on understanding how language is enacted in social contexts and how social life is performed through language. The course begins by considering how language reflects social variables such as gender, social class and ethnicity. It then focuses on the use of English across social groups, including the analysis of register, speech functions, politeness, power and solidarity in interaction. Finally, it considers the place of bilingualism and multilingualism in English-speaking societies, and the reasons why some people 'code-switch' between languages when they interact.
title: Language, Culture and Society
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores the dynamic intersection of game design and production with culture on a global scale. Students in this course will discover how games are marketed and consumed differently across regions and what drives these differences. Throughout the course, students will research and engage with global game developers, game genres, and platforms to discover how they are produced, published, received, and transformed by different cultures around the world. Students in this course will develop a deep understanding of the challenges and strategies involved in producing and localising games for different cultural contexts as global citizens.
title: Global Games: Culture and Engagement
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Comprehensive Prosthetics develops a critical understanding of the concept's principles, and theories applied to the practice of removable dentures. Students will gain critical knowledge that supports professional practice to enhance employment and opportunities as a dental prosthetist.
title: Comprehensive Prosthetics 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course is the final professional practice education placement. Students will be allocated to a placement provider where they will work under the supervision of an occupational therapist for a period of ten weeks full-time (or a combination of full and part time where required by the placement provider). Students will be assessed using the Student Practice Evaluation Form Revised (Second Edition) (SPEF-R2). The course learning outcomes relate directly to the SPEF-R2 but the manner in which these are achieved will vary depending on the nature of the placement. At the completion of this course students are expected to be performing at the level of emerging student practitioner.
title: Occupational Therapy Professional Practice Education IV
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will prepare students with the knowledge, skills, and attitudes for practice education in contemporary contexts. You will have opportunities to observe practicing occupational therapists and develop self-management, communication, documentation, and teamwork abilities necessary for professional practice.
title: Introduction to Professional Practice Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: In this course you will continue to develop your knowledge, skills, and attitudes in occupational therapy, with a focus on working with individuals. You will explore ways of understanding the occupational issues facing individuals and barriers to health and participation. You will further develop your professional understanding through application of the occupational therapy process. This course will also examine topics such as client-centred practice, therapeutic communication, ethics, and professional reasoning.
title: Occupation, Health and Participation - Individuals
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is the first fourth year professional practice placement. Students will be allocated to a placement provider where they will work under the supervision of an occupational therapist for a period of up to 10 weeks full-time (or a combination of full and part time where required by the placement provider). Students will be assessed using the Student Practice Evaluation Form Revised (Second Edition) (SPEF-R2). The course learning outcomes relate directly to the SPEF-R2 but the manner in which these are achieved will vary depending on the nature of the placement. At the completion of this course students are expected to be performing at the level of emerging student practitioner.
title: Occupational Therapy Professional Practice Education III
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is a part time Professional Practice Education placement that provides an opportunity for students to examine the occupational therapy contribution to an emerging / future practice area. Students will be allocated to a placement provider, usually in pairs or small groups, where they will work under the day to day supervision of a member of staff at the placement provider. Students will also receive regular supervision from an occupational therapist. At the completion of this course students are expected to be performing at the level of beginning student practitioner.
title: Occupational Therapy Professional Practice Education II
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Fabrication and Construction is a practical skills-based course designed to equip students with foundational fabrication and construction skills pertinent to Visual Arts Practice. Students in all major areas would benefit from this course.
title: Fabrication and Construction
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course provides an introduction to pharmacology for dental practitioners, focusing on the fundamental principles that affect drug action within the human body. It is particularly relevant for those interested in dental care, as it covers drugs topics commonly used in this field.
title: Pharmacology for Dental Practitioners
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course explores the highly specific environmental issues associated with the aviation industry. It will introduce students to environmental principles, such as Sustainable Development Goals, climate change concepts and sustainable aviation fuels, and applies these concepts to the aviation industry.
title: Aviation and the Environment
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course will cover analysing large environmental datasets through multivariate statistics, spatial modelling techniques such as habitat suitability mapping, and data visualisation methods. It will also cover finding environmental datasets and preparing them for analysis. Students will be provided with opportunities for hands-on practice of these skills every week. They will also deepen their knowledge of the R language, as this course will be taught using R and RStudio. This course aims to prepare students for becoming environmental professionals, or researchers, working on environmental management issues using highly sought-after quantitative skills.
title: Environmental Data Analytics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Outbound Griffith Exchange students who are studying at a partner university must enroll in exchange courses for the trimester(s) they will be studying overseas. The tuition fees for each trimester will be determined by the course code(s), which considers the credit points and field of study. These factors are set by the Australian Government. This course is specifically tailored for both undergraduate and postgraduate students who are pursuing fields of study that include Professional Pathway Psychology.
title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

description: This course provides a foundation for professional communicators in the public sphere, including considerations of communication and professional identity in contemporary environments. This includes awareness of social and political change, diversity, environmental change and ethics and legal issues. This course introduces essential research and writing skills required for a range of media and communication roles and provides a foundation for considering which communication professions students wish to pursue.
title: Empowering the Professional Communicator
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course enables students to develop a critical understanding of ethics and professional practice in the contexts of journalism and strategic communication. It offers a highly practical, 'hands on' focus on ethical decision-making and social considerations in the workplace.
title: Ethical Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course equips students with the skills to identify patterns in information or source material; to make deeper connections and follow leads; and understand and visualise data. It introduces them to Freedom of Information investigations and journalism as a process of simultaneously uncovering and publishing best available truths.
title: Skills for the Investigative Reporter
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores the legal foundations and institutional pillars of the criminal justice system, focusing on how law, policing, courts, and corrections interact to respond to crime and deliver justice. Students will examine the structure, roles, and evolving practices of justice agencies in Australia, with particular attention to the experiences of frontline professionals and the people they serve. Key topics include the rule of law, discretion, due process, historical and contemporary developments in policing and corrections, and the challenges of delivering justice in diverse and complex social contexts. The course encourages critical thinking about the effectiveness, fairness, and reform of justice institutions.
title: Justice in Action: Law, Policing, Courts and Corrections
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will explore key concepts and characteristics of big data analytics, artificial intelligence fundamentals, the latest developments in ICT, and their application cases in building business strategies. It will help you understand how new systems are designed and implemented, and then decide if your business/organisation can take advantage of AI and machine learning technology to increase efficiency and resilience.
title: Introduction to AI and Data Analytics
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Personality psychology is the study of the whole person in their social and cultural context. Personality psychologists seek to explain the origin of human universals and to understand how and why people differ from each other. The primary aim of this course is to offer an introduction to the study of personality by surveying the major theoretical approaches to personality in addition to the latest findings from contemporary research. Prerequisites must be completed prior to enrolling in this course. It is the students' responsibility to ensure these requirements have been fulfilled.
title: Personality Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Building on Indigenous Media 1, the emphasis is upon establishing an independent practice. Students will be encouraged to pursue individual processes of inquiry and research in Indigenous media, placing emphasis on the integration of concept, visual expression and ways of making. Prerequisite: 1915QCA Indigenous Media 1
title: Indigenous Media 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Priority for enrolment into this course will be given to students in one of the following degrees: Bachelor of Marine Science (1328), Bachelor of Science (1018, 1210, 1330, 1634) with major in Marine Biology. Marine Megafauna and Planetary Health spans a spectrum from fundamental vertebrate biology and ecology, to investigation of major Planetary crises, their cause, environmental impact, and strategies for mitigation. Students will gain insight into how a species' unique biology/ecology may place it at elevated risk from human impacts, and how this sensitivity can be leveraged for effective ecosystem biomonitoring. Students will gain field experience associated with long-term monitoring of humpback whales. On the basis of their course experience, students will be challenged to develop conservation communication and action strategies.
title: Marine Megafauna and Planetary Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Acquire tools and understanding needed to help improve health outcomes for mothers across the globe. Through case studies, you will synthesise global healthcare knowledge and critically analyse social determinants of maternal health through a gender lens. You will evaluate strategies to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality and identify enablers and barriers to enhancing health outcomes, including what worked well in the past, what did not, and approaches to enhance future outcomes. You will investigate cultural frameworks and learn to apply Cultural Safety principles to enhance and transform your professional and collaborative maternal healthcare practices when communicating and working with women from diverse cultures. You will identify strategies to ensure your professional practice progresses toward congruence with the sustainable maternal health development agenda 2016-2030.
title: Global Maternal Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course deals with a range of project management concepts in the contemporary engineering workforce context. Students will be guided through their selected major project through a series of expert workshops and individual supervisor consultation to produce a project report on an advanced project management technique or tools' application in the engineering sector.
title: Project Management Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course examines China's evolving domestic politics and its changing role in global affairs. Students will explore contemporary political developments within China, the country's foreign and security policies, and its most significant bilateral relationships. Through the study of key political, economic, and strategic issues, the course provides insights into China's growing influence on regional and international politics. This course is offered at the Nathan campus in even-numbered years and at the Gold Coast campus in odd-numbered years.
title: China's Foreign and Security Policy
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This subject provides students with an opportunity to study the principles of human resource management, in particular the integration of functional practices and processes in systems that drive the achievement of the strategic objectives of the organisation. Health services are open systems and human resource management is a critical process for developing organisational competency to transform inputs into affective and performance outcomes. Health service workforces are highly complex and the environment is one of competition for resources, rapid technological change and high levels of community demand. The industrial relations environment is impacted by the dominance of the public sector in the labour market, high levels of union membership, rapid change and the culture of health professionals. Students will examine the interrelationships of workplace systems and the external environment and explore integration strategies to achieve strategic outcomes. The content of this subject will provide students with frameworks and models to analyse and develop strategies for the management of the health workforce.
title: Health Workforce Planning and Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course aims to equip you with the skills needed to conduct quality engineering research and statistical analysis of data, in both applied industry and academic contexts. As an engineer you will be faced with problems that require you to devise innovative and practical solutions. Being able to source valid and credible information, and analyse such information and data statistically, to formulate solutions to applied and theoretical problems, is a vital skill that all engineers need and which Engineers Australia expects you to have. Research is a key component in Postgraduate degrees at Griffith University, including for dissertation projects and other coursework projects you will undertake. Moreover, the skills learnt in this course are of vital importance to students who intend to pursue higher degree research studies.
title: Research Methods for Engineers
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides students with an understanding of the relationship between nutrition, health and exercise performance. Students will develop an understanding of nutrient metabolism during exercise and the role of food, fluid and nutrition supplements in enhancing exercise performance, training and recovery. Current nutrition recommendations for overall health and well-being will also be covered along with nutrition and physical activity guidelines for modifying body composition and preventing and managing chronic disease.
title: Exercise Sports Nutrition
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces students to numerical and computational methods for the solution of mathematical problems that cannot be solved in a straightforward way by hand using analytical mathematics. Topics covered include nonlinear equations, linear systems, data fitting via interpolation, differentiation, integration, and solution of systems of differential equations. This course also develops student skills in the use of programming to code implementations of numerical algorithms, as well as using industry-standard software packages for built-in functions and data visualization.
title: Numerical Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Arts Education 2 will provide students with opportunities to build upon the knowledge they developed in Arts Education 1 (Arts in the Early Years) and engage with the five Arts (Drama, Dance, Media Arts, Music, Visual Arts) - this time focusing on learners in Years 3-6. Here the intention is to deepen student knowledge, understanding and experience in the practice and appreciation of these Arts subjects while also developing an understanding of how children's skills and knowledges develop over time. Students will also extend their artistic development by exploring the way each Arts discipline can contribute to the cultural, intellectual, social, spiritual and economic life of communities. Within this course they will develop planning and implementation skills, as well as their understanding of the approaches to assessment that are unique to the Arts. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of professional experience placements.
title: Arts Education 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Experimental Writing takes what you thought you knew about creative writing and turns it upside down. As a third-year course in the Creative Writing major, Experimental Writing is an opportunity for Creative Writing students to spread their wings and explore far-off and hitherto forbidden (and forbidding) regions of creative practice. The course examines experimental theory and technique, and draws on literary histories of innovative poetry and prose. In the first half of the course, students are introduced to a rich field of experimental possibilities, and are encouraged to utilise these in the development of their own projects. Then, through ongoing discussions with their tutor and peers, students are supported to produce the boldest, most original and most unusual project of their degrees.
title: Experimental Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course facilitates student involvement in a second structured Work Integrated Learning (WIL) placement, building on their prior industry exposure. Under the guidance of an academic supervisor, students will further deepen their practical experience while critically reflecting on industry practices and standards, advancing their understanding of their field of study. PREREQUISITES: Students must have successfully completed 3531LHS Industry Internship.

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

Students will develop their academic, therapeutic, and interprofessional communication skills, along with information and communication technology capabilities so they may provide safe, collaborative nursing care. Prerequisites : NIL Corequisites : NIL Incompatible : 1801NRS Effective Communication
1008HSV Interpersonal Skills

academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

Prerequisite: 2302NSC Modern Physics Lab.
title: Physics Laboratory III
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The project will allow the student to combine all of the knowledge and practical skills which have been developed during the degree. Students will be required to conduct a short research project. Although not essential, students may be sponsored by an organisation or individual within the aviation industry. The research project will address an issue of relevance to the industry.
title: Aviation Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This Capstone course brings together the learning across your degree, and covers the principles of pathology, the molecular basis of disease, and modern molecular approaches to the diagnosis and treatment of disease. This content will be taught with a case-oriented problem-based learning approach to biomedical science. In addition, this course will further develop your scientific written communication skills and provide you with an opportunity to reflect on your degree and future career.
title: Biomedical Sciences Capstone
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course is one of two final courses comprising the Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice is a prescribed academic qualification for registration as a migration agent in Australia. 7234LAW is a future-focussed course in which students learn how to establish and operate an ethical migration practice. Consistent with its companion course, 7134LAW, in 7234LAW students commence their transition into the real world and life as a registered migration agent, as they examine professional ethics in depth, learn how to plan and manage a business and manage Code of Conduct compliant financial records and client accounts. The 7234LAW modules will support students as they simultaneously complete the assessment in the companion course 7134LAW. In addition to this horizontal alignment between 7134LAW 7234LAW, both courses also align with the learning outcomes in the previous courses. The deliberate alignment and capstone nature of this course allow students to progress logically through the growing complexity of both legal and practitioner skills culminating in this future-focussed practical course.
title: Establishing and Operating an Ethical Migration Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course emphasises Modern Physics. It includes experiments on topics such as black-body radiation, gamma rays from radioactive sources, interferometry, microwave devices, resonance phenomena, diffraction and Fourier transforms, the Hall effect, the electronic charge-to-mass ratio, the Frank-Hertz experiment and the photoelectric effect. Prerequisites: 1031SCG Physics 1A or 1018ENG Engineering Science AND 1032SCG Physics 1B. Incompatible: 2324SCE Physics Laboratory II
title: Modern Physics Laboratory
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides a detailed, critical examination of the adolescent in contemporary society. It builds upon earlier courses in human/child development, and offers theoretical understanding and practical skills relevant to all people who interact and/or work with adolescents.
title: Adolescent Development

description: Provides a critical overview of the context in which there is increased pressure to monitor and evaluate human service practice in order to be more accountable to service users, managers and funders; and aims to develop the capacity of students to understand, use and develop research knowledge and 'evidence'. Develops understanding of the concepts of effectiveness and outcomes in human services.
title: Evaluation, Effectiveness, Outcomes
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

The dissertation courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. The dissertation involves the identification of a research question, selection of any appropriate research design and data analysis. At the completion of the five dissertation courses students will submit a research report for examination. Students may have to defend their work at a research seminar. Students are advised to consult the relevant course convenor regarding appropriate word limits or expectations concerning the amount of work to be produced in their disciplines. Students should be aware that when they enrol in the final dissertation component (6001DOH_P5) they are required to submit their dissertation by Friday of the first week of June for students submitting in Trimester 1 or Friday of the last week of October for students submitting in Trimester 2.

A summary of the essentials for small business success is presented with the necessary activities involved in getting a new business started as a series of stages. The basics of planning and managing the four key resources and areas of activity found in all small enterprises - marketing and sales, finance, operations and human resources - are presented. Finally, management of small business growth and change is explained.

academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Pedagogy in Practice is a program of studio lessons designed to consolidate the student's musical skill and technique, expose the student to repertoire suitable as the vehicle for teaching and provide opportunity for interaction with skilled teachers on the faculty. It addresses the practical skills of studio teaching while also catering for the needs and experience of the individual student. Students are taught in pairs to enhance the teaching and learning experience by direct observation and reporting. This course allows the student to put into practice the theoretical skills that are taught in Pedagogy 1 and Pedagogy Practicum 1.

academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: The Course introduces students to advanced materials and their applications with the aim to deepen their understanding about i) how materials properties guide materials selection at the product design stage, ii) how core materials properties (either surface- or bulk properties) are changed, adapted or mended to specific user environment and/or an application field through a variety of manufacturing methods, and iii) how commercial material objects (or products) are manufactured in a factory setting. The Course will endue students with relevant knowledge on current materials surface technology, material treatment processes and manufacturing and production system processes, process technology and manufacturing systems design. Additive and rapid prototyping technology and lean engineering/lean production will be also be discussed in this Course. The Course is designed for 3rd year engineering students that already possess university-level fundamental knowledge on properties of common engineering materials such as metals, polymers, ceramics and attained theoretical and practical knowledge on fabrication and processing methods for these materials. The Course is developed to provide a practical, project-based immersion into materials selection process (with real, commercial products used as study samples) where students will learn how initial material selection process effects the geometry, structure, performance and cost of a final product. Assessment is by group assignment, oral presentation and individual examination. Please check the "Assumed Knowledge" for this course under the Course Profile to ensure you meet the pre-requisites required for enrolment.
title: Materials and Manufacturing
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course offers Griffith students a unique opportunity to undertake a transformational work integrated learning (WIL) experience. You will be supported to undertake a full-time, unpaid internship with a company in Asia. Internship destinations are chosen to offer maximum exposure to the vibrant Asian economy in businesses, government offices, or not-for profit organisations. The program offers in-country global WIL experiences in selected destinations. This course is part of the Griffith Asia Institute (GAI) initiative to offer meaningful Asia experiences to Griffith students; students are invited to be contributing members of the GAI community and experience the advantages of GAI networks throughout Asia. Students are matched with a placement that best aligns with their academic discipline and career aspirations and that advances student academic interests, experiential immersion, and vocational intentions with appropriate Asian connections. The aim of this course is to increase students' skills and experience in the workplace enhancing employability at the time of graduation. By the end of the course, we expect students to develop advanced skills in areas that are in high demand by employers, such as, problem solving, working in teams, critical analysis, time management, networking, and innovation. Thus individual reflection on personal attributes such as independence, curiosity, motivation and maturity is encouraged. All students applying for this course must meet minimum requirements and will be selected for the course in a competitive process. Please note: This course is not available for credit based on prior studies or external studies.
title: PG Global Mobility Internship II
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: Rock mechanics is an important branch of Civil and Mining Engineering that deals with the engineering behavior of rock material. Students wishing to become successful engineers will need to have a thorough understanding of fundamental principles of rock mechanics and develop skills that will allow them to apply such knowledge to solve real-life problems. In this course students will have opportunities to learn about the origin of rocks and the role of geology in the formation of geotechnical properties of rocks. Students will also learn how to apply relevant theories into practice so that they can effectively conduct field surveys and laboratory examination of rock samples, correctly interpret and analyse results of such investigations, select appropriate parameters for numerical models, evaluate stability of rock slopes, and develop skills to write comprehensive and concise reports. Students will be provided with the opportunity to become familiar with leading computer programs, which are commonly used in the industry, and through performing project-based assignments students will acquire sufficient knowledge and develop critical computer skills that will enable them to solve various practical problems.
title: Rock Mechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

Furthermore, research and presentation skills will be applied to a capstone assessment item focusing on quality improvement in a food service system.

academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

It inquires into the nature of some important border-spanning ethical issues, and it considers what an ethical response to them would be by individuals, states and some other actors. This course will critically examine the genealogy of international ethics and the idea of 'cosmopolitan ethics'. Having established the foundation of thinking about international ethics, we will explore contemporary issues in international ethics from Just War and international development aid to COVID-19 pandemic and artificial intelligence.

academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

While emphasising oral proficiency, 2082LHS continues a communicative approach to language learning and teaching which develops all four communicative macro-skills. 2082LHS progresses you towards a basic 'social' proficiency, equivalent to the B1 Threshold level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. As a 20CP course, 2082LHS comprises approximately 340 hours of work in total.

description: Painting Studio 2 is a studio-based course informed by key concerns of modern, post-modern and contemporary discourses on painting. Referring to the work of significant figures in twentieth and twenty-first century painting, students will develop work that engages with painting as an historical, technical and conceptual practice. By reflecting on major chapters of painting's recent history to the present, students will be required to reflexively address central themes of painting through the development of studio work and critical discussion. Importantly, students will also reflect on the relationship between those themes and broader interdisciplinary practices. Pre-requisite: must be undertaking 1651 Bachelor of Visual Arts OR must be undertaking 1652 Bachelor of Visual Arts/Bachelor of Business OR must be undertaking 1187 Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art AND must have completed 1216QCA Introduction to Art Theory AND must have completed 1217QCA Introduction to Art Theory 2 AND must have completed 2016QCA Painting Studio 1
title: Painting Studio 2

description: Islamic Law and Politics in a Changing World explores the origins, principles, and contemporary applications of Islamic law within diverse political contexts. This course examines the foundational sources of Islamic legal thought the Qur'an and Sunnah and how Islamic jurisprudence has evolved across different historical periods, from pre-modern societies to post-colonial and modern nation-states. Through engaging lectures and tutorials, students will critically analyze key legal concepts, the role of Islamic law in governance, and its intersection with international legal frameworks. Case studies from various Muslim-majority countries, including Indonesia, Iran, Malaysia, and Saudi Arabia, will offer insights into how Islamic law is applied in diverse political and social landscapes. Topics such as human rights, gender justice, economic systems, and international humanitarian law will be explored, enabling students to assess contemporary debates surrounding Islamic law and politics. You will learn about the historical development, principles, and sources of Islamic law; relationship between Islamic law, ethics, and governance in modern nation-states; comparative analysis of legal systems in Muslim-majority countries; the role of Islamic law in issues such as human rights, gender, criminal justice, and finance; and the interaction between Islamic law and international legal frameworks. This course is ideal for students interested in law, political science, international relations, religious studies, or Middle Eastern and Islamic studies. No prior knowledge of Islamic law is required.
title: Islamic Law and Politics in a Changing World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Introducing Communication Studies is a postgraduate level introduction to the interdisciplinary practice of Communications Studies. It identifies key features of communication as a field of study: forms of communication; theories and histories of mass communications media; the diverse and evolving field of Australian mass media communications; and media communications issues in 21st century public policy and politics. The subject identifies key communication research traditions and examines their characteristic concepts, themes and issues. Introducing Communication Studies familiarises students with a range of social and cultural issues related to creative and communications industries and technologies.
title: Introducing Communication Studies
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: From the mid-18th century to the present time we have witnessed a series of major technological innovations that have transformed business, work and jobs. Examples include the steam engine, electricity and steel, Henry Ford's production line system of manufacturing and, nearer our own time I.T. biotechnology and nanotechnology. The Austrian economist, Joseph Schumpeter famously referred to such innovations as "gales of creative destruction" old industries being swept away, to be replaced by new ones. Schumpeter's gales of creative destruction continue to impact business, work and jobs. Organizations now have to compete globally; organizational structures have to be flatter, work contracts more flexible, business functions more interlinked, and strategies more innovation-based. Business has become a learning race, with human talent and intangible intellectual capabilities at its core. This course is about how contemporary organizations are dealing with these issues and what we can learn from their attempts to anticipate, adjust to and take advantage of change. The course is both theoretical and practical with insights being provided from the academic literature and businesses. We will look at change from an organizational perspective and seek the answers to a number of questions that are important to those of us that live our lives in organizations. What is happening in the world that may deliver changes in the future? What is the best way to manage change? What do I do if I am asked to lead a change? How do we effectively implement a change? What do we do about resistance? How can we better adapt to the changes we encounter as employees?
title: Leading Policy and Organisational Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

Success and failure of organisations can often be attributed to strengths and weaknesses with the recruitment and selection process. However, these activities need to be carried out within a legislative framework that increasingly influences our practice. This course will provide you with an understanding of the activities involved in the more complex and difficult areas of recruitment and selection, from the viewpoint of a human resource practitioner and/or business manager. Incompatible: 7016EHR OR 7014EHR
title: Recruitment and Selection
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management
