description: Injury and disability management are often practiced in the context of workers compensation and motor accident insurance legislation. Concern over injury and disability in the workplace and in communities is growing as a result of escalating costs, as well as economic and personal impact on injured persons. This course will focus on promoting an understanding of the impact of injury in relation to the individual, return to function, the return to work process and society. Furthermore, it will promote a greater awareness of methods of effective injury management. Current legislative approaches to Injury Management throughout Australasia are based on the concept that an individual who acquires a compensable injury, is able to be returned to function, maintained at work and/or return to the workplace in some capacity as soon as is practicably and safely possible. Provision of suitable duties by employers is an integral part of this process. Counselling and support for the injured person is also crucial to obtaining a safe, successful and durable outcome. Discussion of the role of the Rehabilitation Counsellor in understanding the perspectives of stakeholders in this process will be undertaken. Students will also learn how to develop and monitor an injury management plan for an individual who is injured or ill, that incorporates a continuum of care from the onset of the condition through to recovery.
title: Injury and Disability Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the evolution of rehabilitation philosophy, theory and practice in the Australian context. Against this background students will come to appreciate the nexus between theory and practice, models and systems of service delivery and the roles of people working in the rehabilitation and disability fields. During this course students start to build their inter-professional knowledge as well as their professional identities as rehabilitation counsellors and are required to have some contact with practicing Rehabilitation Counsellors. In the event of high enrolment numbers, enrolment preference will be granted to students who have this course listed in their program in the first instance.
title: Introduction to Rehabilitation Counselling
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Job development and placement covers the second stage in the vocational rehabilitation process, and covers the processes and practices employed in rehabilitation to assist people with disabilities to locate work. This course evaluates career development theories in terms of their applicability to people with disabilities. It also covers practical techniques associated with job finding, job placement, job seeking skills training, labour market surveying and job analysis. This course was formerly 7011HSV. Incompatible: 7011HSV is incompatible with 7311AHS
title: Job Development and Placement
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces journalism genres and writing skills that appear in longer forms of journalism such as news features, in-depth features and profile writing. This course provides students with the skillset to package feature or profile pieces for publication; and takes students through best-practice and leading examples of different genres of longform, literary, narrative and non-fiction journalism.
title: Beyond Hard News: Writing for Longer Formats
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces students to the critical role of communication in the public understanding of contemporary environmental issues and climate change. The course will examine successful environmental and climate change journalism and communication strategies, and furnish students with an opportunity to develop their own.
title: Environmental and Climate Change Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces students to solutions-oriented forms of journalism. Students will be encouraged to explore their practice beyond conventional journalism production to explore innovative and interactive storytelling techniques that utilise a suite of media tools to produce web-based journalism.
title: Journalism for Solutions and Social Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides the opportunity for pre-service teachers to acquire knowledge and skills in planning, teaching, evaluating, and reporting in the areas of The Arts, Prep to Year 6.
title: The Arts Prep to Year 6
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Mathematics underpins and informs all scientific fields and is the language of science. Quantitative Reasoning is a mathematics course with a difference. Students will learn how to translate scientific problems into mathematical form, and how to understand and interpret mathematical and numerical results. With modern software, they will use case studies to learn how to apply mathematical concepts, from basics up to simple calculus, to real-world scientific problems.
title: Quantitative Reasoning
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Biological Systems is an introductory course that provides an appreciation of the main concepts of modern biology. Students will gain an understanding of the origin, function and structure of living organisms by examining life at increasing levels of biological complexity, from the molecular and cellular level to whole organisms and ecosystems. Course content will be delivered through a combination of lectures, workshops, laboratory sessions and online material. Incompatible: 1601ENV Biological Systems
title: Biological Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to respond to industry client projects. Students will work in teams to design innovative solutions that considers client and stakeholder needs to contribute to solving the real-world crises. Student teams will be guided by industry mentors as they explore solutions-based opportunities and engage in design thinking. Through this course, students will develop their problem solving capabilities and understanding of how organisations can be responsive to the concept of sustainability. While also reflecting on their own professional capabilities and the impact they can make as professionals and as a member of the global community.
title: Co-Design Incubator
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course introduces students to the law of civil wrongs. This is the body of principles aimed at compensating, rather than punishing, the victims of conduct causing harm, distress, or interference with property or reputation.
title: Torts 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course covers the laws that govern the creation and operation of government institutions within their political, social and economic contexts, especially the powers and limits on powers of parliaments to make laws under Australia's federal Constitution. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Constitutional Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course explores the history and nature of Equity and its relationship to the common law, and covers equitable rights and assignments, estoppel, fiduciary duties and unconscionability. It also describes the law relating to trusts including informal trusts, family settlements, superannuation and managed investment funds. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Equity and Trusts
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: The Event industry has long been recognised as a major market sector in the tourism and hospitality industry, and business event tourism is a fast growing sector in the tourism industry. Its complex and diverse nature is represented in the diversity of operational aspects it covers: accommodation management; food and beverage management; tourism destination marketing; engineering and technical services; front office; facility marketing and sales; risk management and project management.
title: Conference and Convention Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course provides a broad introduction to the law of contracts. We will examine which promises are legally binding and how contracts are formed. We will also be examining the different categorisations of contracts and the contents and effects of contracts. This course provides students with an understanding of contractual principles which will be built upon in 1030LAW Contracts 2.
title: Contracts 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course aims to foster the development of ethical, reflective, collaborative, and creative practitioners. Students work as part of a collaborative studio team under the guidance of expert teaching staff, connecting with external industry partners on numerous public-facing design projects. Students will develop a working knowledge of professional design practices while creating a range of industry-connected design outcomes. IMPORTANT: refer to www.liveworm.com.au for more information and how to gain permission to enrol.
title: Liveworm 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Through a combination of theoretical learning and practical application, students will gain a strong foundation in the principles of using information systems, data collection, and data management in health services management. The course emphasizes the role of data in evidence-based decision-making, improving patient outcomes, optimizing resource allocation, and enhancing operational efficiency. Key topics include electronic health records (EHRs), health information exchanges (HIEs), data analytics, health informatics, and decision support systems. Students will learn to assess and implement health information systems, analyze large datasets, and translate findings into actionable insights that can influence healthcare policy, clinical practices, and organizational strategies. The course also examines some of the governance requirements included ethical and privacy issues surrounding health data usage and how to ensure compliance with regulatory standards. By the end of the program, students will be equipped with the knowledge and tools to integrate information systems into healthcare environments effectively, driving data- driven improvements in patient care and organizational decision-making.
title: Health Services and Information Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Supply Network Modelling aims to develop students' skills and ability to model supply networks and quantitatively assess their design and operations, identify gaps for performance improvement and properly appraise the proposed solutions to address such gaps.
title: Supply Chain Modelling
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Paramedics are required to develop knowledge about medical and toxicological conditions across the lifespan. In this course students develop knowledge, critical thinking, decision making and technical skills required to undertake an assessment of, and how to manage the patient in a healthcare setting.
title: Medical and Toxicological Conditions in Paramedic Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course covers the applications of differential equations to model complex phenomena. This begins from the applications of systems of ordinary differential equations (both linear and non-linear) using matrix and phase plane methods. Techniques such as the Frobenius method and Green's functions are used for solving ordinary linear differential equations, followed by use of Bessel functions with applications to initial value, and boundary value problems. Analytic techniques for solving linear partial differential equations (including Laplace and wave equation in three dimensions) are also studied.
title: Advanced Differential Equations and Modelling
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Appropriate communication skills are an important aspect of any mathematical career and the ability to present mathematical arguments and results in an accurate, coherent and logical manner, and at a level appropriate for the intended recipient, is an essential attribute for any potential employee. During this course the student will receive instruction on writing and seminar presentation, with a particular relevance for the discipline of Applied Mathematics. In parallel with this, the course will also examine an area of Applied Mathematics at an advanced level. The assessment for the course will be constructed in such a way that it will allow the student to demonstrate oral and written communication skills in relation to the mathematics that has been studied. Assumed Knowledge: Undergrad Science degree with (Applied) Mathematics Major. Incompatible: 6303NSC Topics and Research Methods in Physics
title: Topics in Applied Mathematics 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course covers the anatomical structure, physiological function and control of a wide range of human physiological systems.
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Spectacular advances have been made in molecular cell biology in recent years. The course aims to integrate the biology of cells, sub-cellular compartments, cellular communication and signalling, and cellular processes. The course will address the functions of the many different types of proteins and lipids in eukaryotic cells, how cells interact with their environment, and how these processes are regulated normally and in disease.
title: Molecular Cell Biology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course deals with advanced methods in DNA cloning, analysis of gene expression and analysis of the control of gene expression. It also considers the molecular basis of the control of gene expression in development and homeostasis, and advanced molecular genetic systems including their application. Students will not be permitted to enrol without a Pass grade in the prerequisite course.
title: Molecular Biology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides skills for cultivating, isolating, identifying and enumerating microorganisms, and enables students to apply these skills to more complex microbiological laboratory tasks. The course gives an appreciation of the wide diversity, large numbers and important functions of microorganisms in everyday life. It combines the basic skills required to conduct fundamental and applied research in microbiology with standard methods and testing procedures commonly used in commercial microbiology laboratories.
title: Microbiology Laboratory
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The course provides a foundation in mechanics of materials for structural stress and failure analysis. It reviews the principles of statics, equilibrium, loads and support reactions. Stress and strain are examined in the context of axial, bending, transverse shear and torsional stresses. These concepts are extended to include stress and strain transformations, failure criteria, and beam deformation.
title: Strength of Materials
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course will provide the students with an integrated overview of the most important aspects in the process of drug discovery and of the mechanisms that underpin modern drug discovery research. The course content has been selected on the basis of modern practices in drug discovery research, and will provide students with a general understanding of drug discovery and issues that surround the development of a drug candidate. Prior Assumed: Acceptance into an Honours program with significant content in the relevant field.
title: Topics in Drug Discovery
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course covers the nature and presentation of forensic evidence in court; the role of the expert witness from the perspective of both Prosecution and Defence; the Jury's perception of forensic evidence and expert witnesses. This is a Capstone course intended for Forensic Science Program students in their final trimester of study.
title: Forensic Evidence and the Expert Witness
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The course has been designed to provide graduates with a strong theoretical foundation in Integrated Water Management (IWM) and Catchment Science (CS) good practice, strengthened by a practical applied research skill set developed through the final project experience. In the course students design and undertake self-directed project work to consolidate and apply concepts, principles and methodologies learned in the coursework components of the Masters Programs. Students are encouraged to base their final project on a focal issue that is of personal or professional development interest, which they will explore under the guidance of dedicated professional and academic supervisory expertise. Professional placements with NGOs, research institutes, water industry service providers, private consultants, or natural resources management organisations are encouraged. Where possible, students will be linked with IWC partners and associates.
title: Final Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The course provides opportunities to develop technical, professional, legal and managerial competencies to survey property, diagnose defects, design and alter premises, manage contracts and provide professional advice to clients. Particular emphasis will be placed on compliance with the regulatory requirements of refurbishment and new build projects.
title: Building Surveying
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course introduces students to the science of food. The course explores the nutritional composition, chemistry and function of foods and introduces students to theoretical and practical issues of food safety, food regulation and food as a form of therapy in the prevention and management of disease. This course forms the foundation for professional applications of nutrition and food in all domains of dietetic practice.
title: Food Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is an applied skills-oriented course in the Bachelor of Psychological Science and associated degrees, Bachelor of Psychology (Hons), and Bachelor of Counselling. The course focuses on effectiveness of practitioners at the small and large group level. The course introduces key models of facilitation and coaching for groups. An important aspect of this course is the linking of these models to the development of students' skills in many aspects of facilitation and coaching. At the end of this course, students will understand and have basic skills in the application of facilitation and coaching in a range of settings such as counselling, clinical, organisational, sport, and health settings.
title: Group Facilitation and Coaching Skills
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Economics is undergoing rapid changes with existing assumptions being challenged. This course provides students with an understanding of traditional and new economic models and frameworks. In short, this course brings forward the economic frameworks that students will need for the challenges of this century. This course is normally offered every 8 teaching periods.
title: Economics for a Sustainable Future
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This subject identifies, examines, and evaluates current and emerging policies and structures of the criminal justice system. It focuses on debates and problematic issues in the provision of criminal justice. Components of the system are examined in terms of fairness, justice and effectiveness. The extent to which the Australian system is effective in maintaining maximum levels of social harmony is explored. Alternative models of criminal justice are critically examined within the context of liberal-democratic society.
title: Making Sense of the Criminal Justice System
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is an elective course for students undertaking the Bachelor of Aviation. For students who meet the pass requirements set down by CASA this course delivers the theoretical and practical requirements to obtain the CASA Remote Pilot Licence (RePL) qualification and the Aviation Radio Operators Certificate (AROC). This allows the commercial operation of Remotely Piloted Aircraft (RPA) outside CASA defined standard operating conditions.
title: Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides an introductory overview of personal financial planning and several of the core components of it. Its primary focus is on developing a strong foundation in financial planning for students who intend to pursue a career in financial services, and in particular financial planning.
title: Financial Planning Fundamentals
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course integrates learning and acquisition of specialist knowledge in a series of clinically-based, research informed seminar/tutorials, assignments, case presentations and journal reviews and clinical practice involving the acquisition of advanced clinical skills and management of complex cases.
title: Advanced knowledge and clinical practice I
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course develops an advanced and integrated understanding of a complex body of knowledge in the discipline and develops expert specialised cognitive and clinical skills in specialist practice to independently manage complex cases
title: Advanced knowledge and clinical practice II
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Engineering mechanics is both a foundation and a framework for most engineering disciplines. This course provides a basic knowledge of Newtonian mechanics, rigid-body mechanics, elasticity and structural analysis. In particular, the principles of statics and their applications in engineering, the methods of static analysis, and techniques of engineering computation are expounded. Students are expected not only to acquire a good grasp of the principles but also to develop the computational and analytical skills which are vital in obtaining correct engineering solutions. In practice, a wrong solution can lead to an engineering disaster. This course is designed to enable students to acquire fundamental knowledge in engineering. It forms an integral part of the analysis and design training provided in the Engineering programs. This course is offered in trimester 2 and 3 at both the Gold Coast and Nathan campuses.
title: Engineering Mechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course introduces the core principles of materials science and engineering, with emphasis on the composition, structure, properties, processing, and engineering applications of major material classes, including metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites. Students examine how atomic bonding, chemical composition, and material structure govern material behaviour, and how mechanical, thermal, electrochemical, electrical, magnetic, and optical properties influence performance in engineering applications. By the end of the course, students will be able to analyse material behaviour using a range of destructive tests (e.g. tensile, compression, hardness, and thermal degradation) and non-destructive methods (e.g. visual and magnetic examination), evaluate key mechanical properties such as strength, stiffness, elasticity, plasticity, and ductility, as well as physical properties including electrical conductivity and resistivity, and select and apply materials appropriately in practical engineering contexts.
title: Engineering Materials
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course evaluates the response of Asian business to the disruptions of the 4th Industrial Revolution and Covid-19. In both events Asia has shown a unique ability to embrace the disruption and emerge with resilience models that are the envy of other trading nations. The socio-economic histories of selected countries will be evaluated to evidence the contemporary unique business cultures that contribute to the continued Asian business growth and robust economies.
title: Disruption in the 4th Industrial Revolution in Asia
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Social Work Theory for Practice provides foundational knowledge on social work theory, models, methods and contemporary issues in social work practice including traditional, therapeutic and critical perspectives, and issues of professional identity. The capacity to critically appraise various approaches is developed.
title: Social Work Theory for Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is available only to students enrolled in the Bachelor of Science Advanced with Honours program and is a compulsory component of the degree. The Advanced Studies Project is an individual research project, either theoretical or experimental, undertaken under the supervision of an academic mentor. The project provides students with the opportunity to apply and extend the knowledge and skills developed through the Advanced Studies Task in the design, conduct, analysis, and communication of research. Assessment consists of a written research report and an oral seminar presentation. The seminar is presented at the Advanced Studies Symposium held at the end of Trimester. The research report must be submitted to the mentor by Week 12 of the trimester in which 3094SCG_P2 is completed and will be assessed by the mentor and an additional academic staff member.
title: Advanced Studies Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course aims to develop students' knowledge and understanding of the normal anatomy and physiology of the human body. Students will gain an understanding of the relevance of such knowledge to the maintenance of human health and professional nursing practice. Prerequisites : NIL, Corequisites : NIL, Incompatible : 1974NRS Anatomy and Physiology 1
1016MSC Human Anatomy and Physiology Systems I
title: Human Anatomy and Physiology 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: "Flight Procedures" is a workshop style course series, where students implement aviation theory and regulatory rules in a simulation laboratory environment. Flight Procedures II uses the Cessna 182T software to introduce the constant speed propeller, retractable landing gear and glass cockpit design features initially, before exploring Instrument Flight Rules and procedures based on the Private Instrument Rating - all without any weather issues. We cover Instrument Flight Rules and associated Standard Operating Procedures ending with 2D non-precision approaches. Prerequisite: 1505NSC Flight Procedures I
title: Flight Procedures II
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course commences you on a lifelong journey to becoming a culturally safe and capable health professional who can positively contribute to closing the gap in health disparities between Australia's First Peoples and other Australians. This will be achieved by interacting with lecturers, attending seminars and yarning circles with community members and working with students from across all health disciplines on communication scenarios and case study activities and opportunities for critical reflective practice.
title: First Peoples Health and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course builds upon first year physics and further develops the two pillars of modern physics quantum mechanics and the theory of relativity and provides an introduction to the production and properties of elementary particles.
title: Quantum Mechanics, Relativity and Elementary Particles
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course is one of four 10 Credit Point courses that make up the research component of a School of Allied Health, Sport & Social Work Graduate Diploma or Masters level research project. The combined 8002AHS courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, approval from relevant ethics committee/s, data collection, analysis and write-up of findings. At the completion of the four Dissertation courses students will submit a thesis for examination.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is one of five Physiotherapy Practicum courses designed to enable you to develop capabilities reflective of a new graduate physiotherapist with a range of clients in a variety of clinical and environmental settings. The key component of this course is a five week full time clinical placement across the areas of acute care, musculoskeletal, rehabilitation or community.
title: Physiotherapy Practicum 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is one of five Physiotherapy Practicum courses designed to enable you to develop capabilities reflective of a new graduate physiotherapist with a range of clients in a variety of clinical and environmental settings. The key component of this course is a five week full time clinical placement across the areas of acute care, musculoskeletal, rehabilitation or community.
title: Physiotherapy Practicum 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is one of five Physiotherapy Practicum courses designed to enable you to develop capabilities reflective of a new graduate physiotherapist with a range of clients in a variety of clinical and environmental settings. The key component of this course is a five week full time clinical placement across the areas of acute care, musculoskeletal, rehabilitation or community.
title: Physiotherapy Practicum 5
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is one of a series of courses undertaken to complete dissertation requirements for your program. Each dissertation course has specific milestones to complete, which are available on the program website on Learning@Griffith. Dissertation courses involve the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, and the execution of experimental protocols. Results from these experiments are evaluated and conclusions drawn with findings presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This 40CP Dissertation is offered within the 5263 Master of Public Health (MPH) and the 5725 Master of Global Public Health (MGPH) programs. The 40CP dissertation is similar to an Honours dissertation in type and scope and gives students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest. The Dissertation involves the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, collection and analysis of data. The background literature, methodology. findings and conclusions are presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis. The thesis is expected to be between 15,000 and 20,000 words in length, depending on disciplinary demands and problem requirements. Please note that Course Convenor approval is needed to be able to enrol in the Dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The design and manufacturing of electronic products are skills that are highly sought after in industries. This course develops students' ability to apply engineering knowledge and systematic design processes to the end-to-end development of electronic products. Students translate product requirements into a system design and develop, integrate, test, and validate electronic, mechanical, and user-interface components to produce a functional prototype. The course covers circuit and PCB design, mechanical housing, user interface integration, system testing, and design for manufacture and assembly, with consideration of performance, safety, reliability, cost, and sustainability.
title: Workshop Technology
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Interior Design Practice Studio prepares students for professional interior design practice through a simulated real-world design studio format, replicating the pace, expectations and workflow of an industry design office. Through lectures and studio-based project work, students progress a self-directed commercial design project from concept through to developed design and construction documentation, applying research, creative experimentation and a professional code of ethics at each stage. The course emphasises industry-standard skills in concept development, universal design, sustainability, materials and FFE selection, and documentation, while building career-ready capabilities in meeting deadlines, responding to client briefs and presenting to professional standards. Students will communicate and defend their design decisions to academic, industry and client audiences using appropriate visual, verbal and written modes.
title: Spatial Design and Identity
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Key aspects of Health and Physical Education (HPE) curriculum are implemented in this course, including: the importance of health, physical activity, a social-cultural perspective in HPE and the application of social justice principles. This course prepares you to plan and deliver integrated learning experiences using the Australian Curriculum, Assessment and Reporting Authority (ACARA) syllabus in Health and Physical Education.
title: Health and Physical Education 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course will provide students with an understanding of how characteristics of autism interact with the learning and the educational experience. Students will be introduced to the principles of learning and learning theories before exploring how the cognitive profiles of people with autism can influence the learning experience. The importance of transitions and transferring of information, within and between educational settings is also explored. As part of this course, students will explore the elements required for creating a positive learning environment with, by and for autistic individuals all ages and abilities.
title: Autism, Thinking, and Learning.
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is an introduction into the photographic darkroom and analogue photographic processes and techniques. Students will gain an understanding into the fundamentals of photography such as time and duration, exposure and light and will explore how these controls are employed as a language within historical and contemporary portraiture. Students will develop skills in black and white film exposure, processing, and printing. Pre-requisite: RESTRICTED access for 1651 Bachelor of Visual Arts OR 1187 Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art OR 1189 Bachelor of Design OR 1567 Bachelor of Education
title: Introduction to Photography
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course introduces students to the profession of physiotherapy. Students will develop an awareness of ethical, legal and professional issues related to physiotherapy practice, and have the opportunity to develop strong communication, interpersonal, and rapport-building skills. Students will develop skills in the observation, description and measurement of joint movement. Students will develop and apply those skills in the context of introductory knowledge and skills related to therapeutic massage.
title: Foundations of Physiotherapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Mobile technologies are fast becoming ubiquitous and are being used to meet a diversity of purposes from business and industry, to education, entertainment and medical applications. In this course, students work with popular mobile application development environments and methods to create mobile applications. In so doing, students build the knowledge and skills necessary to develop native mobile applications that exploit the device capabilities including camera, compass, gestures, and sensors such as accelerometer to create effective and highly interactive mobile applications. Pre-requisite: 1811ICT (For Bachelor of Computer Science only) OR 2807ICT Programming Principles OR 2701ICT Interactive Application Development OR 2006ICT Object Oriented Software Development.
title: Mobile Application Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course introduces contemporary views of child development and a range of theoretical perspectives for understanding the complexity of influences on children's development. It provides opportunity for students to develop the skills and resources required to support the diverse strengths, abilities interests, and cultural practices of children based on principles of equity and diversity.
title: Child Development, Families and Communities
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Students enrolled in the Honours program will undertake an Honours Dissertation relevant to their study of urban and environmental planning under the guidance of one or more supervisors appointed by the Honours Convenor. The topic and nature of the Dissertation will be determined through consultation and mutual agreement of the student and supervisor and must be approved by the Honours Convenor. Students in 1658 and 1660 will be required to align the topic of their Honours Research Project to that of their major if they have chosen a major. The Dissertation will involve original research but this can include the collection and analysis of primary data, the analysis of secondary data, or the development of new theoretical or conceptual models. Assessment will comprise a written report of the work, prepared in the form of a thesis and submitted for independent examination by at least two assessors. Students will also be required to make two presentations: one of their research proposals and one describing their work and provisional conclusions. The quality of these presentations will contribute to the overall assessment of the Project. Pre-requisite: Students must have passed 4029ENV Project Proposal in Honours and must have completed 200 credit points or have the permission of the course convenor before enrolling in this course.
title: Honours Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course analyses Southeast Asia's intrusive, but often ramshackle state apparatuses, its diversity of political regime types, its partially globalised economies, its diverse political cultures, and its plural, often divided societies. Its most fundamental aim is to assess the challenges that these ambiguous political and socio-economic factors pose for the introduction and perpetuation of political democracy, and the resilience of autocracy. As such, this course can best be understood as part of a sub-field of comparative democratisation and authoritarianism.
title: Democratisation and Authoritarianism in Southeast Asia
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course provides a comprehensive overview of the animals, with the content largely organised by major evolutionary groups, typically phyla. The course examines the many aspects of the diversity of the animals, including their classification and evolutionary relationships, form, structure, function and interrelationships with other organisms (especially humans).
title: Zoology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Every organisation relies on one thing above all others, people. However, ensuring people who work in an organisation are treated as people and not just a resource is critical to ensuring that the organisation can achieve its objectives, face its challenges and undertake the opportunities it wishes to realise. Managing people is akin to social impact management with respect to the lives of employees. This course is about leading people to achieve sustainable people outcomes. This course examines how leaders can maximise employee outcomes through a better understanding of individual differences of the self and others; how to lead individuals and teams, including those with difficult behaviour, through effective communication, coaching, mentoring and sponsorship; how organisational structure and culture can influence sustainable people outcomes; and it explores factors that will challenge and disrupt the leading of people now and in the future. All students are expected to begin studies at the first designated session (face to face or online).
title: Leading for Sustainable People Outcomes
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This dissertation course gives research students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest and is a good preparation for the student to undertake higher research studies and other research endeavours. This course involves the execution of a research proposal, including experimentation and analysis of research results. It involves the preparation and presentation of a completed master degree thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Students may have developed research skills in the completion of pre-requisite research methodology courses with the view of undertaking a research topic in this course. description: Somewhere right now, a foreign mining company is threatening to sue a government for billions of dollars. Not in a domestic court, not before an international court, but before a three-person panel of private arbitrators operating largely out of public view. The government's offence? Raising a royalty rate. Introducing an environmental review. Enacting a public health measure its own parliament voted for. Or, maybe, while a foreign company spends a decade negotiating with a government, building a mine, employing thousands of workers, and relying on the legal framework it was promised when it invested, the government changes, the rules change, and the investment becomes worthless overnight. This is investor-state arbitration. And whether you think it is an indispensable guarantee of the rule of law for foreign investors, or a mechanism that quietly constrains democratic governance, you cannot understand modern international law without it. This course makes a case for why investor-state arbitration (ISA) belongs at the centre of serious study of public international law, and why it is one of the most contested legal systems operating in the world today. ISA does something unprecedented in the international legal order: it gives private actors (companies, and in some cases individuals) the right to sue sovereign states directly before international arbitral tribunals, bypassing domestic courts entirely. The traditional view of international law as a system for regulating relations between states is fundamentally challenged the moment a tobacco company files a claim against a government for enacting plain-packaging legislation, or an energy firm demands compensation from a state that decided to exit nuclear power. Understanding ISA means understanding the most significant expansion of individual access to international adjudication since the creation of the international human rights system. Can Australia impose a mining super-profits tax without triggering billion-dollar claims from foreign investors under its trade agreements? Can a government committed to net zero phase out coal-fired power stations ? These are not hypothetical questions. They are live disputes, live regulatory dilemmas, and live constraints on what governments believe they can do. The states most critical of ISA (those who have denounced their investment treaties, refused to pay arbitral awards, or supported the push for a Multilateral Investment Court) are not wrong that the system creates asymmetric risks. A state regulating in the public interest can find itself defending against a nine-figure claim. But the states that dismantled their investment treaty networks also watched foreign direct investment fall. Bilateral investment treaties attract capital. They signal legal stability to investors who would otherwise price political risk into the cost of doing business in a country. The tension between investor protection and state sovereignty is not rhetorical. It is structural,
title: Investor State Arbitration
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course develops advanced applied statistical skills for health, medical and population-based research. Through hands-on activities, students will develop practical skills in using SPSS and R to manage, analyse, visualise and report health research data. A key component of the course is meta-analysis and quantitative evidence synthesis, developing students' skills to critically appraise research evidence and evaluate effect measures, heterogeneity, model selection and potential sources of bias. The course also explores emerging applications of data analytics and AI, providing students with practical insights into how AI can be applied and critically evaluated, with consideration of ethical and responsible integration into health research and healthcare. description: Commercial disputes do not respect national borders, but courts do. When a deal sours between parties based in different States (when assets are scattered across jurisdictions, when litigation erupts in more than one forum simultaneously, when a judgment needs to be turned into money) the question of which court decides, on whose terms, and with what effect becomes as consequential as the underlying merits. This course is about those questions. International Commercial Litigation examines the legal framework governing transnational commercial disputes before Australian courts. It is organised around the three-stage analytical framework that structures all such disputes: jurisdiction, applicable law, and recognition and enforcement. The course begins with jurisdiction (the power of a court to hear a claim at all, the circumstances in which it will decline to exercise that power, and the tools available to manage or restrain proceedings brought elsewhere). It then turns to choice of law (the rules determining which legal system's substantive norms will govern the dispute) before concluding with the recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments, the question that ultimately determines whether a judgment can be turned into a practical result. The approach throughout is analytical and practical in equal measure. Students engage with the leading Australian cases and the Commonwealth legislation that shapes daily practice, while developing the capacity to advise on strategy, anticipate risk, and think across legal systems. Comparative perspectives drawn from the United Kingdom, the European Union, or Singapore are woven in selectively, not as decoration, but as a lens through which Australian doctrine can be evaluated and, where necessary, questioned. Assessment in this course is designed to reward consistent intellectual engagement rather than a single high-stakes performance. A single scenario runs across all six weeks, with each module introducing new developments that students must analyse from the applicant or defendant position depending on the week. Four low-stakes weekly assessments, supported by peer review and AI-generated feedback, build the habit of reading facts with a conclusion already in mind. The final assessment takes the form of a take-home Brief for the Senior Partner, written in the same register and style practised throughout the course, followed by a dynamic dialogue in which students explain their brief and defend their arguments in a client and solicitor discussion with an examiner. Students who engage with the scenario consistently from the outset will find the final assessments a natural extension of work already done.
title: International Commercial Litigation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course looks at issues that affect international families - that is, families who are connected to two or more countries. It particularly focuses on the resolution of international family disputes, especially using litigation as the primary formal means of dispute resolution. This course includes a general introduction to private international law issues relevant to family law as well as studies of three specific areas. These are cross-border disputes involving children, including international child abduction and international surrogacy; the definition and regulation of marriage in different legal systems, including forced marriage, polygamy and same sex marriage; and the resolution of international property disputes between family members. This course includes discussion on the work of the Hague Conference on Private International Law in the context of family law.

description: Over the last decade, populists have come to power in the world's four largest democracies: India, the United States, Indonesia and Brazil, among a range of other countries. Populists have run on platforms challenging the checks and balances of liberal democracy, rejecting globalization and international institutions, and opposing free trade and movement. This course will enable students to gain a deeper understanding of the unique challenges posed by populism to democracy in the twenty-first century, including in Australia and Asia. It examines what happens when populists take power, what the impacts of populism on global politics are likely to be in the 2020s, and how political leaders can respond.
title: The Rise of Global Populism
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course is the first in the advanced research pathway that enables students to design, conduct and report a research project, under the supervision of an academic member of staff. This course will culminate in students submitting a written Dissertation and providing a verbal presentation of their research and associated study findings.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the relationship between popular genres and popular culture since the late 19th century. By focusing on three of the most popular genres in the world: crime, romance and speculative fiction the course examines how the style and focus of popular texts reflects shifting attitudes and tastes in society and culture. These popular genres are examined in a range of modes including fiction, television, film and a variety of screen based cultures. The course develops a range of skills and knowledge that explore the relationship between written and screen-based texts and publishing in popular genres. Students should note that content referred to in this course can be challenging or explicit when exploring genre intent, parameters and innovations. Students will be provided with learning options and context in relation to this material. PREREQUISITE: Minimum of 20CP of Writing or Literature courses. CO-REQUISTE: NIL. INCOMPATIBLE: 3723LHS Popular Genres; 3109HUM Popular Fiction and Mass Culture.
title: Popular Genres
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides students with an understanding of the lifespan development and learning of the person from psychological, sociological and biological perspectives, and the inter-relationship of these perspectives with cultural, social, legal, economic and political frameworks.
title: Development across the Lifespan
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Studio Immersion is a visual arts practice based course. Students will be introduced to foundational contemporary visual arts practices and will create works and undertake research for presentation. Lectures and tutorials will be studio specific and students are required to engage with, and gain knowledge and foundational expertise of their chosen studio specificity.
title: Studio Immersion 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course explores a range of theoretical perspectives to support students to gain insights into the developmental competences of children aged birth to 5 years. There is a focus on strength-based approaches and how to work with a team of professionals within an integrated early education setting. Students will complete 10 days of placement with children aged birth to 3 years.
title: Engagement with Young Children
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides an in-depth look at the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of oncological, neurological and psychiatric diseases. The course adopts an integrated approach to learning, taking the student through the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of the disease, including a thorough understanding of the pharmacological basis of treatment and its relation to drug structure. Lectures, aseptic laboratories and problem-based clinical workshops serve to equip students with theoretical knowledge, an evidence-based approach, and practical clinical skills including aseptic technique for the promotion of and contribution to optimal use of medicines, delivery of health information and provision of health education in relation to the therapeutic areas covered in the course.
title: Integrated Pharmacotherapeutics IV
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course focuses on developing students' skills in creative writing through the study of fiction, non-fiction, poetry and other forms of writing. Students will explore a range of approaches that authors take to developing and refining a sustainable creative writing practice, discuss avenues for generating original ideas and problem-solving during the writing and editing process, and develop an understanding how the writing and publishing industry works. Students read and discuss a series of classic and contemporary works of creative writing, and learn to exchange considered interpretations with their peers as well as developing critical analysis skills to apply to their own writing and the work of other writers. The course takes a scaffolded approach to introducing key creative writing skills and techniques, which students are then invited to apply across a range of different forms and styles of writing, drawing on themes and ideas that are relevant to their own interests. The course introduces students to the rich and vibrant world of contemporary creative writing, and offers students opportunities to experiment with a range of established and new creative writing forms and approaches.
title: Introduction to Creative Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: In this second of a four-course series Physical Skills students will continue to explore their potential as performers through sequences of practical classes developing the fundamental skills and techniques of Movement; Jazz Dance; Vocal Techniques, usage and healthy production. There will be an emphasis on activating the body as a physical instrument through exploring with Neutral Mask and developing a physical imagination. RESTRICTION: Entry to this program is subject to audition.
title: Acting: Physical Skills 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course will support you to develop your foundational knowledge of the design, conduct, and results of clinical trials of healthcare interventions, and the regulatory requirements and professional standards surrounding clinical trials. You will develop an understanding of the roles of various personnel who make up a clinical trial team, and general clinical trial business, alongside the skills necessary for critiquing the quality of published clinical trials.
title: Clinical Trials - Principles and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course guides students in exploring and mapping the diverse contexts that inform and shape their cinematic arts practice. Students will identify key areas including industry, cultural, artistic, technological, and /or social contexts, that inspire and situate their creative work, identifying opportunities for innovation within these spheres. Through this research and exploration, students will develop a nuanced understanding of their strategic niche and unique position within the broader landscape of cinematic arts.
title: Industry Research and Awareness
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: GFS Academies are intensive, immersive and industry-focused production experiences. Through problem-based scenarios students are encouraged to innovate through hands-on projects, collaborative and/or cross-disciplinary practice, analysis and reflection. Such challenge-driven settings could include but are not limited to technology, production scenarios, impact opportunities. In completing this course, students will gain experience and skills in the areas of problem solving, experimentation, prototyping and be positioned to foresee future possibilities and opportunities in cinematic arts practice.
title: Innovation Academy
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course introduces the principles and methods that enable robots to perceive and understand the physical world using cameras and vision-based sensing. It covers coordinate frames, image formation, camera calibration, geometric vision, feature extraction, motion estimation, depth perception, object perception, visual localisation, mapping, and vision-guided robotic operation. Students learn how computer vision supports embodied intelligence in mobile robots, robot manipulators, and other autonomous systems, and how perception modules are integrated into complete robotic pipelines. The course emphasises robotics-specific computer vision rather than general machine learning or generic image classification. Students will develop the conceptual and practical foundations needed to design perception pipelines for tasks such as localisation, mapping, tracking, grasping, navigation, and autonomous operation in real-world environments. Students must be enrolled in either 1534 Bachelor of Computer Science or 1585 B Engineering (Hon)/BComp Science.
title: Robotics and Computer Vision
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The course offers a comprehensive understanding of deep learning fundamentals and practical applications. Students explore principles and algorithms, gaining hands-on experience in building and training deep neural networks with PyTorch (or TensorFlow), covering topics like convolutional, recurrent neural networks and their applications.
title: Deep Learning
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course introduces students to foundational principles in art direction, emphasizing observation as well as drawing techniques and processes used in screen media production. The course emphasises analog and digital tools for life drawing, perspective, and structures. Through analysis and reflective practice, students develop fundamental artistic skills essential for effective visual storytelling.
title: Foundations of Art Direction
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course advances students' understanding and skills in the analysis of qualitative data. It focuses on the difference qualitative methods commonly applied within criminology and social science more generally. It will further develop students' understanding of qualitative research design, including the ability to reflect critically on the implications of qualitative research within diverse communities. Students will develop specific skills in some basic qualitative data analysis, such as computer assisted thematic analyses.
title: Qualitative Methods for Social Research
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Origins is a core course that introduces examining and contextualising identity to create a body of artwork that is informed by your indigenous perspective. This course is restricted to Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art students and other First Nations students only. Prerequisites: Nil
title: Origins
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course will provide students with statistical and data-analytic tools applicable to problems in business, finance, and economics.
title: Business Analytics and Quantitative Tools
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is a 10CP version of 2010LHS. It develops further students' communicative capacities in Mandarin Chinese acquired in the first-year Chinese courses (i.e.,1084LHS and 1085LHS) through practice of listening, reading, writing and speaking skills. Emphasis is on daily-life situations, highlighting Chinese social and cultural patterns of communication.
title: Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin) 2A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores notions of change, renewal and inequality in literary texts. Students gain an introductory understanding of approaches to reading and writing literary forms, including fiction and poetry, and interrogate how literature shapes and responds to changing cultural and social contexts.
title: Writing and Reading in a Changing World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course examines how the digital world works and the relationships among humans, technology, and data. Students explore the fundamentals of the digital world and theme-based issues such as identity, communities, power, and politics. Students will interpret, analyse, and visualise research using digital skills. These skills are important for bringing a critical understanding of intercultural and social issues to contemporary workplaces.
title: Engaging the Digital World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is the first of a four-course studio suite simulating the experience of working in a professional film and television production studio. Students will apply skills developed in associated majors and electives to a range of projects while examining the industry, social, cultural and ethical implications of screen production, as well as their emergent career paths. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies across all aspects of film and television production and receive guidance and feedback from experienced mentors. At the end of the studio suite, students will have developed high quality work of a professional standard, developed professional skills and knowledge of industry-standard production processes and procedures, and are adept at working collaboratively with requisite professional attitudes and practices.
title: Film and TV Studio 1: Associate
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This is the second of a 4-course studio suite simulating the experience of working in a professional animation studio. Working in small teams, students will apply skills developed in associated majors and electives to a range of projects while engaging with industry professionals throughout the process. In these studio courses, students will gain experience in all aspects of animation production, including the social, cultural, and ethical implications of producing animation. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies and receive guidance and feedback from experienced mentors. Guest lectures and engagement with the animation industry will provide students with a deeper understanding of career opportunities across various fields. At the end of this studio suite, students will have developed high quality work towards a professional folio, be abreast of studio processes and procedures, and be adept at working collaboratively with requisite professional attitudes and practices.
title: Animation Studio 2: Intermediate
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course explores the practical application of inclusive education philosophies, policies, and practices aimed at maximising learning outcomes for diverse students with disability. Students will gain an in-depth understanding of the characteristics, challenges, and educational approaches for students with disability, including those who are twice-exceptional (gifted students with disability). The course will examine a nuanced understanding of the considerable diversity that exists in special education contexts. Students will explore the unique characteristics, strengths, and challenges for learners in special education contexts, recognising the importance of personalised approaches to evaluation, support, and instructional strategies. Students will explore evidence-based practices and instructional methodologies and examine a range of approaches, assistive technologies, and accommodations designed to foster inclusive learning environments and maximize student engagement, participation, and academic success. The course will consider students who are gifted and talented, exploring strategies to identify and nurture their unique talents and abilities while ensuring they receive appropriate challenges and support. Collaboration and multidisciplinary teamwork will be highlighted as essential components of effective special education practices. By the end of this course, students will have developed a comprehensive understanding of inclusive education practices, gained insights into the diverse range of special "needs" and disabilities, and acquired practical strategies for creating inclusive learning environments that empower and support the unique needs of all learners.
title: Special Education in Context
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course introduces students to the foundational principles of medicinal chemistry and pharmacology, focusing on the relationship between drug structure and biological function. Students will explore the molecular mechanisms of drug action, structure-activity relationships (SAR), and the pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties that influence drug efficacy and safety. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking and problem-solving in the context of drug design, discovery, and therapeutic application. The course prepares students to understand how chemical structure impacts drug behaviour in biological systems and supports the development of evidence-based pharmaceutical care. Through integrated case-based learning and problem-solving exercises, students will apply scientific principles to evaluate therapeutic strategies and make informed clinical decisions. This course supports the development of core competencies required for safe and effective medicine use and prepares students to contribute meaningfully to patient care and interprofessional healthcare teams.
title: Structure, Function and Drug Action
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: New business ventures typically start with no recognised brand name, no customers and no market reputation. Without a strong brand and effective promotion the new venture is likely to fail. One of the key challenges for new ventures is to create awareness of their business offering, and to build customer interest in the new business enterprise. Potential customers must be converted to actual customers by building their desire to purchase the new venture's product or service. This course provides an introductory smorgasbord of creative and cost-effective promotional techniques in the special context of new business ventures, small and family businesses. In the case of self-employed professionals, building a personal brand is imperative to differentiate your business offering to stand out from your competitors and build increased customer loyalty. This course provides students with the skills and knowledge necessary to successfully build their brand, utilise their social networks, and employ other cost-effective promotional tools to communicate with their customers.
title: Branding and Promoting New Business Ventures
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This block focuses on teaching students in Years 3 to 6. Learners extend their understanding of curriculum design and pedagogical approaches in literacy and mathematics. They also explore curriculum design and pedagogical approaches to support student health and wellbeing through health and physical education across the primary years. Learners continue to build confidence in lesson planning, differentiation practices, and creating positive, inclusive learning environments. They will also continue to shape and develop their professional identity as a teacher of older primary students.
title: Upper Years of Primary Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Outbound Griffith Exchange students who are studying at a partner university must enroll in exchange courses for the trimester(s) they will be studying overseas. The tuition fees for each trimester will be determined by the course code(s), which considers the credit points and field of study. These factors are set by the Australian Government. This course is specifically tailored for both undergraduate and postgraduate students who are pursuing fields of study that include Visual and Performing Arts.
title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

title: Exchange Studies

title: Exchange Studies
