title: Exchange Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith International

description: This course provides information from a range of theoretical perspectives to enable you to gain insight into the developmental characteristics and competencies of children birth to five years of age. The course has a focus on soft entry early intervention and prevention and provides a transdisciplinary approach to working with children and families which aims to produce practitioners who can engage with children in integrated settings. You will engage in professional practice with children birth to five years of age and their families across a range of early year settings. You will complete 15 days with birth to 3 years and 5 days with 3-5 years in an early childhood setting. As part of the embedded placement students are required to attend all on campus classes or online tutorials.
title: Engagement with Children
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is a basic introduction to digital media production, providing students with exposure to the theory and practice behind communicating with and through a variety of digital media formats including photography and web design.
title: Digital Media: Portfolio Production
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides knowledge and skills in the development of professional social media and considers theory and practice to take advantage of the opportunities of social media while navigating the risks that come with the terrain.
title: Social Media for Global Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces students to solutions-oriented forms of journalism. Students will be encouraged to explore their practice beyond conventional journalism production to explore innovative and interactive storytelling techniques that utilise a suite of media tools to produce web-based journalism.
title: Journalism for Solutions and Social Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: The Critic focuses on arts reviewing. Reviewers play a special role among responses to creative work, beginning public conversations about meaning, value and legacy. This course explores writing about the arts through reviewing film, literature, video games, and theatre.
title: The Critic: Arts and Culture
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Griffith Chem is a Griffith University Head Start At School course. Griffith Chem is an online, two year, part-time university course for Year 11 and 12 students. Complementing and building on Senior Chemistry delivered at school, Griffith Chem enables students to experience an integrated university course whilst completing their senior high school studies. 1000ENV_Y2 is the Trimester 2 component of Stage 2.
title: Griffith Chem
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: In this course students will firstly be introduced to the fundamental coastal hydrodynamic processes that are an essential consideration in the practice of coastal engineering/science. These processes include wind wave generation, wave transformation and storm surge development. Students will then learn how to apply the basic principles of computational fluid dynamics and numerical skills to solve coastal engineering problems.
title: Coastal Engineering and Modelling
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course helps future leaders develop the skills they need to succeed in enterprise management. The skill set required begins with students studying the basic processes of businesses, leading into how to manage effectively, how to manage teams and concludes with leadership theory and an introduction to business ethics and sustainability. The course begins by exploring management ideas and theory and moves into the world of applied management and concludes with discussions on how to be an ethical and excellent leader.
title: Managing and Ethically Leading the Enterprise
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course deepens students' understanding of criminological theory and its application to real-world crime prevention. Building on foundational knowledge, students will explore advanced criminological perspectives alongside practical frameworks used to reduce and prevent crime. A particular focus is placed on environmental criminology, situational crime prevention, and place-based strategies. Through the integration of theory and practice, students will critically examine how knowledge about the causes and patterns of crime can inform effective, ethical, and evidence-based responses in contemporary justice settings.
title: Crime, Place and Prevention
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This research informed seminar/tutorial course develops the cross-discipline areas of basic and clinical sciences and is designed to form a platform to support the specialty discipline programs
title: Clinical Sciences
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Careers are pervasive individual and social phenomena: everyone should have a career. Yet, the dramatic changes to the labour market over the past few decades, brought about by advances in technology, globalisation, and trade deregulation, have revolutionised the way that people work; and there are more changes ahead. You will (a) be introduced to the theories of career development and how they are applied across the lifespan, and (b) gain beginning practitioner skills, including how to conceptualise a career pathway, explore existing and developing barriers, undertake a career assessment and a mock career counselling session, and write a professional report on an individual client. The course is ideal for anyone who is planning a career working with people. Topics include the meaning of work, work in the 21st century, career theories, career assessment, and career counselling and interventions.
title: Career Psychology and Counselling
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: In this course, PSTs will identify and apply pedagogies and practices that are most effective in creating a positive learning environment to support student learning, motivation and engaged behaviour. Drawing on a range of research informed learning theories, PST will plan learning sequences responsive to their students' stage of learning and become increasingly challenging (incorporating spacing and retrieval practice) as students work towards mastery. Considering school-wide frameworks and classroom-level proactive approaches to behaviour management and learning, PSTs will apply evidence-based teaching practices and develop skills in how to practically implement tier 1 in the classroom. This course also includes a professional experience placement in schools. Preservice teachers must reach an 80% threshold for tutorial attendance and active participation in the lead up to placement for all Professional Experience courses. Preservice teachers who cannot attend the full tutorial and thus cannot actively participate during the tutorial will not be able to proceed with the placement and complete the course..
title: Pedagogies for Engaged Learners
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course prepares the registered nurse for advanced and/or extended nursing practice. Students will explore and critique the professional role of the nurse in advancing collaboration and navigating political contexts in advanced practice.
title: Preparing for Advanced Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course introduces emergency care principles and focuses on common emergency presentations and management based on evidence. Along with common presentations, students are introduced to principles of triage and prioritisation and undertake clinical skills assessments in context.
title: Foundations for Specialist Emergency Nursing Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Injury Management and Prevention will be studied from anatomical, biomechanical and patho-physiological perspectives, building upon knowledge from previous courses. The emphasis is on understanding the mechanisms, prevention and immediate management of injury in different populations and environments. The theoretical knowledge will be integrated with a variety of practical aspects including accurate identification of important joint lines, tendons, ligaments, bony landmarks, application of modalities such as ice, bandaging, taping, therapeutic massage and spinal board management procedures. This course will broadly examine the context in which sport is situated in our society, discussing in particular moral, ethical and medico-legal aspects.
title: Injury Prevention and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces students to the theory and practice of community engagement and project management. Students work on priority health promotion issues in the community and devise projects to address these. It provides students with theoretical understanding and practical skills required to manage a public health community engagement project. This is a core competency for public health and health promotion practitioners. Students are required to have completed 2214MED Public Health Research Methods and 2218MED Needs Assessment, Program Planning, and Evaluation before enrolling in this course. Core knowledge and skills acquired from these two courses, along with other first and second-year public health courses, are applied in 3132MED.
title: Community Engagement in Public Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores some of the pedagogical implications of the global ownership of English for TESOL practitioners. Students will engage in critical discussions of current research in Global Englishes, the narratives and histories of diverse English-speaking societies, and the paradigm shifts in traditional English language teaching. Students will also consider classroom opportunities for translating theory into practice.
title: Global Englishes in TESOL
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Utilizing case-based learning, this program capstone will provide opportunities for integrating and applying knowledge acquired through courses already studied in the Bachelor of Medical Science Program; to understand the concepts of foundational sciences that underpin disease, and develop skills of problem-solving and clinical reasoning.
title: Integrative Medical Sciences
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: The aim of this course is to provide graduate students with the paradigms and methodologies used in Information Technology. Students will develop the skills necessary to engage in higher degree research and will gain an understanding of the scientific research practices and conventions appropriate for a topic of their choice with the view to producing a research paper.
title: Research for IT Professionals
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Epidemiology plays a fundamental role in public health. In this course, you will learn how to assess disease patterns in different population groups and investigate determinants contributing to the occurrence of disease or health-related events. You will be introduced to various epidemiological study designs and the applications of them to identify potential causes of specified diseases or ill health in community or clinical settings. Importantly, you will learn the tools to identify common sources of error in public health studies and employ a critical appraisal approach to evaluating epidemiological evidence in the health literature. In addition, you will explore the applications of the basic concepts and tools of epidemiology to specific topics on infectious disease outbreak investigation and surveillance, screening and other strategies for disease prevention. Having demonstrated your understanding of the basic concepts of epidemiology and critical analysis approach to investigating health issues, you'll have the skills to apply problem solving techniques to disease control and prevention in communities.
title: Epidemiology: Principles and Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course aims to develop foundational knowledge, values and skills for professional practice as a Registered Nurse. Students will learn about reflective practice, critical thinking, the nursing process, and explore factors that impact nursing practice in contemporary Australian healthcare system. Note: This course is restricted to Bachelor of Nursing and Diploma of Nursing Science (Logan) students ONLY. Prerequisites : NIL Co-requisites : NIL Incompatible : NIL
title: Foundations of Professional Nursing
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course develops students' knowledge and skills to perform comprehensive patient assessments, identify patient deterioration and safely perform complex nursing interventions. Students undertake 80 hours of placement to develop nursing competence in clinical settings congruent with a third-year student level.
title: Complex Clinical Care
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Foundations of Tourism and Hospitality facilitates students to gain a firm grounding in both understanding and working within tourism and hospitality industries. Particular emphasis is placed on the tourism and hospitality systems, sociocultural and environmental factors influencing tourism and hospitality visitor experiences. The effective management of tourism and hospitality industries calls for understanding and foundations in managing human resources, visitor demand, tourism and hospitality product development, and maintaining quality expectations. These skills will be developed in the course through lectures, seminars, a field visit, and a final project. In completing this course, students are encouraged to identify clear career opportunities for themselves within the tourism and hospitality industries.
title: Foundations of Tourism and Hospitality
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The Tourism and Hospitality businesses are largely affected by the intense market competition and other global activities. To overcome these challenges, businesses must implement efficient control systems that can improve resources' utilisation and the processes. This course will develop students' skills and knowledge necessary for efficiently managing the key resources and processes, and equip them to critically evaluate the performance of individual and departments in a timely manner.
title: Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality Control
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course envisions and explores a new paradigm for how the water cycle interacts with the urban landscape to support liveable, sustainable, productive and resilient cities. The course aims to provide participants with an interdisciplinary understanding of the interplay between society, technology and urban design to ensure water security, water resource efficiency, waterway health, flood mitigation, public health and amenity. Participants will critically engage with the underlying principles of a Water Sensitive City and examine socio-technical pathways for facilitating its delivery.
title: Urban Adaptation: Delivering Water Sensitive Cities
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces philosophy generally and the philosophy of education in particular. Content is examined through the lens of practical applications to ethical and critical reasoning in and about education.
title: Philosophy and Ethics in Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course, students will learn how to practically respond to refusals, compliance and other sanctions, appeals and reviews with respect to visas. In this context, students will also gain an understanding of how to formulate appropriate submissions to government. Students will practise in depth submission writing and learn how to respond to a notice of intention to cancel. This course covers preparing for, and assisting at, client appearances before the government or relevant tribunals. Students will appear in a tribunal hearing to demonstrate their developing advocacy skills. This course is the sixth of eight courses that comprise the Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice is a prescribed academic qualification for registration as a migration agent in Australia. The companion course to 7233LAW is 7133LAW which simultaneously builds on the theoretical background necessary for the practical requirements for 7233LAW. Like the other companion courses in the Graduate Diploma Program, in 7233LAW students will learn and apply practitioner skills they need to effectively integrate the legislative content they acquire in 7133LAW. This course is offered in online mode only.
title: Advocacy Skills in Migration Casework
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: The Australian population is ageing, with around 3.5 million (15.1%) aged 65 years or plus (ABS, 2015). The ageing population is anticipated to increase to 20% of the total population by 2026 (Commonwealth of Australia, 2015). Whilst 5.2% of older people reside in care accommodation such as nursing homes, 94.8% live in households and actively participate in community life (ABS, 2015). However, our society still has many stereotypes, myths and negative perceptions. It's time for us to challenge the traditional views of ageing as deficits, dependency, fearfulness and burden. Ageing can also be an active and productive process with participation in employment, social interaction, lifelong learning, and community involvement. This course will help students develop a better understanding of the concepts, theories, and key knowledge of ageing from a positive and critical perspective. Students will also learn how to work with older people. Restriction: This course is not available to Master of Social Work students.
title: Contemporary Issues in Ageing
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces students to the application of the fundamental finance principles and theories in the analysis of real estate and property financing and investment. This course therefore studies the relevant finance tools and techniques in the context of the real estate and property markets paying particular attention to the important features and characteristics of the property markets as well as the relevant aspects of the financial markets and economy.
title: Real Estate Finance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is designed to introduce students to the concept of evidence-based practice (EBP) as a tool to underpin their future practice. Students will develop a broad understanding of the principles and processes of EBP, including formulating clinical questions, searching for and identifying evidence to answer those questions, and appraising evidence. Students will gain an appreciation of qualitative and quantitative methods of research and their use within evidence-based frameworks. Students will also be introduced to the notion of practice change and its management.
title: Research Evidence and Clinical Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course allows students to explore the complex issues relating to clinical, public health and psychosocial aspects of sexual health. Students are encouraged to develop an awareness of sexually transmitted infections, sexual health and sexuality as an integral part of well-being and how this can be related to broader fields of health service delivery. Basic principles of aetiology, transmission, clinical presentation and management relating to sexually transmissible infections will also be addressed. Understanding sexual health and how to identify, treat and prevent sexually transmissible infections, is critical to the enhancement of a broad orientation to health. The central purpose is to provide a sound theoretical basis that underpins this specialty and to develop awareness of its applicability to other areas of practice.
title: Introduction to Sexual Health and STI
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The course will serve as a capstone for the program. It will provide an opportunity for students to reflect critically on their personal and professional development over the program, and use this as a basis for planning their early career. Students will develop an understanding of the importance and required skills for knowledge translation as evidence-based graduates in practice. They will also be supported to further develop a reflective approach to professional practice as a foundation for continuing professional development.
title: Emerging as an Occupational Therapist
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: The relationship between paper, printmaking and books has been one of the most productive and varied in human histories. With the consistent supply of a new substrate, paper, on which the first mechanically printed books were printed, artists began experimenting with prints and have since generated a rich history of artists making prints. This history includes the substrates onto which artists print such as the walls of the Leang Jarie cave in Sulawesi and the Altamira cave in Spain. The handprints in both these caves are examples of relief prints that transport us back thousands of years in time to the moment when they were first printed. This course provides students a foundational understanding of the print making process and introduces them to the essential processes of making relief prints, on paper, and for a book. Prerequisites: Nil
title: Print Foundations
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Introduction to Jewellery and Small Objects offers students the opportunity to explore the materials and processes fundamental to the making of three dimensional objects. A major emphasis of the course will be the development of individual concepts and responses to the set project. Students will be required to undertake independent research into their concept. During class students will be encouraged to develop a range of studio skills to enable them to communicate their individual conceptual, formal and aesthetic concerns in relation to the set project. Prerequisites: Nil
title: Jewellery and Small Objects Foundations
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course involves development of a research project under supervision, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms.
title: Dissertation 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course involves development of a research project under supervision, analysis of literature and execution of experimentation. Results and conclusions are presented in oral and written forms.
title: Dissertation 5
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course will develop skills and knowledge concerning research methods and practices applicable to languages, humanities and social sciences. The course will provide students with frameworks and tools for investigating, analysing and critiquing research practices. It will familiarise students with a broad range of approaches to research, as well as some of the practical considerations of conducting research.
title: Research Methods and Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: The course intends to offer students a deeper perspective of project management within the aviation industry. The course includes discussion of key elements of project management in aviation. This includes consideration of planning, controlling, time management, managing conflicts, controlling costs, executive involvement, performance, review, communication and decision-making. A number of industry specific cases are discussed to illustrate the application of project management theory. Incompatible with: 3512BPS/3512NSC Managing Projects in Aviation.
title: Aviation Project Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Aviation security affects all areas of operation and is of great concern for everyone in the industry. This course provides students with a sound understanding of security measures and regulations in the aviation industry, including principles and practices of risk management in addressing aviation security.
title: Aviation Security and Risk Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course presents an overview of motor development and motor learning theories and investigates the role that movement plays in the educational and developmental contexts of children and adolescents. It is based on the understanding that movement is often integral to one's full participation in a range of educational and life settings such as using a pencil or a spoon to participating in games, sports or recreational activities.
title: Motor Development and Programming
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In today's world, terrorism is one of the inescapable worldwide forces that defines, shapes and reshapes our age. This course will put terrorism and political violence into broad historical context, exploring the experiences of terrorism through the ages and how societies responded to the threats of political violence. From antiquity, through the Middle Ages to the global terrorism of today, this course will unravel the meaning of terrorism and how it was experienced throughout history.
title: A History of Terrorism and Political Violence
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides students with an understanding of the cultural and national factors that affect people management issues in organisations that operate across national borders. It also examines the efficacy of different employment policies and practices within the world economy. The course explains the reasons for the development of different forms of employment practices and the extent to which these differences are sustainable.
title: International and Comparative Human Resource Management and Employment Relations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course provides an overview of legal constraints on public communication, along with an outline of law as it impacts on the Australian media and social media environment. It also addresses some key communication business laws affecting freelancers.
title: Media Law
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course helps students become competent and ethical communicators in the context of public writing. Student are immersed in the craft of persuasive writing within contemporary communications industries, while considering relevant conceptual and ethical issues that are typically encountered in a professional communications environment.
title: Public Writing and Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course considers the role of media relations in strategic communication and equips students with relevant skills, knowledge and theory. Students will develop an understanding of the critical relationship between the strategic communicator and the media. INCOMPATIBLE: CMM220 Media Relations (OUA Course Equivalent).
title: Media Relations
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Coding is an important part of today's world. In this course you will learn how to code in a creative context, utilising a practical and hands-on approach, producing generative art, data visualisations, and interactive interfaces. This course will also introduce the concept of agentic programming, leveraging powerful modern large language models to assist in coding and feature development.
title: Creative Coding
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course, 1008NSC Principles of Forensic Investigation, is available only to students enrolled in the programs 1264 Bachelor of Forensic Science or 1368/1433 Bachelor of Forensic Science/ Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice or 1706 Bachelor of Forensic Science/Bachelor of Criminology and Criminal Justice. It is a core course for the Forensic Molecular Biology Major and for the Forensic Chemistry Major. This course is important within your degree because it aims to instil a broad understanding of the principal investigative methods underlying your professional practice.
title: Principles of Forensic Investigation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Paramedics are required to develop knowledge about respiratory conditions across the lifespan. In this course students develop knowledge, critical thinking, decision making and technical skills required to undertake an assessment and how to manage the patient in an out-of- hospital setting.
title: Respiratory Conditions in Paramedic Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores issues, crisis and disasters communication within a range of contexts drawing on case studies, theory and practice. Students develop the skills to build a crisis communication response plan and team, and effectively manage communication during a crisis. Prerequisites: NIL; Co-requisites: NIL; Incompatible: 3517LHS Risk and Crisis Communication; CMM317 Crisis and Disaster Communication
title: Crisis and Disaster Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Explore social media law and stakeholder theory in the context of social media risk management. Using a series of problem-based social media and crisis communication scenarios, you will apply your understanding of the law and stakeholder theory and test your ability to be a proactive social media manager. You'll identify the key areas of law applying to social media communication internationally and then evaluate a series of legal scenarios and assess how you can respond effectively. These lessons can be applied to developing an effective social media policy, promoting digital literacy and leadership in communication within your organisation. You will analyse social media policies in terms of their risk management for identified stakeholders and create best practice alternatives. These skills are essential for professionals with decision-making roles in social media management and social media marketing. You'll leave this course with a new suite of social media strategies and tools for helping people in your organisation assess social media risk.
title: Social Media Law and Risk Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is the first of two final-year courses in the SPI Major. The course assists students in developing a significant body of work for submission to the Graduation Exhibition, emphasising experimental and preparatory aspects of studio practice. This course should be undertaken during the same trimester and year as 3378QCA 'Studio Thinking' and in the same year as the final Major 4 course leading into the Graduate exhibition. Pre-requisite: Must be undertaking 1651 Bachelor of Visual Arts OR must be undertaking 1652 Bachelor of Visual Arts/Bachelor of Business OR must be undertaking 1187 Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art AND must have completed 2018QCA Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 1 OR must have completed 2391QCA Sculpture Studio 1 AND must have completed 2395QCA Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 2 AND must have completed 2439QCA Memory and Trauma in Visual Culture OR must have completed 3426QCA Art of Portraiture: History and Theory OR must have completed 2440QCA Abstraction OR must have completed 3403QCA Australian Art OR must have completed 2431QCA Art, Gender, Sexuality and the Body OR must have completed 2916QCA The Art of Resistance
title: Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course explores how political actors and institutions shape voting behaviour among ordinary citizens. The analytical approach of the class is comparative, and the empirical material covers young and consolidated democracies.
title: Parties, Campaigns and Elections
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: The mass media have a unique fascination with sport. Sport obtains its own section in newspapers, as well as in radio and television broadcasts. There are numerous magazines devoted to sport. Coordination of relations between sport organisations and media has become a specialised realm of sport management. Sport organisations coordinate their media relations through the Sports Information Director (SID) or media liaison officer. That person is responsible for developing relations with reporters and editors, formulating a media plan, and providing information to the press. Sport information is a pivotal component of the sport organisation's marketing communications campaign.
title: Sport Digitisation and Communication
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course provides an overview of the various political, economic, social, environmental, demographic and technological factors that influence the delivery of sport. The contexts examined in class range from community sport organisations to elite sport and events, and an array of contemporary issues and examples are used to illustrate how each factor is impacting sport management.
title: Contemporary Issues in Sport Business
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Volunteers are important to the sport and events industry. Not only do they provide labour to sport and events from local to international levels, volunteering provides opportunities for community engagement and the development of social capital. This course seeks to understand volunteer participation and involvement in sport and events from individual, organisational, management and policy perspectives.
title: Managing Volunteers for Sport and Events
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The Rooms Division of a hotel/resort enterprise generates the most revenue, and their staff and management have the most interaction with the guests. Therefore the management of the Rooms Division is crucial to the overall profitability and level of guest service that a hotel/resort provides. This course allows students to learn both management theory and management operational skills that are relevant to the successful operation of the Rooms Division of a hotel/resort.
title: Rooms Division Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course is an introduction to western twentieth-century art history. It covers mid-century to the 1980s. This course must be successfully completed prior to commencing 2nd year level art theory courses.
title: Introduction to Art Theory 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: What are the determinants of sexual health and wellbeing? In this course you will explore and reflect on this important aspect of health within your profession and in a range of contexts. You will analyse determinants of sexual health, wellbeing and wellness to inform and implement strategies for sexual health promotion. You will critically discuss the concept of safe(r) sex from a wellness perspective and use a public health lens to analyse the impact of ethics and legislation on sexual health promotion and outcomes. You will be given the tools to design and justify a sexual health promotion initiative that meets the sexual health needs of a specific population of interest
title: Promoting Sexual Health and Wellness
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course covers key theories common to a range of communication professionals, and introduces students to strategic considerations in communication. The course encourages students to think critically about the role of communication in modern society, and how both theory and practice are necessary to effective strategic communications.
title: Communication Principles and Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course enables students to develop a critical understanding of ethics and professional practice in the contexts of journalism and strategic communication. It offers a highly practical, 'hands on' focus on ethical decision-making and social considerations in the workplace.
title: Ethical Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Students will consolidate midwifery knowledge and extend understanding regarding the role of the midwife in supporting women and families experiencing significant challenges that impact maternal and infant wellbeing and childbirth. Ethically challenging areas including domestic violence, perinatal mental health, grief and loss will be examined within a Trauma Informed and supportive framework.
title: Challenges in Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course considers different ways of conceptualising and implementing curriculum in early childhood settings and explores ways in which teachers and children can work together to create curriculum that is meaningful to children whilst meeting the expectations of parents and society.
title: Curriculum and Pedagogy in the Early Years
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This 40CP Dissertation is offered within the 5263 Master of Public Health (MPH) and the 5725 Master of Global Public Health (MGPH) programs. The 40CP dissertation is similar to an Honours dissertation in type and scope and gives students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest. The Dissertation involves the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, collection and analysis of data. The background literature, methodology. findings and conclusions are presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis. The thesis is expected to be between 15,000 and 20,000 words in length, depending on disciplinary demands and problem requirements. Please note that Course Convenor approval is needed to be able to enrol in the Dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In this course, students will identify the requirements and procedures relating to refusals, compliance and other sanctions, appeals and reviews with respect to visas. Students will also review and appraise alternative pathways to meet client needs. They will learn how to develop appropriate strategies for providing effective advices to clients particularly in relation to character cancellations and sanctions, cancellation of sponsorships, exclusions and deportations. This course is the fifth of eight courses that comprise the Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice is a prescribed academic qualification for registration as a migration agent in Australia. The companion course to 7133LAW is 7233LAW (Practitioner Focus) which simultaneously builds on the practical background to immerse students in a virtual office environment. Like the other companion courses in the Graduate Diploma Program, in 7233LAW students will learn and apply practitioner skills they need to effectively integrate the legislative content they acquire in 7133LAW. This course is offered in online mode only.
title: Visa Compliance, Cancellation and Review
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Pre-service teachers will demonstrate mastery of foundational knowledge for teaching health and physical learning and of social and personal development from Prep to Grade 6. Pre-service teachers will critically reflect on the sociocultural perspective of the HPE curriculum, which includes demonstrating an understanding of the multidimensional nature of health and physical education. This course will prepare pre-service teachers by providing them with the essential knowledge and communication skills necessary to justify and interpret models and theoretical frames and guiding propositions necessary for successfully teaching health and physical education. Thus, pre-service teachers will be able to implement appropriate ways to plan, teach, assess and evaluate health and physical education lessons throughout the schooling years Prep - 6.
title: Health and Physical Learning in the Primary years
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Students in this course will have the opportunity to develop their understanding of global women's health including the social determinants of health (e.g. cultural, environmental, economic and political determinants) and the principles of primary health care. Due to the health-related content of this course it is only recommended for current or previous students of health programs. The course is a level 3 course and students must have successfully completed at least 80CP of undergraduate study to participate.
title: Global Women's Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: East Asia's pursuit of rapid economic growth, marked by authoritarian developmentalism in Northeast Asia and 'rationalised' corruption in Southeast Asia, has been challenged in recent years. This course examines the causes and processes associated with the adoption of democratic procedures in Asia, as well as the reasons for reversals in democracy and authoritarian resilience. It explores the relationships between democratic quality, rule of law, market liberalisation, political culture, civil society and 'good governance' in Asia, as well as the prospects for tackling corruption in business and politics, and promoting transparency and governance-based reforms across the broad range of political regimes that are to be found in Asia. Covering democracies of varying quality through to military regimes and one-party socialist states, case material can be drawn from the contemporary experiences of Japan, Korea, Taiwan, and the People's Republic of China in Northeast Asia, and Singapore, Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, Cambodia and Myanmar in Southeast Asia.
title: Democratisation, Business and Governance in Asia
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course has a dual role. Firstly, it examines ethics and ethical practices in the investment profession. Secondly, it is designed to provide students with an understanding of alternative investment vehicles, tools of their analysis and applications. Ethical practices instil public trust in the fairness of financial markets and transactions, allowing them to function efficiently. The perspectives acquired in this subject should be useful to students in their chosen finance profession as this subject presents a framework for ethical conduct in the investment profession by focusing on the CFA Institute Code of Ethics and Standards of Professional Conduct.
title: Ethics and Alternative Investments
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course continues to focus on developing the skills, knowledge and personal qualities for supporting communication and/or swallowing in individuals and communities across the lifespan. To develop skills in evidence-based speech pathology practice, you will attend a 2-day per week external placement, working within different service delivery and supervision models. You will work under the supervision of a speech pathology practice educator. Learning is further supported by skills-based tutorials, professional practice workshops, interprofessional learning activities, and a simulated learning experience. Competencies required for speech pathology practice are informed by the Professional Standards (Speech Pathology Australia, 2020) and assessed by COMPASS® (Speech Pathology Australia, 2011).
title: Speech Pathology Skills and Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course incorporates essential professional knowledge for clinical physiologists including issues such as ethical and legal implications of clinical practice in the Australian Healthcare system, psychological aspects of communication with patients, reflective practice and reflective writing in a health care setting, essential elements of career planning and employability in healthcare, and the application of clinical research methodologies and statistical analysis.
title: Professional Issues: Research methodology, legal and ethical issues
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Human Biology provides foundational knowledge in human anatomy, physiology, and cell biology essential to the biological and biomedical sciences. The course explores major body systems and the integration and regulation of these systems to maintain homeostasis. Incompatible with 1014MSC Cells, Tissues and Regulation.
title: Human Biology: from Cells to Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course aims to equip you with the skills and knowledge required to secure excellent digital photographic images of scenes and exhibits of forensic interest, and to prepare them for evidential purposes. You will also develop crime scene examination skills including searching and documentation of evidence incorporating both written and digital photographic recording techniques. It therefore covers digital image processing techniques of interest and importance to the forensic practitioner, providing a significant "hands-on" component of training in digital photographic techniques.
title: Forensic Evidence Imaging and Documentation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course builds on 2003ESC Forensic Biology and examines contemporary forensic DNA profiling for human identification and investigative applications. Students will evaluate short tandem repeat (STR) profiles generated using multiplex PCR-based systems, including single-source and mixed DNA profiles, and interpret evidential weight using match probabilities and likelihood ratios. The course also examines mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA), single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analysis and emerging forensic genomic technologies. Applications include activity-level DNA evidence evaluation, wildlife forensic DNA analysis, and the communication of DNA evidence in forensic reports and court.
title: Forensic DNA Profiling
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Students will apply widely used techniques (e.g. immunoassays, protein assay and characterisation tests, and a variety of clinical and/or neuroscience tests) to design and execute experiments. They will present scientific reports and a group seminar. In addition, there will be one short formative assessment about the first practical component of the course and a final quiz at the end of the term on the theoretical and practical aspects of the work carried out.
title: Biomedical Sciences Laboratory
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course highlights the importance of formal accreditation of forensic laboratories and the significance and purpose of quality assurance, quality control and quality systems for world-class forensic laboratories.
title: Forensic Laboratory Accreditation and Quality Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course explores the highly specific economics associated with the aviation industry. It will introduce students to basic economic theories and concepts and applies these concepts to the aviation industry. Prior Assumed: Nil Incompatible: AVN7004 Aviation Economics
title: Aviation Economics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The aviation industry is a high cost undertaking relying on sophisticated technology in all areas of its business activities. There is a need for future aviation sector managers to understand this complex environment and the many management challenges and pitfalls that are present. The course is designed to provide an insight into all management areas of the aviation business so that future managers have a broad perspective in a growing competitive and increasingly globalized industry. Prior Assumed: Nil Incompatible: AVN7001 Airline Management, AVN3008 Aviation Management for Pilots and 3008AVN Aviation Management for Pilots
title: Aviation Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This IPS course is designed to facilitate, guide and stimulate your interest and commitment to an increased understanding of what constitutes effective communication. It is a skills-based course, constructed to assist you to develop necessary communication skills to maintain personal and professional interactions. Using an active learning approach, 1008HSV teaches you communication theory, as well as affords opportunities to apply practically to solidify learning. In preparation for your role as professionals in the field, you will be encouraged in this course to think of yourselves as practitioners-in-training. One of the implications of this, is that we expect you to be self-managing in terms of your own learning and the learning of your colleagues. The skills acquired will subsequently serve as a scaffold for more advanced skills as you progress through your degree. Trimester 3 (Intensive Offering) is restricted to students in external/distance Human Services and Social Work programs (Programs 1394, 1637, 1263, 1372, 1416, and 8073 only).
title: Interpersonal Skills
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will introduce students to the processes and procedures of cost planning as a cost control tool in the pre-construction process. They will examine the impact of design on the capital and life cycle cost of buildings, and develop their understanding of concepts such as value engineering and management. This course will foster their appreciation of bidding strategies and build their understanding of the relationship and differences between the cost planning and tendering processes.
title: Cost Planning and Tendering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course requires the execution, analysis and presentation of a scientific research thesis. This course involves the development of a research project, an analysis of appropriate literature background and the execution of research methodology, data collection and data analysis. Results from these experiments are also evaluated and conclusions drawn with findings presented in a formal context in written form. Restriction: FOURTH YEAR BY APPLICATION ONLY
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course requires the execution, analysis and presentation of a scientific research thesis. This course involves the development of a research project, an analysis of appropriate literature background and the execution of research methodology, data collection and data analysis. Results from these experiments are also evaluated and conclusions drawn with findings presented in a formal context in written form. Restriction: FOURTH YEAR BY APPLICATION ONLY
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Communication and Counselling in Dietetics (CCD) will provide students with the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct a dietetic consultation, including counselling individuals to change food choice and eating behaviours. Students will develop and practice communication and counselling skills in workshops and in consultations with real and simulated patients, and will learn to work as an effective member of an Interprofessional team. This course forms part of the knowledge base for the Nutrition Care Process placement in Year 4.
title: Communication and Counselling in Dietetics
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This is an introductory course to Aviation law with respect to the aviation industry in Australia. The course will cover two primary topics: (i) Basic principles of law in relation to the aviation industry. - Contract law - Tort law (Negligence, Trespass and Nuisance) - Administrative law (relating to the Civil Aviation Safety Authority (CASA), and - International law (ii) Introduction to Aviation Regulation, designed to guide students through the extensive regulatory system governing aviation. Incompatible: 2509NSC Aviation Legal Studies; 2509BPS Aviation Legal Studies.
title: Introduction to Aviation Law
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course includes a project consisting of a supervised design investigation and structured assessments. Students will gain knowledge pertinent to architecture and/or landscape architecture as well as develop critical, creative and analytical thinking and effective problem-solving and communication skills. Enrolment depends on the 1492 Program Director consent. This course is only available to students enrolled in program code 1492. Prerequisite 2902ENV - Studio 3.
title: City and Landscape Design Special Topic
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this course students will undertake a 10,000 to 12,000 word research paper over the course of one year, as part of a staged process and under supervision. Prerequisites: Students must be in their final or penultimate year of their LLB or JD degree program AND have a minimum program GPA of 5.50 to undertake this course. Co-requisite: 6001LAW Legal Research Methods.
title: Thesis Work in Progress
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Finance has a central role in any organisation, as it helps managers make decisions on how to fund the business, where to responsibly invest and how to allocate financial resources for responsible value creation. This course provides students with a broad understanding of important finance concepts and introduces new frameworks that allow business leaders to make informed and responsible decisions for a sustainable future of their organisations. The course covers a variety of modules that focus on how to make informed and responsible decisions in relation to corporate governance, valuation, risk, capital budgeting, and dividends amongst others. The course will empower students with a novel toolkit that allows sound financial decision making and an understanding of how 'good' finance goes beyond shareholders' value creation. Students will be able to use finance to make beneficial decisions that go well beyond profit. This course is normally offered every 4 teaching periods.
title: Finance for Responsible Value Creation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This subject examines strategies for changing criminal behaviour. The interventions explored in the subject are most frequently observed within the correctional system in both custodial and community settings; however, programs utilised in other sectors of the criminal justice system (i.e. police, courts) and in affiliated social service organisations are also included in the subject where forensic populations are their target treatment group. The subject draws on psychological principles and research evidence, linking theories of crime causation to foundations of behaviour modification and propensity-reducing interventions. A review of specific programs is presented, although the focus of the subject is on the overarching design principles associated with positive client outcomes.
title: Interventions for Correctional Clients
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will introduce students to the Fundamental Biology of Microbes, including Bacteria, Viruses and Eukaryotes. The course will cover how Microbes survive in niche environments, Microbes as Pathogens, and will include focus areas of Medical Microbiology, Industrial and Applied, and Environmental Microbiology.
title: Fundamentals of Microbiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: It is conservatively estimated that 70% of forensic mental health (FMH) clients in Australia are males of functioning intelligence who have English as their preferred language and who align themselves with the dominant Australian culture. As they comprise such a large proportion of the FMH client group, the majority of resources and interventions are targeted towards them. This then means that there are a number of minority populations within FMH, who without our intentional investment and understanding would not receive effective assessment, intervention and management. This subject examines the special needs of these minority FMH groups, namely the specific needs of the elderly, adolescents, women, people with an intellectual disability, people of a different culture or language, and Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Incompatibles: 7105CCJ Special Needs in Forensic Mental Health, MCCJ7105 Special Needs in Forensic Mental Health
title: Minority Populations in Forensic Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: In this course, teachers will develop their knowledge and understanding of the personal, social, environmental, cultural and historical significance and relevance of science. Today's science students need to be able to make informed, evidence-based decisions about current and future applications of science. Students also need to recognise that science has advanced through, and is open to, the contributions of many people from different cultures at different times in history, and that science offers rewarding career paths. This course will provide teachers with explicit curriculum materials and contemporary pedagogical strategies to enable them to successfully integrate the teaching of the Australian Curriculum strand Science as a Human Endeavour into their science classes.
title: Science as a Human Endeavour
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Concentrating on effective communication within a variety of digital formats and mediums, this course develops students' theoretical and practice-led understandings of usability, visual hierarchy, 2D and 3D visual structures, and creative visualization, applying these through a variety of interactive media technologies.
title: Visual Communication Strategies
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Students will learn about the 12 body systems contributing to normal human physiology to enable them to integrate anatomical and physiological processes in the context of pregnancy and childbirth. Students will also develop applied physiological and pharmacological knowledge that will be required in later courses.
title: Foundational Anatomy and Physiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course focuses on human behaviour within organisational contexts. It highlights the relationships among people and organisations through relevant theories and concepts that are important in obtaining critical insight into current organisational behaviour issues.
title: Organisational Behaviour and Wellbeing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This subject is designed to consolidate the knowledge gained in the previous courses by analysing a live crime problem. Students working as a group will generate hypotheses, apply various analytic techniques to test these, prepare a report to be presented to the relevant command team.
title: Intelligence Led Policing
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

The combined 8002AHS courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, approval from relevant ethics committee/s, data collection, analysis and write-up of findings. At the completion of the four Dissertation courses students will submit a thesis for examination.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: As a physiotherapist your knowledge, understanding, and skill in the assessment and management of patients with spinal musculoskeletal conditions is critical to your professional competence. For this reason, this course provides you with valuable opportunities to develop your understanding of, and skill in the assessment, diagnosis, treatment and overall management of patients with spinal musculoskeletal conditions. As a student, you will extend your knowledge and skill in musculoskeletal physiotherapy practice through exposure to theoretical and experiential learning activities that focus on manual therapy, exercise rehabilitation, clinical reasoning, communication and education.
title: Spinal Musculoskeletal Physiotherapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces students to hazardous waste treatment and disposal. The contents of the course include introduction to hazardous waste, hazardous waste generation and characteristics, transportation and storage of hazardous waste, physical, chemical and biological treatment, thermal treatment and energy recovery, stabilisation and solidification and land disposal of hazardous waste.
title: Hazardous Waste Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Religion has returned to the public stage in recent decades, not only in the less-developed world, but also in emerging economies and wealthy post-industrial states. Our contemporary era is now often referred to as a post-secular age. This course examines the resurgence of religion in the context of globalisation and its consequences for politics and international relations. We investigate the historical and sociological conditions that have given rise to this phenomenon in addition to more immediate political, ideological, and religious factors. We investigate the nature of resurgent religions and the challenges posed to liberal assumptions about secularism, democracy, human rights, violence and conflict, and international relations. The course takes a multidisciplinary approach in using sociological, political science and international relations' perspectives to gain an understanding of the complex intersection of religion, politics, and globalisation in the contemporary world.
title: Religion, Politics and Globalisation
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course is a capstone experience in students' training as a professional counsellor. 3015PSY is one of two final-year professional placement courses for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Counselling. Through this course, you will augment your developing knowledge and skills through working with real clients under supervision in an organisation that provides counselling-related services to the community. You will further develop professional counselling competencies, build theoretical knowledge, and expand your industry knowledge and experience working in a team, including interdisciplinary teams where applicable. Prerequisites: Student must complete 150 credit points of the Bachelor of Counselling including: 1018PSY Counselling Skills & 3005PSY Counselling Theory & Professional Practice & 3002LFC OR 2023PSY & 3007HSV OR 2023PSY.
title: Counselling Practicum 2: Reflective Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: The available internship is placement with the Griffith Tax Clinic. Students working at the Griffith Tax Clinic provide important assistance to vulnerable members of the community, by providing tax advice to members of the public who are struggling with their tax obligations. Students will have a fantastic opportunity to learn first-hand how their studies are relevant and can be applied to real taxpayers. The course challenges motivated students to apply their knowledge and training in this real-world setting by offering them the opportunity to participate in a work integrated learning (WIL) activity at the Griffith Tax Clinic. This internship is relevant to students studying Commerce, particularly Accounting, Finance, Financial Planning and/or Economics majors. The Griffith Tax Clinic operates from the Logan campus and/or online via Teams. Students are expected to attend and perform their duties as directed (in-person or online). Allocation of students to a place in the Griffith Tax Clinic is at the discretion of the Course Convenor. Students are supported by the Course Convenor, a WIL Coordinator and/or an Academic Supervisor, and a registered tax agent. Despite this support, students must maintain professional standards and take responsibility for their learning and development. Prerequisites: Completed approximately half of their relevant degree and the successful completion of the course: Taxation Law (2150AFE). There is an application process which closes approximately 4 weeks prior to the commencement of the Trimester. This requires students to formally register their interest in the Griffith Tax Clinic and submit their CV and academic transcript. Shortlisted applicants will be interviewed to determine selection. Enrolment is strictly restricted to students who have completed this application process, secured an internship placement, and received formal class enrolment permission.
title: Tax Clinic
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Global Health and Human Rights aims to promote students' understanding of the concepts and processes of human rights that underpin public health in the global context. The course will examine the history and theoretical concepts surrounding human rights including the international human rights system and rights-based approaches to health. Case studies will be used to explore ways these concepts have been integrated into public health practice including the importance of engaging the community, facilitating community mobilisation and stimulating positive social change.
title: Global Health and Human Rights
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course focuses on current perspectives on globalisation as it investigates the links between globalisation and education. Students will gain advanced knowledge and understanding of the economic, political and cultural dimensions of globalisation and of the major interpretive approaches to globalisation. They will analyse and synthesise the impact of globalisation on world trends in education, including on cross-cultural and trans-national trends in education provision and on the emerging global and regional structures in education. Particular emphasis will be placed on understandings of knowledge as a global construct and the subsequent positioning of students and educational professionals as knowledge workers in learning communities in a globalising world. In response to understandings of global learning communities, students will have the opportunity to study an approved course in another (global) university.
title: Learning and Teaching in Global Communities
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This foundational course introduces students to the Australian legal system, legislation and healthcare professional bodies. title: Legal and Ethical Principles in Healthcare
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course develops the ability to engineer integrated mechatronic and automated systems. Students combine mechanical, electrical, electronic, computing and control engineering through a structured design process spanning problem definition, system design, implementation, integration and verification. Practical activities and a substantial project develop the technical judgement required to create and evaluate functional mechatronic systems.
title: Mechatronic Systems Design and Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: As a student in this course, you will explore the role of physiotherapy in assessing and treating individuals across the lifespan, with a focus on paediatric populations. You will emphasise preventative and rehabilitative care in a variety of clinical settings to children as they grow and develop. You will also acquire the knowledge and skills to plan, deliver and evaluate high quality, effective physiotherapy and inter-professional services for paediatric clinical populations within a family-centred model of care. This course builds on the foundations acquired in year one and two and links with future clinical placements.
title: Physiotherapy Across the Lifespan 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: In this course students will examine the Queensland Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Child Protection (QATSICPP) Practice Standards in the context of the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Child Protection Sector. Students will develop foundational skills and knowledge to provide services to Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander children, young people and families. Students will examine foundational documents of the Practice Standards including (but not limited to), 'Taking Responsibility: A roadmap for Queensland Child Protection' (Carmody Report) and the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Child Placement Principle. RESTRICTED: Enrolment in 7050HSV is by permission only and is limited to QATSCIPP members and Indigenous Department of Child Safety employees.
title: Qld Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Community Controlled Child Protection Practice Standards
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

Students will be introduced to techniques and tools in mining associative and sequential patterns, abnormality detection, correlation analysis, clustering, and forecasting.
title: Applied Data Mining
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This interdisciplinary online course introduces students to transnational eco-cinema studies through an exploration of 21st-century films. Designed for a diverse student cohort, it brings together those with interests in Italian studies, the environmental humanities or screen studies. No prior knowledge of film analysis is required; the course presents the necessary concepts and tools for analysis from an eco-cinema perspective. However, students who do have experience in screen studies will be able to extend their knowledge of the cinematic traditions informing contemporary film-making as well as exploring the new methodological framework of eco-cinema. Students of Italian will further develop their linguistic, cultural and intercultural competence through access to additional resources in Italian and completion of assessment in Italian. For those not studying Italian, all necessary materials are provided in English.
title: Eco-Cinema
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: In this course, students will learn to design, evaluate, interpret, and report the findings of behaviour change interventions. Using case studies, students will apply these skills to increase socially significant behaviours in ways that make positive differences in people's lives. Co-requisite 7804AHS Ethical and Professional Conduct in Applied Behaviour Analysis. Prerequisites 7801AHS Introduction to Applied Behaviour Analysis and 7802AHS Assessing and Measuring Behaviour
title: Behaviour Change Interventions
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

This course will introduce the analysis of forensic chemical trace evidence both in theory, and within the laboratory where students will examine items relating to a fictitious arson case. It will include chemical trace evidence - glass, paint, fibres, impression evidence - fingermarks, shoeprints and toolmarks, arson and explosives. It will be restricted to students in the forensic science program.
title: Forensic Chemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Creativity can drive innovation in business and provide unique competitive advantage. In this course you'll learn about how to foster the behaviours that contribute to creativity so you can work collaboratively to facilitate game-changing products, systems and services. It all starts with ideas: how they are generated, nurtured and implemented through teams and projects. You'll investigate the components of creativity and how others apply their creative skills to strategic thinking and planning. With the recognition that creative outcomes are achieved through a variety of approaches, you will have the tools to build collaborative space to guide an agile approach to team-based projects within your organisation, driving enhanced performance.
title: Managing Creativity in Organisations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Pharmacists are ideally placed to provide advice on minor ailments, such as skin disorders and support complex health consumers, such as those with mental health conditions. This course invites students to consider the current evidence of the pharmacist's role/s in these therapeutic areas and to explore their personal and professional attitudes and beliefs towards supporting mental health consumers. This course continues and extends the development of students' understanding of the professional role of a primary health care provider, medication manager and specific services offered within a multidisciplinary health care team. The course will engage students with problem-based learning activities and real-life case scenarios that are relevant to pharmacy practice.
title: Pharmacy Practice III
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Gain an introduction to ethical, anti-colonial and collaborative practice with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander communities and community-run organisations. You will learn ways of seeing, being and doing that strongly align with the knowledges and philosophy of Indigenous peoples. Organisations striving to foster diversity and inclusion need leadership that's grounded in critical thinking, strategic thinking and cultural humility. You'll examine anti-oppressive practices from a social justice and human rights perspective and discuss connection between historic policy and practice and the current socio-economic circumstances of First Peoples Communities in Australia. The long-term sustainability of multicultural organisations and the wider society depends on getting this right, with a focus on ethics, cultural safety, social equity and social justice. By completing this course, you'll be able to explain key principles to deliver equitable, culturally safe and socially just services to these communities. You'll finish with a range of practice models that support you and your organisation to successfully deliver sustainable services in partnership and collaboration with First Peoples Communities, centring Indigenous knowledge and Aboriginal culture and identity.
title: Working with First Peoples Communities
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides an introduction to symbolic logic and automated reasoning, which together form a branch of artificial intelligence known as symbolic AI, as well as a branch of mathematics and philosophy. The course covers classical and non-classical logics, proof theory, and automated reasoning for these logics. Trending topics such as neural reasoning with large language models and hybrid neural-symbolic reasoning are also discussed.
title: Logic and Automated Reasoning
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology
