academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Discrete structures are foundational in that many areas of computer science require the ability to work with concepts from discrete structures and it is pervasive in the areas of data structures and algorithms. Discrete structures includes important material from such areas as set theory, relations, functions, logic, proof techniques, basic counting graph theory, and linear algebra.
title: Discrete Structures
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This clinically-based, research informed course expands on the basic principles and concepts relating to the specialty discipline and introduces clinical procedures and management of patients, research-informed case presentations and journal reviews.
title: Knowledge and clinical practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Literacy and gender are two of the biggest issues facing contemporary Western educational systems. Both can have significant impacts on students' educational experiences, outcomes and life trajectories.. This course critically examines the relationships between gender, literacy pedagogies, behaviour and schooling to give insights into the ways in which educators might think differently about addressing students' behavioural and academic (under)performances. Drawing upon a range of contemporary theories, frameworks, media artefacts and real world examples, the course provides students with opportunities to undertake research into a pressing and significant educational issue and to present their findings to a community of peers.
title: Gender and Literacy
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Project and Cyber Security Management is a designated field of study. It involves the project management for cyber security. It requires Issue identification and solution development for cyber defence, which is critical for organisational governance. It is about thoroughly understanding cyber threats, attacks, and incidents and addressing them through state-of-the-art technologies, tools and methods. This course will lead the student to understand further cyber issues (threats, attacks, incidents) and establish a project around cyber issues using state-of-the-art project management principles, including conceptual solutions, project planning, task workflows and execution for end-to-end project delivery.
title: Project and Cyber Security Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course provides a comprehensive understanding of theory and research relevant to all aspects of development for people with autism across the lifespan from childhood to late adulthood. Change and development in real life environments for people with autism and their communities over time are the focus of this course. Topics explore experiences in school, co-morbid mental health issues, managing vocational environments, tertiary education, and ageing.
title: Across the Lifespan
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Mechanics of Materials 1 (also known as Stress Analysis) provides techniques by which engineers can predict stress and strain distributions resulting from known loading conditions so that the stability and strength of structural members and machine components under load can be assessed. Mechanics of Materials 1 is an essential tool in the analysis and design of structures and machines under load.
title: Mechanics of Materials I
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course focuses on the complex conditions of Trauma, Shock and Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome. Students will explore aetiology, pathophysiology and the complexity involved in multidisciplinary interventions required to manage and effectively care for people with these conditions.
title: Trauma, Shock and Multiple Organ Dysfunction Syndrome
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course provides students with further knowledge of anatomy and physiology during pregnancy, labour, birth and the postpartum period, and of the fetus and the neonate. There is a beginning understanding of alterations in normal physiology. Students learn basic microbiology as it relates to childbearing and methods of controlling infection. On completion of this course students will be able to relate their knowledge of the human body to midwifery practice.
title: Life Science for Midwives
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The Financing Health and Social Care course has been designed to be relevant for industry and will offer a range of activities that participants may encounter in a typical workplace. The course links theory and practice by discussing contemporary theoretical concepts and applying this knowledge in the reflective questions and assessment items. This course will provide industry-based scenarios designed around financial decision-making in health and social care services which provides further links to practice and enhanced understanding of the application of theoretical principles.
title: Healthcare Finance and Budgeting
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Epidemiology is the study of the distribution and determinants of health-related states or events in specified populations. The application of this study involves studies that elicit information pertaining to prevention, planning, control of population health problems." This course introduces the fundamental principles and practices of epidemiology in public health. Students will examine basic epidemiological concepts and methods, explore their application, perform elementary epidemiological reviews and critiques, and reflect in the role of epidemiology in public health.
title: Epidemiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores the use of mobile, online and digital technology to assist and enhance language learning/acquisition. Students are introduced to theories underpinning the design and implementation of technology enhanced language learning programs. This course provides students with opportunities to develop professional and personal competence in a wide range of applications of technology for language learning and teaching including the use of computers, mobile devices, websites and apps. Students will also learn how to critically evaluate pedagogical applications of technology for language learning and teaching.
title: Technology Enhanced Language Learning and Teaching
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Designers are increasingly working in the digital realm, with advances in electronics opening up new possibilities and challenging preconceptions about the design of interactive products and electrical devices. This course provides designers with an introduction to how electronics are supporting design innovation, and practical studio experience of the fundamentals of how electrical devices operate and how to build electronic circuits.
title: Electrics and Electronics for Designers
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course explains Australian law as it applies to Business and Commerce, including the Australian legal system, law of contract, Australian Consumer Law, the law of general and professional negligence and other torts, Business Structures (including the law of agency and partnership), company law and Corporate Governance. This course aims to ensure you can identify legal issues, apply relevant law to resolve problems, defend your application of law, and provide reasoned legal conclusions in the face of scrutiny. You will also learn the historical context of these laws, so you understand how and why they came into practice. These are crucial skills in business, as the rule of law modulates the relationships between companies and consumers, government, suppliers, customers and competitors. You should, through oral and written communication, be capable of applying legal knowledge in order to reach reasoned conclusions about complex business situations, relating to business regulation or corporate governance. Your newfound problem-solving skills should help you make more informed decisions about how the law impacts your business dealings.
title: Principles of Business and Corporations Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: In this course, students will learn about transitioning into professional nursing contexts, including managing and leading intra/interprofessional teams, and using digital information for quality and safety. Students will create a practice portfolio to support their development as a Registered Nurse.
title: Transition to Professional Nursing
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The history of humanity is a tale of empires: their rise, their fall, and the complicated legacies they leave behind. This course examines how and why empires shaped our understanding of humanity across a vast sweep of time. Through a selection of case studies from the ancient to the modern world, we will examine the ways that empires comprehended both human diversity and human unity through the experience of conquest and colonisation, corruption and collapse. Our case studies will include: Ancient Rome (c. 100 BCE-200 CE), Europe's "Gunpowder Empires" (c. 1400-1600 CE), and Britain's Empire (c. 1700-1800 CE). By using a range of primary sources (texts, maps, images, and artefacts), the course will provide an opportunity to develop vital analytical and communication skills by engaging in historical research. In the process, the leading ideas that have shaped our world will be located and extracted from the human past.
title: History of Empire: Humanity from the Ancient to the Modern World
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course examines advanced concepts in organic chemistry, building on topics introduced in Second Year. This course provides students with advanced knowledge and skills for concepts in organic synthesis, reaction mechanisms, the role of catalysis (organometallics), understanding the 3D-shape of organic molecules (stereochemistry) and experimental techniques in organic chemistry. Knowledge and experimental skills in these areas are required for a career in industries such as pharmaceuticals, chemicals and materials science. Prerequisites: 2103NSC Organic Chemistry (Nathan) OR 2014MSC Organic Chemistry (Gold Coast). Incompatible: 3131SCE Advanced Organic Chemistry.
title: Advanced Organic Chemistry
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will examine the key elements of a safety management system and the associated systems, processes and procedures used in achieving high safety standards in aviation organisations. There will be a strong emphasis on the importance of critical thinking with regards to methods, systems and processes used to implement safety management systems to enhance aviation safety.
title: Safety Management Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: You will identify, examine, apply and evaluate the principles and practices of curriculum design, programming and the selection of pedagogical strategies for quality teaching and learning. The course emphasises theory/practice connections and balances internationally recognised theoretical principles with practical, constructive applications.
title: Foundations of Curriculum, Pedagogy and Assessment
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course focuses on the teaching of reading in the early years as a research-informed and research-led practice. It begins by exploring how important it is for primary teachers to make best-practice decisions based on published educational research across the following elements of early reading instruction: phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension and oral language. To do this effectively, beginning teachers need to learn how to read research literature that makes use of a range of research methodologies. Beginning teachers must also develop skills relating to the effective use of student data, including how to read, moderate, interpret and then employ these data to enhance learning and teaching process.
title: English Education 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course explores how children acquire language and become literate. It examines how literature can be used to support emergent and early literacy including knowledge of the process that occurs in a novice brain during progression towards mastery. It will develop knowledge of, and skill in the need to adjust practice in response.
title: Language, literacy and literature for Prep to Grade 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The course places the learning and developmental needs of preservice teachers in primary and secondary education settings within the broader frame of lifelong learning which promotes self-directed learning across the lifespan, including the shift from scaffolded to self-directed learning of preservice teachers as they move towards mastery of knowledge and skills. Focusing on the interrelated nature of development within school-aged students across four domains and an understanding of how teachers can support development and the role of the brain in learning, PST explore the implications for their teaching practices as their students move from novice to expert. including how the brain learns, the function of memory, and the implications for practice including adjustments as students move towards mastery.
title: Understanding the child learner
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course applies the principles of marketing to oneself. As such, broad topic areas include the self-marketing mix, self-marketing research, self-marketing tactics and implementation and self-marketing evaluation. In doing so, students learn how to develop, manage and sustain positive self-images/brand that are well-received in the "real world", both on a professional and personal basis.
title: Self-Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course advances the physiology taught in first year with particular emphasis on the cardiovascular, respiratory, metabolic and renal body systems. The course focuses on the integrated functions of these systems from a clinical perspective. It forms the foundation of applied physiology courses that follow and will consist of on-line lectures, workshops, laboratory sessions and case study analysis.
title: Integrated Systems Physiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides students with an opportunity to explore key aspects of occupational therapy in greater depth, in preparation for becoming a professional. The course will focus on specific areas of knowledge, skills and attitudes that are relevant to occupational therapy in a range of settings. Topics covered will include professional reasoning, evidence based practice, negotiating complex practice situations, legal, ethical and safe approaches to working with individuals, communities and populations with complex needs.
title: Advanced Occupational Therapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is the first in the research dissertation component. This course requires you to complete a dissertation under the supervision of an academic staff member. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, analysis of data and completion of a research project and thesis for examination. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. Students are encouraged to publish their findings with their supervisor/s.
title: Dissertation Part 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Pedagogy in Practice C is a continuing program of studio lessons designed to consolidate the student's musical skill and technique, expose the student to repertoire suitable as the vehicle for teaching and provide opportunity for interaction with skilled teachers on the faculty. It addresses the practical skills of studio teaching or conducting while also catering for the needs and experience of the individual student. NOTE: This course consists of individual lessons and as such is not timetabled. Please contact your Head of Area to arrange a mutually convenient lesson time.
title: Pedagogy in Practice C
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Electromagnetic Waves and Propagation is a lecture and laboratory based course in which students are introduced to tools and design techniques for engineering applications in which electromagnetic waves generated by sources of alternating current play a dominant role. These applications typically involve the transmission of waves over metallic or dielectric transmission lines or through free space, with the purpose of transporting either information or electric power. Prerequisites for Undergraduate programs only.
title: Electromagnetic Waves and Propagation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course constitutes Part 2 and 20 cp of a 40CP individually supervised project in which a student may complete written and (where appropriate) practical work on an approved topic. The research project undertaken will be relevant to the music discipline and incorporate high levels of competence and academic excellence. Assessment will be by dissertation or a combination of creative/practical output and dissertation. This will be delivered by a supervisory team, which will be tailored to the needs of each student's project (this might include a combination of a practical study teacher and research supervisor or a research supervisor only).
title: Honours Research Project 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course covers industrial water and wastewater treatment. Topics include water quality requirements, wastewater characteristics, and water and wastewater treatment systems in industries, as well as principles and applications of industrial water and wastewater treatment processes and technologies, and integrated and AI-assisted water and wastewater management strategies and case studies.
title: Industrial Water and Wastewater Treatment
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Foundations of Research Inquiry introduces students to the application of research approaches in health and community services. It provides students with knowledge and skills for conducting and appraising research.
title: Foundations of Research Inquiry
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: 6000NRS_P4 is the fourth of five 10 Credit Point courses that make up the research component of the Bachelor of Nursing and Bachelor of Midwifery Honours programs. The Dissertation courses (6000NRS_P1-P5) require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, data analysis and carrying out the research project. At the completion of the five Dissertation courses students will submit for examination a thesis (with an upper limit of 25,000 words) describing the research project and will deliver a seminar describing their findings.
title: Dissertation 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This postgraduate course is designed to assist students to gain knowledge and understanding in relation to quality and safety in the healthcare environment. Students will identify, appraise and critique strategies to prevent adverse events and improve critical care quality and safety, and apply relevant safety and quality knowledge and research evidence into their specialty clinical practice.
title: Quality and Safety in Healthcare
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course provides students with an understanding of the cultural and national factors that affect people management issues in organisations that operate across national borders. It also examines the efficacy of different employment policies and practices within the world economy. The course explains the reasons for the development of different forms of employment practices and the extent to which these differences are sustainable.
title: International and Comparative Human Resource Management and Employment Relations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course teaches skills for the systematic study of human languages, focusing on understanding words and grammar in English and other languages around the world. This involves learning about word structures (morphology) and about structures of phrases and sentences (syntax).
title: Words, Sentences and Grammar in the World's Languages
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course consolidates the language skills acquired in first year Chinese (1084LHS Modern Standard Chinese 1A and 1085LHS Modern Standard Chinese 1B) and second year Chinese (2010LHS Modern Standard Chinese 2A and 2011LHS Modern Standard Chinese 2B). It focuses on the development of communicative ability in listening, speaking, reading and writing through the study of texts on Chinese social customs and patterns of behaviour. Assessment is based on oral tests, weekly exercises and written tests. NOTE: Any student who is a native/proficient speaker of Mandarin Chinese or has completed their secondary education in a Mandarin or Cantonese speaking country is NOT ELIGIBLE to enroll in this course.
title: Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin) 3A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course asks the 'so what' question of research in Marine Biology; How does it translate into better decisions for sustainable use of marine resources? To do this, it brings together analyses of the need for management of marine biological resources; historical (including traditional) and contemporary approaches to managing and conserving marine environments; modern approaches to quantitative marine protected areas design, including software tools; evaluation of management effectiveness, including stock assessments, recruitment dynamics models, effects of marine protected areas. Prerequisites: 2804ENV Coastal Environments or 2302ENV Marine Animal Diversity or 2303ENV Zoology
title: Marine Conservation and Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course provides professional development opportunities in the areas of art collection management, registration, conservation, education, public engagement and curatorship. As a real workplace internship, participants engage in the day to day activities undertaken by staff at the Griffith University Art Museum. Students will gain an understanding of 'best practice' within the museum sector. Past participants have used the skills acquired during the Internship Program to establish careers in the arts industry as curators, registrars, gallerists, arts educators, preparators, writers and specialist framers. Restriction: Due to high demand, this course involves a competitive application process.
title: Griffith University Art Museum Internship
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course examines issues in personal risk management and its application in financial planning. This includes technical content in general, life, health and personal credit insurances and the operation of the insurance industry. Client attitudes and behaviours (including the assessment of these) are also examined within the context of personal financial advice.
title: Personal Risk Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This is the first of two final-year courses in the Painting Major. The course assists students in developing a significant body of work for submission to the Graduation Exhibition, emphasising experimental and preparatory aspects of studio practice. This course should be undertaken during the same trimester and year as 3378QCA 'Studio Thinking' and in the same year as the final Major 4 course leading into the Graduate exhibition. Prerequisite: Must be undertaking 1651 Bachelor of Visual Arts OR must be undertaking 1652 Bachelor of Visual Arts/Bachelor of Business AND must have completed 2016QCA Painting Studio 1 OR must have completed 2384QCA Painting Studio 1 AND must have completed 2385QCA Painting Studio 2 AND must have completed 2439QCA Memory and Trauma in Visual Culture OR must have completed 3426QCA Art of Portraiture: History and Theory OR must have completed 2440QCA Abstraction OR must have completed 3403QCA Australian Art OR must have completed 2431QCA Art, Gender, Sexuality and the Body OR must have completed 2916QCA The Art of Resistance
title: Painting Studio 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course examines up-to-date theory and practice related to the management of human resources and employment relations in the 21st-century. Issues and challenges related to institutional conditions that affect employment relationship factors are canvassed. The global, knowledge intensive context, characterised by the blurring of employment boundaries and evolving organisational forms, will provide a backdrop for the content analysis.
title: Principles of Human Resource Management and Employment Relations
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This is the capstone course of the dual degree and offers students the opportunity to summarise evaluate and integrate learning from a range of learning experiences in criminology and information technologies courses and to engage with a task which addresses a contemporary issue/problem facing a particular criminology and information technology.
title: ICT and the Justice System
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Comprehensive coverage of the repertoire of soft skills required by IT professions in today's employment market. It is based on the principle of "Essential Soft Skills for IT Professionals". Communication Skills: Clear, effective communication across various mediums and audiences. From writing compelling emails and reports to delivering persuasive presentations, you'll learn to convey complex technical concepts with clarity and confidence. Teamwork: The essential ingredients of high-performing teams. How to work team dynamics with skill. Explore modern collaboration tools and agile methodologies that drive innovation in today's tech companies. Problem-Solving & Critical Thinking: Sharpen your analytical skills and learn creative problem-solving techniques that will help you tackle challenging IT issues. Time Management & Organization: Develop strategies to handle multiple projects, meet deadlines, and maintain peak productivity in the fast-paced tech world. Project Management Fundamentals: Learn about the project lifecycle and essential skills for planning, executing, and delivering successful IT projects. Professional Ethics: Explore the ethical dimensions of IT, including data privacy, intellectual property, and corporate social responsibility, ensuring you're prepared to make sound decisions in complex situations. Customer Service & Client Relations: Learn to build strong relationships with clients and users, translating technical jargon into user-friendly language and delivering excellent service. Cultural Awareness & Inclusivity: Prepare for the global nature of IT by developing cross-cultural competencies and strategies for fostering inclusive work environments. Leadership: Discover your leadership potential and learn how to inspire and guide teams towards achieving ambitious tech goals. Personal Development: Cultivate self-awareness, emotional intelligence, and a growth mindset that will fuel your continuous improvement throughout your IT career.
title: Professional ICT Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Paramedics are required to develop knowledge about trauma management and environmental conditions across the lifespan. In this course students develop knowledge, critical thinking, decision making and technical skills required to undertake an assessment and how to manage the patient in an out-of- hospital setting.
title: Trauma and Environmental Conditions in Paramedic Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides students with clinical placement experience during their third year within the Bachelor of Paramedicine program, enabling them to apply and consolidate theoretical knowledge and clinical skills in real-world settings. Students undertake supervised placements as a third officer within operational ambulance services, rotating through rosters alongside qualified paramedic crews. Placement is six (6) weeks in duration and exposes students to the realities of paramedic practice, including shift work across day, afternoon, night, and weekend shifts. While immersed in the prehospital setting, students complete associated assessment tasks designed to scaffold learning, enhance clinical reasoning, and encourage professional development through authentic operational experience.
title: Work Integrated Learning 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Paramedics are employed in a wide range of clinical settings and regularly encounter non-emergency patients. In this course students will develop the attitude, knowledge and skills required to objectively evaluate and examine, non-emergency patients. Students will establish the factors that contribute to clinical and nonclinical problems impacting the patient. Students will also learn to prioritise and formulate collaborative care plans for ongoing care.
title: Introduction to Community Paramedicine
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course will cover advanced topics relating to Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS). Students will undertake flight training and theory related to more advanced operations, both in day, night and long distance operations. Flight operations will also be carried out in a number of the rapidly advancing application areas, such as cinematography, photogrammetry, agriculture and industrial inspections. The technical requirements for such operations as well as the underlying theory will be explored. Students will undertake field missions to gather data for practical assignments.
title: Advanced RPAS Applications
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Advanced Public Writing offers a broad understanding of the techniques, modes and impacts of public writing and within contemporary communications industries, and related ethical and conceptual issues. The course assists participants in developing skills as powerful and engaging writers, fluent in persuasive writing techniques, practiced in speech and advocacy writing, informed by an understanding of the theory and practice of public communication, propaganda and citizenship. This course contributes to a professional qualification for those who may wish to work in fields where advanced skills in professional communication are needed, or who may wish to undertake higher degree studies in public relations, writing and journalism. The course will provide a lively and supportive framework through which students have the opportunity to gain deeper knowledge and understanding of the field.
title: Advanced Public Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides a basic grounding in main concepts of biodiversity and ecology with an urban focus. Students will gain an understanding of the different types of terrestrial plants and animals, how they have evolved and are classified, and how they interact with the biotic and abiotic environments in cities. The focus will be on a practical understanding of Australian ecosystems and their interactions in an urban setting, and the benefits that urban biota and ecosystems provides to people living in cities. Assessment is by assignments, laboratory work and final examination.
title: Urban Ecology and Biodiversity
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: In modern market economies, the government-business relationship is a close and interdependent one. This course examines this relationship both nationally and globally. It compares different political systems, explores the impacts of globalisation, and considers a range of contemporary issues.
title: Government-Business Relations in Global Context
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Jewellery and Small Objects: Repetition introduces students to the materials, processes and conceptual context of contemporary jewellery and three-dimensional objects. Students will be taught a range of studio skills, including embossing, etching, repousse and chasing to enable them to communicate their individual conceptual, formal and aesthetic concerns in relation to the set project. This course is designed to provide a comprehensive range of experiences. Prerequisites: 1320QCA Jewellery and Small Objects Foundations
title: Jewellery and Small Objects: Repetition
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Sculpture 2 introduces students to the value of materiality within the broad field of Contemporary Sculpture. Through learning activities and self-directed studio projects, students will gain insight to the diversity of materials that are being employed within contemporary spatial and sculptural discourse. Students will develop skills transforming and manipulating materials prior to developing a major spatial outcome. The course requires students to engage with themes relevant to their personal, social and/or cultural interests and develop outcomes that employ conceptually appropriate processes and material interventions.
title: Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course provides students with a critical understanding of development within the Australian sport system. An underlying theme is the tension between developing participation rates and performance standards. From a systems perspective students will develop an understanding of the policies, programs, processes and structures that influence the development of sport.
title: Sport Development Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The planning, implementing and evaluating of major sport events is characterised by dynamic management environments that bring together a wide array of stakeholders. Large multi-sport events present both logistical and organisational challenges for host cities, as well as opportunities to plan for and create a range of short- and long-term benefits and event legacies. This course will introduce students to the complexity of managing major sport events. Students will study a number of planning, operations and event legacy management issues across the life span of major sport events, from the bid phase to event evaluations. This course will offer students practical as well as theoretical insights into the dynamic and at times challenging nature of sport event management.
title: Sport Event and Facility Planning
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course focuses on sustainable tourism operations following the triple-bottom-line principle. It explores the dynamic relationships of tourism and environmental conservation, addressing the critical need for responsible and sustainable approaches in the tourism industry. Students will gain a profound understanding of the social, economic, and environmental impacts of tourism, while also delving into key measurement methods and practices aimed at fostering sustainable tourism development.
title: Sustainable Tourism Practices and Impacts
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The Business Events market (meetings, incentives, conference and exhibitions) is a major sector of the event industry and the tourism and hospitality industries more broadly. This course provides students with an understanding of the many facets of this sector. Students will learn how to access and use relevant information resources, plan and manage meetings, and understand the role of the MICE sector in the context of the broader industry.
title: Business Event Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course describes and evaluates key aspects of rules relating to lawyers' professional conduct and also investigates contemporary issues affecting legal practice.
title: Canadian Legal Professional Responsibility
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Genetics and Evolutionary Biology is an introductory course that will provide foundational concepts in molecular genetics and evolutionary biology. Students will gain an understanding of the process of inheritance and mutation, population genetics, and evolutionary theory at the molecular, organismal and population level. Students will also learn commonly used genetic analysis methods and techniques employed by scientists. Course content will be delivered through a combination of lectures, workshops, and online material.
title: Genetics and Evolutionary Biology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Communication and Interpersonal Skills is an applied skills course intended to facilitate, guide and stimulate your interest and commitment to communicating effectively. The rationale for offering this course is that all human service and allied health professionals, no matter what setting they may be working in (i.e., with individuals, groups, and/or organisations), will require skills for interacting with others. Incompatible: 1008PSY Interpersonal Skills This course was formerly 7022HSV. Incompatible: 7022HSV is incompatible with 7322AHS.
title: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: For millennia humans have waged war and come to understand themselves and others through the experience of war. This subject explores the different ways that we can understand what war means how it has changed across time, what are the rights and wrongs of war, who are its victims, and how it has shaped the modern world. Understanding this history enables us to think more clearly about how war has shaped the modern world, and how the changing nature of war remains central to humanity's hopes for the future.
title: A History of War
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This 50 Credit Point course provides the individually supervised context in which a student may complete written and (where appropriate) practical work for a dissertation/project at one-year Honours level in the humanities, languages and social sciences. Assessment is by Dissertation (100% weighting, between 15,000 - 18,000 words) or by Creative or Professional product (60% weighting) with a minor dissertation/exegesis (40% weighting, between 5,500 and 7,500 words).
title: Dissertation/Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course will provide knowledge and skills for pre-service teachers to approach the teaching of technologies positively and with an accurate and thorough understanding of learning experiences that critically respond to community-based priorities, focus on creativity, problem-solving, and project-based learning, and satisfy The Australian Curriculum: Technologies from Foundation to Year 6. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on Learning@Griffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of professional experience placements.
title: Digital and Design Technologies for Primary Teachers
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The course introduces students to written and geometric communications used in building design and construction. It includes: Introduction to personal, project and practice communication. Detailing domestic building elements and components including foundations, footings, floors, walls, roofs and finishing trades. Preparation and use of the lifetime specification. Using engineering and surveying documentation.
title: Construction Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course continues the work begun in Performance Project 1, 2, 3 and 4 and the Acting courses. The acquisition and development of Acting, Voice and Speech, Singing, Movement and Dance techniques are interdependent elements in a process that culminates in a Performance Project, a learning opportunity consisting of a series of fully produced existing works presented to an audience of tutors, fellow-students and paying public or on screen. This course develops the student's potential as performer as fully as possible, through rehearsal, research and public performances. There is potential for a student to take up a professional work integrated learning internship in place of one of the performance projects.
title: Performance and Engagement 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course examines contemporary views of children and childhood, the theories that inform these views along with the political, economic, social and cultural influences that shape them both locally and internationally. The foundations of early chlldhood education and care, along with contemporary views of children's rights, educators' ethics and professional practice are also investigated.
title: History and Philosophy of Early Childhood
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Foundations of Law introduces key legal concepts and ways of understanding the law that are fundamental to the entire law program. Throughout the trimester, you will develop your knowledge of the key principles and institutions that collectively constitute Australia's legal system. We examine the basis on which these principles and institutions were adopted in Australia, and the implications for recognition of the rights and legal systems of First Nations People. We introduce legal ethics and examine the roles played by lawyers in Australian society. We provide you with frameworks for effectively accessing state and national laws and conducting other forms of legal research. Building on that knowledge, we develop and apply key legal skills, including reading, analysing and summarising the essential features of cases and legislation, and interpreting statutes, helping you to respond effectively to legal problems.
title: Foundations of Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course considers core aspects of the private law governing compensation for injuries and economic loss. The course focuses on common law remedies arising out of the law of negligence and non-intentional tort, as affected and modified by recent statutory tort reforms. Students are also introduced to other sources of injury compensation. These include the related torts of Breach of Statutory Duty, and statutory schemes such as Products Liability and Workers' Compensation. The course is taught and assessed in a critical vein, with students asked to consider the goals and efficacy of the common law and statutory compensation schemes, and the central role of policy in shaping legal responses to social problems. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Torts 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course introduces students to the law of associations and partnerships, before turning to focus on the nature and legal structure of the corporation in Australia. The doctrinal areas of corporate law covered include: pre-incorporation issues, incorporation, authority and agency, directors' duties, members rights, corporate finance and external administration. Students are encouraged to examine these through theoretical frameworks. Students must be enrolled in a Law program. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Corporations and Associations
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course examines the processes involved in the resolution of civil disputes in the context of our court systems. Following a consideration of the differences between, and the interrelationship of, substantive and procedural law and the theoretical foundations of our procedural system, students will closely examine the various steps involved in a civil matter. The emphasis of the course will be on the operation of the Uniform Civil Procedure Rules 1999 (Qld). Consideration will also be given to Federal procedure. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Civil Procedure
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: In today's highly competitive world it is no longer the sole responsibility of the marketing division to promote programs and services related to the sport and event management organisations. All employees within these industry sectors must be aware of the fundamental roles of marketing and the importance of being customer oriented. This course introduces students to external marketing environments and provides them with an awareness of the unique marketing challenges faced by event and sport organisations as they seek to provide programs and services that are responsive to consumer needs.
title: Sport and Event Consumer Experiences
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course draws together many of the significant concepts which are studied in other courses in the Master of International Tourism and Hotel Management degree program. In particular, it explores notions of competitive advantage as it is applied specifically to the industry contexts of tourism, hospitality and event management. It provides students with important skills in formulating and defending policies, strategies and processes to achieve continuous competitive advantage. The course also examines risk management concepts and strategies which are relevant in these industry contexts.
title: Competitiveness, Strategy and Risk Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Global Law introduces students to the legal systems, traditions and procedures that have importance to Australia but which exist and operate beyond our national jurisdiction and boundaries. In this course you will learn about the basic features of the civil law system and tradition, which in different forms operate in countries like Germany, Brazil, France and Japan. Of particular relevance to Australia's foreign relations is the Chinese legal system and tradition, which has developed out of the Socialist and Confucianist cultural tradition. Knowing some basic things about these other markedly different legal systems will support your learning throughout the law degree and will enable you to become more innovative and entrepreneurial as global lawyers. This will also help you to understand the origins and modes of practice of both private and public international law, which are legal systems that aim to support how people, private entities and States cooperate at the international level. This course will also introduce you to private international law and the way in which people and corporations rely on it to communicate, trade and generally engage with each other globally while ensuring that their transactions are legally secure. Most importantly, this course will introduce you to the basic features of public international law, which is the legal system for ensuring that states like Australia can continue to cooperate and co-exist peacefully with other countries in the world. This course is designed to give you an introductory experience of the range of legal systems and traditions that as global lawyers you need to be aware of and be able to draw on and use as legal advisers or consultants. It also aims to enrich your engagement with other courses in the law degree, so that you can broaden your understanding of the legal and intellectual influences that bear upon Australia's legal system and the people as globally engaged lawyers. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Global Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course is designed to provide an overview of musical theatre styles and practices from the early 20th century to the present day. The course discusses compositional features, structures and dramatic conventions to allow students to identify and evaluate functions of musical theatre. There are no pre-requisites for this course. Students from backgrounds other than music are welcome to undertake the course.
title: Introduction to Musical Theatre
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Each of these courses will examine an area or areas of Applied Mathematics at an advanced level. The areas selected will depend on the expertise and availability of staff and will be relevant for the student's area of applied mathematics. The specialised mathematics studied will allow students to hone their technical, analytical, problem solving and communication skills. Students undertaking multiple Topics in Applied Mathematics courses will undertake a different topic for each separate course.
title: Topics in Applied Mathematics 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Each of these courses will examine an area or areas of Applied Mathematics at an advanced level. The areas selected will depend on the expertise and availability of staff and will be relevant for the student's area of applied mathematics. The specialised mathematics studied will allow students to hone their technical, analytical, problem solving and communication skills. Students undertaking multiple Topics in Applied Mathematics courses will undertake a different topic for each separate course. Assumed knowledge: Students enrolled in this course are expected to have completed an undergraduate science degree with a mathematics major
title: Topics in Applied Mathematics 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course examines the molecular and cellular basis of the immune system which protects animals and humans from infection by pathogens such as viruses, other microbes and parasites. The importance of the immune system in health and disease is emphasized and topics covered include vaccination, auto-immune diseases and cancer immunology. Topics covered include the nature of immunity; self versus non-self recognition; antigen recognition and the clonal selection theory of the immune response; innate immunity; the humoral immune response; antibodies - structure, diversity, function and mechanisms of action; the cell mediated immune response; recognition of antigen by T cells; antigen presentation; the major histocompatibility proteins; the role of cytokines and the regulation of immune responses; the immune system in health and disease - response to infection, development of vaccines; the development of allergies and auto-immune diseases; transplantation immunology. At the end of the course, the concepts learned about the functioning on the immune system are reexamined in the context of clinical case studies where you will identify the value of the concept in a more practical context.
title: Immunology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course covers emerging areas in microbiology. It integrates the latest knowledge in fundamental microbial processes with genomics to understand the functioning of microbial cells and their interactions with the surrounding environment. It looks at the critical roles played by microbes in the environment, health, evolution and energy production.
title: Applied Microbiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course takes a cross disciplined approach to the role of human error in the aviation industry and why it is the major cause of accidents and incidents. It considers the physical, physiological and psychological interactions; human performance models, accident causation, decision making, and preventive strategies.
title: Human Factors for Aviation Managers
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course has been designed to provide graduates with a strong theoretical foundation in Integrated Water Management (IWM) and Catchment Science (CS) good practice, strengthened by a practical applied research skill set developed through the final project experience. In the course students design and undertake self-directed project work to consolidate and apply concepts, principles and methodologies learned in the coursework components of the Masters Programs. Students are encouraged to base their final project on a focal issue that is of personal or professional development interest, which they will explore under the guidance of dedicated professional and academic supervisory expertise. Professional placements with NGOs, research institutes, water industry service providers, private consultants, or natural resources management organisations are encouraged. Where possible, students will be linked with IWC partners and associates.
title: Final Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Global health is concerned with all strategies for health improvement. Global health issues commonly require health system action at a national or local level. Understanding the challenges faced by diverse health professionals, the impact of the local context and the role of health prevention is pivotal to effective policy creation. By identifying and describing key global health system actors, drivers and goals, and the key components of health systems and their interactions, you'll be equipped to analyse, critique and advocate for policy settings that improved public health outcomes. You'll also be prepared to work in collaboration with diverse disciplines and apply your systems thinking skills to identify and solve complex health problems.
title: Global Health Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Excellence in practice is predicated on a reflective and rigorous approach to creative practice as a method of inquiry and comment. This course introduces students to a number of exemplarily research practices through which they may contextualise their work. It looks at different modes of inquiry and encourages students to develop research practices that are appropriate to their particular area of study. This course provides an opportunity for students to explore the basic principles of research methods and consider how these may be applied to their research project. Students will identify their topic/research question and appropriate methods of inquiry through peer review, students will present their research topic, investigations and work-in-progress for scholarly interrogation.
title: Visual Arts Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Excellence in practice is predicated on a reflective and rigorous approach to creative practice as a method of inquiry and comment. This course introduces students to a number of exemplarily research practices through which they may contextualise their work. It looks at different modes of inquiry and encourages students to develop research practices that are appropriate to their particular area of study. This course provides an opportunity for students to explore the basic principles of research methods and consider how these may be applied to their research project. Students will identify their topic/research question and appropriate methods of inquiry through peer review, students will present their research topic, investigations and work-in-progress for scholarly interrogation. Students are expected to have completed 80 credit points of the MVA program
title: Visual Arts Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course introduces students to the principles of law, contract administration and dispute resolution in the construction industry. The course content comprises a range of issues and claims arising in construction process. In particular, the students will develop an understanding of certain general conditions of contract; the relevance of legal concepts including unjust enrichment, frustration, waiver, estoppel, and specific performance; gain knowledge of alternative dispute resolution methods; and become familiar with the Building and Construction Industry Security of Payment Act.
title: Construction Contract Administration
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Throughout history, human civilization has developed near water bodies. Unfortunately, this essential resource is relatively under threat due to climate variability. Therefore, it is essential that this scarce resource is carefully managed to ensure sustainability of both the natural and built environments. The main purpose of this course is to investigate recent developments in the engineering principles and processes that are applied to the design of sustainable water engineering related projects. It introduces students to advanced engineering design practice utilising real world design exercises and international design codes. The course delivery mode is a combination of lectures, labs and project based workshops. Professionals from industry may be invited to present case studies, with particular emphasis on Australia. Prior assumed knowledge: other Undergraduate Water Engineering related courses.
title: Advanced Water Engineering Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is designed to engage students with food and nutrition content at this early stage of their degree. Specifically this course will explore student's personal food knowledge, attitudes and beliefs, and will investigate food's place in society.
title: Food and Society
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is suited to business people who wish to engage in strategic decision-making in the 21st century. Decision-makers need to understand both the nature of the macroeconomic environment in which they take decisions and the nature of the market in which their organisation operates. In short, this course brings forward the economic frameworks that you will need, given the challenges of this century. This course provides a practical approach, with a particular focus on the responsibility of business and the role of government in enabling sustainability and acting responsibly. This course is a compulsory core course for students enrolled in the MBA, and the Graduate Certificate in Business Administration. All students are expected to begin studies at the first designated session (face-to-face or online) for each course of their program. Students who cannot attend must gain written approval from the MBA Director to continue in that trimester.
title: Economics for a Sustainable Future
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course integrates core elements of financial planning, the regulatory framework and the Financial Planners and Advisers Code of Ethics 2019 into the design of client strategies and the delivery of quality advice. The focus of learning activities is on the application of financial planning skills and practices that underpin successful client-adviser relationships, including the use of technology.
title: Applied Financial Planning
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course integrates learning and acquisition of specialist knowledge in a series of clinically-based, research informed seminar/tutorials, assignments, case presentations and journal reviews and clinical practice involving the acquisition of advanced clinical skills and management of complex cases.
title: Advanced knowledge and clinical practice I
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This project-based learning course introduces students to the engineering design process and some of the aspects of being an industry professional. Students will work in teams to develop solutions for a real-world need while considering the increasingly complex interactions between engineering systems, project stakeholders and the environment.
title: Engineering Design Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This subject examines the relationship between mental disorder and criminal offending. The course aims to increase students' knowledge and understanding of models of criminal behaviour and mental disorders, and the potential interaction between the two. The course aims to develop in students a critical appreciation of the issues involved in defining both mental disorder and criminality, and an evidence-based understanding of the extent to which criminal behaviour is caused by mental disorder. The course also addresses specific mental disorders, in the context of their potential relationship with criminal offending. The course aims to develop students' knowledge and critical thinking skills applicable in a forensic mental health setting.
title: Mental Disorder and Crime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: All construction projects have the common feature of utilising engineering principles, people, machines and materials as well as requiring organisation and planning. This course covers the range of construction equipment and techniques in common use and the planning and direction of construction works. Attention is also given to rock and bulk excavations, health and safety at work sites, preliminary works, formwork design and an introduction to engineering economics. Assessment is by assignments and examinations.
title: Construction Methods and Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides students with a deep understanding of the core concepts and principles that underpin contemporary criminological theories. By exploring the problems, questions and ideas that have shaped modern criminological thought, students will gain knowledge of the contexts that influence the emergence and reception of modern criminological theories and the modes of social intervention that different criminological perspectives expressly or implicitly propose. Additionally, this course will equip students with the tools to evaluate the efficacy of criminological theories in explaining crime and responses to crime. Upon completing this course, students will be able to apply criminological theories to crime prevention and criminal justice programs. Theories covered will vary from year to year but are likely to include: social process and control theories, theories of crime and place, developmental theories, and theories of criminal justice.
title: Applied Criminological Theory
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course develops and integrates students' theoretical knowledge and practical skills in order to competently provide safe nursing care for individuals experiencing acute health conditions. Students undertake 160 hours of clinical practice to develop nursing competence congruent with a second-year undergraduate student level.
title: Acute Nursing Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course offers students the opportunity to develop knowledge, skills and approaches relevant to the care of individuals with mental health problems. Students undertake 80 hours of clinical practice to develop nursing competence in mental health clinical settings.
title: Mental Health Nursing Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The effective delivery of healthcare involves numerous decisions, both large and small, relating to service provision, policy development, resource distribution, workforce management, infrastructure planning, and more. Successfully managing and responding to these decisions is essential for any health services manager or leader. In this course, you will enhance your skills in critical and creative thinking, decision analysis, offering informed advice, and evaluating choices skills fundamental to leadership and strategic decision-making in health, aged and social care sectors. You will also learn to navigate complex and uncertain situations, addressing constraints that may affect your decision-making when implementing strategies in organisational activities. The course integrates theory with practice through activities based on the real-world experiences of health managers, giving you the knowledge and confidence to tackle real challenges in health service delivery, both domestically and internationally.
title: Strategic Decision Making in Health
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course is the final component of the Dissertation. This course requires you to complete a dissertation under the supervision of an academic staff member. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, analysis of data and completion of a research project and thesis for examination. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. Students are encouraged to publish their findings with their supervisor/s.
title: Dissertation Part 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is one of a series of courses undertaken to complete dissertation requirements for your program. Each dissertation course has specific milestones to complete, which are available on the program website on Learning@Griffith. Dissertation courses involve the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, and the execution of experimental protocols. Results from these experiments are evaluated and conclusions drawn with findings presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course covers the theory of Navigation under the Visual Flight Rules (VFR) in accordance with the CASA CPL Navigation syllabus. Note: Incompatible with 2508BPS/2508NCS Navigation
title: Navigation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In the public sector and beyond, management is more than just a job title. It's a philosophy that's shaped by each person's unique experiences, formal education, and professional development. These personal theories of management are incredibly powerful, and have a profound impact on how individuals lead their teams and organisations. To truly become great managers, we need to both critically reflect on and take steps to expand our personal theories of management. The Managing Public Sector Organisations subject guides students to do both. The Managing Public Sector Organisations subject gives students an opportunity to think critically and creatively about management. By challenging their assumptions, considering new perspectives, and exploring cutting-edge research, the subject helps students become better managers and leaders in their organisations.
title: Managing Public Sector Organisations
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course builds on the underpinning knowledge of atmospheric Science and applies this knowledge to a practical aviation environment in accordance with the CASA CPL Meteorology syllabus. Incompatible with: 2507BPS/2507NSC All Weather Operations
title: Aviation Meteorology
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course is organised around the three strands of the Australian Mathematics curriculum: Number and Algebra, Measurement and Geometry, and Statistics and Probability. Knowledge and understanding in these areas form the foundation on which mathematical specialties and professional applications of mathematics are built. The course develops preservice teachers' deep understandings of mathematics content, pedagogy, assessment and curriculum knowledge, and effective teaching of numeracy including the explicit teaching of mathematics and building of fluency, understanding, problem solving and reasoning to support their teaching of mathematics in the primary years of schooling.
title: Working mathematically in the later primary years
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course introduces the diverse socio-cultural influences on the developing child, their health, wellbeing and safety. It focuses on children's physical, social, emotional, cognitive, creative and spiritual development, drawing on neuroscience to inform our understandings. It considers the importance of developing authentic family and community relationships that support children's diverse learning and developmental pathways.
title: The Developing Child within Family and Community
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course enables students to extend critical thinking and problem-solving skills to manage complex client situations at an advanced level. Students apply knowledge and skills to prevent harm and promote recovery with a patient and family-centered focus. NB: Students must hold a current and unrestricted license as a registered nurse or for another clinical role (other roles to be approved by the Program Director).
title: Managing Complex Clients
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course explores common modulation techniques including amplitude and angle modulation for both analogue and digital information signals. Applications examined include radio, television and telecommunications. The course looks at both system level and circuit level. Many examples are examined for circuits for mixers, modulators, demodulators, oscillators, frequency synthesisers, RF amplifiers and radio and television receivers and transmitters. Design of amplification stages utilising classes A, B, C and D are examined. Methods and importance of shielding at high frequencies is also covered. A series of laboratories explore construction and measurement of communication circuits. Incompatible: 2304ENG Communication Systems and Circuits.
title: Communication Systems and Circuits
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course explores disease processes and their evolution, assessment and treatment, and develops problem-solving skills to enable the development of competent practitioners who can solve real life problems in nursing care. The primary focus is on disorders of the cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, gastrointestinal, reproductive, endocrine and haematological systems.
title: Human Pathophysiology and Pharmacology 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Master of Medical Research thesis, including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussions and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words. Enrolment depends on availability of research topic and supervisors.6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor. Prerequisite: 6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course helps build students' understanding of the knowledge, skills and activities required to lead change in organisations in a range of sectors. A complexity approach to leadership is presented to show how sustainable development goals are central to businesses for the future.
title: Leadership for Sustainable Business
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Tourism and hospitality operations tend to be complex due to the unique characteristics of the industries and the dynamic and interactive environment in which operations are conducted. This course aims to broaden students understanding of relevant and applicable theories and models of operations management, and equips students to apply the understanding to specific situations. Indeed, operational problems can be effectively unscrambled by focusing on appropriate performance objectives and strategies, designing marketable products, services and processes, managing capacity and improvements, as well as implementing sustainable practices.
title: Tourism and Hospitality Operations Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course is part of a series of courses in which students plan and execute a substantial piece of research, which is reported in the form of a thesis or creative/professional product with dissertation. The thesis or dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 30,000 words. This research is designed to build on previously studied research courses that have developed student's understandings of current social, cultural and educational theories, research methodologies and design. The main objective of the thesis or dissertation is to provide students with the opportunity to engage in a major piece of research in the Humanities within a relevant discipline. By doing this they will come to understand better the nature and dynamics of the discipline and to demonstrate the capability to work at a high level in the application of theory and research skills to a substantial piece of research and to further doctoral study.
title: Dissertation 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.
title: Research Thesis
