title: Project Management and Software Engineering
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The purpose of this course is to prepare students for employment by introducing them to the role of effective interpersonal communication, business communication, management, business principles, ethics, and professional association within contemporary contexts. This course explores the major professional issues arising from the widespread use of digital media and highlights dilemmas that may be faced by creative media practitioners. By providing the fundamentals of professionalism, this course aims to make students 'job ready'. Pre-requisite: Students must be in their final year in the Bachelor of Design program. Students from other cogent areas must apply in writing to the course convenor.
title: Business Practices in Creative Industries
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: "Despite the public's obsession with crime, victimisation and criminal justice, despite the morbid fear that crime and victimisation arouses, despite the endless volumes written to account for offending, victimisation and criminal justice processing, gender, the most powerful social factor of all has been virtually ignored by criminologists." (Leonard, 1982). This course explores the persistent and profound differences women and men's experiences of crime. The course considers how gender intersects with other social categories such as race, class, socioeconomic status, and ethnicity to shape crime and responses to it.
title: Gender, Crime and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The course considers the most widely accepted approaches, in Forensic Mental Health (FMH), to risk assessment. Course content primarily focuses upon the prediction of an individual's likelihood of harming others or being harmed by others. Risk and protective factors are examined beyond that of a present based individual level to include an understanding of developmental and environmental factors. The utility and applicability of different risk assessment tools is also considered as a component of an effective functional analysis and more broadly risk management in Forensic Mental Health.
title: Risk Assessment and Management in Forensic Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course will introduce students to the profession of occupational therapy with a focus on the occupational therapy process. Students will be introduced to the occupational therapy process and will learn the theory and practice of the initial stages. Students will also consider the history of the profession and how that influences current practice. Prerequisite: 1311AHS Occupation & Occupational Therapy I and Fit for Professional Practice Mandatory Requirements
title: Occupation and Occupational Therapy II
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: In this course you will learn about the role and impact of digital technologies in the health industry. Learners will explore future and current applications for digital health and informatics. The key concepts, principles and issues associated with the use of technology in health care will equip health leaders and managers with foundational knowledge in digital health. The role of government with respect to health information and communications technology, policy, strategy, and funding is also examined.
title: Digital Health
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course provides opportunities for Pre-Service teachers to understand how children develop an understanding of science concepts and processes, practices used to develop scientific knowledge, and its application in their lives. The course is designed to prepare pre-service teachers with key pedagogical and conceptual knowledge related to the teaching of science for learners from Prep to Year 6. It examines supporting young children's scientific investigations, and provides a comprehensive overview of how an inquiry-based approach can be used to scaffold children's understanding of the Australian Curriculum: Science. Pre-service teachers will extend their scientific knowledge and explore appropriate ways to plan, program, and evaluate science learning in the primary years.
title: An Inquiry Approach to Science: Primary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: 6000MED_P1-P5 are five, 10 Credit Point Dissertation courses that make up the research component of the School of Medicine and Dentistry Honours programs. The Dissertation courses (6000MED_P1-P5) require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, data analysis and carrying out the research project. At the completion of the five Dissertation courses students will submit for examination a thesis (with an upper limit of 25,000 words) describing the research project and will deliver a seminar describing their findings.
title: Dissertation 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: 6000MED_P1-P5 are five, 10 Credit Point Dissertation courses that make up the research component of the School of Medicine and Dentistry Honours programs. The Dissertation courses (6000MED_P1-P5) require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, data analysis and carrying out the research project. At the completion of the five Dissertation courses students will submit for examination a thesis (with an upper limit of 25,000 words) describing the research project and will deliver a seminar describing their findings.
title: Dissertation 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Criminal advocacy is an art. In this course, students will work in a small group to prepare and practice basic advocacy technique in a variety of situations.  You will practice: -basic speaking technique such as pace, pitch, posture, gesture, use of notes etc. -legal advocacy to judges; advocacy on factual matters to judges and juries; -examination-in-chief; cross-examination; and written advocacy.  Students will perform a speaking role each week. There are no recordings of the classes and weekly attendance at class is essential. Students should take from the course an understanding of the fundamentals of advocacy to form a foundation upon which to build in their careers. NOTE: Information on application process is available at the LLB and JD Organisation sites on Learning@Griffith. Limited places are available in this course.
title: Criminal Advocacy
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course provides students with an overview of the Australian legal system as it pertains to commerce and management. It also provides detailed knowledge in the area of contract law and a knowledge of the law as it applies to torts, particularly professional negligence and to partnership.
title: Introduction to Business Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is an introduction to the theory and practice of public health and health promotion. It examines the various determinants that impact health in relation to specific issues, populations, and settings, and explores strategies to address some of the most pressing health issues facing contemporary society. The course links theory with practice through a case study approach, introducing students to the practice of promoting health at an issue, population, and settings level. Introduction to Public Health is a first-year core course in the Bachelor of Public Health and an open elective for other undergraduate students. It contributes to these programmes by broadening students' understanding of health and the determinants of health.
title: Introduction to Public Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course prepares the students for a professional life in which they will inevitably discuss issues relating to the economics of built facilities. The course discusses three key aspects: the economics of building designs, project feasibility appraisals, and the economics of the construction and property industry. The skills and expertise acquired in this course are vitally important for working in the construction and property industry.
title: Construction Economics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides participants with an understanding of environmental, technical, social, and economic dimensions to be considered when supporting the development of domestic water supply, sanitation and hygiene services that are climate resilient, sustainable, and appropriate for underserved communities. These communities exist in resource-constrained low-middle income countries, as well as in developed economies including Australia. The course also situates WASH within broader issues including catchment management and whole-water cycles, gender and social inclusion, and Sustainable Development Goals. Please note: this course is particularly relevant to students enrolled in one of the following programs: GCert/GDip or M Integrated Water Mgt, M Business Administration; M Global Health, M Public Health. Students studying other PG degrees, or interested in taking this as a standalone course, can seek permission from the Program convenor.
title: WASH: Water, Sanitation and Hygiene, and Climate in low resource settings
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course aims to equip students with a working knowledge of both global and domestic air traffic management environments, as the transition to the new Communications, Navigation and Surveillance/Air Traffic Management systems described in ICAO's Global Air Navigation Plan for CNS/ATM Systems is implemented. The online offering of this course is only available to 'professional entry' students. Those students should email the Program Officer, Aviation, at aviation@griffith.edu.au for permission to enrol. Incompatible with course AVN3004 Airways Operation and Design.
title: Airways Operation and Design
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is designed to provide students with an insight into the practices involved in the Sport Development industry. Students will explore aspects of Sport Development including: pre-exercise screening; motor learning and development; nutrition; interpersonal relationships and considerations; and reflective practice in Sport Development.
title: Sport Development II
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides an introduction to the legal skills and ethical frameworks utilised in migration law practice. This course provides students with a sound knowledge of the regulatory role of OMARA and the Code of Conduct. It particularly contextualises utilisation of the Code of Conduct in relation to dealing with new clients and outlines the requirements for initial client contact. This course trains students in legal research processes necessary for the practice of migration law including access to information under legislation. Finally, this course introduces legal writing pertinent to the practice of migration law. In a full-time study load, this course is undertaken simultaneously with 7131LAW Foundations of Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma is one of the prescribed knowledge requirements for eligibility to be registered as a migration agent with the Migration Agents' Registration Authority. As the second course in the program, and the companion course to 7131LAW, in 7231LAW students focus on developing practitioner skills to apply their growing legislative and ethical knowledge of migration law. The companion course to 7231LAW is 7131LAW which simultaneously builds on the theoretical background necessary for the practical requirements for 7231LAW. Like the other companion courses in the Graduate Diploma Program, in 7231LAW students will learn and apply practitioner skills they need to effectively integrate the legislative content they acquire in 7131LAW. 7231LAW is offered in online mode only.
title: Introduction to Migration Legal Skills and Ethics
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course prepares students to be successful senior secondary school mathematics teachers. In particular it focuses on developing an understanding of the content and practices in the senior phase mathematics curricula, and the pedagogical practices to assist school students to learn it. This will include specific teaching approaches appropriate for senior phase mathematics, planning strategies that enable effective teacher preparation, and associated relevant assessment practices. In addition, this course will encourage students to reflect on their own mathematical experiences, and to consider how they can build positive learner attitudes and dispositions towards mathematics.
title: Mathematics Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Health Care Systems is designed to give the student a deeper understanding of key concepts in how health systems are funded, operated and evaluated. The course will introduce the student to concepts such as social determinants of health; how health care decisions are evaluated; health reform; disadvantaged groups and health; and assessing quality of health services. The course will explore the Australian health care system in detail and compare it to other health care systems in developed and developing countries.
title: Healthcare Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course is designed to ensure students are equipped with the necessary content knowledge, pedagogical skills and technological competence to teach all aspects of the Australian Curriculum, Mathematics Foundation to Year 6, and have appropriate subject matter expertise in the effective teaching of numeracy including the explicit teaching of mathematics and building of fluency, understanding, problem solving and reasoning. This is achieved through an explicit focus on curriculum, pedagogy and assessment to ensure pre-service teachers have specialised knowledge for professional practice and further learning.
title: Working mathematically for Prep to Year 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Equity investments constitute a significant segment of the investment market. The aim of the course is to gain solid understanding of how equity markets function, to master a range of equity valuation techniques. The peculiarities of valuation of private companies, equity markets, as well as issues for valuation in emerging markets are also examined. This course assists with preparation for CFA Level 2 examinations.
title: Equity Investments
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course equips students to perform molecular genetics experiments and understand the major components of genetics from molecular mechanisms to phenotypic expression. Students learn laboratory skills necessary for research in molecular genetics by doing experiments using their own DNA. Students will learn genetic phenomena from many examples, including clinically relevant syndromes resulting from partial or complete gene inactivation by both mutation and epigenetic mechanisms. Genetics at the individual level is expanded to include examples from population genetics, selection and evolution. The intersection of genetics and response to drugs will be explored in examples of pharmaco-genetics. Students will develop useful skills in the presentation of data in a seminar setting. Students will also be equipped to consider and debate the ethical dimensions of the rapid progress in genetic technology, both gene testing and gene engineering and how it may affect human culture.
title: Molecular Genetics
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Mental health policy and services have evolved considerably over the past 50 years. To be effective in their role, established and emerging practitioners must understand the many developments in mental health classification and diagnosis that have occurred in that time. This course will equip you with the knowledge and skills to examine a variety of cultural, social and philosophical perspectives about mental health and mental illness. You'll explore the impact of theoretical and policy frameworks on the experience of people with mental illness, and build critical decision-making skills as you reflect on ethical, medical, psychological and social implications of mental health policy and practice. Throughout this course, you'll gain a foundation in mental health policy, service delivery and theoretical frameworks that are underpinned by empathy. You'll be capable of formulating proactive responses to contemporary challenges in mental health practice, including the influence of labeling and diagnosing mental health problems and the impact such labels can have on people diagnosed with psychiatric illnesses.
title: Understanding Mental Health : Theories and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course requires candidates to prepare and write a detailed plan of their proposed major research project. It extends the work undertaken in the course 8240EDN Initial Research Planning and is taken in conjunction with 8265EDN Research Design and Proposal 1. A significant part of this course will involve reviewing the appropriate literature in relation to both contemporary theory and recent research findings. The research plan should include four sections - a rationale for the project, a survey of the relevant literature, the proposed methodology, and a time schedule for the project. Candidates should also prepare an application for ethical clearance for the project. The proposal developed in this course will be a basis for the candidate's confirmation seminar presentation.
title: Research Design and Proposal II
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides an overview of the various areas within the criminal justice system in which front-line workers come across people with mental disorders. It examines the way in which the criminal justice system (including police, court, and correctional staff) deals with individuals with mental disorders. In particular, the course focuses on the identification and treatment of individuals with mental disorders; relevant processes and decision-making in different elements of the criminal justice system; examining contemporary approaches to definitions, diagnostic tools, notions of criminal responsibility and fitness to stand trial; and the use of psychological knowledge, theory, and research to guide reflective practice and build personal, professional resilience.
title: Mental Health, Psychology and the Criminal Justice System
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course constitutes Part 1 and 20 cp of a 40CP individually supervised project in which a student may complete written and (where appropriate) practical work on an approved topic. The research project undertaken will be relevant to the music discipline and incorporate high levels of competence and academic excellence. Assessment will be by dissertation or a combination of creative/practical output and dissertation. This will be delivered by a supervisory team, which will be tailored to the needs of each student's project (this might include a combination of a practical study teacher and research supervisor or a research supervisor only).
title: Honours Research Project 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Cleaner production and circular economy can bring overlapping benefits to business performance by simultaneously increasing profitability, efficiency, competitiveness and environmental performance. Harnessing the economics of sustainable consumption and production that can drive these benefits requires expertise in understanding, communicating and then applying complex ideas and strategies. In this course, you will explore how to use various tools, including cleaner production planning and assessment, to achieve sustainability goals. With an advanced and integrated understanding of cleaner, sustainable practices you will be capable of promoting the uptake of resource efficient, cleaner production and circular economy practices. You'll be a responsible and adaptable professional with a global perspective, able to find solutions to complex situations using advanced problem-solving skills that will help us move towards being a sustainable society with clean air and clean water and prosperous businesses. This course is aligned strongly to Sustainable Development Goal 12 on responsible consumption and production.
title: Cleaner Production and Circular Economy
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Community Internship provides students with the opportunity to integrate academic learning with real-world experience through a minimum of 50 hours of volunteering in a non-profit organisation. The course focuses on community engagement, social justice, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as a framework for understanding and responding to local and global challenges. Students can select from university-supported placements or propose their own (BYO), and are required to complete pre-placement processes, including interviews and relevant compliance requirements such as a Blue Card where applicable. Alongside the placement, students participate in structured academic learning through workshops and guided activities that support reflection, critical thinking, and understanding of their role as emerging professionals and active citizens. The course emphasises the development of key employability skills, including communication, teamwork, problem-solving, and adaptability. Available as a 10 credit point elective for students who have completed at least 80 credit points within a Griffith University degree program, this course supports career readiness while encouraging students to build a deeper awareness of community issues and their capacity to contribute to meaningful social impact.
title: Community Internship and Partnerships for SDGs
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Get the skills required to play a critical role in disaster preparedness and management, with a specific focus on pandemics and responding effectively to reduce risk and optimise public health. In our inherently risky world, the skills required to systematically assess the threats we face and create strategies to manage and prevent crises are vital. In this course you will focus on the assessment and evaluation of disaster and pandemic risks in the local context. You will critically discuss the principles of disaster management and pandemic responses, describe the purposes of management practices and assess the techniques used to evaluate them. You will be prepared to play an essential role in the front line of pandemic preparedness.
title: Emerging Issues in Disaster and Pandemic Planning, Response and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Building on 1080LHS, 1081LHS continues a broadly communicative approach to language learning. Through regular contact hours each week, you progress towards the A2 Waystage level of proficiency of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, thereby preparing you for intermediate Spanish language study (2080LHS or 2082LHS). Prerequisites: 1080LHS or admission via a placement test administered by our Spanish teaching staff. Corequisites: nil. Incompatible: nil.
title: Spanish 1B
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This unit introduces students to a representative selection of Shakespeare's best-known drama, inviting them to undertake both detailed critical analysis, and some historical research on the contexts from which they emerged. The unit will also consider the impact of film and television on the global reach and contemporary relevance of Shakespeare's work. Students will be required to read five of Shakespeare's plays.
title: Global Shakespeare
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides professional development opportunities in the areas of art collection management, registration, conservation, education, public engagement and curatorship. As a real workplace internship, participants engage in the day to day activities undertaken by staff at the Griffith University Art Museum. Students will gain an understanding of 'best practice' within the museum sector. Past participants have used the skills acquired during the Internship Program to establish careers in the arts industry as curators, registrars, gallerists, arts educators, preparators, writers and specialist framers. Restriction: Due to high demand, this course involves a competitive application process.
title: Griffith University Art Museum Internship
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course provides students with a sound understanding of the principles and practices relating to airport planning, operation and management. The course introduces students to the airport sector of the aviation industry, how airports are planned and developed, current and contemporary strategies for obtaining revenue and identifying and controlling costs
title: Airport Planning, Operations and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this course, PSTs will identify and apply pedagogies and practices that are most effective in creating a positive learning environment to support student learning, motivation and engaged behaviour. Drawing on a range of research informed learning theories, PST will plan learning sequences responsive to their students' stage of learning and become increasingly challenging (incorporating spacing and retrieval practice) as students work towards mastery. Considering school-wide frameworks and classroom-level proactive approaches to behaviour management and learning, PSTs will apply evidence-based teaching practices and develop skills in how to practically implement tier 1 in the classroom. This course also includes a professional experience placement in schools. Preservice teachers must reach an 80% threshold for tutorial attendance and active participation in the lead up to placement for all Professional Experience courses. Preservice teachers who cannot attend the full tutorial and thus cannot actively participate during the tutorial will not be able to proceed with the placement and complete the course.
title: Pedagogies for Engaged Learning: Primary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines the human experience of disaster and conflict, and how organisations seek to support people displaced from their homes and communities. It examines human rights, civilian experiences of war, and human responses to environmental disaster, to consider practical ways that humanitarian organisations and governments respond to crisis. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Geographies of Disaster and Displacement
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is the second of two complementary courses concerned with preparing English teachers for the secondary school. The central purpose of this course is to develop further knowledge of theory and practice issues related to the teaching of Senior English, English Communication and English Extension (Literature). A working knowledge of the current Queensland English syllabus documents is integral to the work undertaken in this course. Students will prepare curriculum materials that will be useful in schools.
title: English Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is concerned with the design and implementation of school subjects that reflect the nature of teaching history in secondary schools. In particular, it investigates the planning, teaching and assessment issues for history subjects in the senior secondary curriculum. 4060EDN provides opportunities for students to develop pedagogical skills as teachers of history and undertake critical and reflective analyses of topical debates about the discipline. This course also develops students' knowledge of relevant syllabus documents, school based work programs and the various curriculum materials which impact upon the teaching of history. Typical assessment tasks include research based assignments along with the analysis and construction of curriculum materials.
title: History Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Governments in many ways create the world within which business operates, for example through regulation, taxes, policies, specialized programs. This course explores the business-government nexus, giving students comprehensive and practical insights on ways in which governments and businesses influence, respond to and engage with one another. It includes exercises and engagement designed to give students a deeper understanding of the roles that various political and business actors play in real-life business and government settings.
title: The Government Business Nexus: Intervening, Lobbying and Responding
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Students undertake a practical public health internship in their field. Students undertake duties, for example program planning, evaluation and policy development, under the supervision of an assigned industry supervisor/mentor and a university supervisor.
title: Public Health Practicum
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Paramedics are required to develop knowledge about mental health conditions across the lifespan. In this course students develop knowledge, critical thinking, decision making and technical skills required to undertake an assessment and how to manage the patient in an out-of- hospital setting.
title: Mental Health Conditions in Paramedic Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course will cover conceptual and applied topics relating to current concerns in the theory and practice of ecological conservation. Topics will include the conservation of populations, species and communities and ecosystems as well as matters concerning decision-making, policy, planning and implementation. Students will be provided with the opportunity to delve deeply into a major conservation problem as well as to experience a broad range of perspectives regarding key emerging issues. Workshop sessions will also introduce major technical and communication approaches to addressing these issues. Prerequisite: 2051ENV Ecology OR 2603ENV Ecology
title: Emerging Topics in Conservation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will introduce students to contemporary areas of design practice, tools and prototyping. It will offer advanced knowledge into Additive Manufacturing and Digital Fabrication tools and processes and apply this to a practical or strategic project outcome.
title: Prototyping
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The emergence of print cultures in the East and the West were reliant on three skill sets, papermaking, printmaking and bookbinding. Combined in print cultures these mediums continue to transform the relationship between images and text. Examples of this relationship can be traced back to China in the 800's AD, however it was Johannes Gutenberg's "invention" of movable type that dynamically activated the democratic print, and has indelibly shaped our world and the way we think. The print (or the replicated image) plays an increasingly pivotal role in contemporary art practices and cross-disciplinary thought. This course provides creative artists drawn to the rich mark making of prints an opportunity to learn new skill sets across hand paper making, relief and letterpress printing and bookbinding as well as providing a framework to build those skills into an art practice. Prerequisites: 1319QCA Print Foundations
title: Print: Culture
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course offers students the opportunity to explore the indexical nature of prints, fundamental to all printed matter, and to integrate intaglio/etching and/or silkscreen printing into their creative practice. The course is delivered through three streams of integrated instruction; grounding print culture's historical presence within visual art practice and culture at large, positioning student's engagement with print within a contemporary context, and providing the skill set(s) needed to achieve a resolution to the course project. The course project provides ample choice for diverse outcomes and having completed the course students can expect to have a clearer understanding of the significance of print to contemporary art practice, the potential that prints hold for their own practices, and skill sets to expand their investigations into print. Prerequisites: 1319QCA Print Foundations
title: Print: Making
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The buying and selling of residential and commercial property and development land is governed by a range of legal acts and government regulations. In addition, there are also a range of financial transactions that are part of the buying and selling process. This course will provide specialist knowledge of the legislation, regulations and transactions for these industries.
title: Real Estate and Property Development Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The Sport Marketing course has a focus on exploring consumer behaviour in sport - both spectator and participant - to equip students with the knowledge and skills required to work in sport organisations. In applying theoretical sport consumer behaviour frameworks to real-world examples, students are taught the implications of that behaviour for management practice in marketing sport, and marketing through sport. The course has an emphasis on authentic assessments and building student capacity via completing tasks leveraging research, presentation, and reflective skills.
title: Sport Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Sport Management Principles is designed to provide students with an understanding of the Australian sport industry, the unique features of sport, and how sport organisations operate in the public, non-profit and professional sectors. The course provides an understanding of the roles and responsibilities of sport managers, relationships between professional administrators and volunteers, and current issues facing the industry.
title: Sport Management Principles
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Understanding the complex, systems-based nature of the global tourism sector, and what that means for the social and natural communities that host this major sector, is vital for its on-going sustainability. This course will help you appreciate the range of contemporary issues facing the sector, and how they relate to social, environmental and economic sustainability. You'll learn how to identify trends that can support or hinder sustainability at destinations, and what tourism operators and relevant government agencies can actively do to design for tourism experiences and operations that support the communities around them (human and non-human) while remaining financially viable. The course will also explore the importance of ethics in sustainability, and the emerging paradigm of regenerative tourism and how this differs from sustainability tourism. As a tourism operator leading a small and medium enterprise, you'll be equipped to identify your niche market and consistently deliver authentic, life-changing experiences while running an agile business that's safe and highly connected to your community.
title: Sustainable and Regenerative Tourism
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The adaptability and ultimate survival of any organisation depends on the ability of its management to make informed decisions based on valid research. To this end, it is essential that modern managers have a sound appreciation of the nature and role of research and the application of research methods, as well as an ability to critically evaluate research outputs. This course, which is the capstone course for the Event Major, will give students the opportunity to revisit the content of the other event major courses by undertaking a research project to evaluate some aspect of the impact of events. The course will also allow students to draw on the skills acquired in 2230THS Interpreting Tourism Management Information (or equivalent) to provide them with experience in applying practical research skills as are commonly used in the events industry.
title: Event Evaluation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: There are few management positions in contemporary business environments, including event management, that do not involve some responsibility for managing discrete projects. Project management entails techniques to achieve specific and often unique objectives, with limited resources and a given time-frame. This course will introduce students to these techniques, which can then be applied in an array of business environments, such as in the organisation of events and real estate projects.
title: Managing Projects in Service Industries
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: In today's world, terrorism is one of the inescapable worldwide forces that defines, shapes and reshapes our age. This course will put terrorism and political violence into broad historical context, exploring the experiences of terrorism through the ages and how societies responded to the threats of political violence. From antiquity, through the Middle Ages to the global terrorism of today, this course will unravel the meaning of terrorism and how it was experienced throughout history.
title: A History of Terrorism and Political Violence
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of the role of public participation in policymaking. Students will engage with theories and case studies to understand how organised political movements influence decision-making, as well as the complexities of stakeholder engagement on policy and project implementation. Through interactive seminars, group discussions, and case-study focused assessments, students will develop the skills to critically analyse public participation in vastly different social, political and economic contexts.
title: Policymaking, Public Participation and Human Rights
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Spanning a range of pop and rock eras, including 'beat', psychedelic, glam, punk, reggae, rap, dance and metal, a key aim of the course is to look at how popular music influences notions of identity, politics, taste and belonging in contemporary culture. Additionally, given the increasingly historical nature of many aspects of pop and rock, perspectives from work on ageing, memory and cultural heritage will also be drawn on in the course. A range of artifacts will be considered including songs / albums, film and documentary, fashion and style as well as the increasing importance of social media as a means of accessing and connecting with popular music.
title: Popular Music, Culture and Identity
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores the theory and practice of transport and land use planning. The course covers such topics as the theoretical underpinnings of transport planning, contemporary transport policy, the impacts of transport systems on the environment, transport modelling, planning for walking, cycling and public transport, disruptive technology and transport and transport and land use integration.
title: Transport Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This third course in a series of three Performance Projects. You will be required to draw upon skills acquired in the previous year and 2079QCM Acting III. This course continues to build and deepen students' performance capacity through ensemble-focussed workshops. Students study and rehearse an abridged version of a Shakespeare play and tour to local schools.
title: Performance Project III
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course continues the work begun in Acting I, II, III and IV. The acquisition and development of Acting, Voice and Speech, Movement and Dance techniques. Students are introduced to the audition platform. This course connects with Performance Project IV. This course continues the development of the student's potential as a performer as fully as possible, through class tuition in Acting, Voice and Speech, Movement and Dance and through master classes, workshops, seminars and public performances.
title: Acting V
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Business Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course is the third of eight courses that comprise the Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice. The Graduate Diploma of Australian Migration Law and Practice is one of the prescribed academic qualifications for registration as a migration agent in Australia. In this course students will acquire a detailed knowledge of the legislative requirements and related policy for various visa classes and subclasses. In order to apply this legislative knowledge and accurately advise their clients according to individual circumstances, they will also learn how to gather relevant information from their client. Using this knowledge they will learn how to provide accurate advice to clients on visa options and complex visa-related issues, and also prepare and lodge a successful visa application. While legislative knowledge is the focus of 7132LAW, students will learn to apply this knowledge in the context of problem-based client scenarios which provide a practical background to the more theoretical focus of this course. The companion course to 7132LAW is 7232LAW (Practitioner Skills) which simultaneously build on the practical background to immerse students in a virtual office environment. Like the other companion courses in the Graduate Diploma Program, in 7232LAW students will learn and apply practitioner skills they need to effectively integrate the legislative content they acquire in 7132LAW. In addition to the horizontal alignment between 7132LAW & 7232LAW, both courses are also aligned with the previous courses in the Program (7131LAW & 7231LAW) and the subsequent courses 7133LAW & 7233LAW and 7134LAW & 7234LAW. The deliberate alignment allows students to progress logically through the growing complexity of both legal and practitioner skills as they follow the life of a client file from initial client contact to file closure.
title: Australia's Visa System
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Conducted through seminars and lectures, this course considers contemporary visual arts in the context of a global cultural landscape. The course is designed to engage students directly with the histories, tensions and circumstances of global visual arts practice. An investigation of the nuances, sensitivities, protocols and complexities of specific practitioners, movements and events will enable the student to apply a sophisticated and critical knowledge to global contexts with an understanding of a diversity of perspectives. Students will also develop communication skills that reflect contextual awareness and responsiveness to rich and complex intercultural dynamics. It is recommended to complete 7040QCA prior to undertaking this course.
title: Global Visual Culture
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Crime 1 addresses the nature and purposes of criminal law and a review of some of the major substantive law provisions in Queensland. The course will examine the concept of criminal responsibility; and the elements of offences such as murder, rape, assault, and drug offences. It will also cover accessorial liability and attempts. Further, the course will examine defences and excuses, including self-defence, provocation, and mistake of fact. By the end of the course students should be able to understand some of the policy implications of criminal law, as well as be able to apply the law to a factual scenario to identify whether offences covered in this course have been established and if so, whether any defences or excuses may apply. Building on the knowledge acquired in Crime 1, students' studies of criminal law are completed in Crime 2 2020LAW.
title: Crime 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Administrative Law is the body of common law, statute law and procedural rules through which government institutions and bureaucratic actions are supervised and regulated. This course examines the major principles of administrative law and the various institutions through which the law is developed and applied in practice. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Administrative Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: The term social problem is usually taken to refer to social conditions that affect a significant number of people within society in a negative way. Social problems are seen as being disruptive or damaging to society, as social injustices that we should be striving to solve. For example, crime and safety, violence, alcohol, and drug use are often constructed as significant social problems for many people in Australia while others are more concerned with inequality and discrimination. In fact, social problems like crime are often the consequence of factors extending beyond the individual's control, such as inequality, discrimination, prejudice, oppression, and concomitant social injustice. Sociology provides us with the critical thinking skills to understand the connection between social problems and the social structure including how social problems come to be 'problems' in the first place. In this course, you will develop frameworks for critical sociological thought by exploring multiple intersectional axes of power, oppression, inequality, and social injustice including classism, racism and colonialism, sexism, heterosexism and transmisia, ableism, adultism, and ageism. You will learn how oppression and power within these spheres (and the intersections between them) are vital to understanding the social problems of most concern to the discipline of criminology and reflect on how (in)justice might be mitigated. The knowledge gained will equip you with the tools to do criminology in a socially just way.
title: Social Problems - (In)Equality and (In)Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course introduces students to the disciplines of criminology and criminal justice. It begins with an examination of the nature of crime and how it is defined and measured in contemporary society. The course then provides an overview of the impact of criminological theories on our understanding of crime problems and the implications for criminal justice responses.
title: Introduction to Criminology and Criminal Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The World Health Organization (WHO) defines health as "a complete state of physical, mental and social well-being, and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity." In Australia, social work is the largest allied health group employed in the health sector. This course prepares social work students for practice in community and institutional health settings by exploring social work in a variety of health and mental health contexts; developing an understanding of health and mental health systems; diagnoses and treatments; the structural and individual factors that impact on health; and social work and consumer perspectives on health and mental health. The course combines theory and practice skills including multidisciplinary team work to develop student knowledge, skills and confidence working with other disciplines.
title: Social Work in Health and Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to develop an understanding of the curriculum knowledge and pedagogical skills required to assess children's developing understanding of the world in which they live. It introduces the Humanities and Social Sciences (HASS) Learning Area in the Australian Curriculum.
title: Humanities and Social Sciences
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will demonstrate technological pedagogical content knowledge needed for teaching in the 21st Century. Their ePortfolio will be designed to demonstrate their achievement of the National Professional Standards for graduates, using evidence drawn from their entire program.
title: Preparing to Teach in the Digital Classroom
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Ecotox and Impact Assessment provides a sound understanding of the science of ecotoxicology and how to assess the impact of contaminants on our environment, with a focus on the effect of chemical contaminants on the aquatic environment. Previous civilisations have ignored their environmental impacts at their own peril, we now know that we need to understand how to minimise our impact on our environment if we want to ensure our future quality of life and healthy ecosystems. The purpose of the course is to develop skills in ecotoxicology and apply them to assess environmental impact of human activities.
title: Ecotox and Impact Assessment
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course aims to foster the development of ethical, reflective, collaborative, and creative practitioners. Students work as part of a collaborative studio team under the guidance of expert teaching staff, connecting with external industry partners on numerous public-facing design projects. Students will develop a working knowledge of professional design practices while creating a range of industry-connected design outcomes. IMPORTANT: refer to www.liveworm.com.au for more information and how to gain permission to enrol.
title: Liveworm 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course provides the opportunity for learning and experience on the requirements, responsibilities, and impact of effective leadership to those who will manage healthcare organisations in the health, aged and social care sectors. The course aims to improve leadership capability through understanding the theory and practice of leadership. The course is designed to focus on leadership traits, behaviours, skills, competencies, and opportunities for people with different roles and responsibilities, and working in different teams, units, and organisations, now and in the future. The course enables development of motivation and influencing capabilities that are relevant in creating positive outcomes and leading innovation in health care. Students can examine and enhance their own individual leadership styles and approaches in nurturing culture and capability towards high performing teams, and organisations.
title: Leadership in Management for Health Services
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course introduces students to a number of exemplarily research practices through which they may contextualise their work. It looks at different modes of inquiry and encourages students to develop research practices that are appropriate to their particular area of study. This course provides an opportunity for students to explore the basic principles of research methods and consider how these may be applied to their research project. Students will identify their topic/research question and appropriate methods of inquiry through peer review, students will present their research topic, investigations and work-in-progress for scholarly interrogation. Students undertaking this course will have completed a bachelor's degree.
title: Design Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course explains the laws introduced by the Australian government in response to terrorism, from those enacted in response to the 9/11 attacks to those passed more recently in response to Islamic State and right-wing extremism. It focuses on theories of prevention, the impact of these laws on Australia's criminal justice system, and questions of accountability and human rights. The course also considers policy strategies for countering radicalisation and violent extremism.
title: Counter-Terrorism Law
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: The course examines the role of financial statement information evaluates the financial performance of public companies, and attempts to predict a firm's future performance by parties external to the firm. Topic coverage includes traditional ratio analysis; analysis of inventory, long-lived assets, non-current (long-term) liabilities, evaluating financial reporting quality, and 'red flags' and accounting warning signs. Evaluation of reporting quality in the attempt to predict financial distress is an important part of the course.
title: Financial Statements Analysis
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course extends your understanding of speech pathology practice for individuals and communities across the lifespan. Through inquiry-based learning the course will focus on the assessment and treatment of communication and swallowing changes experienced by people across the lifespan. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health continues to provide a framework for understanding of clinical situations, with an evidence-based practice approach underpinning your knowledge about speech pathology management.
title: Communication and Swallowing Disorders 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Modern software frameworks reduce development time and provide a solid foundation for building high quality software applications. This course covers full-stack development of real-world software applications using the selected frameworks. Prerequisite: Programming Principles (2807ICT for BIT students or 1811ICT for BCS students). Previously known as 3813ICT Software Frameworks and is therefore incompatible with 3813ICT Full Stack Development.
title: Full Stack Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The real-world performance of any software system depends on the algorithms used and the efficiency of their implementation. The ability to select algorithms appropriate to solving particular problems, based on understanding the range of algorithms that address well-defined problems, analyzing their complexity and performance, and their suitability in particular contexts and implementing them is critical for building effective software. A number of general algorithmic strategies are presented including brute force, heuristics, greedy, recursive backtracking and divide and conquer. Common algorithms pertaining to searching, sorting, binary trees, graphs, and string / expression parsing are also discussed. Also, both in-memory and file data structures and their interrelationship with specific algorithms are reviewed.
title: Computing Algorithms
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: In this course students will develop the knowledge to be able to administer medications safely. Routine screening tests used in pregnancy are outlined and students will be introduced to interpretation of results and situations where consultation and referral to a medical practitioner is required. The legal, ethical and professional frameworks underpinning drug administration and clinical screening tests are discussed in relation to midwifery practice.
title: Medication, Pharmacology and Screening for Midwives
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course examines the major disciplines of forensic chemistry and forensic toxicology, with examples to demonstrate their specific contributions to forensic analysis. This course builds on the principles of forensic chemical analysis introduced in second year. This course provides students with an opportunity to undertake a moot court experience as practice for the capstone Forensic Evidence and the Expert Witness course. Prior Assumed: 1008NSC Principles of Forensic Investigation.
title: Forensic Chemistry and Toxicology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of leadership: theory, application and skill development in the context of the aviation industry and competitive environment. The course will cover leadership theory and concepts whilst improving students ability to apply the theory through critical thinking, and to develop leadership skills.
title: Leadership in Aviation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: An aviation professional needs to possess strong leadership and communications skills. This course develops the leadership theme by looking at the various leadership styles and students will research a successful aviation leader. The communications theme focuses on writing styles that lead to success in the industry.
title: Aviation Leadership and Communication
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The aim of this course is to provide knowledge of the various facets of airport planning and management. Particularly, this unit focus on master plan development, governance models, airport regulatory environments, community relations, airport marketing, economics, financing and operations. Guest lecturers with industry background will deliver this unit in a seminar style to ensure that students actively engage with the material at an appropriate depth of airport planning and management.
title: Airport Operations and Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course has been designed to provide graduates with a strong theoretical foundation in Integrated Water Management (IWM) and Catchment Science (CS) good practice, strengthened by a practical applied research skill set developed through the final project experience. In the course students design and undertake self-directed project work to consolidate and apply concepts, principles and methodologies learned in the coursework components of the Masters Programs. Students are encouraged to base their final project on a focal issue that is of personal or professional development interest, which they will explore under the guidance of dedicated professional and academic supervisory expertise. Professional placements with NGOs, research institutes, water industry service providers, private consultants, or natural resources management organisations are encouraged. Where possible, students will be linked with IWC partners and associates.
title: Final Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course introduces students to the disciplines of criminology and criminal justice. It begins with an examination of the nature of crime and how it is defined and measured in contemporary society. The course then provides an overview of the impact of criminological theories on our understanding of crime problems and the implications for criminal justice responses.
title: Introduction to Criminology and Criminal Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course comprises a period of program-approved industry-based work placement relevant to your discipline. The unit requires you to complete a minimum of 130 hours of workplace experience during the trimester, plus approximately 20 hours to complete the assessments. The course provides students with valuable professional experience and the opportunity to apply and further develop the knowledge, skills, and principles of their discipline within a real-world professional environment. Students may be involved in a range of activities such as project work, design and planning processes, client and stakeholder engagement, teamwork, communication, and professional practice. The type of experience will vary according to the student's discipline, skills, academic level, and host organisation. The student will engage in work and projects agreed upon and negotiated between the host organisation and the course convenor. For students enrolled in the following programs, Bachelor of Architectural Design 1492; Bachelor of Architectural Design / Construction Management (Honours) 1688; Bachelor of Architectural Design / Business 1689, an emphasis on understanding the application of the 2021 NSCA performance criteria in a practice environment is a key learning opportunity. How to Enrol (Departmental Consent Required): · Students must independently secure a suitable placement relevant to their discipline before requesting enrolment in this course. · Email: wil-gs@griffith.edu.au (WIL Office) · The WIL Office will send you some paperwork to complete. · Once you have completed the paperwork, the WIL Office will contact the course convenor to confirm departmental consent. · After consent is confirmed, you will be able to enrol in the class. Prerequisites: Restricted course: students must refer to the Course Profile for information on the enrolment process. The listed prerequisites are discipline/program specific. Prerequisites for students enrolled in 1492 (Arch.) are 2901ENV Architecture Studio 2 or 2903ENG Studio 3 - Contextual Response. Prerequisites for students enrolled in 1658 (Plan.) are 2067ENV Development Processes Studio or 3097ENV Strategic Planning Studio. Prerequisites for students enrolled in 1407 (Ind. Des.) are 1508ENG Digital Design and Modelling or 2608ENG 3D Digital Modelling for Manufacture.
title: Work Integrated Learning Special Topic 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course aims to develop specific skills and knowledge gained in Pharmacotherapeutics. This course introduces students to advanced clinical pharmacy practice, with a focus on a collaborative approach to healthcare in the form of inter-professional learning. This course will involve collaborative activities with medical, nursing and allied health students at a similar stage in their degree. Students will need a good understanding of therapeutics, professional pharmacy practice and reflective learning.
title: Advanced Clinical Skills
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: The 21st century has been described as being the Asian century in part because of its rising economic power. This course will explore the region providing a holistic perspective of the key trends in the Asia-Pacific region and the governance, economic and societal frameworks; thus enabling students to effectively formulate strategies for their organisations to operate across the dynamic and diverse region. This course is only available to students enrolled in Program 3328 Graduate Certificate in Business Administration OR 5670 Master of Business Administration. This course is normally offered every 8 teaching periods. This course is incompatible with 7709GBS Management.
title: Doing Business across Asia-Pacific
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: In this course, we explore contemporary theories of design, learning, and teaching for thriving digitally mediated educational futures. For this, learning situations and environments are understood as intimately intertwined with the positioning of educators and learners through design and approaches of design. From this, workshops provide opportunities to design for digital learning in formal and informal educational settings.
title: Designing Digital Learning and Teaching
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course covers the principles of electric motors and generators. Both DC and AC motors and generators are explored along with the application of single and multi-phase machines. State of the art drive, control and protection circuitry will also be considered along with solid state methods of providing AC supply. Practical work will enhance the understanding of these topics. Pre-requisite: must have completed 1018ENG Engineering Science Incompatible: must not have completed 6509ENG Electrotechnics
title: Electromechanics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Numerical methods facilitate the solution of many design problems commonly encountered in electrical and electronic engineering (EEE) with the aid of powerful digital computers, which have multiple core CPUs, large memory capacity, and fast networking. Machine learning, in particular, has greatly benefitted from advances in numerical techniques and computing capacity, and is increasingly becoming an important skill set for modern practising electrical and electronic engineers. This course aims to equip students with working knowledge of machine learning concepts as well as some common numerical methods encountered in EEE (systems of linear and non-linear equations, root finding, optimisation, regression, etc.). Students will also learn how to use the UNIX/Linux operating system to efficiently implement numerical methods on modern multicore computers that utilise code concurrency and parallelism, as well as text utilities for extracting data from files. The course will be delivered via lectures and computer-based labs, where coding will be undertaken using the C and Python languages within the Linux operating system.
title: Numerical Engineering Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course develops awareness and knowledge of contemporary issues in global public health nutrition. The course will examine the current situation of both over-nutrition and under-nutrition including potential causes and risk factors. Having established the global state of nutrition, current public health nutrition practice priorities, strategies and initiatives at the local, national and international levels will be critiqued.
title: International Nutrition
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides an introduction to midwifery and the Bachelor of Midwifery Curriculum for commencing students enrolled in the Bachelor of Midwifery program.
title: Knowing Midwifery
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Public Health Practice is a capstone experience grounded in evidence-based practice. This course enables students to autonomously apply advanced discipline knowledge to a substantive public health initiative. This is a project-based course. Students are expected to deliver a significant output rather than simply accrue fieldwork hours. While the format of the deliverable will align with the project's specific audience, ranging from an industry-style evaluation report to a journal manuscript, all work must demonstrate analytical rigour and be underpinned by relevant theories, models and evidence appropriate for the type of project. Students work under the guidance of academic and/or industry supervisors. Mandatory Preparation (PREP): This course involves a mandatory preparation and project set-up stage (PREP), which must be completed during the trimester prior to your enrolment in 7707MED. Detailed information on PREP is available: https://lms.griffith.edu.au/courses/8124 Enrolment Timing: For most full-time MPH students: This course is typically completed in the third trimester of study. MPH Pathway 1 (1-Year Program): Students may complete this course in the second trimester. MPH Pathway 3 (T3 Entry, Full-Time): Students may need to complete 7708MED concurrently with this course. For most full-time MGPH students: This course is completed in the fourth trimester of study. Prerequisites: To enrol in this course, you must have successfully completed 60 credit points (60CP), consisting of: -Required Foundation Courses: 7311MED, 7708MED, 7881MED, AND -Any three additional courses from the foundation (7233MED) or core list (7231MED, 7415MED, 7312MED, 7001HSV, 7232MED, 7111MED). Note: MPH Pathway 2 students are not required to complete the foundation courses: 7311MED, 7708MED, 7881MED as pre-requisites.
title: Public Health Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In Flight Procedures III students are introduced to the added systems complexity of a multi engine aircraft as well as the fundamental performance aspects relating to normal two engine and abnormal one engine in-operative operations. The twin engine platform is also used to extend their exposure to glass panel technology by introducing the full range of departure, arrival and approach procedures available under the Instrument Flight Rules [IFR]. Prerequisites: 1505NSC Flight Procedures I and 2533NSC Flight Procedures II OR 2531NSC Flight Procedures I/II
title: Flight Procedures III
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is one of four 10 Credit Point courses that make up the research component of a School of Allied Health, Sport & Social Work Graduate Diploma or Masters level research project. The combined 8002AHS courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, approval from relevant ethics committee/s, data collection, analysis and write-up of findings. At the completion of the four Dissertation courses students will submit a thesis for examination.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is the first in the research dissertation component. This course requires you to complete a dissertation under the supervision of an academic staff member. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, analysis of data and completion of a research project and thesis for examination. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. Students are encouraged to publish their findings with their supervisor/s.
title: Dissertation Part 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides some of the essential mathematical techniques to mathematicians and physical scientists, and applies them to scientific problems. The course covers basic material on multiple integrals of scalar functions as well as line and surface integrals of vector fields, the theorems of Gauss, Green and Stokes, Fourier series and integrals. It also introduces some of the common partial differential equations of applied mathematics and methods to solve them. It also covers some topics on ordinary differential equations. Please note: for students enrolled in Program 1567 1201SCG Linear Algebra is a co-requisite.
title: Calculus II
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This 40CP Dissertation is offered within the 5263 Master of Public Health (MPH) and the 5725 Master of Global Public Health (MGPH) programs. The 40CP dissertation is similar to an Honours dissertation in type and scope and gives students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest. The Dissertation involves the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, collection and analysis of data. The background literature, methodology. findings and conclusions are presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis. The thesis is expected to be between 15,000 and 20,000 words in length, depending on disciplinary demands and problem requirements. Please note that Course Convenor approval is needed to be able to enrol in the Dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The course explores Australian art history from its First Nations foundations and early Colonial art, through to the present day. It includes the study of art of the First Fleet, Colonial art, Aboriginal art of the 19th century, Australian Impressionism, landscape and figure painting, Modernism, art and war, myth, figuration, abstraction, and international developments such as conceptual and performance art. Revolutionary art of the late 20th century is also investigated, including Indigenous art, women's art, environmental art, and art engagements with the Asia Pacific, which continue to grow in fascinating ways into the new millennium.
title: Australian Art
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Community engagement is central to effective health promotion practice. This course introduces students to the theory and practice of community engagement. Students work on priority health promotion issues in the community and devise projects to address these. It provides students with theoretical understanding and practical skills required to manage a public health community engagement project. This is a core competency for public health and health promotion practitioners. This course is a core course of the MPH program. It is expected that participants have either completed or are concurrently completing other core MPH courses. As the course focuses on the practical application of theory, it may be challenging to complete this course in the first trimester of study without prior relevant work experience or knowledge in public health.
title: Community Engagement in Health Promotion
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides an in-depth look at the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of diseases related to the respiratory tract, ear, nose and throat (ENT) and gastrointestinal (GI) tract system. Building on the knowledge of infections and the immune system gained in second year, the course adopts an integrated approach to learning. It guides students through the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of diseases. This includes a thorough understanding of the pharmacotherapeutic basis of treatment and its relation to drug structure. Through lectures and problem-based clinical workshops, students will acquire theoretical knowledge, an evidence-based approach, and practical clinical skills. These will contribute to the optimal use of medicines, delivery of health information, and provision of health education about the therapeutic areas covered in the course.
title: Integrated Pharmacotherapeutics II
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course has a major design project which further develops the practical engineering design skills students have already gained through the Environmental Engineering Design 1 and 2 courses. Students are required to design the basic infrastructure for a proposed site development with significant environmental issues to be addressed. The development of a cost effective and appropriate design solution and development of design and documentation skills are emphasised. The design project is carried out in teams, giving students the opportunity to experience the issues involved in working in teams towards a realistic project outcome.
title: System Design Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The course introduces students to the fundamental principles of psychology as applied to the areas of exercise, sport and rehabilitation. Issues relevant to participants (across the lifespan and functional capacity), patients, coaches, practitioners, and promoters involved in the optimisation of individual and group performance are considered. From 2027, this course will only be taught in Trimester 2.
title: Exercise and Sport Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces students to the concepts, methodology and practice of public health planning and evaluation. Students develop knowledge and skills in the planning cycle from needs assessment through to program design, program implementation and program evaluation.
title: Needs Assessment, Program Planning and Evaluation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course invites you to move out of your comfort zone, try something new, and to challenge yourself professionally and personally, with support and guidance. Students report that international work integrated learning (WIL) makes them more employable, and employers back this up, reporting that international experience favourably influences their perception of students' abilities. Students say WIL helps them assess their career direction, complements their learning, increases their networks, increases their motivation to study and helps them prepare for future employment.
