description: Business and Company Law provides an introduction to the legal framework governing business activities in Australia and offers students a foundational understanding of Australian business law and company law. The course introduces the Australian legal system, with particular emphasis on the primary sources of law, the roles of courts and legislatures. It examines key areas of law relevant to business, including contract law, data protection and privacy law, Australian Consumer Law, the law of negligence and partnership law. The course also focuses on company law, corporate governance, accounts, auditing and financial reporting and corporate insolvency. Through practical examples and case studies, students will develop the ability to identify legal issues, apply relevant sections of legislation and case law and understand how the law affects business activities and commercial decision-making. The knowledge gained in this course will be invaluable throughout students' careers, particularly in fulfilling their business and professional responsibilities. Incompatible: 2105AFE Introduction to Business Law.
title: Business and Company Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course introduces students to the tools and techniques for character animation in 3D software, emphasizing traditional animation skills' adaptation to digital realms. Through practical exercises and theoretical insights, students explore keyframe animation principles, refining their ability to bring characters to life with depth and expression in a 3D environment.
title: 3D Keyframe Animation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course introduces students to fundamental animation techniques, incorporating a breadth of media and animation styles. In applying animation in various settings, students will adopt an attitude of exploration, working with physical materials on outcomes as diverse as visual music, motion paintings, pixilation and environmental animations. This course is suitable to novice animators keen to discover the expressive possibilities of accessible media and techniques.
title: Exploring Animation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The course provides a comprehensive understanding of essential techniques, tools, and best practices for handling and visualising data. Students will learn how to collect, clean, integrate, transform, and reduce data efficiently. The course emphasises principles of effective data visualisation, including selecting appropriate visualisation types, encoding data attributes, and applying design principles. Through hands-on experience, students will create visualisations for various data types such as numerical, categorical, time series, spatial, and textual data. Additionally, advanced techniques for large-scale data processing, statistical analysis, and machine learning are covered, equipping students with the skills needed to derive and present meaningful insights from complex datasets.
title: Data Wrangling and Visualisation
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Integrated Financial Accounting builds on and extends students' knowledge of core accounting principles covered in Principles of Accounting and Analytics. This course is concerned with recognition and measurement of specific financial statement elements. Issues covered include the conceptual framework, acquisition and revaluation of assets, accounting for liabilities, leases, shareholders' equity, revenues, financial statement presentation, and cash flow statements and analysis and interpretation of financial reports.
title: Integrated Financial Reporting
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course is only available to students enrolled in a Master of Science program offered through the School of Environment and Science. Students will undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of one or more supervisors within the School. The topic and nature of the Research Project will be determined through consultation and mutual agreement of the student and supervisor/s and approved by the Program Director. The project will involve original research and will be under the direct supervision of an academic staff member. Assessment will comprise a written report of the work, prepared in the form of a thesis submitted for examination and a seminar defending the work. The thesis is expected to be no longer than 60,000 words in length.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Immersive experience of language learning and discovering cultures in China! This course (10cp) is for students approved to participate in a global mobility experience funded by the New Colombo Plan. This exciting opportunity will provide students with the chance to experience overseas cultures, and to engage in partnerships with local stakeholders in their destinations. RESTRICTION: Permission is required to enrol into this course.
title: Chinese Language and Culture: Discovering China Tour
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Filmmaking Hierarchy and Departments course provides students with the practical framework to understand clearly the hierarchical structure of a film set and understand the responsibilities of each department and each crew member's role; develop effective communication strategies for navigating the chain of command; gain practical insights into departmental workflows and interdependencies, whilst building confidence to identifying the right person or team for any production or on-set requirement.
title: Filmmaking Hierarchy and Departments
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course orients students to the diverse and important roles music and music-making can play in our contemporary world. Across a range of local and global contexts, students will investigate how music intersects with today's most pressing social, cultural, political, and environmental concerns. Students will have opportunity to explore issues of particular interest or concern to them.
title: Music and Society
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Rapid changes in society, international relations, technology and communication have led to flexible ways of, and increasing numbers of people, working across global borders. This course provides an opportunity for students to critically analyse global dimensions of the core aspects of human resource management, such as linkages with business strategy, structure, policies and practices; staffing, recruitment, and selection; training and development; rewards management; and performance management. The course examines how human resources are managed and problems solved within and across differing global cultural, political, economic, legislative and technological contexts. The course aims to develop globally engaged and responsible future leaders of GHRM and cross-culturally competent globally mobile employees.
title: Global Human Resource Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course is aimed at final year undergraduate business students wishing to develop greater understanding of some of the complex strategic issues facing organisations today and in the future. In a marketplace where organisations are continually being disrupted through industry landscape change and technological innovation, strategic management can be the key to delivering a solid bottom line. As traditional sources of competitive advantage are being eroded, managing strategic change is becoming a crucial factor in the survival and performance of business organisations. As parts of this course, students will explore the following broad areas: the concepts and techniques of strategic position, strategic analysis and implementation at the business and corporate levels. These will include the external environment, competitive industry dynamics, resources and capabilities, stakeholders and governance, business and corporate strategic choices, international strategy, mergers and acquisitions, strategy evaluation, the strategy development process and the practice of strategy.
title: Managing Strategic Change
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course provides students with essential knowledge and skills for personal, academic, and career success, while fostering introspection on personal attributes and career aspirations. Students gain insight into the interconnectedness of knowledge and professional attributes, crafting personalized career plans for undergraduate studies aligned with their strengths and areas for improvement. Pre-requisite: 9100EPP University Preparation.
title: Career Pathways
academicOrgDescription: EmpowerED

description: This course will provide students with a critical understanding of international human rights law and practice. Topics to be covered include: human rights 'enforcement' mechanisms and institutions at the global and regional levels. We then move to look at the substance of human rights, including limitations to rights, economic social and cultural rights, as well as some specific human rights. We also examine human rights in the non-governmental sphere e.g business and human rights.
title: International Human Rights
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: In this course, students develop practical, technical, and theoretical skills for the production and presentation of screen-based moving image designs. This involves exploring image structures, composition, animation, sequencing, motion design, motion graphics, sound production, and video and audio editing using digital SLR cameras, smartphones, audio recorders, and file management systems. Students experiment with Adobe CC - Lightroom, After Effects, and Premiere Pro - to capture digital imagery, create animations, design motion graphics, and produce visual and aural effects. These fundamental skills are required by most creative disciplines in visual communication and are used by designers, visual artists, photographers, and animators to create both narrative and abstract representations.
title: Motion Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The real-world performance of any software system depends on the algorithms used and the efficiency of their implementation. The ability to select algorithms appropriate to solving particular problems, based on understanding the range of algorithms that address well-defined problems, analyzing their complexity and performance, and their suitability in particular contexts and implementing them is critical for building effective software. A number of general algorithmic strategies are presented including brute force, heuristics, greedy, recursive backtracking anddivide and conquer. Common algorithms pertaining to searching, sorting, binary trees, graphs, and string / expression parsing are also discussed. Also both in-memory and file data structures and their interrelationship with specific algorithms are reviewed.
title: Data Structures and Algorithms
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Research by Practice Workshop 2 is supervised design research that required students to demonstrate mastery in the processes of developing design through research, detailed assessment of options and the integration of technical solutions value and cost control processes to maintain or enhance the design intent. The research based framework of the course prepares students for higher degree design based research. Students will progress the whole or part of the outcomes from 7008ENV Research by Practice Workshop 1 to evidence intelligent, creative, iterative and culturally responsive design processes. The research outcomes and their significance as knowledge will be communicated in forms appropriate to the architectural profession and the discipline. Research outcomes must evidence a design that conforms to the design brief (Assessment 3 7008ENG), respects Country and is capable of compliance with planning controls and construction codes. This course is supported by 7181ESC. Prerequisite 7008ENG. Incompatible 7702ENV.
title: Research by Practice Workshop 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides students with a critical understanding of development within the Australian sport system. An underlying theme is the tension between developing participation rates and performance standards. From a systems perspective students will develop an understanding of the policies, programs, processes and structures that influence the development of sport.
title: Sport Development Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces students into the tax consequences of many investments that individuals in Australia may make. This course primarily considers the tax outcomes from the individual's perspective, such as the receipt of dividends, rental properties, sale of investment assets and superannuation.
title: Taxation Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: In this course, you will learn communication, physical examination, and procedural skills, with a primary focus on neurological and musculoskeletal systems. You will also participate in work-integrated learning (WIL) activities to apply these clinical skills in real practice settings. Clinical practice courses emphasise hands-on learning and supervised skill development, which cannot be fully achieved through independent study. Therefore, attendance is mandatory for all sessions. Students must meet both of the following requirements: Minimum Attendance Requirements At least 80% of total sessions (16 of 20) At least 70% attendance in each module: Communication skills: 5 of 7 Physical examination skills: 4 of 5 Procedural skills: 3 of 4 GP teaching: 5 of 6 (GC) and 3 of 4 (SC) WIL (e.g., bedside teaching, phlebotomy, community placements): Successful submission of the ITA. Note: Session numbers may vary depending on delivery, and attendance thresholds will be adjusted proportionally. Permissible vs. Unexplained Absences Permissible absences (up to 20% for the course and 30% per module) apply only to exceptional circumstances such as illness, emergencies, or other valid reasons. These must be reported promptly through the Student Absence Form (available in Course Essentials) and supported by appropriate documentation (e.g., a medical certificate). Where appropriate, the Course Convenor may assist students with approved absences by offering alternative sessions, subject to availability and class capacity. These sessions are for skill attainment only and do not count toward attendance requirements. No provisions will be made for unexplained absences, and individual remediation sessions cannot be arranged.
title: Introduction to Clinical Practice 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 1 (SPI 1) integrates art history, theory and practice in a structure that fosters artistic experimentation across any media including installation, video, live performance, painting, drawing new media and sculpture in the expanded field. Students will have the chance to explore the interdisciplinary language of contemporary art emphasizing conceptual and thematic responses to set projects that shape greater self-direction in SPI 2.
title: Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course examines the role wrongful convictions play in shaping, facilitating, or impeding justice within the Australian legal framework. By dissecting real-life cases and analysing the systemic flaws contributing to wrongful convictions, students develop a nuanced understanding of the legal system's vulnerabilities and their far-reaching consequences and how these can be prevented. This fosters critical thinking skills, empathy, and a profound appreciation for the imperative of fairness and equity within the justice system.
title: Wrongfully Convicted
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Advanced Technologies focuses on the integration of structural, construction and service systems in complex buildings with an emphasis on environmental sustainability. The course develops students' technical skills in design, development and implementation of structures, construction and building services that address the physical, environmental and cultural demands of large-scale buildings. Students are supported in developing skills to evaluate and integrate regulatory requirements in their projects. It also equips students with design strategies and skills to incorporate sustainable design and renewable energy technologies to meet requirements of relevant environmental rating tools. Incompatible with 7604ENV.
title: Advanced Technologies
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Exegesis 2 follows Exegesis 1, and is the final of two 20cp components and includes the assessment in a single submission for examination upon completion of the program. Students will engage with the rigors of research to complete their research at an advanced level of study within visual practice. The Exegesis will consist of a major research project accompanied by an exegesis of 5000 words (min). The expectation is that the research project will be based within the visual and demonstrates high levels of visual literacy.
title: Exegesis 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course examines psychological and social models of behaviour in the context of individual and group decision making. It provides insights into the approaches and perspectives that can be taken to more deeply understand the client-adviser relationship, the advice process and design of financial strategies. Incompatible and co-taught: 3227AFE Behavioural Insights, 3218AFE Behavioural Finance, AFE328 Behavioural Finance
title: Behavioural Insights
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: How might we begin to think and represent traumatic events? What is the relationship between trauma, memory and mourning? This interdisciplinary course examines the representation of trauma and memory across a range of mediums including film, photography and visual art. Topics examined include: the limits of representation, authenticity, post-memory, affect and reparative aesthetics. Students will be introduced to theories of memory and trauma drawn from art history, feminist theory, history, literature, postcolonial studies and psychoanalysis.
title: Memory and Trauma in Visual Culture
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This final course in the Sculpture, Performance and Installation Major (SPI) assists students in developing a significant body of work for submission to the Graduation Exhibition. Drawing from the skills and knowledge acquired throughout the SPI Major and the Bachelor of Visual Arts, students will produce artwork within their major areas and work with students and staff from other disciplines to present the final Graduation Exhibition. Pre-requisite: Must be undertaking 1651 Bachelor of Visual Arts OR must be undertaking 1652 Bachelor of Visual Arts/Bachelor of Business OR must be undertaking 1187 Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art AND must have completed 3370QCA Sculpture, Performance and Installation Studio 3 AND must have completed 3378QCA Studio Thinking
title: Sculpture Performance and Installation Studio 4
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Dental Hygiene Practice 4 is designed to provide comprehensive scientific knowledge essential to the role of the Dental Hygienist. Students will be integrated into the clinical environment as vital members of the Oral Health Care Team, developing a thorough understanding of the pathogenesis and best practice management principles for gingival and periodontal diseases, while adhering to principles of equity. To enroll in 2037DOH Dental Hygiene Practice 4, students must be enrolled in the Bachelor of Dental Hygiene program and must have successfully completed all Trimester 1 coursework, including 2036DOH Dental Hygiene Practice 3. Additionally, 1205MED must be completed in Trimester 2 for students in 1613
title: Dental Hygiene Practice 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores the fundamental mechanisms underlying human disease, including cell and tissue injury, regeneration and repair, ischaemia and infarction, thrombosis and embolism, and benign and malignant neoplasia. These core principles of general pathology are then integrated with organ-based systems to provide a clinically relevant understanding of systemic pathology. Building on prior knowledge from anatomy, physiology, biochemistry, and microbiology, this course equips students with a structured framework to understand how disease develops, progresses, and presents across different body systems, forming a critical foundation for clinical decision-making in dental practice. Pre-requisites: 1016MSC Anatomy and Physiology Systems I, 1017MSC Anatomy and Physiology Systems II, 2005MSC Biochemistry, and 2015MSC Microbiology for Oral Health. Students must be enrolled in Year 2 of the Bachelor of Dental Health Science (1577).
title: Pathology General for Dental Practitioners
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Preclinical Dental Sciences 4 develops a critical understanding of the concepts, principles and theories in Cariology and Preventive Dentistry, Communication Skills for Oral Health, Equity, Diversity and Sustainability, and Dental Hygiene. Pre-requisite: Students must have successfully completed all preceding year courses to progress to year 2.
title: Pre-Clinical Dental Sciences 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Advanced Dental Hygiene Practice 1 is designed to give the student a deeper understanding and practice in a clinical environment. The course provides students with the opportunity to learn and practice along side other students preparing for dental specialties. Students will apply the principles of patient care and practice management required to achieve a high level of clinical proficiency in the provision of dental hygiene care. Prerequisite: Students must have completed 2037DOH Dental Hygiene Practice 4 to enrol in this course.
title: Advanced Dental Hygiene Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The Transition to Clinical Practice capstone bridges classroom-based learning with clinical environments through masterclasses focused on core clinical skills, clinical placements, and the application of knowledge and problem-solving using case-based learning methods. This course has a compulsory attendance requirement for masterclasses and Case-Based Learning (CBL) sessions. See the attendance policy below. Students who are unable to attend a session must formally inform the Course Convenor prior to the session that will be missed, or as soon as possible after the session, by submitting a Student Absence Form available in Course Essentials. Where relevant, a medical certificate or other supporting documentation should be provided. Attendance Policy: Total number of compulsory masterclasses per course is 12. You may have two valid, reported absence without being required to complete make-up work. If you miss a third masterclass (even for valid or medical reasons), you will have exceeded the permissible absences. In this case, the Course Convenor may require you to complete an alternative learning activity, such as a presentation or viva, to demonstrate your understanding of the missed content. The Course Convenor will determine the format, deadline, and whether the alternative activity meets the required learning outcomes. There are 5 CBL sessions in this course and the permissible absences with a valid reason is 2. If your total absences exceed either attendance threshold (more than 3 masterclasses or more than 2 for CBLs), you will be considered non-compliant with the course requirements. Monitoring and tracking attendance is the student's responsibility. No warnings will be issued when a student approaches or reaches the non-attendance threshold. Students arriving more than 10 minutes late or leaving more than 10 minutes early will be marked absent, unless exceptional circumstances are documented.
title: Transition to Clinical Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course examines diverse approaches and ways of knowing. It explores knowledge systems across cultures, interrogating how information is interpreted and paradigms constructed. Students examine how knowledge is generated and the various forms this might take. In the development of their own methods, students will explore philosophical aspects to 'knowing' and reflect on their role as emerging researchers in the cinematic arts.
title: Ways of Knowing
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course considers theoretical, empirical and practical aspects of financial risk management. It provides an in-depth study of some of the risk management aspects of derivative securities eg options, futures, and forward contracts. The course highlights practical applications of these securities focusing on the concept of financial engineering. The central questions with which this course is concerned is, "What are the characteristics of the most commonly used derivatives securities, how are these instruments priced and which strategies are available in order to manage financial risk with them?"
title: Derivatives Securities
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This subject focuses on developmental prevention to construct a framework for thinking about the prevention of crime and associated problems at the individual, family and local level. Students will examine the challenges associated with developing and implementing evidence-based programs for disadvantaged communities. This will involve consideration of the influences of multiple risk and protective factors as well as strategies to empower local residents and change developmentally relevant institutions and social policies.
title: Developmental Crime Prevention
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course is a Dissertation undertaken in an area chosen in consultation with the student's supervisor(s).
title: Dissertation 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course introduces undergraduate students to academic learning skills for successful progression to further University studies and beyond. Through this course, you will develop transferable life skills, including time and self-management, learning skills and digital literacy, as well as become oriented to university and consider your career goals. With an emphasis on academic integrity, research, and academic communication, this course provides an opportunity for you to build confidence as an independent learner.
title: Foundation Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: We all communicate. Communication plays a major role in all human activity. It is part of our culture. Within the business community, in both public and private sectors, communication is often associated with specific activities such as interacting, informing, instructing and persuading. People who possess demonstrable skills in these activities are employed, prized and promoted. If businesses are to survive in an increasingly competitive and information-oriented environment they will need trained communicators who can speak, write and interact with others efficiently, effectively and professionally. This course is intended to provide participants with advanced understanding of the concepts and principles of professional business communication and to support the development of their skills in interpersonal, spoken and business related communications through practice and feedback. Course participants will be encouraged to participate actively in the course. Prerequisites: NIL. Co-requisites: NIL. Incompatible: 2088EHR Business Communication/ EHR208 Business Communication/ 1008HSV Interpersonal Skills. Co-taught and Incompatible: 2102GBS Business Communication.
title: Business Communication
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: Personal Finance integrates economics and personal finance concepts, such as interest rates, time value of money, probability, diversification and biases in consumer finance, to help students appreciate the implications of economic events and the complexities of financial decision-making. You will gain economic and financial literacy to better plan for your future and make more informed financial decisions through practical financial decision-making applications, including saving, investing and planning for retirement, evaluating student loans and mortgages, and personal taxes. Incompatible and co-taught: 1205AFE Personal Finance
title: Personal Finance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This advanced practical course explores technique and processes applicable to directing for theatre. A studio-based experience of praxis applications provides students with knowledge of the analytical, theoretical, practical and technical skills necessary to directing theatre production. Students learn to develop and articulate artistic vision specific to contexts of directing for theatre in its various genres, forms and styles. This course is essential for students studying the a theatre major and/or drama education.
title: Theatre Direction
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This clinic placement runs in partnership with our Community Legal Centre partners for a day a week during the Trimester. Attendance at your centre on the allocated day of the week is compulsory. Students will assist clients who rely on Community Legal centres to access justice, promoting social justice and inclusion. This course invites you to move out of your comfort zone, acquire practical legal skills in a supportive environment, and to challenge yourself professionally and personally. You will be guided and supported by experienced supervisors and will finish the clinic with a real sense of accomplishment. Students report that work integrated learning {WIL) makes them more employable, and employers back this up, reporting WIL favourably influences their perception of students' abilities. Students say WIL helps them assess their career direction, complements their learning, increases their networks, increases their motivation to study and helps them prepare for future employment.
title: Social Justice Lawyering 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course simulates the experience of working in a professional game development studio. In an advanced role, students will take on complex tasks in-game production and work in small teams to create fully functioning video games from initial concept to launch while engaging with industry professionals. In this course, students will gain experience in all aspects of game development, including the social, cultural, and ethical implications of producing games. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies and receive guidance and feedback from experienced game development mentors. Guest lectures and engagement with the games industry will provide students with a deeper understanding of game development and its potential career opportunities. At the end of this course, students will have developed a polished, playable game, focussing deeper into the technical aspects of game development and beginning to specialise in areas such as programming, game art, animation or virtual production.
title: Game Studio 3: Advanced
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: In this course students will work towards a major body of work suitable for professional presentation, exploring arts-based research processes. Prerequisite: 2908QCA Identity Project
title: Visions Major Studio Project 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course provides a cultural foundation for communicating ideas and information visually. It covers the fundamental principles of cultural arts practices and its relationship with society, the environment, and contemporary culture. Through studio-based projects, students will learn how to understand cultural semiotics and the ability to develop their own signs and symbols to support cultural understandings through relationships. They will learn to embrace and respect Cultural Protocols, promote inclusivity and representation, learn about semiotics, symbol design and cultural ethics.
title: CAIA Visual Communications
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: In this course students critically interrogate the role of the creative producer, which sits at the intersection of art and commerce. To do this, students will analyse how creative producers build projects and slates within shifting financing and market conditions and develop the necessary skills to lead a team towards a unified creative vision. Students will leave this course equipped with a critical understanding of the evolving industrial, commercial, and cultural role of the creative producer across all screen media, and the dynamic relationship between creative vision and commercial viability.
title: Creative Producing
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course explores the design of animated characters. Through extended practice in both analogue and digital drawing, students will gain specific knowledge in the creation of functional, believable and appealing characters for use in animation and games production or for illustrative purposes in the communication design and art fields. The course includes 'bible' development, and advanced figure and creature design.
title: Concept Design: Characters
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: In this course, students will explore the areas of language and communication and health and physical education (HPE) in the curriculum and create suitable learning experiences that support young children. Students will develop an understanding of supporting learners who have English as an additional language and design learning environments that allows play and inquiry to foster language/communication and HPE. Students will complete 20 days of placement with children aged 3-5 years.
title: Language, Communication and HPE
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides an entry point to music psychology, the field of research attempting to answer these kinds of questions. The course will introduce ways of critically thinking about music, and will analyse research using the scientific methods used by psychology. This is a generalist course without any prerequisites that can be taken by any student. It will be conducted entirely online, with readings and audiovisual material, online lecture and online tutorial discussions.
title: Music, Mind and Brain
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course guides students in discovering and developing their own research methods for creative practice in cinematic arts. Students will explore and experiment with various research approaches, connecting these to their cinematic arts practice. By engaging with different methods of practice-based inquiry, reflective techniques, and research design, students will develop their unique research voice. This process will enable students to conduct rigorous practice-based research with the potential to innovate in their specific areas of cinematic arts.
title: Research in the Cinematic Arts
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: In this course you will explore your unique personal attributes and career aspirations. This reflective process will help you gain a deeper understanding of how your strengths, interests and areas for growth align with your future academic and career goals. Throughout this course you will complete a variety of professional pathway activities which include maths essentials, science fundamentals, and innovation, creativity and leadership.
title: Professional Pathways
academicOrgDescription: EmpowerED

description: This course applies psychological theory and research to understand culture and cultural diversity. The core aims are to enable students to recognise the importance of culture in guiding thoughts, feelings and behaviours; to develop an understanding of issues of inclusion and exclusion; and to build awareness of each student's own culture as well as encourage competence in working with culturally diverse others. This course is relevant to a range of contexts and disciplines, including psychology, counselling, health, education, business, and humanities, or any subject area which requires effective interpersonal/social relationships. Students will learn what psychology has to say about what happens when societies become more culturally diverse (or begin to recognise existing diversity) and apply principles from Cultural, Cross-Cultural, and Indigenous Psychology to the Australian specific context, as well as to the broader international environment. Prerequisites: Must have completed a minimum of 80 credit points.
title: Psychological Perspectives on Cultural Diversity
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course provides students with the opportunity for work experience in a professional studio environment. The aim is to foster the development of reflective practitioners. Students will develop a working knowledge of organisational culture/s, technical skills and ethics in commercial design/art practice. Students will gain a critically informed understanding of their major area of study in a professional context.
title: Creative Internships
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This capstone block challenges learners to apply their business capabilities to real-world problems. Drawing on financial, ethical, and global perspectives, they develop innovative responses to systemic challenges facing business and society.
title: Foundations of Finance and Problem-Solving in Complex Contexts
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: From mythical beasts to extraterrestrial beings, in this course, students will learn to bring imaginative creatures to life using advanced 3D sculpting techniques. Students in this course will experiment during the production process, from initial concept and sketching to digital sculpting, texturing, and final rendering, emphasising anatomical plausibility, expressive detailing, and creative innovation. Aimed at learners with a foundational knowledge of 3D modelling, this course deepens understanding of complex sculpting techniques and their applications. Through intensive workshops and project-based learning, students will master high-resolution detailing, realistic texturing, and effectively integrating sculpted models into professional games, animation, and film production pipelines.
title: 3D Art: Digital Creatures
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course examines the theoretical concepts of artificial intelligence (AI) and physics programming for games through the lens of experimental practice. Students will work individually to develop unique ways of interacting with gamespaces by rapidly prototyping game ideas that explore the creative application of AI or physics. Through focused experimentation, students will employ creative programming solutions that provide unique gameplay experiences in various contexts and genres. Students will reflect on and critique their design solutions by researching and applying theoretical design concepts in their approach.
title: Games Programming: A.I. and Physics
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course investigates seminal screen works and their historical, industrial and cultural context. Students will examine a diverse range of cinematic art works, from films and television to games and immersive art, that influenced and inspired generations of creators to innovate the art form and captivated audiences around the world. Through readings, critical analysis and peer discussions, students will consolidate and synthesise their understanding of screen culture and its place in society.
title: Advanced Screen Studies
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This foundational course provides a comprehensive overview of the historical and contemporary contexts of special education and inclusive education. Students will examine the evolution of special education from its origins to modern approaches, exploring key milestones, legislative actions, and societal shifts that have shaped the field. Building on this foundation, the course delves into the theoretical frameworks and models that underpin current special education practices. Students will critically analyse the social and affirmation models of disability, neurodiversity perspectives, and the principles of social justice and equity. The course will focus on identifying and addressing barriers to education, such as communication, disability, ability, and accessibility. Students will develop strategies to address these barriers and ensure meaningful engagement with the curriculum for all learners. Throughout the course, students will explore effective collaboration strategies with paraprofessionals and other stakeholders to facilitate genuine participation and learning for students in special education contexts.
title: Equity in Special Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course explores second language acquisition (SLA) theories and their implications for teaching and learning. It examines SLA from three perspectives: linguistic knowledge, cognitive skill, and socially and personality-mediated processes. Individual learner differences and affective variables are also investigated.
title: Second Language Acquisition
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course offers a conceptual framework covering public policy perspective on international trade, the impact of multilateral institutions and trade blocs on global business, foreign direct investment and management of multinational corporations. The course provides a basic foundation for understanding specialised courses in technology and the global economy, global marketing and entrepreneurship in a dynamic business environment.
title: Global Business
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The course will deepen students' knowledge and skills in, and attitudes towards evidence-based practice and research as it is applied in professional practice and knowledge generation. Students will specifically further their knowledge and skills in the evidence-based practice pathway and research methods relevant to professional practice. Students will apply their knowledge and skills to a particular scenario, requiring them to explore ethical considerations and responsibilities, develop research objectives/questions, collect and analyse data, and report research findings.
title: Research and Evidence for Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course provides an in-depth exploration of aerodynamics tailored specifically for pilot students, emphasizing practical applications rather than theoretical engineering complexities. The course focuses on equipping future pilots with a comprehensive understanding of aerodynamic principles and their direct impact on flight performance, safety, and operational decision-making. Key topics include the fundamentals of airfoil shapes, lift, drag, and thrust forces, the behavior of airflow around various aircraft structures, and the influence of environmental conditions on flight. Students will explore different aircraft configurations and their effect on aerodynamic performance, with a focus on practical application during key flight stages such as takeoff, cruise, and landing. Additionally, the course introduces high-speed aircraft aerodynamics, covering topics such as shock waves, compressibility effects, transonic and supersonic flight considerations, and their influence on aircraft performance and control. Students will learn how high-speed aerodynamic phenomena differ from subsonic flight, enabling a comprehensive understanding of performance characteristics, stability challenges, and critical factors to consider during high-speed operations. Incompatible with 2521NSC Aerodynamics for Aviation AND 3520NSC Aerodynamics Part II.
title: Aerodynamics for Aviation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course designed for students eager to explore the dynamic world of artificial intelligence (AI). The comprehensive journey unfolds ten enriching topics, covering the fundamental principles of AI, classical machine learning algorithms, and the revolutionary landscape of deep learning and neural networks. Delve into the intricacies of Natural Language Processing (NLP) and the captivating realm of computer vision (CV). Explore knowledge representation and reasoning, paving the way for a deeper understanding of AI applications across diverse domains. Cap off your exploration by engaging in thought-provoking discussions on AI ethics and its profound societal impact. This course is your gateway to a practical understanding of AI, empowering you to apply these concepts in your future endeavors and stay ahead in our AI-driven world. Join us on this exciting exploration into the heart of practical AI knowledge!
title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course introduces students to law, politics, and criminal justice in Australia. It explores how laws are made, the influence of politics on law reform, the role of the media, human rights protections, and criminal responsibility. It considers the historical treatment of First Nations peoples in Australia's legal system and the role that law plays in promoting justice and accountability. This knowledge provides a foundation for further study on criminal law and justice systems.
title: Law, Crime and Justice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This subject examines strategies for changing criminal behaviour available within the correctional system, drawing particularly on psychological principles and research. The implications of the various theories of crime causation for correctional programming are considered. A review of specific rehabilitation programs, in institution and community settings, is presented. A critical assessment of the rehabilitation ideal, in terms of ethical, theoretical and practical concerns, is undertaken.
title: Rehabilitating Offenders
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Wellbeing in the Creative Arts is a core course for the Bachelor of Music degree. In this course you will have the opportunity to develop strategies to positively impact wellbeing in your creative practice, gain an understanding of accessibility principles in the creative arts, learn about First Australian's perspectives of wellbeing, and develop your artistic research skills.
title: Wellbeing in the Creative Arts
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This is an Honours/Masters Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course building on the learning from 6009QCM, providing students with an opportunity to apply their skills in an industry work placement, or self-directed industry environment, working at least 100-150 hours during the course. Pre-requisite 6009QCM.
title: Work Integrated Learning 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course examines how consumer psychology and marketing research combine to inform effective, evidence-based communication strategies. You will learn how to analyse consumer behaviour, design and conduct marketing research, and interpret findings to uncover what motivates different audience segments. Using these insights, you will create integrated marketing communication plans that align message, medium, and timing to defined objectives. Ethical, inclusive, and sustainable communication practices are embedded throughout, ensuring strategies are both impactful and socially responsible.
title: Marketing Communication and Consumer Insight
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course critically examines how systems of justice intersect with identity, power, and inequality. Focusing on young people, women, and First Nations peoples, students will explore the historical, social, and institutional forces that shape diverse experiences of crime, victimisation, and justice. Drawing on feminist, decolonial, and critical criminological perspectives, the course unpacks how justice systems can both reproduce and resist social disadvantage. Through contemporary case studies and reflective learning, students will consider pathways to more inclusive, responsive, and culturally appropriate justice practices.
title: Justice and Diverse Populations
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Strong writing skills are fundamental to success at university and highly valued in professional environments. You'll be introduced to the principles and practices of academic writing, helping you develop the skills needed to communicate ideas clearly, construct persuasive arguments and engage with scholarly sources. Explore key concepts that underpin effective academic communication, including purpose, audience, genre and argumentation. Through practical writing activities, you'll learn how to analyse information, evaluate evidence and develop a clear academic voice while meeting the expectations of university-level study. This subject focuses on source-based writing, teaching you how to locate, interpret and integrate information from scholarly and non-scholarly materials using appropriate academic conventions. You'll also build an understanding of academic integrity and the responsible use of information. Rather than treating writing as a one-size-fits-all skill, the course recognises that different disciplines have their own ways of communicating knowledge. You'll examine how writing varies across academic contexts and develop strategies that can be transferred to future subjects in your chosen field of study. Particularly relevant for students in the humanities and social sciences, this subject provides a foundation for academic success while developing communication skills that are valuable across a broad range of careers and professions.
title: Foundations of Academic Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

title: Work Integrated Learning Music Industry Internship Music Industry Internship
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course introduces students to advancements in criminological theories to better understand criminal behavior at both the micro (individual) and macro (societal) levels. Students will learn how criminologists engage with new research to improve our understanding of how and why people engage in criminal activity.
title: Advanced Criminological Theories
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course constitutes Part 1 and 10CP of a 30CP individually supervised project in which a student may complete written work on an approved topic. The research project undertaken will be relevant to the music discipline and incorporate high levels of competence and academic excellence. Assessment will be by dissertation. This will be delivered by a supervisory team, which will be tailored to the needs of each student's project.
title: Dissertation Part 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course engages with Philip Auslander's reconsideration of live performance in a media-dominated culture. Activities are driven by the question: what is it to be live in a virtual world? Students augment their existing audio media skills to acquire skills in camera operation and digital movie editing. Practical strategies to capture, present, and disseminate live performance activities in a form suitable for Internet distribution are at the foreground. The overall goal is to reimagine the skills and techniques of live performance with Music Technology in a format suitable for fixed media output.
title: Liveness in a Virtual World
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This advanced-level course aims to further develop your ability to respond to more complex challenges such as design for inclusivity, design for repair, or design for future contexts. Through studio-based projects, you will gain a deeper understanding of national and international standards, intellectual property governing patents and design registrations, nuances of applied design practice, systems thinking, and client interaction. By the end of the course a future product and user experience designer emerges; adaptable, collaborative, and resilient, contemplating product service systems, design-led futures, speculative or social design constructs while responding to external industry or research-led design briefs.

academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course introduces students to teaching as a research-informed profession. It includes exploration of how published research and student data inform the work of teachers, while also developing the skills and understandings required for teachers to work as researchers.
title: Research Informed Teaching in Secondary Schools
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

In this course students will reflect on their knowledge and practice to develop and apply advanced clinical and decision-making skills.

academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words.

academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course will familiarise students with qualitative and quantitative research approaches that are typically used to investigate issues in the context of education. Students will be provided with opportunities to explore and evaluate both methodological paradigms to critically analyse research reports and interpret the implications of research for professional practices in education. The course will also investigate ethical and political concerns relating to education research. A key outcome of this course involves students critically reviewing relevant research literature, synthesising findings, and drawing conclusions in connection with a specific context of professional practice in education.

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course provides a sound theoretical and practical background in clinical exercise testing including specificity, sensitivity, reliability, and validity of selected tests and procedures. Particular attention is given to the interpretation of test results from patients with cardiovascular or lung disease as well as athletes and aged persons. Case studies will be used as appropriate learning models. The laboratory sessions are designed to help students develop technical skills needed to conduct clinical measurements for the pre-assessment and conduct of graded exercise testing, in addition to extending understanding of the theoretical principles associated with exercise testing.
title: Clinical Exercise Testing
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This foundation course provides students with knowledge that is fundamental to the practice of speech pathology. The course encompasses two streams: 'Anatomy and Physiology' and 'Linguistics and Phonetics'. The two streams will cover key concepts and skills that are central to understanding human communication and swallowing processes. Knowledge of these concepts and skills will prepare students for effective participation in the Communication and Swallowing Disorders and Speech Pathology Skills and Practice courses. The Anatomy and Physiology stream will see students learn about: (i) the anatomy of the head, neck and thorax and (ii) neuroanatomy (human nervous system) as they pertain to understanding human communication and swallowing. The Linguistics and Phonetics stream will introduce students to the different components of speech (phonetics and phonology and language (form, meaning and use). You will learn how these concepts relate to communication and communication difference or disability.
title: Foundations of Speech Pathology
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the major issues and debates concerning Islam and Muslim communities in the West, including Australia, Europe, and North America. Its focus is not confined to Muslim communities but extends to the manifestations of Islam in Western Muslim-minority contexts of the late twentieth and early twenty-first centuries. The course offers insights into the development of Islam as part of the lived experiences of Muslims in the West in response to developments in the broader Muslim world as well as the challenges and opportunities associated with various Western societies. The topics addressed include immigration, multiculturalism, integration, female religious authority, conversion to Islam, home-grown terrorism, Islamophobia, Islamic jurisprudence and the emergence of a Western Islam.
title: Islam and Muslim Communities in the West
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Discourse, which means 'language-in-use', influences every aspect of our lives, from the personal to the social, public and global. Some discourses lie above our level of consciousness (overt) and others below it (covert), but they all affect our everyday existence and define our culture. At a personal level, you engage in interplays of discourse, text and power every time you argue with a family member. At the global level, discursive battles are waged on news screens and social media among groups seeking to advance their ideologies. This course explores the questions 'How is language used to exercise power?' and 'How can we analyse it?' As such, a strong focus is on the nexus of language and socio-political issues. We look at the discursive strategies employed by politicians, the media, organisations, educators, advertisers, spin doctors, extremists, authorities of all kinds and more. No prior knowledge is assumed.
title: English Discourse, Text and Power
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course aims to sensitise students to the structure of language, with a particular focus on English. Students learn some key terms and tools with which to analyse the features of written and spoken text. The course also aims to raise students' awareness of some of the difficulties speakers of other languages may have with English. It provides a foundation for further personal language awareness development. 7901LHS must be completed before enrolling in 7903LHS, or 7901LHS and 7903LHS can be enrolled in together in the same trimester.
title: Language awareness for second language teachers
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

Students may undertake work-experience, study tours, short-courses or other projects during a study abroad period. This is the 10-credit point version of 3192LHS Language In-Country Independent Study Enhanced. The course can be taken as part of a short-term study abroad program or in conjunction with an exchange program. Students will define the in-country experience in consultation with the course convenor and other academic staff from the students' program of study. The assessment is in the form of pre-departure tasks, an online reflective journal and an oral presentation, to be delivered on return in the language of the chosen country and/or in English, depending on the students' level of language proficiency.
title: Language In-Country Independent Study
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course engages students in a critical examination of health promotion and public health nutrition interventions to priority health issues within local, national and international contexts.
title: Priorities and Interventions in Health Promotion
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course introduces the process of scientific inquiry and the application of appropriate research methods to address questions relevant to public health and health research more broadly. It equips students with the foundational knowledge and skills needed to critically appraise and conduct health research.
title: Health Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: In Australia, the law plays a fundamental role in the provision of healthcare. It has a powerful influence over the structure and operation of the Australian health system and regulates the delivery of healthcare services. In addition, the law establishes the rights and obligations of health practitioners and care recipients. This course provides an understanding of the law in relation to health, healthcare, and healthcare service delivery as well as an understanding of the Australian system of governance, the legal system, and sources of law. Ethics and law are similar in that they seek to guide and affect individual behaviour. Ethical principles are often found within legal judgements and reasonings, particularly where there have been morally complex situations such as end-of-life decisions. However, ethics and law are both distinct disciplines with their own language, characteristics, and objectives. Within healthcare delivery, both ethics and law have an influential role in decision-making for health services managers. This course addresses ethical concepts and the differences between ethics and the law. It also lays the foundation for ethical decision-making and examines ethical philosophies and approaches for resolving ethical dilemmas.
title: Applied Ethics and Law for Health Service Managers
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The effective management of risk depends critically on what people in your organization (including your safety people) understand risk to be. Misconceived ideas about risk can lead to wasted money and effort trying to manage risk - and worse, it can lead to unanticipated side effects and even greater risk. If you see risk as a kind of unconfined energy that might harm people, then you can put barriers between people and that source of harm. But this can backfire if the barrier is a social one, and can easily get circumvented if your processes aren't simple, linear or sequential. Also, a barrier doesn't help if your risk consists of a gradual drift toward failure and a continuous re-negotiation of what your organization will accept under cost and efficiency pressures. If you see risk as worker non-compliance or other behavioral problems, then you might put behavioral controls, surveillance or performance management in place. This, however, does nothing to improve the error-tolerance or error-resistance of the tools, tasks and organization your people work with, and can leave behavioral traps firmly in place. It also hampers your people's adaptive capacities that your organization undoubtedly relies on to get stuff done on the frontline. In this course, you will learn about the background and history of ideas that have shaped what is safety science and practice today. You will study the research and practical insights that drove and developed the various concepts and theories about risk and safety, the accidents and societal trends that led to new developments and insights, and begin to understand how each of these models takes only a limited look at the world, enabling you to do certain things while excluding others. You will be better able to match safety problems to solutions in your own organization and beyond.
title: Foundations of Safety Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course places water management in the context of human development and poverty alleviation, focusing on social analysis and tools for water management: safe, secure and equitable access to water and river resources; and the links between water supply, energy, sanitation, hygiene and improved public health. Effective and equitable water management requires an understanding of the socio-cultural, gender and economic factors impacting on water policy, plan, access and use. Students will be trained in the application of different participatory approaches, including various tools such as gender analysis, PRA, Sustainable Livelihoods Framework, and participatory design and evaluation of water and sanitation projects. A strong focus is placed on capacity building, including effective education in Integrated Water Management; practical tools for the development of formal and informal institutional analysis and frameworks for water management; and strategies for managing community participation and strengthening relationships between governments, NGOs and communities. The course will be focussed mostly around a field based learning experience including mini research project.
title: Community, Livelihoods, Development and Water
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will introduce students to the history of international aviation, and investigate the formation, structure and roles of the International Civil Aviation Organisation (ICAO), one of the specialised agencies of the United Nations, and its interactions with other international organisations that affect international civil aviation operations. There are no prerequisites for this course. Incompatible with: 1506BPS International aviation; AVN2004 International Aviation Organisation; AVN7010 and 7010AVN International Aviation; 7506BPS and 7506NSC International Aviation.
title: International Aviation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In the tourism and hospitality industries, the characteristics of fixed capacity, perishable inventory and fluctuating demand require a dynamic approach to pricing and capacity allocation across a range of transparent distribution channels. This course covers the principles of revenue management in order to maximise the profitability of tourism and hospitality operations. In this course you will learn how to apply revenue management techniques, such as forecasting and pricing models, overbooking policies and length-of-stay tools, as well as evaluate the revenue management performance of hotels through industry-specific metrics such as RevPAR and GOPPAR.
title: Tourism and Hospitality Revenue Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course, which includes an embedded 15-day school experience, will help PSTs to develop an understanding of young people aged 10-18 years with a special focus on their diverse and complex interests and abilities. PSTs will also consider research about how learning occurs (such as how the brain learns and retains information) and the influence of the social context on young people's lives and learning. Various teaching approaches, responsive to students needs will be examined (including explicit teaching, modelling, and scaffolding) and ways to develop culturally safe classrooms will be investigated.
title: Understanding Diverse Learners 10 - 18
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is designed for the purpose of educating first year students in basic meteorology in the Australian region, informing them, as well as providing a sound knowledge base of weather systems, which not only impact on flight planning, but could compromise aviation safety. The course is only available on campus, and not suited to 'professional entry' students. There are no prerequisites for this course.
title: Atmospheric Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course is the second of two designed for pre-service teachers of secondary school sciences, with a focus on Senior Biological Science. The course covers curriculum, pedagogy and assessment relevant to teaching senior secondary school students in Queensland and across Australia. Lectures and labs have been designed to develop and expand student knowledge and skills within the biological sciences. The central purpose of the course is to enable students to develop their knowledge and understanding of conceptual and procedural issues associated with curriculum decision-making, planning and assessment, and to develop associated skills. Lectures will be delivered live and accessed synchronously as hybrid whilst also being recorded.

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

Influential research papers will also be introduced to illustrate the use of these techniques within these domains. Topics include linear regression, VAR, co-integration, discrete choice models, event studies, volatility models, time-series analysis, panel-data analysis and cross-sectional analysis.
title: Advanced Quantitative Methods and Econometrics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

Students will undertake either an experimental research project or a systematic review, involving data generation or the application of evidence-based research methods to synthesise and critically evaluate the literature, followed by analysis and interpretation of findings, oral presentation, and communication of outcomes through a written scientific report. Students will also complete a second self-directed independent research project, culminating in the communication of research findings through written and oral scientific outputs.
title: Clinical Laboratory Discipline Based Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course explores the diversity and development of Indigenous Australian art. It aims to give students a critical and contemporary understanding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander contexts and perspectives, and the foundational knowledge required to engage with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, communities and organisations.
title: Indigenous Art and Protocols
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Educational leadership is a context-specific, complex and contradictory process and practice. This course introduces students to broad understandings of educational leadership in diverse professional settings. It examines contemporary debates and issues in educational leadership. It analyses the nexus between leading, learning and social change. Key assumptions that underpin the course are: the fundamental importance of changing contexts in rethinking understandings of educational leadership; an understanding of educational leadership as practice/praxis that questions taken-for-granted assumptions about leading, learning and pedagogy; the inherent diversity of educational contexts and the consequent social justice implications for educational leadership; and the intrinsic relationship between educational leadership, pedagogy and change as it applies to students' particular professional settings and interests.
title: Leading Learning and Change
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Fitness Programming will provide students with the skills required to conduct and interpret pre-exercise health screening and exercise testing. Topics covered include the assessment of cardiorespiratory endurance, body composition, and muscular strength, power, endurance and flexibility. Students will also learn how to design and delivery exercise programs for low risk individuals and groups.
title: Fitness Programming
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

title: Foundational Anatomy and Physiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

As a 10CP course, 2080LHS comprises approximately 150 hours of work in total.
title: Spanish 2A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides an introduction to the study of the Italian language and to contemporary Italian culture and society. It is offered in a semi - intensive (6.5 - week) online mode with synchronous classes in Trimester 3, and in both on-campus and online modes in Trimester 1. The course serves as the foundational prerequisite for all subsequent Italian language subjects at Griffith, including 1091LHS Italian 1B, which is available in the same modes in Trimester 3 and in Trimester 2. While designed primarily as the entry point for further study, the course also offers a valuable and engaging introduction for students seeking to acquire basic Italian for personal, academic, or professional purposes. Class recordings are provided to support study and revision. Students with prior experience in Italian need to contact the Italian Studies Coordinator to ensure appropriate placement.
title: Italian 1A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides a range of activities that will further develop inquiry and problem-solving skills and put the professional responsibilities of science students into practice. A range of authentic learning experiences will see students conduct investigations (open investigations, experiments, field assessments, application of theory) as individuals, occasionally working in small teams if necessary, in which data is collected, recorded and interpreted using appropriate discipline specific approaches. Conclusions will be drawn and questions for future investigation highlighted. Assessment will be by the combination of a high-quality written report and an oral defence of this report.
title: Science Capstone
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: In this first year beginner's-level course, students learn to read Chinese sentences, engage in simple oral and written communication on everyday topics, and gain a preliminary understanding of Chinese social patterns and behaviour. This course focuses on the sound system of Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin), its writing system, texts and role-play exercises. Assessment is based on progressive spoken and written tests, weekly exercises and class participation. NOTE: Any student who is native/proficient speakers of Mandarin Chinese or has completed their secondary education in a Mandarin or Cantonese speaking country is NOT ELIGIBLE to enroll in this course.
title: Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin) 1A
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This first-year beginner's level course focuses on the sound system of Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin), its writing system, texts and role-play exercises, through which students learn to read Chinese sentences, engage in simple oral and written communication on everyday topics and gain a preliminary understanding of Chinese social patterns and behaviours. Assessment is based on progressive spoken and written tests, weekly exercises and class participation. NOTE: Any student who is native/proficient speakers of Mandarin Chinese or has completed their secondary education in a Mandarin or Cantonese speaking country is NOT ELIGIBLE to enroll in this course. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: 1010LAL_Y1; 1010LAL_Y2; CHN12 Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin) IB. PREREQUISITE: 1084LAL or equivalent level of proficiency certified by means of a one-to-one interview administered by our Chinese teaching staff.
title: Modern Standard Chinese (Mandarin) 1B
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: NMR spectroscopy is a central technique for studying molecular structure. Thus, NMR spectroscopy is important in a range of chemical and biological fields with applications in organic chemistry, natural products chemistry, drug discovery, design and development, forensic science, agriculture, environmental science and ecology, food safety, personalised medicine, systems biology, and structural biology. Cutting edge NMR techniques are used to study molecules ranging from small organic molecules to large protein-protein complexes, and from pure substances to complex mixtures and biological samples. Students will learn modern NMR methods and their applications though lectures, workshops, and laboratory activities covering topics in natural products chemistry, forensics and analytical chemistry, metabolomics and systems biology, structural biology, and drug discovery, design, and development.
title: NMR in Biological Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will provide opportunities for pre-service teachers to develop an understanding of the curriculum knowledge and pedagogical skills required to assist children's developing understanding of the world in which they live. It introduces the Australian Curriculum areas of Humanities and Social Sciences (history, geography, civics and citizenship, and economics and business) from Foundation to Year 6. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of professional experience placements.
