title: Understanding the world we live in (HASS): Primary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course aims to provide students with a sound understanding of research methods applicable to the aviation industry. The course provides an introduction to the variety of approaches to designing good research. With a focus on research in the aviation industry, the course covers both quantitative and qualitative designs, from experiments to case studies, and map their fit to theory and research question, as well as their advantages and disadvantages. The course aims to provide students with the research skills necessary to tackle 3502NSC, or 3504NSC.
title: Aviation Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is designed to teach students the logic of research methodology and evaluation in the social sciences. Students will learn how to articulate a program evaluation research proposal, formulate research designs, and logically determine what research methodology provides the best avenue to carry out different forms of research.
title: Research and Evaluation Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course travels through different cultures of writing, and writing from different cultures. Focusing on contemporary literature, we will begin by examining the complex interplay between Indigenous and non-Indigenous literature and culture in Australia, before 'packing our bags' to journey across some of the most exciting and unusual literary terrains in the rest of the world. Award-winning and highly influential works of fiction, poetry and non-fiction will provide us with opportunities to study a diverse range of writing techniques, as well as a platform for critical engagement with contemporary cultures and their literatures. Prerequisites: this is a 2nd-year course in the Creative Writing major; ideally, students will have completed at least one other course in the major prior to enrolling in this course. Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Writing Across Cultures
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course will enhance your professional communication skills and work readiness. You will engage in authentic professionally aligned activities through simulated communication scenarios conducted in workshops.
title: Placement Preparation
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: Learn how to more effectively bring about transformative change in the health care sector, applying innovative strategy and personal influence. You will critically appraise leadership, change management and organisational theories and principles and determine their applicability to your practice and institution. Through self-analysis, you will also enhance your personal leadership style and preferences and identify potential for development and growth. With new leadership and management skills, you will be ready to facilitate technological and cultural change in health care organisations to deliver improved evidence-based, person-centred care.
title: Transforming and Leading Healthcare
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: This course will develop students' pedagogical content knowledge and mathematics content knowledge in the areas of number (numeration & amp; computation), numeracy and algebraic thinking necessary to build meaningful approaches to learning and teaching these core mathematics strands. It includes a range of approaches for the effective teaching of numeracy, including the discerning use of explicit teaching of mathematics to build fluency, understanding, problem solving, and reasoning.
title: Mathematics Education 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Foundation Mathematics aims to provide a solid basis from which to build a wider set of mathematical skills across a broad range of disciplines. You may be looking to further studies in Education, IT, Business, Engineering, Environment or Science; all of which require a solid grounding in mathematics. Foundation Mathematics has been designed to cater for those who did not study Mathematical Methods (or equivalent) in high school or have been away from study for several years and need to refresh their mathematical skills. Foundation Mathematics covers the assumed mathematical knowledge required for courses such as 1201SCG, 1202SCG, 1010ENG and 1020ENG. NOTE: Students who have recently completed the Senior Secondary Syllabus of Mathematical Methods or Specialist Mathematics (previously Mathematics B or C), or equivalent, are NOT permitted to enrol in 1017SCG Foundation Mathematics. NOTE: this course is only offered on-campus, and students are expected to attend assessment and weekly classes on campus, in person.
title: Foundation Mathematics
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Successful tourism and hospitality managers require a good understanding of their operating environment, in particular the economy which impacts demand for tourism and hospitality services and costs of doing business. This course takes a very applied approach to demonstrate the importance of understanding both the micro and macro influences on consumer behaviour, specifically within the economic operating environment of tourism and hospitality businesses in the global marketplace.
title: Tourism Economics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course introduces students to the highly competitive and changing marketing environment of the hotel industry, providing them with an awareness and understanding of the unique marketing, sales and distribution challenges faced by hotel operators.
title: Hotel Distribution and Sales
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This 20 credit point elective course is available to all undergraduate Griffith Business School students. The course is designed to facilitate a successful transition from university life to employment. A second but equally important feature of this course is the focus on raising awareness of your own personal attributes. You will participate in a task, activity or project-based internship in a face-to-face, virtual/online or blended mode which can open up possibilities to work with small and medium enterprises, business, government and community organisations in locations outside of South-East Queensland (e.g. regional and remote areas of Australia and other capital cities). Each placement offered by a 'Host Organisation' is carefully considered and matched to a student who demonstrates the required business knowledge, skills, personal attributes and motivation required to complete the activity, task or project to the level expected of an intern. This course is not available for credit based on prior studies or work experience, however flexible arrangements can be organised to allow students to commence their internship component prior to the start of the trimester (e.g., in the case of Summer or Winter Vacation Programs). Please email gbsinternships@griffith.edu.au for more information on flexible arrangements. Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
title: UG Business Internship II
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This 20 credit point elective course is available to all postgraduate Griffith Business School students. Its purpose is to allow students to explore potential career paths and apply the necessary skills for a successful transition from university to the workforce. Throughout the course, students will develop insights into the attributes that contribute to their ability to make meaningful impact. Designed to complement students' participation in internships with organisations such as small and medium enterprises, multinational corporations, government departments, and non-profits. This course offers flexibility in delivery, including face-to-face, virtual or hybrid formats. Internship opportunities extend beyond South-East Queensland, encompassing regional and remote areas of Australia as well as other capital cities. Enrolment in this course is contingent upon completion of an application process in addition to successfully securing an internship placement. Students are encouraged to take ownership of their career development and utilise support resources available through Griffith CareerHub. Students may bring their own internship experience (paid or unpaid) or apply for a range of unpaid internship opportunities sourced by Griffith Business School - though these positions are competitive and not guaranteed. To begin the application process, please contact gbsinternships@griffith.edu.au. Please note: This course is not available for credit based on prior studies or external activities. Fluency in written and spoken English is required.
title: PG Business Internship II
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course provides fundamental knowledge and practical skills in computer networking and data communications. Students explore networking models, protocols, addressing, switching, routing, and peer-to-peer networks that support modern digital communication. Through laboratory-based learning, students design, implement, secure, and troubleshoot basic network solutions using industry-standard concepts and technologies, including VLANs, inter-VLAN routing, Layer 2 security mechanisms, and STP concepts.
title: Computer Networking Essentials
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: Learn how to empower and assist people to plan their lives and gain independence with the lessons from this course. You'll gain an introduction to the values, theories, frameworks, principles and skills of person-centred planning and case management tools regarded as among the most powerful for human services practitioners seeking to help people reach their potential. These skills are relevant for people interested in working in allied health and human services settings, including employment services, occupational and insurance-based rehabilitation, community mental health and NDIS-related services. With the skills learned in this course, you'll become more effective at determining individual need and planning with empathy and ethics. Your procurement of a range of appropriate services, supports and documentation will help promote the goals of diverse clients. You'll be capable of implementing person-centred care frameworks across a range of disciplines, using effective stakeholder engagement, coordination and communication skills as well as new tools to manage caseload, so you can deliver the best community health outcomes for your clients. This course was formerly 7021HSV. Incompatible: 7021HSV is incompatible with 7321AHS.
title: Person-Centred Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Vocational evaluation and planning represents the first stage in the vocational rehabilitation process. This course aims to introduce students to the philosophy and principles underpinning vocational assessment and rehabilitation planning. It will also explore the practical application of techniques used in the rehabilitation field to assist people with disabilities to determine a suitable vocational rehabilitation goal, and look at how such assessment is integrated into the rehabilitation planning process. In the event of high enrolment numbers, enrolment preference will be granted to students who have this course listed in their program in the first instance.
title: Vocational Evaluation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course examines the major, cutting-edge questions for criminology today. These include penal politics, policing, justice and the media, restorative justice, youth crime, and state crime. It introduces students to the contemporary key thinkers and contributors in the field in Australia and overseas. Attention is given to the relationship between research, policy, and politics in linking knowledge to social and systemic change.
title: Justice and Crime
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course provides a foundation for professional communicators in the public sphere, including considerations of communication and professional identity in contemporary environments. This includes awareness of social and political change, diversity, environmental change and ethics and legal issues. This course introduces essential research and writing skills required for a range of media and communication roles and provides a foundation for considering which communication professions students wish to pursue.
title: Empowering the Professional Communicator
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Health, aged and social care system reforms and restructuring require managers to possess skills and competencies in successfully leading change. This course invites students to critically evaluate the ways in which health service management adapts to the competitive and changing healthcare environment and to explore various approaches to effective and efficient healthcare management. During the course, participants will extend their change management acumen with methodologies for planning and evaluation, influencing and negotiation. The management skills in a changing environment that you will develop by completing this course will complement other essential management skills such as leadership, quality management, communication and strategic planning.
title: Change Management in Dynamic Healthcare Systems
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course explores the key issues of development studies in theory and practice. The evolution of poverty reduction strategies will be examined by looking at thematic areas including governance, conflict, trade, energy, environment, gender, health, and public-private partnerships. Assessment will underpin professional reflective reports.
title: Key Issues in Global Development
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: In this course we will consider the causes, conflicts and consequences of colonial invasion and imperial ideologies on Indigenous peoples. Through inquiry based learning, participants consider who is Indigenous? Who has the right to define Indigeneity? And build a knowledge base to reflect on the local expressions of common issues in Indigenous histories across the globe. Using the United Nations Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples as our guide, we will explore a series of historical case studies to consider the colonial/imperial roots of issues disproportionately impacting Indigenous Peoples today, as well as celebrating the unique contributions Indigenous Peoples can make to resolving global scale challenges for all societies.
title: Indigenous Peoples: Global Perspectives
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course investigates the leading edge technologies that define the future of home automation and IoT. It involves the intelligence, control, and automation of lighting, heating, ventilation, air conditioning (HVAC), and security, as well as smart, stationary and autonomous home appliances. Previously known as 3707ICT Home Automation and Robitics and is incompatible with 3707ICT Automation and loT.
title: Automation and loT
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course facilitates the systematic development of a dissertation topic, and the research, analysis and writing of a dissertation of approximately 20,000 words under the guidance of supervisors.
title: Business Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: 6000NRS_P1 is the first of five 10 Credit Point courses that make up the research component of the Bachelor of Nursing and Bachelor of Midwifery Honours programs. The Dissertation courses (6000NRS_P1-P5) require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, data analysis and carrying out the research project. At the completion of the five Dissertation courses students will submit for examination a thesis (with an upper limit of 25,000 words) describing the research project and will deliver a seminar describing their findings.
title: Dissertation 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Property 2 complements the content of Property 1, and continues to explore the concepts introduced there through a detailed consideration of key land law doctrines. The Course focuses on land law and features the regulation of land through the introduction and operation of the Torrens System, and covers doctrinal areas including boundaries to land, co-ownership, covenants, easements, equitable interests, mortgages and general law leasing. Students in Property 2 will develop and refine their skills in hypothetical problem-solving in the context of property disputes involving land. Students must be enrolled in a Law program. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Property 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Evidence Law aims to introduce students to the law governing proof in civil and criminal litigation. The subject matter of the course includes study of doctrinal rules in relation to the differentiated roles of judge and jury, evidential and persuasive burdens of proof, the standards of proof, admissibility of evidence, testimony, privilege and judicial warnings. There will also be consideration of the principles underlying particular doctrinal rules. Emphasis will be on the rules of evidence pursuant to provisions of the Evidence Act 1977 (Qld) and common law. Materials from other jurisdictions may be considered to elucidate principles relevant to practice in Queensland and elsewhere. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Evidence
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course introduces human services within its broader historical, socio-cultural, political and economic contexts. It examines the Australian post - welfare state and the contested ideas, philosophies, theories, institutional forms and professional identities associated with it. The course provides a set of frameworks and concepts for analysing historical, present and future changes in the structures and content of human service provision. The aim is to familiarise students with the language, key concepts, tensions and trajectories of the diverse human services field, whilst assisting students to use such concepts in analysis of specific areas of human service pertinent to their professional interests.
title: Human Services Structures
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course continues to develop the essential skills learners need to understand basic Japanese sentences, communicate in routine tasks, and describe personal and familiar topics. It helps learners gradually progress towards basic social proficiency, equivalent to B1 Threshold level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). In addition to the 4 contact hours of 2042LHS, this course includes a dedicated 2-hour class that utilises authentic and semi-authentic oral and written materials further to enhance listening and reading comprehension and written expression. As a 20C course, 2045LHS comprises approximately 300 hours of work in total. INCOMPATIBLE: 2042LHS Japanese 2B. Students should follow the enrolment pattern for their major. PREREQUISITE: 2040LHS Japanese 2A OR 2043LHS Japanese 2A (Enhanced) OR Equivalent level of proficiency certified by means of a placement test administered by our Japanese teaching staff.
title: Japanese 2B Enhanced
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course develops an integrated approach to understanding and analysis of natural catchments. Principles and methods in hydrology and hydraulics will be used to analyse the dynamics of water and water-borne substances. We will address their sources, transport, mixing and dispersion in the environment as well as the implications to catchment management. Computer modelling software popular in the water engineering industry will be extensively used in this course.
title: Hydrologic and Hydraulic Modelling
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course facilitates an introductory understanding of, and transition into, teaching as a profession. It entails coursework and 10 days of Professional Experience Placement in a school setting to bring to life the knowledge, themes and emergent understandings related to contemporary teaching and learning. To be eligible to attend the Professional Experience Placement component of this course, you must meet the mandatory requirements (please refer to the Other Requisites section for further details). Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of the Professional Experience Placement.
title: Teaching as a Profession
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In just two decades, digital media and the world wide web have fundamentally altered the operations of businesses around the globe. This course gives you a strategic-level working knowledge of digital and social media marketing. The course further introduces best practices in acquiring, communicating with consumers, and retaining customers on the internet. The course examines digital technologies and their impact on, and implications for, marketing strategy, consumer behaviour, market segmentation, advertising and media planning.
title: Digital and Social Media Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: 2658QCA Communication Strategies in Interior Design focuses on developing students' ability to professionally communicate interior design projects at different stages of the design process. The course introduces students to the types of communication, drawings, presentations, and documentation used at each stage, with a focus on understanding what information needs to be communicated, to whom, and when. Students also develop professional communication skills through concept presentations, reports, and industry-related communication practices. Guest presentations from practising designers provide insight into contemporary communication strategies and the coordination processes that support successful project delivery.
title: Communication Strategies in Interior Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course examines the main issues in Australian health policy from an economic perspective and explains the relevance of economic thinking to decision making in health care. The content and issues discussed will consider health care delivery systems within the context of scarce resources competing for a multitude of health needs. The course will also explore health care delivery within a framework of effectiveness, efficiency and equity.
title: Health Economics for Promoting Value-based Care
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course covers the basic concepts, principles and techniques of microbiology. It looks at the domains of Archaea, Bacteria and Eukarya, viruses, microbial diseases, and environmental and applied microbiology including areas such as microbial ecology and microbial biotechnology. Prerequisite 1014NSC Fundamentals of Biochemistry waived for students enrolled in Program 1280
title: General Microbiology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course defines normal function and mechanisms of dysfunction of the major organ systems of interest to the clinical physiologist. The course will be taught by a combination of lectures, case presentations, and tutorials.
title: Pathophysiology of Major Organ Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is the study of solutions for problems that are difficult or impractical to solve with traditional methods. The solutions rely on a broad set of general and specialized search strategies, machine learning and knowledge representation and reasoning schemes. The study of Artificial Intelligence prepares the students to determine when an AI approach is appropriate for a given problem, identify the appropriate representation and reasoning mechanism, and implement and evaluate it. This course will provide an introduction to search strategies and machine learning.
title: Intelligent Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course introduces students to the concept of environmental sustainability and how it can be used to solve real world problems. It explores the relationships between the natural, rural, industrial, and urban environments, and includes the study of the impact humans have upon nature. The course also considers the way environmental sustainability can be used to address environmental, economic, and social issues in an integrated way. Assessment consists of an online training log, weekly online tests and a short recorded presentation.
title: Introduction to Environmental Sustainability
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course will be undertaken in the final trimester for full time students and in the final year for part time students, who will produce a dissertation to apply an advanced body of knowledge. It is between 15,000 and 25,000 words in length depending on the research topic and methodology. Students work with an academic supervisor who maintains regular contact and provides support and direction in the design and execution of the dissertation.
title: Aviation Management Research Paper
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This 50 Credit Point course provides the individually supervised context in which a student may complete written and (where appropriate) practical work for a dissertation/project at one-year Honours level in the humanities, languages and social sciences. Assessment is by Dissertation (100% weighting, between 15,000- 18,000 words) or by Creative or Professional product (60% weighting) with a minor dissertation/exegesis (40% weighting, between 5,500 and 7,500 words).
title: Dissertation/Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course covers the principles and rules of building measurement using the Australian Standard Method of Measurement of Building Works, and applies them to the measurement of detailed construction works examples. Alternative approaches to measurement for detailed builder's quantities and estimates are demonstrated.
title: Construction Measurement
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Business operations have been facing several ethical and sustainable issues, impacting people and the planet around the world. As a manager, it is essential that you have a grounding in the key economic, social and environmental impacts of business and its implications for management practice and decision making. As a part of this course, you will explore ethical and sustainable business, by referring to the concepts and theories of business ethics and sustainability. You will be able to identify, analyse and resolve ethical, social and environmental issues impacting various stakeholders, such as employees, shareholders, customers, government and civil societies.
title: Creating Ethical and Sustainable Business
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Community and public health nutritionists plan, implement and evaluate programs aimed at improving the nutritional health of communities and populations. Topics will include public health nutrition competencies, nutritional epidemiology, and monitoring of the food supply and nutritional status in communities and populations. The course prepares students to meet the competencies required to practice as a Community and Public Health Nutritionist.
title: Community and Public Health Nutrition
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course covers fundamental and advanced topics of communication systems which are essential for engineering students specialised in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Mechatronic Engineering, and Software Engineering. Topics include (i) analog communication systems, (ii) digital communication systems (baseband and bandpass), (iii) wireless communication systems, (iv) modern communication systems ( computer communication systems, cellular phone systems, global positioning systems) , and (v) applications of communication systems.
title: Communication Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: Develop a teaching philosophy that links theory to practice for your ongoing health education. The teaching and learning strategies that you will design will be underpinned by recognised theories of learning, teaching, evaluation and assessment of student learning. They will help you to employ evaluation methods and critical reflection to your health education practice so you can continually improve your health education practice. You will develop skills in curriculum development at the subject or course level, and craft improved teaching strategies to get the best out of your students.
title: Applied Learning and Teaching for Health Professionals
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The Bachelor of Counselling offers applied training in real world settings. This is the first of two professional placement courses for students enrolled in the Bachelor of Counselling in which you will work under supervision with real clients in designated counselling settings. In the professional placement courses, you will develop your clinical counselling skills and knowledge, put theory into practice, build industry knowledge and gain experience working in a team, including interdisciplinary teams where applicable. Prerequisites: Students must complete 150 credit points of the Bachelor of Counselling including: 1018PSY Counselling Skills & 3005PSY Counselling Theory & Professional Practice & 3002LFC OR 2023PSY & 3007HSV OR 2023PSY.
title: Counselling Practicum 1: Applying Theory
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: Today's world is filled with complex problems. The way we have handled the business world has led to crises that are almost insurmountable. Given the challenges of global supply chains and complex social issues, how can a supply chain manager learn to be successful in the modern logistics environment? What is needed to handle these massive challenges? This course offers a practical approach to managerial problem solving that walks students through different approaches to managing the difficult issues faced by the modern supply chain manager. It is expected that this approach will help those in management to come to grips with the social, political and managerial reality of current logistics. It will also provide students with the core skills needed to be adept at management problem solving. This course is only available to students enrolled in Programs 3328/3047 Graduate Certificate in Business Administration, 5670/5158/5159 Master of Business Administration OR 5737 Master of Professional Engineering Leadership. This course is normally offered every 8 teaching periods. Incompatible: 7712GBS Managerial Problem Solving and 7106IBA Managerial Problem Solving
title: Managerial Problem Solving
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course in Application Systems introduces students to the analysis, integration, and design of socio-technical systems focusing on the impact and user experience. It covers various topics, including the analysis of human activity systems, ontological modelling, and specifying the organisational and external context of computing systems, providing aspiring IT professionals with fundamental knowledge and skills necessary to analyse, design, and implement effective application systems while considering user experience and contextual factors in various ICT domains. This course was previously known as 1803ICT Information Systems Foundations and is incompatible with 1803ICT Information Systems Foundations.
title: Application Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The course revises and extends basic integral and differential calculus of one variable and introduces differential equations. It provides a foundation in the mathematical sciences needed for later studies both in an engineering and science context. This course is for Engineering or ICT students ONLY. Prior Assumed: Successful completion at senior level Mathematical Methods or equivalent study over four semesters of a high school subject that includes the study of calculus. For students who do not have this level of mathematics background, it is strongly recommended you first complete 1017SCG Foundation Mathematics. NOTE: this course is only offered on-campus, and students are expected to attend exams and weekly classes on campus, in person.
title: Engineering Mathematics 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: The focus of this course is on the role of the midwife as a guardian of normal childbirth and gaining a deeper understanding of midwifery strategies that support the woman and her family to achieve an optimal childbirth experience. This includes the promotion of childbirth as a normal physiological process and midwifery as a social model of care provided across the childbirth continuum.
title: Promoting Normal Birth
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Explore how to integrate theoretical approaches into real-life scenarios in responses to public health issues. You will apply qualitative, quantitative and mixed methods to field-based investigation of disease prevention, infection management, epidemiology, environmental health, health policy and other related challenges. The analytical and communication skills you will learn in this course will ensure you can effectively disseminate your findings to stakeholders and the wider community. You will also investigate how to translate theory into practice, developing practical approaches to field studies, methods of stakeholder communication and decision making when investigating health problems at the population, and community and medical levels. You will be engaged in the field processes that characterise community health work in response to priority issues within local and international contexts. These field skills are central to the practice of public health.
title: Applied Field Methods in Public Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course explores the experience of people who live with chronic conditions including the principles and practices of chronic condition nursing. This course requires students to integrate pathophysiology, pharmacology, and evidence-based healthcare into nursing practice. Students undertake 80 hours of clinical practice to develop nursing competence congruent with a second-year student level.
title: Chronic Condition Management
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Aviation Science is an introduction to scientific themes as applied in the world of aviation. The syllabus covers selected concepts from algebra and geometry, and from physics, with emphasis on forces and movement of bodies. The study is essential to understanding of aerodynamics and a variety of aviation-specific studies at a later stage
title: Aviation Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is one of four 10 Credit Point courses that make up the research component of a School of Allied Health, Sport & Social Work Graduate Diploma or Masters level research project. The combined 8002AHS courses require students to undertake a research project relevant to their area of specialisation under the guidance of a supervisor. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of appropriate research design, approval from relevant ethics committee/s, data collection, analysis and write-up of findings. At the completion of the four Dissertation courses students will submit a thesis for examination.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course is the second stage of the Dissertation. This course requires you to complete a dissertation under the supervision of an academic staff member. This will involve the identification of a research question, selection of an appropriate research design, analysis of data and completion of a research project and thesis for examination. The dissertation should embody currently accepted standards of method and reflect knowledge and understanding of contemporary literature in the field. Students are encouraged to publish their findings with their supervisor/s.
title: Dissertation Part 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course serves as an introduction to the field of sport development, providing students with insights into sport participation and development across various life stages. It explores the factors that influence involvement in sports and physical activity, while also offering practical experiences to expose students to a broad range of career opportunities within the sport industry.
title: Sport Development I
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This 40CP Dissertation is offered within the 5263 Master of Public Health (MPH) and the 5725 Master of Global Public Health (MGPH) programs. The 40CP dissertation is similar to an Honours dissertation in type and scope and gives students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest. The Dissertation involves the development of a research project, analysis of background literature, collection and analysis of data. The background literature, methodology. findings and conclusions are presented in a formal context both orally and in a scientific research thesis. The thesis is expected to be between 15,000 and 20,000 words in length, depending on disciplinary demands and problem requirements. Please note that Course Convenor approval is needed to be able to enrol in the Dissertation.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course educates students in modern onboard navigation systems and associated ground based technology. In addition, the course consolidates prior knowledge gained in the fields of Meteorology, Flight Planning and Performance, Basic Navigation and Aviation Regulation.
title: Navigational Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course is the second part of 2520NSC (Light Aircraft Operations, Performance and Planning Part I) in accordance with the CASA CPL Operations, Performance and Planning syllabus. Prerequisites: 2520NSC Aircraft Operations, Performance and Planning
title: Advanced Aircraft Operations, Performance and Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course provides an in-depth look at the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of cardiovascular disease, infections and diseases related to the immune system. The course adopts an integrated approach to learning, taking the student through the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of the disease, including a thorough understanding of the pharmacological basis of treatment and its relation to drug structure. Lectures and problem-based clinical workshops serve to equip students with theoretical knowledge, an evidence-based approach, and practical clinical skills for the promotion of and contribution to optimal use of medicines, delivery of health information and provision of health education in relation to the therapeutic areas covered in the course.
title: Integrated Pharmacotherapeutics I
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course provides an in-depth look at the pharmacist's role in the therapeutic management of diseases of the musculoskeletal system and endocrine diseases. The course will build on knowledge gained in second year and adopts an integrated approach to learning, taking the student through the epidemiology, risk factors, clinical presentation, pathophysiology, clinical course, and therapeutic management of the disease, including a thorough understanding of the pharmacological basis of treatment and its relation to drug structure. Lectures and problem-based clinical workshops serve to equip students with theoretical knowledge, an evidence-based approach, and practical clinical skills for the promotion of and contribution to the optimal use of medicines, delivery of health information and provision of health education in relation to the therapeutic areas covered in the course.
title: Integrated Pharmacotherapeutics III
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: In this course students undertake a research project related to exercise science or similar fields under supervisory arrangements approved by the course convenor. The course provides an opportunity for students to develop specialised research knowledge and skills on a particular topic. Restriction: The course cannot be undertaken without the agreement of a nominated supervisor.
title: Exercise Science Research Project
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of electronics from the systems and signals perspective. Hardware implementations, such as A/D and D/A converters, rectifiers, wave-shaping circuits, and amplifiers are developed by making use of operational amplifiers, diodes, resistors, and capacitors to emphasise the system-building concepts (feedback, frequency response, transfer characteristics, impedance matching, and analysis by equivalent circuits). Circuit simulation (using SPICE) is used concurrently with real circuits and measurements to establish links between theory and practice.
title: Introduction to Electronics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course includes career development learning, including self assessments of skills, setting goals and negotiating learning plans for placement-based work integrated learning. Students in the Bachelor of Public Health complete this Public Health professional practice course prior to and in preparation for commencing their public health placements (in 3209MED).The negotiated learning plans are linked to the learning in 3209MED when students undertake a practical internship in their field of public health. Students undertake duties, for example program planning, evaluation and policy development, under the supervision of an assigned industry supervisor/mentor and a university supervisor.
title: Public Health Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course is centred on providing you with experience in teaching within the early years of school (Prep to Year 3). It is framed around the Australian Curriculum English and consists of 15 days of classroom experience. It includes observation and monitoring of children, program planning and decision-making, and teaching and reflecting on practice with an emphasis on the teaching of language, literature and literacies and using the professional standards for teachers (AITSL). Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of the Professional Experience Placement.
title: English in the Early Years of School
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course introduces students to the specialty practice area of paediatric nursing. This courses aims to provide an awareness and understanding of acute and chronic paediatric health care issues, family centred care and cultural values in a diversity of settings. Pre-requisite: Students must hold a current and unrestricted license as a registered nurse or for another clinical role (other roles to be approved by the Program Director)
title: Paediatric Nursing Care
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: Students are required to complete 500 hours (4 days per week for approximately 18 weeks) of practice based learning and engage in professional supervision with a social work qualified field supervisor. The course will focus on facilitating students' development of the skills, knowledge, attitudes and analyses necessary to enter the field as a social work practitioner. Learning tasks assessed on a pass/fail basis.
title: Social Work Field Placement 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Understanding of autism is an evolving field. From changes in diagnostic classification and reported prevalence rates to the demonstrable increase in research on how autism characteristics impact on a person and their community, the abundance of new knowledge about the condition has heightened the need for professionals to be aware of, and educated about, its ever-changing face. This course will use historical and current contexts to help you understand the behavioural and social characteristics of autism, examine changing perspectives across time and explore how the characteristics of autism may present in an individual. You will explore the interrelationship between family, cultural influences and autism, and learn to critique disability models - and your own conceptions of autism - based on a range of perspectives encountered through the course's lessons. Learning through a mix of virtual classrooms, video presentations and traditional readings, you will complete the course with an up-to-date knowledge of autism and its characteristics which will assist you to succeed in the workplace.
title: Understanding Autism
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course focuses upon firstly understanding and then supporting behaviours that others may find challenging. Although this course is focused on behaviour, it is not an ABA based course. Through this course you will develop a stronger understanding of how context can impact behaviour. First, the need to show a behaviour is considered in relation to the characteristics of a person's profile (i.e., their communication skills, sensory profile). This leads us towards understanding how behaviour can be viewed as a form of communication. We will also then move on to explore how the physical environment can impact the need to show a behaviour. Students will learn evidence- informed methods of determining the function(s) of behaviour and how to use this to write a behaviour plan to address environmental issues, promote social emotional learning, and support behaviours that are viewed as challenging using proactive and reactive strategies.
title: Understanding Behaviours
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: The cornerstone of understanding how to effectively work, manage, and lead in health services is to fundamentally understand how healthcare systems are structured and operate. The course will equip students with knowledge on the evolution, rationale, approach, and structures found in health systems. The course focuses on the Australian healthcare system, but also provides opportunities to examine international systems to provide information, comparison, and contrast. The course content is transferable to a range of different healthcare settings and enhances decision-making skills. Healthcare systems are examined in a range of delivery and work settings including public, private, and acute and community health. Numerous activities are drawn from real experiences of managers and are used to integrate theory and practice within the course. This course is incompatible with 7233MED Global Health Systems.
title: Health System Design and Challenges
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation and presentation of the completed Master of Medical Research thesis, including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussions and conclusions. The thesis would normally be expected to be approximately 40,000 words. Enrolment depends on availability of research topic and supervisors.6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor. Prerequisite: 6001HLS Dissertation preparation, research proposal and ethical application (needs to be completed during 6001HLS course) and availability of a supervisor.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The aim of this course is to define health within a biopsychosocial framework and present the current issues in the area, providing students with an introduction to key areas of Health Psychology. The course will situate Health Psychology as a specialisation within psychology and will develop students' understanding of the biopsychosocial factors involved in health promotion and maintenance, illness prevention and treatment, and improving healthcare systems and health policy. The course will have a focus on Health Psychology in an Australian context and will develop students' understanding of the key theoretical, research, and methodological approaches applied to the discipline of Health Psychology.
title: Health Psychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: In today's highly competitive world, all employees working in Tourism and Hospitality must be aware of the fundamental role of the hospitality experience. This course introduces students to the philosophy of hospitality, the creation of superb guest experiences, and a dynamic external marketing environment to design and deliver experiences that are responsive to guest needs.
title: The Hospitality Experience
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: The dynamic, people-focused nature of the tourism and hospitality industries demands managers call on specialised skills to be effective. Contemporary leadership and management practices and styles all apply, but they must be tailored to suit a diverse workforce. It's critical to understand the conceptual elements of Human Resource Management (HRM), as underpinned by effective and ethical leadership of tourism and hospitality workforces. In this course, you will explore all of those topics and emerge with an understanding of the relationship between HRM systems and the broader strategic planning functions, so you can help get the best out of your team as they strive to achieve business objectives. Your ability to generate strategies to effectively recruit, develop, and appraise employees within the sector will be strengthened, giving you the all-round HRM skills to assemble, manage, and lead a high-performing team.
title: Managing the Tourism and Hospitality Workforce
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Students enrolled in the Honours program will undertake an Honours Dissertation relevant to their study of urban and environmental planning under the guidance of one or more supervisors appointed by the Honours Convenor. The topic and nature of the Dissertation will be determined through consultation and mutual agreement of the student and supervisor and must be approved by the Honours Convenor. Students in 1658 and 1660 will be required to align the topic of their Honours Research Project to that of their major if they have chosen a major. The Dissertation will involve original research but this can include the collection and analysis of primary data, the analysis of secondary data, or the development of new theoretical or conceptual models. Assessment will comprise a written report of the work, prepared in the form of a thesis and submitted for independent examination by at least two assessors. Students will also be required to make two presentations: one of their research proposals and one describing their work and provisional conclusions. The quality of these presentations will contribute to the overall assessment of the Project. Pre-requisite: Students must have passed 4029ENV Project Proposal in Honours and must have completed 200 credit points or have the permission of the course convenor before enrolling in this course.
title: Honours Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course encourages students to develop an understanding of our current definitions and interpretations of suicide and suicidal behaviour. Students will gain insight into some basic epidemiological and sociological research in the field of suicide. Prerequisites: NIL Co-requisites: NIL Incompatible: NIL
title: Advances in Suicide Research 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course aims to integrate and consolidate your understanding of speech pathology professional standards relating to employment, ethical issues, lifelong learning, and models of practice. The course emphasises preparing students for the workplace through participation in an intensive program of seminars and masterclasses.
title: Transition to Professional Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: The aim of the course is to explain the way people behave and make decisions in a business environment and the role that information has in the context of decision-making. It will also tackle some of the critical questions around the use of information for business decision making: how to assess the validity/reliability and relevance of the information we receive, how to use it effectively, how to simplify information, make it relevant, and present it to different audiences.
title: Business Decision-Making
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: 'What's the best way to learn a language?', 'How can I remember all the new words and grammar rules?', 'Will I be able to sound like a native speaker by the time I graduate?', 'How many hours a week do I need to study?' 'How can I lower anxiety and increase motivation?', 'Can I do well with languages even though I never studied one before?' These are some of the questions that worry many students starting out on their language learning journey. 1012LHS will answer these questions and give you the skills and strategies to learn more effectively in the years ahead. ASSUMED BACKGROUND: Being a first-year course, no previous knowledge is expected. However, in order to enrol in this course students have to be currently studying a foreign/second language.
title: How to Learn Languages
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is an introductory course focused on what is forensic science. It introduces the various fields of forensic science and covers the principles of forensic science and how science is used in a court of law.
title: Introduction to Forensic Science
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course focuses on curriculum and pedagogy for effective learning and teaching of food technology and hospitality practices in junior secondary school (Years 7-10). Students will gain an understanding of key curriculum documents that inform food technology and hospitality practices in junior secondary schooling and in the broader field of Design and Technology education. Students will be supported to confidently design unit plans and lessons and develop assessment strategies in food technology and hospitality practices for junior secondary students.
title: Food Technology and Hospitality Practices Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course examines the way the law regulates workplace relationships and conditions of employment in Australia. The course content revolves around the fixing of employment conditions, rights and obligations through the federal regime via the Fair Work Act 2009 (Cth). The interaction between the common law contract of employment and statute will be explored, as well as the role of other legal instruments such as awards, enterprise agreements and National Employment Standards.
title: Workplace Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course consolidates and extends your understanding of speech pathology practice of communication and swallowing changes with a lifespan focus. Through inquiry-based learning, the course will support your development of comprehensive understanding of assessing, planning and implementing suitable management plans for individuals and communities with a focus on more complex clinical situations and on culture and language diversity. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (ICF) continues to provide a framework for analysis and understanding of clinical situations, with an evidence-based practice (EBP) approach underpinning your knowledge about speech pathology management.
title: Communication and Swallowing Disorders 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: In this interdisciplinary course students will explore the realities of aging and dying through a range of perspectives drawn from literature, philosophy and film. Topics of discussion include: Western perceptions of aging and dying; the medicalization of illness and the body; patient autonomy; the challenges and incapacities of aging; facing end of life. INCOMPATIBLE: 2022LHS (Re)Imagining Aging and Dying 1
title: (Re)Imagining Aging and Dying 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Gender and Security provides an introduction to key debates on gender and security in International Relations. The course has two parts. In the first part, we examine the relationship between gender and security with particular focus on gender and international security, feminist International Relations, and the methods available to analyse gender experiences in natural disasters, conflict, and post-conflict situations. In the second part of the course, we examine the relationship between gender and (in)security with particular focus on gender roles during war, sexual violence in armed conflict, peacekeeping, post-conflict reconstruction, and health security among other topics. The course material and assessments are designed so that students can have informed discussions to problem solve real solutions each week and design their own research project.
title: Gender and Security
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This course introduces key characteristics, concepts and trends in social entrepreneurship that are emerging locally, nationally and globally. Through applied practice and engagement, students will explore how innovation approaches can used for the common good and are the key success factors of delivering both commercial and societal outcomes.
title: Social Entrepreneurship
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course aims to introduce the basic knowledge and necessary skills for analysis of Big Data. Big Data Analytics is regarded as one of the important emerging technologies in different fields. The course is designed to stimulate interest in big data analytics in a popular scenario, i.e. social media. As such, some topics will be covered in depth while some will be covered only on an introductory level. Students will be shown how to collect data and extract and visualise information deeply hidden in huge volumes of social media data. This is important for many businesses to understand the perceptions or opinions of their services or products.
title: Big Data and Social Media
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course continues to develop the student's potential as an instrumentalist through individual tuition, and as a performer through ensemble workshops focusing on musicianship and stagecraft. Skills and knowledge established in previous performance courses are utilised to develop, test and implement quality live performances of original material. This course is delivered through one to one lessons and workshops.
title: Popular Music Project 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This subject introduces students to the law relating to financial products, financial markets, lending and other finance related activities of Australian banks and other financial institutions in the private sector. Topics covered include the Australian financial system; the relationship between lender and borrower; the statutory regulation of credit; loans to differing forms of business organisations; consumer credit - including Consumer Credit Code, EFT Code of Conduct, payment system and mechanisms, Managed Investment Schemes: real and personal property and the law and enforcement of securities and consequent remedies through the courts/tribunals as well as alternative dispute resolution methods.
title: Law of Finance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course aims to develop students' with knowledge of psychopathology and the skills to provide interventions for a range of high frequency common psychological disorders across the lifespan.
title: Lifespan Psychopathology and Therapy 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course will cover advanced statistical methods used to make sense of biological and environmental data. Topics covered will include data analysis and data visualisation methods in bioscience and environmental science.
title: Scientific Data Analysis
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: The aim of this Subject is to apply critical perspectives to popular music as a key form of cultural production, consumption and leisure in contemporary everyday life. In doing so the Subject will apply a range of sociological concepts and theories ranging from Marxism and cultural Marxism through to more recent post-structuralist approaches including postmodernism, reflexive modernity and risk. The Subject will also draw on approaches applied to the study of popular music in corresponding disciplines such as cultural studies and media studies.
title: Popular Music, Culture and Identity
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course introduces students to object oriented programming using modern C++ (C++11, C++14, C++17, C++20, C++23). C++ is a widely deployed language and is used in this course to demonstrate understanding of the concepts presented and for solving practical problems. Prerequisite: For students in 1534 BCompSci:1806ICT Programming Fundamentals or 1811ICT Programming Principles or 1013ICT Mathematics for Computer Science. For students in 1585 BEng(Hons)/BCompSci: 1305ENG Engineering Programming or 1013ICT Mathematics for Computer Science. Previously known as 2800ICT Software Development Processes and is therefore incompatible with 2800ICT Software Development Processes.
title: Object Oriented Programming
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course will provide an opportunity for students to consider contemporary issues facing the profession, health care and society. Students will be supported to understand these current issues from an occupational perspective and to consider the contribution occupational therapy might make.
title: Contemporary Issues in Occupational Therapy
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This dissertation course gives research students the opportunity to undertake a substantial piece of research work on a topic of interest and is a good preparation for the student to undertake higher research studies and other research endeavours. This course involves the execution of a research proposal, including experimentation and analysis of research results. It involves the preparation and presentation of a completed master degree thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, rationale, literature background, experimental design, methods, results, discussion and conclusions. Students may have developed research skills in the completion of pre-requisite research methodology courses with the view of undertaking a research topic in this course. Alternatively, a research project may be fully developed within the size and scope of the topic as part of this course. This course is a 40cp dissertation study.
title: MHSM Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will explore in detail the modern implementations of electronics in the control of aircraft. Sensors, navigational instruments, control systems, collision avoidance systems and glass cockpit integration, will all be studied. The course will also introduce students to the practical skills used in the construction of aircraft mechanical and electrical components. Students will participate in the construction of a full scale aircraft. The course is restricted to students enrolled in1542 Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) (Electronic and UAV major) and 1584 Bachelor of Engineering (Honours) / Bachelor of Aviation.
title: Avionics and Aircraft Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course aims to introduce students to aspects of professional practice as they relate to an Accredited Exercise Physiologist. Students will gain an understanding of professional, legal and ethical issues in practice, and learn to navigate the public and private health systems. Students will be taught report writing skills and formulating referrals. Additionally, this course will also highlight some of the current/emerging roles of an Exercise Physiologist; for example, in occupational health assessment, workplace injury management and return to work strategies, that are specific to the Australian setting and within the scope of practice of an ESSA-accredited Exercise Physiologist.
title: Professional Practice in Exercise Physiology I
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: Foundations of Law introduces key legal concepts and ways of understanding the law that are fundamental to the entire law program. Throughout the trimester, you will develop your knowledge of the key principles and institutions that collectively constitute Australia's legal system. We examine the basis on which these principles and institutions were adopted in Australia, and the implications for recognition of the rights and legal systems of First Nations People. We introduce legal ethics and examine the roles played by lawyers in Australian society. We provide you with frameworks for effectively accessing state and national laws and conducting other forms of legal research. Building on that knowledge, we develop and apply key legal skills, including reading, analysing and summarising the essential features of cases and legislation, and interpreting statutes, collectively helping you to respond effectively to legal problems. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS. Prerequisite: Students must be enrolled in a Juris Doctor Law program 5734.
title: Foundations of Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Global Law introduces students to the legal systems, traditions and procedures that have importance to Australia but which exist and operate beyond our national jurisdiction and boundaries. In this course you will learn about the basic features of the civil law system and tradition, which in different forms operate in countries like Germany, Brazil, France and Japan. Of particular relevance to Australia's foreign relations is the Chinese legal system and tradition, which has developed out of the Socialist and Confucianist cultural tradition. Knowing some basic things about these other markedly different legal systems will support your learning throughout the law degree and will enable you to become more innovative and entrepreneurial as global lawyers. This will also help you to understand the origins and modes of practice of both private and public international law, which are legal systems that aim to support how people, private entities and States cooperate at the international level. This course will also introduce you to private international law and the way in which people and corporations rely on it to communicate, trade and generally engage with each other globally while ensuring that their transactions are legally secure. Most importantly, this course will introduce you to the basic features of public international law, which is the legal system for ensuring that states like Australia can continue to cooperate and co-exist peacefully with other countries in the world. This course is designed to give you an introductory experience of the range of legal systems and traditions that as global lawyers you need to be aware of and be able to draw on and use as legal advisers or consultants. It also aims to enrich your engagement with other courses in the law degree, so that you can broaden your understanding of the legal and intellectual influences that bear upon Australia's legal system and the people as globally engaged lawyers.
title: Global Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: This course considers core aspects of the private law governing compensation for injuries and economic loss. The course focuses on common law remedies arising out of the law of negligence and non-intentional tort, as affected and modified by recent statutory tort reforms. Students are also introduced to other sources of injury compensation. These include the related torts of Breach of Statutory Duty, and statutory schemes such as Products Liability and Workers' Compensation. The course is taught and assessed in a critical vein, with students asked to consider the goals and efficacy of the common law and statutory compensation schemes, and the central role of policy in shaping legal responses to social problems. THIS COURSE IS ONLY OPEN TO LAW STUDENTS.
title: Torts 2
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: Pre-service teachers will explore key curriculum, pedagogy and assessment principles in order to effectively teach the QCAA Chemistry syllabus at a senior secondary level. Pertinent content from the syllabus will be covered in order to design and create differentiated and inclusive learning experiences that caters to all students. A range of pedagogical and assessment strategies will also be modelled and explored in order the create engaging and academically rigorous sequences of learning.
title: Chemistry Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will continue to develop their midwifery knowledge to ensure that they are prepared to work within the full scope of midwifery practice across the normal complex continuum of childbirth. The student is introduced to pathophysiology and associated complexities that may arise during pregnancy, labour, birth, postnatal and immediate newborn period. The focus is on the ability to identify when the health and well-being of the woman and her baby is compromised, recognise deviations from normal and implement and evaluate care provided.
title: Normal-Complex Continuum of Childbirth
academicOrgDescription: School of Nursing and Midwifery

description: The course places the learning and developmental needs of preservice teachers in primary and secondary education settings within the broader frame of lifelong learning which promotes self-directed learning across the lifespan, including the self-directed learning of preservice teachers as they move towards mastery of knowledge and skills. Focusing on the interrelated nature of development within school-aged students across four domains and an understanding of how teachers can support development and the role of the brain in learning, preservice teachers explore the implications for their teaching practices as students move from novice to expert. Topics include how the brain learns, the function of memory, and the implications for practice including adjustments as students move towards mastery. Incompatible: 1302EDN Understanding the Lifelong Learner
title: Understanding Lifelong Learner
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Arts Education is focused specifically on the teaching of Arts in the primary years of schooling. It is designed to provide you with a broad understanding of the five arts disciplines specified by the Australian National Arts Curriculum: Dance, Drama, Media Arts, Music and the Visual Arts. You will gain knowledge and understanding of the role the Arts play in the individual child's development. There will be a focus on the development of imagination, creativity and symbolic representation through practical exploration of each of the Art forms and the connections between them. Pedagogies specific to each Arts discipline, together with planning structures and classroom organisation strategies will be addressed.
title: Arts Education 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will be introduced to the skills required for effective learning and teaching of languages other than English in the senior secondary years of schooling. Emphasis will be placed upon understanding the relationship between the learner, school context, curriculum, pedagogy and assessment.
title: Languages Other Than English Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course aims to prepare students to teach Digital Solutions in the senior secondary years in alignment with the requirements of the Queensland Curriculum and Assessment Authority (QCAA). It assumes prior familiarity with foundational concepts in computer education, particularly programming and information systems, and builds these into pedagogical practice for senior school settings. Students examine how computer education teaching is shaped by the interplay of learners, school context, curriculum, pedagogy, assessment, and professional judgement. The course introduces specialised teaching approaches, resources, and tools for designing learning that develops students' capacity to teach Digital Solutions. It also addresses curriculum planning, sequencing, inclusive participation, assessment, feedback, and the effective use of digital tools to support meaningful learning in senior secondary classrooms.
title: Digital Solutions - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course prepares students to be successful drama educators within secondary schools. In particular it focuses on developing an understanding of the fields of study and core content areas relevant to drama learning in the senior phase, the skills required for effective curriculum planning at this level, and the ability to confidently engage learners using pedagogies appropriate to the needs of these more mature students. In addition, this course introduces students to the various statutory requirements relevant to the assessment of drama in the senior phase.
title: Drama Curriculum - Senior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is the second of two courses in which students plan and execute a substantial piece of research, which is reported in the form of a dissertation. The dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be approximately 30,000 words. The dissertation builds on previously studied courses that have developed the student's understanding of research foundations, design and methodologies.

academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies
