The dissertation will investigate a topic that is relevant to the student and would normally be expected to be approximately 60,000 - 80,000 words. The dissertation builds on previously studied research courses that have developed the student's understandings of research planning, research methodologies and research design.
title: Research Project - Part 6
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Rapid advances in technology in recent years have helped increase corporate productivity and enabled a global reach for companies, but such advances have also exposed them to criminal and fraudulent behaviour. This course takes an advanced approach to managing and identifying risks associated with financial crime activities via the use of entity wide risk management and governance framework. The role of internal controls, governance, monitoring and communication responsibilities are also covered in the course.
title: Financial Crime Risk Management and Governance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: The course is an intensive activity in the area of Opera Studies. The options available are for classical singers (operatic roles) and pianists (Repetiteur activities.) Vocal technique, musicality, language and ensemble work are combined, consolidated and refined through intensive rehearsals. New skills are integrated into the discipline of the theatre.
title: Opera Project C
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course describes the communication and work practice skills and knowledge required to work with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the various business industry contexts. It deals specifically with cross-cultural awareness, competencies and issues involving working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander individuals, organisations and communities. Graduates from this course will possess the knowledge required to gain a better understanding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander 'ways of thinking' by learning more about Indigenous society (knowledges, traditions, and culture), and the appropriate use of protocols when engaging with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, their businesses and the wider communities.
title: Indigenous Australians: Everybody's Business
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course will familiarise students with arts-based, contemporary indigenous research methodologies; and provide confidence to explore and situate their arts practice within current research dialogue. This course is restricted to Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art students ONLY.
title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: An introduction to Learning and Curriculum in the Learning Support teaching area.
title: Introduction to Learning and Curriculum
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: In this course students will be introduced to the skills required for effective learning and teaching of Economics and Business education in the junior secondary years of schooling. Emphasis will be placed upon understanding the relationship between the learner, school context, curriculum, pedagogy and assessment.
title: Business Education Curriculum - Junior Secondary
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is designed to cover all aspects of aerodynamics; aircraft general knowledge; flight rules and air law; and flight performance and planning in rotary wing operations. On completion of this course, aspiring helicopter pilot students will have good insights into helicopter operations and be able to proceed with helicopter flight training. Prerequisites: 2520NSC Aircraft Operations, Performance and Planning or 2523NSC Light Aircraft Systems or 2539NSC Introduction to Aviation Law.
title: Rotary Wing Operations
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course addresses the psychomotor component of education and the advanced planning and teaching skills associated with it. An emphasis on individualising instruction is maintained in the further analysis of motor development and motor learning. Assessment includes participation in workshops, a written project, a group presentation and an examination.
title: Advanced Teaching Strategies in HPE
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course invites students to work with industry and community groups to create real world public art outcomes. With a focus on large-scale wall paintings, students will develop public artworks that engage with histories of place. Public Art 1, 2 and 3 cover range of theoretical and practical skills integral to collaborative public art projects including concept, artwork and communications development. By encouraging students to link their individual studio practices with these industry-based projects, students will develop important skills for extending their practices beyond the studio setting.
title: Public Art 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The course is designed to introduce students to the fundamental principles of international trade law. The primary goal of the course is to acquaint and familiarise students with the main pillars in this arena of international law and their effect on domestic law and policy. The course covers the key agreements and principles of international trade law and the jurisdiction, policies and processes of the WTO. It also encompasses major critical analyses of international trade law together with an in-depth review of relevant GATT/WTO panel and appellate body decisions.
title: International Trade Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School

description: In this course, you will develop communication, physical examination, procedural, reflective practice, and contemplative practice skills. You will also participate in field studies activities, including community placements, to apply and further develop your communication, reflective, and contemplative practice skills in community settings. Clinical practice courses emphasise hands-on learning and supervised skill development, which cannot be fully achieved through independent study. Attendance is therefore mandatory for all scheduled sessions. Students must meet both of the following minimum attendance requirements: Attendance at a minimum of 80% of all scheduled course sessions; and Attendance at a minimum of 70% of sessions within each module. The number of scheduled sessions may vary across teaching sites. Attendance requirements will be adjusted proportionally where required. Permissible absences (up to 20% across the course and up to 30% within an individual module) apply only in exceptional circumstances, such as illness, emergencies, or other valid reasons. These absences must be reported promptly using the Student Absence Form (available in Course Essentials) and supported by appropriate documentation (e.g., a medical certificate). Where appropriate, the Module Lead may assist students with approved absences by offering alternative learning opportunities, subject to availability and class capacity. Such opportunities are provided to support skill development and do not contribute to attendance requirements. No alternative arrangements will be made for unapproved absences, and individual remediation sessions cannot be provided. Monitoring and recording attendance is the responsibility of the student. No warnings will be issued when a student approaches or exceeds the allowable absence threshold. Students who have concerns regarding their attendance are encouraged to contact the Course Convenor as early as possible. Learning and skill development within this course are cumulative and scaffolded, with knowledge, clinical skills, and professional behaviours progressively developed throughout the semester. As a result, absence from clinical and field-based learning activities may adversely affect a student's ability to achieve subsequent learning outcomes. Students who do not meet the minimum attendance requirements may be required to undertake additional assessment to demonstrate attainment of the course learning outcomes. The nature and format of any additional assessment will be determined by the Course Convenor and the Module Lead/s and may include written, oral, reflective, and/or practical assessment tasks. Such assessment may evaluate learning outcomes and competencies from across the course, rather than solely those associated with missed sessions. Failure to satisfactorily demonstrate achievement of the required learning outcomes may result in a failing grade for the course. Preparation and engagement are essential components of all
title: Introduction to Clinical Practice 1
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course represents stage one of the Doctor of Education degree. It engages candidates in planning and preparing a preliminary research proposal to underpin their studies in stage two of the degree. Candidates work with their supervisors to: identify an area of research for investigation, develop a preliminary research proposal, and prepare a review of the literature relevant to their chosen research question or issue. Assessment in this course will be based on the completion of these tasks.
title: Initial Research Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: This course is focused on both the technical and strategic aspects of impact measurement and reporting to design better businesses and contribute to larger impact goals. It draws together impact assessment, accounting, strategy and design, and examines the latest approaches to measuring impact across fields such as impact investment, achieving the Sustainable Development Goals and sustainable supply chains.
title: Demonstrating Impact for Good
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: The focus of this course is on the various current issues and challenges in the Asian region. The approach will be interdisciplinary thereby encouraging students to apply analysis that best suits the issue. The issues analysed and discussed may include business and economics issues, societal concerns, work practices, and many other issues, relevant to the Asian region as it develops, adapts, and evolves to changing global dynamics. The purpose of the course is to enhance students' understanding of the Asian region by analysing and discussing a wide variety of current issues. Knowledge of contemporary society-based matters in Asia contributes to your suite of Asian competencies valuable to future employability opportunities.
title: Asian Societies: Contemporary Issues and Challenges
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course will develop students' understanding of clinical psychology in relation to psychometric assessment and neuropsychology. Students will expand their skills in assessment and in applying neuropsychological concepts to clinical practice.
title: Advanced Assessment and Neuropsychology
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course includes placement activities, within the practice of Psychology, external to Griffith University. External placements are selected and designed to provide students with rich and varied learning opportunities and experiences in clinical psychology. As part of each external placement students will complete a minimum of 120-140 hours of client contact and 40 hours of clinical supervision. Prior to completing an external placement, students are required to have completed and received a 'Pass' for Internship Practicums, which provide intensive training and supervision within the Psychology Clinics at Griffith University. Incompatibilities: 8184PSY_P1, 8184PSY_P2, 8184PSY.
title: Practicum 4
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This is an individually negotiated, contract-based project undertaken by the student under supervision. It is intended to provide the opportunity for the student to develop a particular theme or activity related to their specialised interests. Examples of possible project areas include: a course of academic reading and research; a performance project; creative project development or administration; industry placement. The project is negotiated with and approved by the Convenor and the contract will specify the required outcomes which will include a detailed written report.
title: Honours Project Study B
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Gothic Afterlives traces the history of the Gothic genre from its origins in the ghoul-infested castles and spectralised landscapes of 18th century art and literature through to the secretive suburban blood-suckers of contemporary television drama. From its beginnings the Gothic has been a popular and controversial phenomenon that has drawn its energies from the darker regions of the imagination and the borderlands of taste. In the Gothic nothing is as it seems. The world of cheerful and comforting appearances, secure homes, grand cities, and the reassuring solidity, identity and sexuality of the body are all made vulnerable by the uncanny effects of the Gothic imagination. In this course we'll follow the development of the Gothic in selected texts, films and TV series.
title: Gothic Afterlives
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course provides students with the opportunity to create a body of artwork informed by the experience of being on Country and from their own Indigenous perspective and ways of knowing, being and doing. This course is restricted to Bachelor of Contemporary Australian Indigenous Art students and First Nations students only. Prerequisites: 1011QCA Origins or 1111QCA Origins
title: Back to Country
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: The Trustworthy AI course provides a concentrated exploration of the technical dimensions involved in uncovering the fundamental principles and methodologies for constructing reliable AI systems. Encompassing topics like safety and robustness, fairness and bias, transparency and explainability, privacy and data protection, as well as regulations and standards, this course equips you to navigate the delicate equilibrium between ground-breaking innovation and conscientious AI advancement. By engaging with real-world case studies and immersive hands-on exercises, you will develop the expertise required to craft AI systems that not only uphold privacy and diminish bias but also cultivate a bedrock of trust among users and stakeholders.
title: Trustworthy AI
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: The Cyber Security of Cyber Physical Systems is a course with a technical emphasis is to educate students on the unique security challenges and vulnerabilities associated with cyber physical systems (CPS), which are systems that integrate physical and computational components, such as Internet of Things (IoT) devices, industrial control systems (ICS), autonomous vehicles, and smart grids. The course aims to provide students with a deep understanding of the technical concepts, methods, and tools used to secure CPS and develop the skills necessary to design, implement, and evaluate effective security measures for these systems.
title: Cyber Security of Cyber Physical Systems
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: In this course, you will complete coursework and an external placement which constitutes the second placement in the Master of Professional Psychology. External placements are selected and designed to provide students with rich and varied learning opportunities and experiences in the practice of psychology. As part of this external placement students will complete a minimum of 178 hours of psychological practice and 24 hours of supervision.
title: Placement
academicOrgDescription: School of Applied Psychology

description: This course brings public relations and strategic communications to life through focusing on three key areas: politics, government, and corporate / not-for-profit sectors. Students will be presented with advanced information about these three areas, and the central role that strategic communications takes within them. Given this is an advanced strategic communications course, students are expected to possess the knowledge and skills necessary to know the basics of communication. This course will build on their already growing skillset in strategic communications, and get them to think critically - while also design - the 'why' and 'how' behind strategy. As such, most of this course's assessment is drawn from students' practical application of acquired knowledge and skills that are then applied to either a political, government, or business case study.
title: Communication Campaigns and Strategies
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Students need high level audio and video production skills for a range of communication professions. This course develops literacy in these styles of production and understandings on how they are used to best communicate with stakeholders and publics. academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This is an intensive course exploring human movement as an expressive and dramatic medium. The focus of the work is on body - alignment, freedom and co-ordination, physical fitness, and various skills for performance on stage. Through practical workshops, students will explore the foundations of coordinated breath and dynamic body engagement, to enhance tone production, articulation, and musical phrasing. Movement sessions will focus on postural awareness and whole body coordination, fostering ease and efficiency of movement. By the end of the course, students will understand how breath, sound, and movement interact, enabling them to perform with greater ease, confidence, and expressive range.Working with masks and developing improvisatory skills will also be included.
title: Movement and Stagecraft
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course introduces the musical, cognitive, social and practical processes of 'being' a music producer for recorded and live performance works. You will develop creative, ideative and collaborative skills in managing music production projects, and begin forming your own musical identity by working across the musical, technical, social and industry sides of production alongside collaborators in different roles. Through practical scenarios, including an online production collaboration with Edinburgh Napier University students and your own recorded or live projects, you will put these skills into practice.
title: Music Production Mindsets
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides an opportunity for students to participate in a range of professionally relevant directed ensembles and/or modules. Delivery in intensive mode, with repertoire and performance opportunities.
title: Music Making 3
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course prioritizes foundational practical abilities in the art and craft of music production; it is located at the intersection of composition/songwriting, performance, and audio applications during the manifestation of recorded and live performative works. Students are mentored through the entire practical process of music production for recorded and performative works that target aesthetic/commercial goals.
title: Studio and Stage Production
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: People and place are critical to the visitor experience. Memorable and iconic precincts enable destinations to differentiate from competitors and are vital for the economic development of a place. This course examines how precincts are planned and developed, as well as how people engage within these spaces.
title: Visitor Precincts and Infrastructure
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This 40CP course, comprising P1 and P2, is conducted primarily as individual placements, or small teams of students within an industrial environment and emphasizes academic and vocational aspects of modern industry practice. Students consolidate their technical knowledge by undertaking a work placement in a professional workplace while simultaneously managing their learning and course assessment. Students work in close liaison with their industry and university supervisor throughout the project and are expected to demonstrate a good understanding of their role, duties and responsibilities.
title: Work Integrated Learning
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: In this course students will explore the key knowledges and skills that underpin academic conventions, expectations, and requirements when researching and studying within the field of education.
title: Academic Research, Reading, and Writing in Education
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Education is one of the most significant and contentious areas of national and global policy-making, and policy decisions impact all areas of education. Frameworks for analysing and evaluating policy are introduced in this course to examine contemporary policy debates.
title: Critical Studies of Education Policies
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: A key component to the discipline of Information Technology (IT) is the understanding and the advocacy of the user in the development of IT applications and systems. IT graduates must develop a mind-set that recognizes the importance of users and organisational contexts and employ user-centred methodologies in the development, evaluation, and deployment of IT applications and systems. This requires graduates to develop knowledge of Human-Computer Interaction, including user and task analysis, human factors, ergonomics, application domains, user interface development tools and graphical user interface frameworks, accessibility standards, and cognitive psychology.
title: Design Thinking in IT
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course extends and advances student engagements with a range of projects in studio and live pre-production, recording and postproduction, including contexts for games, film and on-air broadcast. Emphasis is placed on students being able to demonstrate further growth in leadership and professionalised outcomes over and above those achieved in 5000QCM. This course Includes Work Integrated Learning (WIL) engagements as part of the core learning and teaching. Coverage includes advanced mic and recording techniques not done elsewhere (for studio and for live), post-production and mix workflows, and more advanced work with EQ, compression and reverb with awareness of film, TV, radio, online and other generalist post-graduation employment opportunities. This is all done with emphasis on live-capture of events in conjunction with "clients", where client-based contact is mentored and guided. Further, students undertaking this course have additional mentoring responsibilities toward other students (peers) undertaking 5000QCM with emphasis on management, leadership, mentoring and related professionalised capacities. The course leverages Con events as well as special events that may occur during a semester, and learning is done in-situ as well as in the classroom. The course is intended to provide invaluable experience in working outside the confines of a studio for event-based contexts. While Con events cover a range of genres, content covered in the course is equally pertinent for pop, electronic, experimental, film, games, and acoustic music contexts.
title: Professional Recording Project 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course provides an introduction to multi-camera studio production processes and crew roles, with an emphasis on production skills, teamwork and professional etiquette. Students develop a critical awareness of the history of television and its future in the context of a changing media environment. Through analysis, discussions, hands-on training in multi-camera technologies, and production exercises students will gain a deep understanding of crew roles, career pathways, and creative opportunities in live and 'as live' multi-camera studio production.
title: Foundations of Streaming Television
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Pharmaceutical analysis covers aspects of the theory and application of the most common analytical methods used in drug development, the pharmaceutical industry and the healthcare settings when quantifying or elucidating the structure of simple drug molecules. In this course, you will be introduced to method validation along with several analytical methods including ultraviolet and visible (UV/Vis) spectroscopy, infrared (IR) spectroscopy, mass spectrometry (MS), and various chromatography (HPLC) techniques.
title: Pharmaceutical Analysis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This is the final course in a four-course studio suite simulating the experience of working in a professional film and television production studio. Students will apply skills developed in associated majors and electives to a range of projects while examining the industry, social, cultural and ethical implications of screen production, as well as their emergent career paths. Students will work with industry-standard tools and technologies across all aspects of film and television production and receive guidance and feedback from experienced mentors. At the end of the studio suite, students will have developed high quality work of a professional standard, developed professional skills and knowledge of industry-standard production processes and procedures, and are adept at working collaboratively with requisite professional attitudes and practices.
title: Film and TV Studio 4: Specialist
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The world is filled with captivating stories waiting to be told. This course delves into the exciting realm of non-fiction filmmaking, equipping students with the knowledge and skills to capture real-world stories, craft compelling narratives, and create impactful films. Students will explore the history and concepts of non-fiction storytelling, how to conduct in-depth research, the ethical considerations of filming real people, and the art of conducting captivating interviews. Students will advance their practical and creative filmmaking skills through the collaborative development and production of non-fiction screen narratives based on the creative treatment of actuality.
title: Non-Fiction Craft and Style
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course immerses students in the art and crafts of production design for studio environments. Through case studies, practical exercises and critical reflection, students will delve into set design, lighting techniques and spatial composition. By completing this course, students will demonstrate professional skills and capabilities in creating immersive on-screen experiences through production design, ultimately exhibiting the abilities that will allow them to build a bridge from academic studies into a career in the global screen and television industry.
title: Production Design
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course examines the system of laws governing the employment relationship in Australia, the policy issues concerning the role of law in employment relations and introduces legal research methods, interpretation of case and statute law and legal writing.
title: Regulation of Employment Relationships
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Entrepreneurial leaders are ambidextrous decision makers that organise a group of people to achieve a common goal using proactive entrepreneurial behaviours. They are experts at navigating uncertainty, with a focus on challenging and improving business activities. In this course, using real world business challenges, we evaluate entrepreneurial leaders, their mindset and approaches. We also provide a range of industry relevant tools that entrepreneurial leaders often use in sustainable ethical business choices; with a focus on creating long-term value by taking into consideration how leadership decision making may create business impact in ecological, social, and economic environments.
title: Entrepreneurial Leadership
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This block introduces students to the principles and practices of modern networking and cloud computing. Learners gain hands-on experience with LAN design, switching technologies, and network security, while also exploring cloud architecture. The block equips students with the skills to build, secure, and manage both on-premise and cloud-based network infrastructures.

academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

title: Data Wrangling and Social Analytics
academicOrgDescription: School of Information and Communication Technology

description: This course provides an integrated introduction to the field of criminology and criminal justice, with a focus on developing foundational professional skills, critical perspectives on justice, and a nuanced understanding of crime and victimisation. Students will explore how crime is defined, measured, and theorised, while examining key justice issues such as inequality, victim rights, and serious violent offending. Through case studies, including homicide, and structured activities, students will build academic and professional capabilities, gain awareness of career pathways, and develop a sense of purpose and belonging within the criminology and justice community.

academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course considers the challenges involved in international negotiations including how to effectively prepare for such negotiations, select an appropriate strategy then implement that strategy. International negotiation involves particular complexities and uncertainties that need to be understood and planned for. Various planning and preparation processes will be considered during the course. Different approaches to negotiation will also be discussed with particular attention paid to the appropriate use of integrative and distributive strategies.

description: This course introduces students to writing and developing ideas for any screen medium. Through readings, case studies and writing exercises, students will acquire the skills and knowledge to transform ideas into captivating screen stories and crafting pathways to audiences. By completing this course, students gain a deep understanding of narrative structure, character development and writing dialogue for various screen media, from linear screenplays to narrative design for video games, while gaining the fundamental knowledge of global screen industry landscapes and the journey of getting a story on screen and to audiences.

academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course examines foundation marketing concepts and processes applied in business and market development activities. Section and use of secondary data analysis to gain insights for your marketing initiatives and justify the categorisation of products and services within identified target markets. We'll guide you as you expand your creative and investigative skills to marketing strategy, including the marketing mix, for application in real-world business practices. Upon completion, you will be able to demonstrate high awareness of the nature of the discipline with a clear professional self-concept of marketing.

academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Businesses operate within a dynamic landscape shaped by internal, external, and global influences. In this course, students are introduced to the fundamental concepts, techniques, and principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics, particularly within the Australian context. This knowledge equips students with practical decision-making tools, empowering them to become future business leaders capable of making informed and effective decisions amidst complexities.
