description: Leaders, managers and health professionals work daily in clinical care and service delivery. A major part of these roles and this work is ensuring high quality care outcomes for patients, clients, residents and other consumers. Using a balance of theory and practice, this course enables students to define visions for quality assurance and continuous improvement initiatives as well as being able to implement effective programs and projects in quality, risk and safety. The approach of this course is to provide knowledge and skills in the full spectrum of contemporary quality management responsibilities in a pragmatic way. You will develop your analytical skills and use critical and creative thinking for quality and risk intelligence strategies. In addition, you will gain capacity in understanding and using effective performance review tools, use of standards and accreditation programs, maximise the impact of clinical governance and your communication and leadership impact for quality care and operations. Through your engagement, this course provides opportunities to gain confidence and collaborative abilities in patient and consumer safety science and analytic skills to support contemporary responses in quality management at all levels in health organisations and systems.
title: Quality and Risk Management in Healthcare
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of computer programming in the context of real-time game engines. Students will explore the design and implementation of core gameplay mechanics, player controls, and the manipulation of in-engine graphics. Participants in this course will acquire the essential skills and knowledge required to actively participate as a gameplay programmer in a game production environment.
title: Introduction to Games Programming
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The rapid evolution of digital technologies has transformed marketing practice, enabling more engaging interactions between consumers and brands, and between consumers. From the web to the IOT, social media and mobile apps, and increasingly accessible AI, VR/AR and XR tools, these technologies offer exciting opportunities for marketers. Alongside these opportunities are challenges and risks, and responsible marketers need to be mindful of ethical marketing practice, and cognisant of consumer privacy and data protection issues. This course presents an applied introduction to these tools and concepts, how they sit alongside traditional marketing practice, and key metrics to consider when investing in digital marketing strategies and tactics.
title: Fundamentals of Digital Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This Course employs real world data from a range of sectors including finance, energy and health, to explore issues in gathering, analysing and reporting on data for decision making. You will gain skills in extracting useful information from a data set, and to utilise the information appropriately in business decision making, while exploring different roles and career options relating to various industry contexts. You will hone skills in basic statistical concepts and methods and begin to develop in-demand employment skills including creating and interpreting output from spreadsheets and statistical software packages and the application of programming languages to analyse financial data. This course is offered at Gold Coast in Even years and Nathan in Odd years.
title: Statistics for Business and Commerce
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: GFS Academies are intensive, immersive and industry-focused production experiences. Through hands-on projects, cross-disciplinary collaboration, deep analysis and critical reflection, students will experiment with cutting-edge technologies, unconventional production scenarios, or pioneering impact opportunities. By completing this course, students will gain professional skills in prototyping and experimentation, while gaining a deep understanding of future possibilities in screen content, technologies, markets and careers. Academies will be advertised across and beyond GFS and participation is based on successful application.
title: GFS Academy 1
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: Marketing success is highly dependent on the effectiveness of marketing communication between your organisation and the target customer, and these communications are achieved through various product, advertising and promotional strategies. This course will introduce you to the fascinating world of advertising and the strategic use of advertising to raise customer awareness and appreciation of your organisation's products and services.
title: Advertising and Integrated Marketing Communications
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Strategic marketing decision-making plays a vital role in the success or failure of both business and not-for-profit organisations. This course introduces important strategic marketing concepts and techniques for achieving success, and explains how to develop and manage them in a competitive fast-changing environment.
title: Marketing Strategy and Analytics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: Students learn to manage the employment value proposition developing an understanding of strategic staffing and designing effective performance management and rewards systems.
title: Managing Staffing and Performance
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Through close and creative engagement with the musical concepts that animate a vast range of musical contexts, this course functions as a lively way of studying music theory and developing aural skills. 'Music theory' is a catch-all term that encompasses many activities and perspectives: understanding musical structure and process; crafting a shared language to describe it; refining the skills needed to fluently hear, reproduce, invent and make critical determinations about the various musics we encounter. In this course, we will pursue all these activities in conjunction, through activities that span creative cross-collaboration and intensive investigation into style-specific materials.
title: Music Theory and Aural Studies 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course hones language and literacy for academic and professional communication, developing planning, formal writing, and synthesising skills. It develops written and digital communication skills, bolstering confidence to meet diverse audience needs and strengthening readiness for future success. Pre-requisites: 9100EPP University Preparation and 9200EPP Learning Strategies for University Success
title: Academic Communication
academicOrgDescription: EmpowerED

description: Introduction to Spatial and Interior Design offers students a foundational understanding of the principles, concepts, and practices essential to the fields of spatial and interior design. Through a blend of theoretical learning, hands-on exercises, and visual exploration, students will begin on a journey to explore the diverse world of designing spaces.
title: Introduction to Interior Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This subject offers undergraduate students an introduction to evidence-based policing, and it puts key principles into practice. It serves as an introduction to the terminology, ideas and scientific method associated with evidence-based policy and outlines the existing policing applications. Introductory weeks summarize the origin and goals of evidence-based policy. The subject eases students through a range of practical weekly modules and answer questions that people have about evidence-based practice. For example, what does good science look like? How do I find reliable research on police tactics and strategies? How do I evaluate research on the police? How do you design a good experiment in policing? The subject provides a practical guide for reading and using existing research in policing, but also a roadmap for developing one's own evaluation. The final weeks discuss concerns around evidence-based policing and explore what is in the future for this emerging field. The subject is designed to deliver essential content for policing students and professionals alike.
title: Evidence-Based Policing, Policy and Practice
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Griffith Bridging English caters for domestic mature-aged students who would like to undertake university study but lack the senior English prerequisite, or would like to consolidate and extend their senior English studies since leaving school. Successful completion of Griffith's seven-week Bridging English course meets the English subject requirements for Griffith undergraduate degrees. Griffith Bridging English is an intensive blended learning course comprising of online study in conjunction with a weekly tutorial. Students will study Senior English topics with an emphasis on academic English, and develop the language, literacy and communication skills required to succeed at Griffith University. The course incorporates a high degree of flexibility and responsiveness to cater to students with a wide range of educational backgrounds and experiences. International students are not eligible to enrol in Griffith Bridging English.
title: Griffith Bridging English
academicOrgDescription: Griffith English Language Institute

description: Sport Management Principles is designed to provide students with an understanding of the Australian sport industry, the unique features of sport, and how sport organisations operate in the public, non-profit and professional sectors. The course provides an understanding of the roles and responsibilities of sport managers, relationships between professional administrators and volunteers, and current issues facing the industry.
title: Sport Management Principles
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: In this course students will be made aware of the contemporary practical applications of fundamental Economics analytical frameworks and tools, so as to better grasp the importance and limitations of theory as they enmesh with real world circumstances. The teaching modules are separated two-fold; the first half will examine Microeconomics, encompassing demand and supply and the allocation of scarce resources, the theory of the firm, market structures (competition and monopoly), and their limitations, and regulatory responses to market failure. Macroeconomics covers the second half, and studies the economy as a whole. Relevant modules include national income accounting (GDP), inflation, the role of fiscal and monetary policies in boosting economic growth and economic stabilisation, as well as looking at exchange rates and international trade.
title: Economic Principles and Applications
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: This course will provide students with a detailed understanding of the nature, process, coordination and management of business logistics in achieving sustainable business outcomes. Current issues considered include: warehousing and packaging, transport and its management, supply network designing for material/service/information flows; performance measurement and the engagement with external logistics service providers, logistics in a carbon constrained environment; scheduling in transport and service industries, and redesigning material and service flows in supply chains/networks.
title: International Business Logistics
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: Students engage with community languages of Australia and Pacific, exploring heritage languages, immigrant languages and endangered languages. The course teaches practical skills in linguistic analysis, as well as awareness of issues and ethics when engaging with local communities and organisations.
title: Community Language and Fieldwork
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Students will develop a comprehensive understanding of the normal structure and function of the renal, gastrointestinal, endocrine, and reproductive systems. This course will also cover the pathophysiology, diagnosis, and management of common and clinically significant diseases affecting these systems. Through a combination of lectures, case studies, and practical sessions, students will integrate foundational scientific knowledge with clinical applications, preparing them for further medical study and practice. This course has a compulsory attendance requirement for "Team-Based Learning" (TBL) sessions. Students who miss a TBL session should formally inform the Course Convenor that they will be absent prior to the session that will be missed or as soon as possible following the session by submitting a "Student Absence Form" available in course essentials. Where relevant, a medical certificate or other supporting documentation should be provided. Attendance policy for this course: ----------------------------------------------------- Total Number of compulsory activities per course - 6. Permissible absences with a valid reason - 1 Threshold number of compulsory session attendance for course progression - 4. Explanation: You may have one valid, reported absence without needing to complete make-up work. Missing a second TBL session (even for valid or medical reasons) means you have exceeded the permissible absences, and the Course Convenor may require an alternative learning activity, such as a presentation or viva to demonstrate your understanding of the missed content. The Convenor will determine the task format, deadline, and whether it meets the required learning outcomes; if unsatisfactory, further remedial work may be required. If your total absences exceed the attendance threshold (more than 2) for course progression as specified in the Course Profile, you will be considered non-compliant with course attendance requirements, which will result in ineligibility to sit further examinations and failing the course.
title: Foundations of Medicine 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: The finite element method is regarded nowadays as the standard tool to solve engineering problems in the industrial and academic context. A significant contribution to the success of this method is based on the development of powerful computer hard and software during the last decades. Many user-friendly commercial packages are available which allow the numerical treatment of real engineering problems on personal computers or even notebooks. The method itself integrates the basic knowledge of engineering materials, mathematics, mechanics (statics and dynamics), computing and programming, and computer-aided design that students would acquire in the first two years of their undergraduate studies. The problem of determining forces and displacements, stresses and strains or the vibrational behaviour is fundamental to many applied areas of mechanical engineering including transportation (automotive, aviation, or naval structures) or plant engineering. This course presents continuum mechanical basics and computational algorithms that are used to analyse engineering components and structures under arbitrary loading conditions. Furthermore, students will gain skills in the use of a state-of-the-art finite element analysis package to further deepen their knowledge in the areas of stress/strain analysis and dynamical behaviour. However, only who thoroughly understands the finite element theory, concepts and involved algorithms will be able to obtain reliable and realistic results from this powerful method. The ability to critically analyse and interpret numerically obtained results is a prerequisite for the responsible application of this method in any engineering field. Prerequisite: 1017ENG Engineering Materials AND 2101ENG Mechanics of Materials I Incompatible: 6522ENG Computational Statics and Dynamics
title: Computational Statics and Dynamics
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course offers students the transformational opportunity to join an international study tour. Immerse yourself in diverse cultures, societies, and perspectives across the globe, fostering a deep understanding of interconnectedness and global citizenship. Through experiential learning, students will encounter international industry, communities and peers, cultivating the skills and mindset to become a responsible global citizen empowered to enact positive change in an increasingly interconnected world.
title: Study Tour: First Encounters
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course offers students a second opportunity to embark on an international study tour. Engage with diverse industries, cultures, and perspectives across the globe, and foster a deeper understanding of global careers. Through experiential learning, students will engage with international industry, communities and peers, refining the skills and mindset of a global citizen who seeks international career opportunities and leads positive change in an increasingly interconnected global community.
title: Study Tour: Global Citizen
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This subject introduces the emerging research field of neurocriminology, which integrates the disciplines of neuroscience, biology, psychology and criminology to understand criminal behaviour. Students will learn how principles and methods drawn from neuroscience (e.g., neuroimaging techniques, neuropsychological assessment) can be applied to study the neurobiological foundations of crime. Contemporary and cutting-edge findings from neurocriminology research will provide insight into how criminal behaviour can be influenced by brain structures and functioning, biochemical abnormalities, genetics and psychophysiology. The course will review the application of neurocriminology methods and findings at various levels of the criminal justice process (e.g., prevention, investigation, assessment, prosecution, intervention), including the limitations of these applications.
title: Neurocriminology
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions. Prerequisites: 7010HLS Dissertation Preparation
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course involves the execution of the research proposal, including experimentation, and analysis of research results, under the guidance of two or more supervisors. It also involves the preparation of the completed Masters Thesis including research aims, hypotheses, significance, literature review, experimental design, methods, results and conclusions.
title: Research Thesis
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course examines the various theories used to describe and interpret the archaeological record through focusing on some of the biggest debates in archaeology over the past 100 years. Specific topics covered: Initial peopling of Australia; Neanderthals: Behavioural complexity, symbolism, and 'speciesism'; Origin of dog domestication; The Dark Emu debate; Megafauna extinction; Homo floresiensis - the Flores "Hobbit"; The first "true" cave art; Handaxes and intentionality; The first pigs; the Movius Line.
title: Great Debates in Archaeology
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: Dental Hygiene Practice 3 is designed to provide in-depth scientific knowledge that underpins the role of the Dental Hygienist. Students are guided through the clinical environment as a member of the Oral Health Care Team and develop in-depth knowledge of the pathogenesis and best practice principles of management of gingival and periodontal diseases, while applying principles of equity, diversity and sustainability. Prerequisite: must be enrolled in Bachelor of Dental Hygiene, must successfully complete all Year 1 courses before enrolling in 2036DOH
title: Dental Hygiene Practice 3
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: Clinical Dental Sciences 10 develops a critical understanding of the concepts, principles and theories in Oral Surgery; Paedodontics; Orthodontics; and Oral Medicine.
title: Clinical Dental Sciences 10
academicOrgDescription: School of Medicine and Dentistry

description: This course provides an introduction to the distinctive conventions and practices of academic writing for assessment in university courses. It focuses on the study of and practice with rhetorically-based concepts in English language such as genre, purpose, argumentation, and audience, and the strategies successful academic writers use to incorporate information and viewpoints from existing sources. This will enable you to analyse and meet expectations for writing and learning within your specific disciplines.
title: Foundations of Academic Writing
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This unit provides you with a practical and theoretical understanding of health and safety in Australian workplaces. The unit examines the legal obligations in the workplace and risk management. You will have an opportunity to transfer theoretical knowledge to practice by undertaking analysis of a workplace, a practical exercise which will also require you to consider the theoretical aspects of the Workplace Health and Safety problems that you discover.
title: Work Health and Safety
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: This course exposes students to the fundamentals of leadership design and social design and provides a framework of practices related to design leadership in industry, governmental and community contexts. The students will test these ideas through scenarios involving design leadership implementation in various professional settings and the opportunity to employ social design theory and methods.
title: Leadership and Social Design
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: In this introductory course students will develop foundational skills and knowledge in the concepts of movement and timing in character animation. Through analysis and practical exercises, students explore the fundamentals of body mechanics, while animating characters within a digital context.
title: Foundations of Character Animation
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course applies the principles of marketing to oneself. As such, broad topic areas include the self-marketing mix, self-marketing research, self-marketing tactics and implementation and self-marketing evaluation. In doing so, students learn how to develop, manage and sustain positive self-images/brand that are well-received in the "real world", both on a professional and personal basis.
title: Self-Marketing
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This course describes the communication and work practice skills and knowledge required to work with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people in the various business industry contexts. It deals specifically with cross-cultural awareness, competencies and issues involving working with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander individuals, organisations and communities. Graduates from this course will possess the knowledge required to gain a better understanding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander 'ways of thinking' by learning more about Indigenous society (knowledges, traditions, and culture), and the appropriate use of protocols when engaging with Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, their businesses and the wider communities.
title: Indigenous Australians: Everybody's Business
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This course provides an introduction to the politics of international organisations and international law from the perspective of the International Relations (IR) discipline, with a specific focus on peace and conflict. More specifically, it aims to introduce students to i) the main IR approaches to studying international organisations and law and the key debates surrounding them ii) some of the most influential international organisations and legal frameworks and how they operate and iii) central issues pertaining to international law, norms and organisations in the areas of peacekeeping, conflict prevention and human rights.
title: International Organisations, Peace and Conflict
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: Failure to keep up to date with employment law can lead to fines and other penalties. This course helps prepare you for a career in Employment Relations and Human Resource Management by building the skills necessary to navigate Australia's legal system. It begins with a review of the foundations of the legal system before examining the system of laws governing employment in contemporary Australia. Through this course, you will develop necessary problem solving skills to use in workplace settings. This course is not available to LAW students unless the student is also enrolled in a Double Degree Program majoring in Employment Relations and where it is undertaken as a compulsory course.
title: Introduction to ER and HR Law
academicOrgDescription: Department of Management

description: 'Foundations of Health Sciences' has been designed to provide students studying basic and clinical health sciences an initial understanding of the health system in Australia. This course allows students to explore the multitude of career pathways available to them with a particular emphasis on career readiness, and the skills, attributes, and competencies necessary for enhancing employment potential.
title: Foundations of Health Sciences
academicOrgDescription: School of Pharmacy and Medical Sciences

description: This course aims to train students in a broad range of core practical skills, which have wide applications in the biomolecular and biomedical sciences. Students will complete a variety of practical exercises in biochemistry and molecular biology by attending a 1 x 4 hour laboratory session per week during the trimester. This course provides the opportunity to work autonomously, to develop and apply time management skills and to gain knowledge on workplace health and safety procedures in teaching laboratories.
title: Biotechniques Laboratory
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course is the second in the advanced research pathway that enables students to design, conduct and report a research project, under the supervision of an academic member of staff. This course will culminate in students submitting a written Dissertation and providing a verbal presentation of their research and associated study findings.
title: Dissertation
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course equips students with knowledge and skills they need to work effectively with First Peoples, primarily Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander Peoples, on urban, environmental and planning issues. The accrediting body for this Program, the Planning Institute of Australia, expects Programs to include, as a knowledge area: "Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples' and Indigenous peoples' rights, interests and planning approaches". This course reflects the requirements of accreditation.
title: First Peoples and Planning
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: This course investigates the development and contexts of contemporary performance through an investigation of the historical roots of performance genres, styles and forms. The course explores the socio-cultural, political and philosophical influences that have impacted on contemporary theatre thinking and practice.
title: Contemporary Theatre and Its Origins
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course simulates the experience of working in a professional game development studio at a high level. In a specialist role, participants will work in collaborative development, emphasising leadership, advanced project management, and engagement with significant industry challenges. Students will receive mentorship from seasoned developers and have opportunities to network with industry leaders, preparing them for potential career paths in the gaming industry. In this course, students will gain experience in all aspects of game development, including the social, cultural, and ethical implications of producing games. Students will work with sophisticated tools and technologies and receive guidance and feedback from experienced game development mentors. Guest lectures and engagement with the games industry will provide students with a deeper understanding of game development and its potential career opportunities. At the end of this course, students will have to develop a polished, playable game, focusing on leadership and collaboration aspects of game development. Students will develop specialised knowledge and expertise in areas such as programming, game art, animation, or virtual production.
title: Game Studio 4: Specialist
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: The course is the second of four Masters (practical/research) project components. Each component combines to introduce students to the rigors of research and engage them in an advanced level of study within design innovation. This project will consist of a major research/practice project accompanied by a designed report. The expectation is that the research/practical project will be based within and extend the student's existing creative research/practice and incorporate high levels of design/strategic literacy.
title: Masters Design Project 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: This course explores the innovative techniques of real-time visual effects (VFX) and virtual set design, essential for virtual production professionals. In this course, students will learn advanced photogrammetry techniques to capture detailed real-world textures and geometries, integrating these assets into virtual sets that can be altered and interacted with in real-time. Students will learn how to create and manipulate dynamic VFX in real-time environments and explore the use of virtual backlots for immersive set designs.
title: Real-time VFX and Virtual Sets
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course focuses on concepts of programming within a collaborative game production environment. Through the practical application of programming design principles, students develop a comprehensive understanding of gameplay programming techniques and how to apply them in a professional game studio. Students will engage with and use technical terminology, theoretical concepts, and gameplay systems, acquiring the skills and knowledge needed to design and develop complex game programming solutions.
title: Intermediate Games Programming
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course fosters individual exploration and experimentation within cinematic art forms, guiding students towards professional growth post-graduation. Through hands-on projects and mentorship, students delve into areas of personal interest, pushing boundaries and honing their professional skills, creative voice, and personal aspirations. Emphasizing career development, the course equips students with the skills and mindset needed for success in the ever evolving and convergent landscape of cinematic art forms.
title: Experimental Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course equips students with essential communication skills for careers in industry and academia. Students learn to communicate complex ideas simply across a range of audiences. Topics include crafting pitches, developing grant applications, and communicating across diverse forms of media.
title: Communication for Research Careers
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This Work Integrated Learning (WIL) course aims to foster the development of ethical, reflective, collaborative, and creative practitioners. Students work as part of a collaborative studio team under the guidance of expert teaching staff, connecting with external industry partners on numerous public-facing design projects. Students will develop a working knowledge of professional design practices while creating a range of industry-connected design outcomes. IMPORTANT: refer to www.liveworm.com.au for more information and how to gain permission to enrol.
title: Liveworm 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: In this course, students will develop their high-level performance or creative practice skills. Students engage in a combination of individual practical sessions in performance or composition alongside artistic research workshops. Note: There is a sequential relationship in the Principal Study courses. Students develop their potential as artists through this progression.
title: Principal Study Development
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course guides Masters students through the different processes and skills associated with music research and designing and implementing a research project. These include refining the research topic, devising the methodology and study design, and structuring and writing the early chapters of the dissertation, including the introduction, literature review and study design. The course is designed to align with and support 7220QCM_P1 Dissertation Part 1.
title: Music Research Design 1
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: Contemporary Studio Practice draws on a range of fundamental principles and contemporary concerns informing critical creative practices. Lectures and tutorials will encourage you to discuss how social, cultural and historical context relates to arts practice. Content will include philosophical discourses; cultural history/s and understandings of site and place. Discussions draw upon the many narratives that underpin the understanding of creative practice today, including drawing from history and interrogating conventions. Classes are not specific to media but draw on exemplars from a broad range of practices. Students will use this course to initiate your understanding of the social, cultural and historical context in which you practice and to begin identifying artists that are relevant to your practice and your research.
title: Contemporary Studio Practice
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Studio Immersion is a visual arts practice based course. Students will be introduced to foundational contemporary visual arts practices and will create works and undertake research for presentation. Lectures and tutorials will be studio specific and students are required to engage with, and gain knowledge and foundational expertise of their chosen studio specificity.
title: Studio Immersion 4
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Electrical engineers require a sound understanding of the principles of electric power devices and systems in order to extend the usefulness of electrical technology and to ameliorate the problems of electrical energy. Sustainable electric power systems require that we utilise renewable resources for generating electricity and that we use the energy as efficiently as possible. To achieve these goals, it is important to gain a thorough knowledge of electrical machines and renewable generators. This course covers the fundamental and applied aspects of clean energy systems based on renewable energy resources. You will apply the theory of electromagnetism to electromechanical energy conversion devices and systems. In addition to design, you will learn how to estimate the dynamic parameters of electrical machines and understand the effect those parameters have on the performance of systems incorporating electrical machines. Incompatible: 3320ENG Electrical Machines and Renewable Generators
title: Electrical Machines and Renewable Generators
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: In this second of a four-course series on Techniques and Practice students will continue to deepen the work and explore further their potential as performers through sequences of practical classes developing more nuanced applications of the fundamental skills and acting techniques required for Acting, Text Work and Acting through Song.
title: Acting: Tech and Practice 2
academicOrgDescription: Queensland Conservatorium

description: This course encourages exploration and experimentation in cinematic arts practice. Through practical application and mentorship, students delve into areas of personal interest pushing boundaries and honing their professional skills, creative voice, and personal aspirations. Emphasising genuine curiosity towards personal and professional discovery, the course equips students with the skills and mindset needed to be agile and adaptable within the ever-evolving landscape of cinematic arts practice.
title: Experimental Practice
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course contains the competencies required to present evidence and expert opinion for judicial purposes, undertake reviews of case files and maintain knowledge currency in the field of forensic fingerprint investigation. These competencies will be implemented by police staff involved in forensic fingerprint investigation and should be demonstrated and applied within a courtroom and workplace context. Police staff will demonstrate presentation and communication skills, the ability to adhere to court/judicial procedures and etiquette and the ability to identify sources of current knowledge within the forensic fingerprint investigation discipline.
title: Develop Fingerprint Expertise
academicOrgDescription: School of Environment and Science

description: This course explores children's developing understanding of their place in the world and how to interact within it. You will investigate young children's developing awareness of their emotions and behaviours, the impact these have on others, and their participation in increasingly complex social interactions. You will engage in professional practice in a kindergarten, and you will be supervised by a registered teacher. Please be aware that this course may not follow the standard academic calendar. Please check your timetable on myGriffith for details of when classes commence and the duration of the Professional Experience Placement.
title: Supporting young children's pro-social behaviour
academicOrgDescription: School of Education and Professional Studies

description: Industrial Design Capstone Project 2 builds on the independent project initiated in Industrial Design Capstone Project 1 to execute an innovative and resolved project solution. Students will build on the research and design outcomes from Capstone Project 1 to refine and deliver the final solution to industry standards. The course enables third year students to consolidate their skills in industrial design workflows, project development and leadership, as an emerging industrial designer. Pre-requisites: 1107ENG Industrial Design Studio 1, 2108ENG Industrial Design Studio 2, 2208ENG Industrial Design Studio 3, 3126ENG Industrial Design Capstone Project 1
title: Industrial Design Capstone Project 2
academicOrgDescription: School of Engineering and Built Environment

description: How do we make sense of experiences of disturbance of emotion, perception, and cognition? This is not just a hypothetical question. It is estimated that almost half (43%) of Australian adults have experienced a mental health condition, but everyone will experience periods of difficulty their life. In our contemporary culture, these questions are understood through the lens of mental health. But what is mental health? How can we explain and support positive mental health? And how do our attitudes and beliefs shape our own experiences of mental health and our responses to people experiencing poor mental health? This course provides invaluable insights for professionals working in client-facing roles in human services and health disciplines, as well as those working in leadership, policy, and research.
title: Contemporary and Critical Approaches to Mental Health
academicOrgDescription: School of Allied Health, Sport and Social Work

description: This course will examine the history and theories of portraiture. A diverse range of images will be discussed from Egyptian funerary portraits through to modern and contemporary likenesses. Alongside large oil paintings and monumental sculpture, the course will include the study of coins, miniatures, silhouettes, photographs, prints and caricatures. The major figures in the history of Western portraiture, such as Van Eyck, Hals, Velásquez, Holbein, Goya, Gainsborough, Degas and Bacon will all be included. The course also utilises local collections and includes the study of Australian portraiture. A range of challenging concerns and issues will be addressed: such as likeness and authenticity; memory and commemoration; identity and the projection of self; portraiture and its relationship to class, race, sexuality and gender. We will also explore the curatorial and exhibition practices surrounding portraiture, especially the formation and role of National Portrait Galleries and the popularity of portrait prizes. Prerequisites: 7040QCA Visual Analysis and Critical Reflection
title: Art of Portraiture: History and Theory
academicOrgDescription: Queensland College of Art and Design

description: Good governance in government and business is crucial to controlling corruption, regulating organisational behaviour, and fostering ethical leadership, integrity and accountability in institutions. In this course you will examine long-term and immediate challenges in integrity and anti-corruption, focusing on the knowledge to equip you as an effective integrity practitioner. It is especially designed for current or future investigation, operations or prevention professionals in integrity or accountability agencies; internal integrity, compliance, risk or ethical standards professionals; policymakers, analysts or advisers in regulation and integrity; international development workers; and aspiring leaders in any organisation. By understanding Australian and international integrity and anti-corruption efforts, and the complex institutional and political contexts of integrity work, you will better understand your own legal and professional obligations, how to collaborate with others for stronger integrity systems and outcomes, and design, communicate and execute integrity interventions in support of ethical conduct and robust decision-making across society.
title: Integrity and Anti-Corruption: Professional Foundations
academicOrgDescription: School of Government and International Relations

description: This third year course examines Hollywood's historical evolution as a globally dominant multimedia industry, with emphasis on its industrial structure, the aesthetics of its films, and its cultural impact. PREREQUISTES: 1009LHS Introduction to Screen Analysis OR 2182LHS Introduction to Screen Analysis. Note: Students without the prerequisite course or prior experience of film analytic terms and concepts should contact the convenor. CO-REQUISITES: Nil. INCOMPATIBLE: 2100LHS Hollywood Cinema; CMM28 Hollywood Cinema (OUA equivalent course)
title: Hollywood: From the Nickelodeon to Netflix
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: Designing dynamic simulations involves the creation of realistic 3D scenes and elements that mimic the behaviour of real-world physical systems. In this course, students will learn how to design and create realistic simulations of physical phenomena such as fire, water, smoke, and destruction effects using industry-standard VFX software and techniques. Students will learn the theory behind these effects and acquire hands-on experience designing simulations that can be integrated seamlessly into film and game projects.
title: VFX: Mastering Dynamic Simulations
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course offers a comprehensive introduction to designing immersive 3D real-time environments for video games, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). It emphasises the design and creation of virtual spaces and the integration of 3D assets into real-time engines. Through focusing on real-time game production's unique demands and techniques, students will gain hands-on experience in designing and developing virtual environments that are visually captivating and optimised for interactive experiences.
title: Realtime Environments
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course immerses students in the intricacies of designing for animated productions. Grounded in comprehensive contextual research, students apply advanced techniques in designing for specified production projects; including crafting characters, costumes, sets. Through tailored projects, students hone their ability to evoke mood, tone, and genre while considering diverse distribution platforms and audience preferences, preparing them for professional success in art direction for animation, games or screen.
title: Advanced Art Direction
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course delves into the pivotal roles of production management and first assistant directing across a variety of disciplines in the screen industries. Through immersive case studies, hands-on exercises, and critical reflection, students navigate the complexities of overseeing and managing screen production processes. By completing this course, students gain a comprehensive understanding and professional skills essential for effective management in the dynamic world of screen production.
title: Production Management
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Film School

description: This course is designed to enable students with the knowledge and skills to enable them to discover opportunities which will provide initial insights into deciding on your career journey and your subsequent choice of major/s. Students will begin to develop their professional identity to align with their future career goals. You will discover how you can make an impact in the changing world of business through the skills and knowledge you will develop and apply during your degree.
title: Path to Professional Success: Navigating Your Future
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Business School

description: This 3rd year capstone course is designed to integrate a student's knowledge in the Finance major and apply these principles in an industry related setting. The course will integrate the concepts of global investments, macroeconomics, geopolitics, return and risk which all affect asset classes around the world. Students in this course will design and construct an investment strategy using exchange traded funds (ETFs) to manage a global investment portfolio for an institutional client. The design of the global investment portfolio will consider a variety of factors including asset classes, macroeconomic factors across countries, the various elements of investment returns and risks, as well as sustainable investments. The student will develop an investment proposal, strategy and portfolio to navigate a hypothetical client through the current set of global market risks from today and beyond. On completion of the course, the student will have acquired a global and integrated understanding of the dynamics relating to global investments, markets, short-term versus long-term portfolio construction, macroeconomics, government policy, sustainable investment choices and interaction of these elements.
title: Global Investment and Markets
academicOrgDescription: Department of Accounting, Finance and Economics

description: Hotels generate profit from perishable assets for which there is fluctuating demand. Effective revenue management is integral to the successful operation of hotel properties and chains, and is measured by the revenue per available room (RevPAR) index. This course is essential for all future hotel general managers, as a hotel's RevPAR index is a heavily weighted key performance indicator of a general manager's annual performance review. In this course, you will learn the theoretical underpinnings and the tactical operation of hotel revenue management strategies, including the application of strategic pricing fundamentals and capacity allocation techniques. You will also be able to evaluate the impact of various market segments and distribution channels on the achievement of room revenue targets, profit maximisation and competitive advantage. As a departmental manager in a hotel, this course will enable you to participate in revenue management conversations as an educated professional.
title: Hotel Revenue Management
academicOrgDescription: Department of Tourism and Marketing

description: This subject is designed to teach students the logic of research methodology in the social sciences. Students will learn how to articulate a researchable problem, formulate research hypotheses, logically determine what research methodology provides the best avenue to test these hypotheses, and carry out research. Students will also develop the necessary skills to analyse and write criminal justice policies.
title: Criminology and Criminal Justice Research Methods
academicOrgDescription: School of Criminology and Criminal Justice

description: Effective communication is at the heart of every organisation, influencing how ideas are shared, relationships are built and organisational goals are achieved. Across industries, communication professionals play an important role in connecting organisations with audiences, stakeholders and communities. This subject introduces the theories, concepts and practices that inform contemporary communication professions. You'll examine how communication operates across different contexts while building an understanding of the strategic considerations that guide professional practice. You'll consider the needs and expectations of different audiences, develop practical communication responses and examine how communication professionals create value for organisations and communities. You'll also explore the evolving nature of communication careers, helping you understand the knowledge, skills and professional capabilities required across a range of communication fields. By connecting theoretical foundations with practical problem-solving, you'll gain a strong introduction to communication as both an area of study and a professional discipline.
title: Communication Principles and Practices
academicOrgDescription: School of Humanities, Languages and Social Science

description: This course explores how international and European Union law shape global commerce and foreign investment, giving students a broad and coherent understanding of the legal frameworks that govern cross border economic activity. The course will be presented by three visiting academics from ELTE Law School, Budapest. Students who have completed 120 credit points may complete this course.
title: Issues in International and EU Commercial and Investment Law
academicOrgDescription: Griffith Law School
